# Feature delta — netns-density-295

**Feature ID:** `netns-density-295`
**GitHub issue:** [GH #295](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/295)

**Problem.** A VM workload is attached to the node through the guest's
virtio-vsock device over the kernel vhost-vsock backend of the vendored Cloud
Hypervisor fork, with every guest flow forwarded by an event-driven in-kernel
forwarder in the guest and host kernels (ADR-0197; ordinary guest sockets are
captured by guest-kernel Aya programs). This replaces the per-VM network namespace, TAP device and
shared bridge attachment, whose port ceiling stopped the 16,384-attachment
density target natively (`EXFULL` at the bridge's 1,024 port slots,
`net/bridge/br_private.h:28-29`, `net/bridge/br_if.c:418 @ v7.0`;
`deliver/native-e18-bridge-capacity-falsification.md`). ADR-0145 records the
decision.

**Wave state.** `TCP-CORRELATION` is approved (§ *[REF] TCP capture
correlation*), closing STEP 11-06's `SPECIFICATION_AMBIGUITY`. Its one new
parameterized Tier-3 cell remains a DISTILL prerequisite, and the reconciled
roadmap requires final independent revalidation before DELIVER resumes.
The previously approved DESIGN and authored DISTILL artifacts remain the
baseline outside that bounded addition.
The data path is the in-kernel forwarder, approved for Linux guests with a
guest-neutral host side (§ *[REF] vsock data path — the in-kernel
event-driven forwarder (EVMOD)*); its contract-shaping spikes held on
Linux 7.0. The guest hop of a guest that runs no Linux kernel (Unikraft) is
[GH #321](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/321). DELIVER has
completed through step 11-05; step 11-06 resumes after the bounded DISTILL
addition and final roadmap revalidation.

ADR-0145 replaces the bridge / TAP attachment; its code stays in the tree until
DELIVER deletes it, as listed under *Bridge-era code for DELIVER to delete*.

## Wave: DESIGN / [REF] vsock Attachment Replacement DESIGN

### Status

- Every accepted decision keeps its own approval date in § *Approval record*,
  one row per user ruling. `TCP-CORRELATION` is accepted: Linux 7.0 source and
  the executed final-ACK spike prove the sixth-program contract required to
  construct `GuestIoEvent::OutboundCaptured`. The one authorized Tier-3 cell
  remains DISTILL work and the folded roadmap remains pending final independent
  revalidation.
- Same-node mesh leg-B (LEGB-DIAL): the dial to a guest-prefix peer is
  marked and source-bound; no route covers the guest prefix except the
  gateway `/32` (GW-LOCAL: the guest gateway is the one host-local address
  of the prefix).
- Probes: a VM probe dial is exempt from the allocation's flow quota; a
  `Capacity` or `Quiesced` refusal records no sample (PROBE-NOSAMPLE). The
  probe runner numbers each written run; the row merges by run number;
  `ServiceLifecycle` applies the threshold when it reads the row, acting
  once per crossing; a failed liveness stop is retried on the next probe row
  still past the threshold and never twice on one row (PROBE-RUN-COUNT, D-1).
  Every probe run that writes no row emits one `probe.not_sampled` event.
  Multiple probes per role are kept; `GUEST_PROBE_SLOTS` (8) bounds the
  probes of a spec. An intent persisted with more probes than
  `GUEST_PROBE_SLOTS` is not migrated (greenfield single cut; the Phase-1
  upgrade deletes the intent store).
- A foreign quiescence hold is a fail-stop, checked by the model
  (`quiescence-foreign-hold-ends-in-fail-stop`, run
  `ForeignHoldRestoreChangesNothingThenFailStops`, hazard
  `quiescence-hazard-foreign-ignored`) and by a unit test of the
  supervisor's mapping of `QuiescenceRestoreError::ForeignHold` to
  `SharedGuestNetworkFailStopCause::ForeignQuiescenceHold`; there is no test
  seam (the production composition has one supervisor and one owner).
  Assumption K-A5 is discharged by spike K-A5 (`spike/findings-ka5.md`,
  kernel `7.0.0-29`).
- Proven facts P-62 to P-65 (guest-slot spikes V-1 to V-4) stand:
  END-IDEMPOTENT (a trailing end after a pair's end is a no-op) and
  CLEAN-FULL-END (a clean full end is `0x2` each way before close,
  ADR-0180).
- **The data path is the event-driven in-kernel forwarder (EVMOD-ADOPT).**
  The forwarder (P-67, P-68; ADR-0197) moves every flow's bytes on both
  sides, consuming from a source only what its target accepted. Its
  contracts are approved for Linux guests: EVMOD-LIFE (the module's
  lifetime, unload-safe by module reference counting, ADR-0198), EVMOD-BUILD
  (one in-repository source, built per kernel release, ADR-0203), EVMOD-LOAD
  (loaded by the host image and by `overdrive-init`, never by `serve`,
  ADR-0205), EVMOD-GUEST-KIT (a Linux guest's kernel and module are one
  artifact, checked by the guest, ADR-0206), EVMOD-SAFE (late callbacks,
  ADR-0204), EVMOD-CTL (the pairs' lifetime bound to their control context,
  ADR-0199), EVMOD-REC (one preallocated end record per id, ADR-0202),
  EVMOD-STREAM-END (how a `GuestStream` resolves every end it observes,
  § *Driving port — guest stream dial*), EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT (how an owner
  abort reaches a `GuestStream` and the guest without touching `V_h`),
  EVMOD-ATTACH-END (an ended half is refused with its own errno class and
  the owner aborts the flow, ADR-0210), EVMOD-PORT, EVMOD-END (ADR-0180;
  its watch of a dialled vsock, ADR-0216), EVMOD-PAIR (ADR-0212),
  EVMOD-DGRAM (ADR-0201), EVMOD-KTLS (ADR-0200), EVMOD-WQ and EVMOD-AB (the
  release point at the end record; no guest slot pool, ADR-0209), with the
  EV-PINS corrections and the WATCH-ABORT rule (ADR-0211). D3's flow bounds
  are ADR-0208, apart from ADR-0147's one pair per flow. The contract-shaping
  spikes V-EV-END, V-EV-CTL, V-EV-PAIR and V-EV-DGRAM held on Linux 7.0
  (P-69 to P-72; physical host `7.0.0-38-generic`, guests
  `7.0.0-29-generic`).
- **The host side is guest-neutral (HOST-NEUTRAL, ADR-0207).** The flow
  request, the datagram frame and the end classes are the host-side protocol
  of every guest; the host owner and the host forwarder never branch on
  guest type. The guest hop of a guest that runs no Linux kernel (Unikraft)
  is [GH #321](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/321).
- RESTART-GEN-CRASH: the loss of a generation replacement placed but not
  started at a `serve` crash is
  [GH #325](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/325) and is
  **not** fixed in #295 (§ *Restart decision*, "Defect RESTART-GEN-CRASH").
  The `cid_lease` run `RedeployLeasedAtServeCrashIsPlacedAgain` and hazard
  `crashLosesPlacedGeneration` stay in the model, pending #325 for
  conformance. RECORD-COST (the cost of the `guest-flow-owner` full
  `--record` run) is an outcome-neutral architect disposition
  (§ *Approval record*, "Architect dispositions"); it is not a user approval.
- Quint `specs/quint/probe-count` (`evidence/summary.json`): 31 checks, each
  matching its expect (19 hold, 12 expected violations), all `ci = true`; 9 named runs on the conformance main
  `probe_streak_conf` plus 6 hazard runs; model-checking main `probe_streak`;

- Composition (ADR-0219, ADR-0138): `run_server(config, adapters)` takes
  every driven adapter through a required `NodeAdapters` parameter; the
  intent store, view store, workflow journal and workload-identity CA are
  part of it, built by `NodeAdapters::host(&config, ..)`; `ServerConfig`

  The forwarder is opened, probed, audited and repaired on every node, in
  boot phase 1, before any boot effect (D-8). The vsock ports are node
  configuration with defaults 1234 / 1240 / 1243 (PORTS-CONFIG, ADR-0218);
  a test binds kernel-assigned ports and reads them back from their owners.
  The VM driver passes the three ports on the guest's kernel command line
  (GUEST-PORTS, ADR-0217). `[vsock]` node-TOML loading is
  [GH #327](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/327), outside
  #295. The inbound enforcement port holds leg S's guest dial (LEGS-DIAL,
  D-14, § *leg-S over vsock*).
- Lane prerequisites: `ovd_fwd` is loaded on Lima and on metal by the lane
  setup step `cargo xtask kmod-load` (FWD-PREREQ); the module build and lane
  setup are DELIVER step K, before step 0 (U-3 (b)). `kmod-load` reloads a
  stale idle module and reports any `EBUSY` on a live module as busy/retry
  with a message naming the holder class; no remedy is a reboot. The
  module's identity is its `version`, the whole-tree digest (D-20,
  ADR-0203). V-EV-SAFE and V-EV-UNLOAD
  use no KASAN: their oracles are no oops and the refcount on the stock 7.0
  kernel.
- V-9's measurements are the benchmark
  [GH #326](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/326);
  `vsock_density.rs` is a 64-VM correctness test. The `mtls_guardrails` AC3
  failure at HEAD is out of scope for #295 (no issue). The guest-kit
  microVM fixture (T-1) is built, launching through the production
  `CloudHypervisorVmm` (U-4 (a)). GH #324 is fixed in #295
  (RESTART-SSOT, § *Restart decision*, step 0 of § *Roadmap impact*).
- Quint `specs/quint/guest-flow-owner` (`evidence/summary.json`, kernel
  `7.0.0-38-generic`, Quint 0.32.0, Apalache 0.56.1): 279 of 279 checks
  matched expect (209 hold, 70 expected violations), 44 of them `cid_lease`

  - The scenario tables cite only hazards that exist in the record (the
    hazard table in § *Formal protocol model*, 65 rows).
  - `flows_one`, `flows_two`, `pair_mid` and the hazard-only

  - V-EV-UNLOAD and U-EV-UNLOAD use the stock 7.0 kernel; the stress's

  - `xtask`'s `kmod_load`: any `EBUSY` on a live module is busy/retry.

  `guest_flow` is always `GuestFlowAdapter::host()` out of crate; a

    `RootKeyAeadCodec::new`. `xtask` (`guest_kit_prepare::forwarder_module_path`,
    `kmod-build`, `kmod-load` and its hooks form `--busy-ok` (a stale idle module is
    reloaded, a busy one is refused with the holder class; § *Composition*,
    "`kmod-load`"), the mutants wrapper's
    `OVERDRIVE_KMOD_DIR`) and `overdrive-testing` (`guest_kit.rs`'s module
    lookup from the workspace root) read the module path from the workspace
    root, not `cargo_target_dir`, with the S-12 drift guard extended to the
    module path; the fixture and `kmod-load` compare the module's `version`
    (the whole-tree digest), not `srcversion` (D-20). The init `fwd_pair`
    driver gates its comparisons on the `VmmExit` it applied (the `fwd_pair`
    map); the spec's invariant `CtxGoneIffVmDown` that justifies the gate is
    in `fwd_pair.qnt` (no witness check).
  A fixture added later follows the same rule. (12) The `quiescence` driver's `RestartWith` goes
  through the composed rig (`boot_server`), not `run_server`; the
  `cid_lease` driver replays `PoolExhaustedRestartCleansThePredecessorThenPlaces`
  on `lease_conf_three` with the background leases and relabelling of the
  `cid_lease` map; the D-9 cell follows the descriptor order in § *Roadmap
  impact* 10-02.

- **Module reference counting (MODULE-REFCOUNT).** Test support:
  - **Version surface.** `OVD_FWD_VERSION` returns `abi_version` only; there
    is no `PERMANENT` flag, no `ForwarderError::NotPermanent` and no
    `/proc/modules` check in the probe's `Version` stage.
  - **The fixture's stale verdict** names `cargo xtask kmod-load`, which
    reloads an idle module, and never a reboot.
  - **`kmod-load`'s tests** cover four outcomes: absent → load; current →
    done; stale and idle → unload, then load; stale and busy → refused,
    naming the holder class.
  - **The hooks** run `kmod-load --busy-ok`.
  - **The unload cell, V-EV-UNLOAD** (§ *Validation plan*), is a
    real-kernel cell of the module suite. The `/sys/module/ovd_fwd/refcnt`
    oracle and the placement rule are in that item.
  - **Step K and step 4** (§ *Roadmap impact*) carry the context half and
    the socket half of the cell.

- **T-1: the guest-kit fixture.** The guest-kit Cloud Hypervisor microVM
  fixture is DISTILL-owned test support: an `overdrive-testing` helper that
  boots the CH fork with a guest kernel, `ovd_fwd.ko`, and `overdrive-init`
  or a scripted guest vsock peer, on the native-metal `kvm-tests` lane.
  R5-59 (a) (the real-adapter pair of the sim accept arbiters cited by
  `quint_udp_slots.rs` and `flow_io/sim.rs`), the guest-side `ovd_fwd` cells
  and the in-guest real-kernel cells run on it.
  **U-4 (option (a)): the guest kit launches through the
  production `CloudHypervisorVmm`.** The fixture holds no cloud-hypervisor
  argv of its own: no second renderer, no exemption in the DWD-09 clause, no
  new production API (§ *VMM backend contract*).
- **RESTART-SSOT (GH #324).** DISTILL authors regression obligations 1–5 of
  § *Restart decision* for step 0, and the `cid_lease` driver projects
  `st` (`wait` / `done` / `failed`), `retry`, `ex` and `att` from the fixed
  `restart_status_for_alloc(target, kind, run_desired, row, generation)`,
  `attempt_index_for_alloc` and `current_alloc` over Service-kind workloads
  (QPROJ-2W; the `cid_lease` map, which pins every modelled variable and
  the `Redeploy` map per pre-state). The `cid_lease` map, with the
  recording main `lease_conf_three`, is recorded in `evidence/summary.json`
  (44 `cid_lease` checks, of which 12 hazards): item 7
  (`VmmCrash` and `GuestReset` run no tick; `Assign` places a
  successor while the predecessor's lease is still held; `Launch` cleans the
  predecessor; actions `Finalize` and `AssignRefused`; projected fields
  `pred` and `pst`; the model-only ghost `g.fin`). `Finalize` and `Redeploy`
  carry the `reclaimed` guard (the driver never steps either before
  `vm_reclamation_boot::converge` returned; `Redeploy` is a handler call,
  reachable only once the listener is bound after `converge`), the `retry`
  / `ex` row does not read a launch clash's row (the clash path stays
  unmapped), and the hazards and guard runs are not driver targets. The
  driver's `#[quint_test]` set is every run listed under `cid_lease` item 8
  on `lease_conf_ok` except `CrashIsNotEnabledInThe325Window` and
  `CrashIsEnabledInThe325WindowWithoutTheGuard` (they check a model-only
  guard; production never refuses a `serve` crash), plus
  `RedeployLeasedAtServeCrashIsPlacedAgain` on `lease_conf_325` with
  `#[ignore = "pending #325"]` (GH #325), plus
  `PoolExhaustedRestartCleansThePredecessorThenPlaces` on `lease_conf_three`
  (D-18); its `#[quint_run]` targets `lease_conf_ok`, which excludes the
  #325 window (item 9).

- **Conformance driver targets.** Each driver replays its module's
  recording main (QPROJ-1, D-UP-1, PD-6): `flows_conf` (host and guest
  drivers) and `flows_beacon_conf` (VM driver) for `owner_flows`;
  `pair_conf` for `fwd_pair`; `quota_conf`, `lease_conf_ok`, `quiesce_conf`,
  `slots_conf`; `probe_streak_conf` for `probe-count`. The model-checking
  mains (`flows_ok`, `flows_two`, `flows_sess`, `flows_one`, `flows_beacon`,
  `quota_ok`, `empty_ok`, `quiesce_ok`, `quiesce_live`, `probe_streak`)
  record no `conf_step` and are not driver targets. There is no `flow_end`
  or `udp_empty` module and no driver for either; their scenarios are
  `fwd_pair` (`pair_conf`) runs (§ *Formal protocol model*, "Change list for
  the forwarder").
- **The `fwd_pair` runs the `pair_conf` driver pins** (each holds in the
  recorded run in `evidence/summary.json`), each with
  `#[quint_test]`: the nineteen of § *Formal protocol model* (the seventeen
  of the change list and the prefixes `Paired` and `DgramPaired`);
  `HostHalfCloseThenAbortBeforeGuestAttachIsAbort`,
  `GuestCloseBeforeHostAttachAborts` (the in-flight branch: the guest's
  `0x3` still in transit at the host's attach, U-EV3-1),
  `RemoteFinThenResetAbortsPair`, `ForwarderRecoveryAbortsThenReopens` and
  `ReleasedWatchWithNoRecordReadsAsAbort`; and
  `GuestAppFinThenResetAbortsPairWithEpipe`,
    `EarlyVsockHalfCloseBeforeGuestAttachCompletes`,
    `AppWriteAndFinBeforePairedAttachesInCloseWaitAndCompletes`,
    `IntakeChildResetBeforePairedIsRefusedAndFlowAborts`,
    `DestinationResetBeforeHostAttachIsRefusedAndFlowAborts`,
    `GuestCloseWithEmptyQueueBeforeHostAttachIsRefusedAndFlowAborts`,
    `OwnerAbortOfWatchLeavesVhAndStreamReportsAborted`,
    `OwnerAbortSendsGuestAbortThenHolderDropIsInert`,
    `ContextReleaseShutsWatchedVhAndHolderReadsNotConnected`,
    `DroppedStreamAbortsWatchThenGuestSeesAbort`,
    `TruncatedFrameAtPeerEndAbortsFrameInvalid`,
    `PeerCloseRacingOwnHalfCloseIsClean` and
    `VmmExitWithWatchRecordInFlightResolvesFromRecord`. The driver also
    replays randomized `#[quint_run]` traces on `pair_conf`. It projects
    `gen` and `cgen` from `flow_observation().forwarder_generation` and the
    `Paired` phases' `generation`, `oldCtx` from `SimFlowForwarder` (named
    arbiter), `unclassified` from `inventory()`, and the ended-half, watch and
    stream variables by the spec's names as QPROJ-8, "Ended-half, watch and
    stream variables", classes them (`attRes` and `attEnded` through the
    owners' `forwarder_attach_ended`; `hres` from the production
    `GuestStream`; the holder's own observation `gh.hobs` and the other
    ghosts are model-only). It maps the action names the spec declares: `TcpRst`
    (not `EpRst`), `HolderDrop` (not `DialerDrop`), `GuestAbort`,
    `HolderEnd`, and the orphan sweep as `VmmExit` then `FwdErr(h)`
    (U-EV3-7). The instances `pair_wlive` and `pair_dlive` are
    model-checking mains and record no step; no driver replays them.
- **Foreign-hold fail-stop (user ruling 2026-10-15).** The `quiescence`
  driver maps `ForeignRestore` to the driver's own `restore` with a hold of a
  second `QuiescenceLedger` and compares the owner's state unchanged
  (`ForeignRestoreChangesNothing`); it does not drive the supervisor's
  fail-stop that follows, because no production path presents a foreign
  hold to the supervisor, so the driver does not pin the run
  `ForeignHoldRestoreChangesNothingThenFailStops`. The fail-stop is covered
  by `quiescence-foreign-hold-ends-in-fail-stop` (with its hazard
  `quiescence-hazard-foreign-ignored`) and by a named unit test of the
  supervisor: `restore` returning `QuiescenceRestoreError::ForeignHold`
  ends in `SharedGuestNetworkFailStopCause::ForeignQuiescenceHold`. No seam
  is added for it.
- **Foreign hold dropped unredeemed is leaked at its issuing ledger
  (model-only claim, D-UP-4, PD-1).** The `quiescence` model has one owner
  and represents no second ledger, so it does not check this claim
  (`quiescence.qnt` D-UP-4 comment; README § *Model-only claims and what
  discharges them*), and no conformance driver projects it. Its discharge
  is a named sim/unit scenario of R5-32, through the public ledger surface
  (PD-2): two `QuiescenceLedger`s; the owner's `restore` of a hold the
  second ledger issued returns `QuiescenceRestoreError::ForeignHold`; the
  hold is dropped; the second ledger's `leaked()` rises by exactly one and
  the owner's `leaked()` (and `flow_observation().leaked_quiescence_holds`)
  is unchanged.
- **K-A5 wording (spike K-A5).** The guest owner observes the end of its
  control connection as EOF on `read` or `EPOLLRDHUP`; `ECONNRESET` occurs
  only at `connect()` (no listener, full backlog); a host reset close and a
  graceful close are indistinguishable at the guest. Scenarios and the
  guest-side driver wait for EOF / `EPOLLRDHUP`, never for `ECONNRESET` or
  `EPOLLERR`, and do not assert which kind of host close occurred.
- **The forwarder (EVMOD-ADOPT; EVMOD-LIFE to EVMOD-AB).** The record is
  `evidence/summary.json` (279 checks; `verify-evidence` passes, § *Status*);
  V-EV-END, V-EV-CTL, V-EV-PAIR and V-EV-DGRAM held (P-69 to P-72), and
  their shapes and hazard variants are the module suite's negative controls.
  Every scenario, fixture and driver exercises the in-kernel forwarder
  (§ *[REF] vsock data path — the in-kernel event-driven forwarder
  (EVMOD)*); § *Lifecycle Gate Ownership*, "EVMOD re-derivation of the
  boundary scenarios", lists each R5 scenario's disposition.
- **R5-28 / R5-31 Tier-3 half: the in-guest lane (D-22).** The Tier-3 half of R5-28 and R5-31 (the V-24 shape) runs in
  the in-guest lane (`overdrive-init/tests/integration/in_guest_lane.rs`,
  `kvm-tests`, native metal, the guest-kit fixture of the T-1 ruling), not
  through `serve`. No in-guest observation surface is added to production
  `overdrive-init`.
  - **Roles.** The guest side is the production guest owner
    (`GuestFlowOwner` over `KernelGuestOwnerIo`, the real `ovd_fwd` and a
    Linux 7.0 guest on the Cloud Hypervisor fork), driven by an in-guest
    cell of `guest_flow::real_kernel`. The host side is the lane's scripted
    host peer over the real host vsock (vhost-vsock): it opens V_h to the
    guest's stream port, writes the request and nothing else, then closes
    V_h, in each order the rows name relative to the guest's accept (V_g
    accepted before `Paired`, V_g still queued); it plays the control
    session — a `Paired` for the aborted flow answered with nothing, an
    `Abort` for a flow the guest does not yet hold, a session close
    followed by a reconnect. This is V-24's host script, and the guest is
    the production owner in place of V-24's userspace model.
  - **Where the oracle is read.** Every read is in the guest, by the cell:
    (1) the owner through its pinned crate-private
    `GuestFlowOwner::guest_observation()` (DG-5; no new accessor) — the
    flow leaves `accepted`, no pair is attached (`forwarder_attached`
    unchanged), and the session is held again after the reconnect; (2) the
    cell's in-guest application listener — no connection C (R5-31's "no C"
    case) or C reset, and no byte; (3) the host peer's record of the control
    session — no message for the flow; (4) the kernel shape itself on a V_g
    the cell accepts with its own raw listener under the same host script:
    the request read succeeds, then EOF, `POLLRDHUP`, `EPIPE` on the first
    write — V-24's witness re-run in the lane, so the owner-path cells never
    rest on a kernel fact the lane did not observe. (5) Within 1 s of the
    abort the owner holds no socket of the flow (1) and the application side
    has none (2). R5-31's abort-to-reset latency over a 1,000-flow burst is
    reported (p50 / p99), not asserted. Placement: the
    cell's owner is the guest's **only** owner — the lane boots the guest
    kit with the scripted peer as PID 1 and no production `overdrive-init`
    (`overdrive_testing::guest_lane::run_in_guest_owner_cell`), so no second
    owner contends for the UDP slot binds, the capture programs or the
    control port. R5-28's "counted" clause (the structured event
    `guest_flow.control_discarded`) has no in-guest read surface and is
    discharged by the seeded-sim half only; the lane asserts "no reply".
  - **Why this is the Tier-3 half (`testing.md`, "DISTILL — prove composed
    system behavior").** Neither cause has a production stimulus a `serve`
    test can drive. Quiescence is entered only by a component recovery
    (QHOLD), whose stimuli the approved design drives in seeded sim (R5-32);
    driving one through `serve` needs a test seam (removed by
    NO-OVERRIDE-SEAMS) or a foreign mutation of Overdrive's kernel state (not
    a design driver on the appliance). Control-session loss without a VM
    fault has no production stimulus (D-16, item (5) above). A through-`serve`
    cell could only fabricate the cause, which `testing.md` forbids ("drive
    causes, not fabricated consequences"), and an observation surface on
    production `overdrive-init` would add production API to observe a state
    no `serve` test can reach. The composed behaviour is instead proven in
    two halves that meet at the wire: the host half — the production host
    owner deciding the abort, closing V_h after the request with no write
    (H-1) and discarding a late `Paired` — in the seeded-sim composed rig and
    the `owner_flows` conformance drivers; the wire →
    guest half — the real kernel's close propagation, the production guest
    owner's reaction and the application's view — in this lane. The host
    peer's script is exactly the wire behaviour the host half asserts, so
    no participant of the contract is missing from both halves.
- **Guest-neutral host side (ADR-0207).** Host-side scenarios and drivers
  assert the host's behaviour on the wire protocol only; none selects host
  behaviour by guest kind. The guest-side scenarios are those of a Linux
  guest; a guest that runs no Linux kernel is
  [GH #321](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/321).

| MODULE-REFCOUNT (part of EVMOD-LIFE and EVMOD-SAFE) | 2026-10-20 | User ruling MODULE-REFCOUNT. `ovd_fwd` is not permanent; it is unload-safe by module reference counting, as the data-path ruling of 2026-10-16 allowed ("cannot unload while any socket is hooked"). Every hooked socket and every open control context holds a module reference (`try_module_get` / `module_put`). rmmod is refused while any reference is held and succeeds at zero. The module gains a `module_exit` that tears down its device and workqueue. `kmod-load` unloads and then loads a stale idle module, and fails a busy one with a clear "busy, retry" message, never a reboot. On the appliance the module is still loaded once at boot. A real-kernel cell proves the refusal while hooked and the success after release. The module's lifetime is ADR-0198's reference-counted lifetime; EVMOD-SAFE carries rule 5 (ADR-0204); forced unload stays off. **Architect dispositions.** Settled small decisions the architect took
without a user ruling, because neither changes a contract, a state meaning,
an owner or a check outcome (`.claude/rules/design.md` § "Surface material
design decisions"). They are not user approvals and are listed apart from the
table above.

| Id | Disposed | Disposition |

| RECORD-COST | Architect disposition (outcome-neutral) | The `guest-flow-owner` full `--record` run is the baseline for record cost. The long checks (`fwd-pair-safety-tlc`, `fwd-pair-watch-safety-tlc`, `fwd-pair-dgram-safety-tlc`, the `pair_live` liveness checks) are `ci = false`, so per-change CI cost is unchanged and only the full `--record` run, taken when a spec changes, pays it. Alternatives: lowering the TLC bounds of the long checks (weakens the exhaustive check of the watch and datagram protocols for a cost paid only at record time); asking the user (the cost is outcome-neutral, with no design consequence). Consequence for DISTILL: none |
| ADR-SLUG | Architect disposition (settled small decision) | An ADR's file slug must not misdescribe its decision. A faithful shortened prefix of the title is acceptable; a full-title slug is not required. ADR-0164 is `adr-0164-guest-vip-tcp-resolves-as-mesh-and-datagrams-use-the-connect4-rewrite.md` and ADR-0191 is `adr-0191-the-probe-runner-records-each-runs-streak-and-servicelifecycle-applies-thresholds-at-read.md`. Alternatives: full-title slugs for every ADR (long paths, no added fidelity); stale slugs (a link then misdescribes the decision it points at). Consequence for DISTILL: none |

| DR2-CLOSE | Architect disposition | **F-S1 (EVMOD-SWEEP)** — the orphan sweep's unlocked stores (`drivers/vhost/vsock.c:746-750 @ v7.0`) let a forwarder run read end-of-stream before the sweep's class is recorded. A run that reads an end from a vsock half with no recorded class takes `vsock_table_lock`, which the sweep holds across its stores and its `sk_error_report`, then acts on the class now recorded (`SocketError { ECONNRESET }`); `Unclassified` stays as the alarm for a forwarder defect only (§ *End classification*; ADR-0180). Alternatives: classify every unrecorded vsock end as the sweep's reset without the lock (removes the alarm); an unlocked `sk_err` re-read (no ordering); leave the end pending for the report (hangs the pair if none follows). | DR5-CLOSE | Architect disposition | **Granularity** — a crash-class restart in the `cid_lease` map follows production's steps (`cid_lease` item 7): `VmmCrash` runs no tick; a predecessor lease `pred` / `pst`; `Assign` from `ended`; `Launch` cleans the predecessor; `Finalize` and `AssignRefused`. Below the ceiling no dispatch retires the crashed allocation's lease (the reclaim pass skips the pending restart owner below the attachment cap, `workload_lifecycle.rs:399-478`), and `RestartAllocation`'s dispatch assigns the successor before it retires and releases the predecessor (`action_shim/mod.rs:2707-2716`, `:1760-1789`, `:1808`). Alternatives: make the `VmmCrash` step's tick retire the lease through a new reclaim-on-crash path (changes production to fit the model); keep one lease per workload and project the predecessor lease as model-only (the predecessor's lease is real CID-pool state, and hiding it leaves `CidUnique` unchecked for it). Every `cid_lease` run, hazard, witness, invariant and instance is listed (item 8). Item 6 and the hazard table claim only what a recorded check refutes (`retryOffByOne` refutes `ExhaustsOnlyAtCeiling`, not `ServeCrashPlacesAWorkloadAtTheCeilingAgain`). The restart-accessor proptest covers `Job`, `Service` and `Schedule`. The #325 window is excluded from `lease_conf_ok` by a guard and kept on `lease_conf_325` (item 9; alternative: ignore the driver's `#[quint_run]` too, which would drop all randomized `cid_lease` conformance until #325). Consequence for DISTILL: the `cid_lease` driver pins item 7's map and item 8's run set |
| DR6-CLOSE | Architect disposition | **CI flags (stable rule)** — `ci = true` iff the check's own time (`Seconds`, start-up retries excluded) in the latest full record is under **60 s**, half the two-minute limit of `.claude/rules/design.md`, which absorbs the run-to-run variance of a multi-job record; every other check is `ci = false`. The runner's own warning (`ci_overrun`, over 120 s, `xtask/src/quint.rs`) is the backstop. The `checks.toml` header states the rule. Alternatives: keep the 120 s line on one record (flags flip each record); the maximum over several records (needs records the runner does not keep; git history only); shrink the slow models (weakens checks that defend approved decisions). **Finalize and Redeploy after boot reclamation** — `run_server` runs `vm_reclamation_boot::converge` before it spawns the convergence loop and before it binds the API listener, so no tick and no handler call runs before reclamation; `Finalize` carries the guard `reclaimed`, as `Assign` and `AssignRefused` do, and `Redeploy` (`handlers::restart_workload`, reachable only through the bound listener) carries it too (`Stop` and `Release` need none: after a `serve` crash neither is enabled until an `Assign` of the new process). GH #325 is "WorkloadLifecycle marks a generation observed before its successor exists: a serve crash in that window loses the restart", scope matching § *Restart decision*. Consequence for DISTILL: `CrashIsNotEnabledInThe325Window` and `CrashIsEnabledInThe325WindowWithoutTheGuard` are not `#[quint_test]`s |

**EVMOD-LIFE to EVMOD-AB — approved by the user 2026-10-17, for Linux
guests.** The contracts pinned under EVMOD-ADOPT, with the spike corrections
of EV-PINS and the WATCH-ABORT rule written into them. Contract text:
§ *[REF] vsock data path — the in-kernel event-driven forwarder (EVMOD)*.
V-EV-END, V-EV-CTL, V-EV-PAIR and V-EV-DGRAM ran and held (P-69 to P-72); no
contract-shaping validation item is open (§ *Validation plan*). The host
side of each contract is guest-neutral (HOST-NEUTRAL, ADR-0207, approved
the same day and listed in the last row); the guest-side clauses are those
of a Linux guest, and a guest that runs no Linux kernel is
[GH #321](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/321).

Every open control context holds a reference through the device's `fops` owner, and every hooked socket holds one (`__module_get` at attach or watch, `module_put` at the end of its free work, after rule 5). `delete_module` is refused `EWOULDBLOCK` while any reference is held and succeeds at zero (`kernel/module/main.c:730-751`, `:828-835 @ v7.0`). `module_exit` deregisters the device, destroys the workqueue (draining it) and frees the scratch pool. Forced unload stays off wherever modules can be unloaded. The appliance image kernel has no module unloading (`CONFIG_MODULE_UNLOAD` off; ADR-0068 § 7), so nothing unloads a module there. ### Charter and inputs

- **Trigger.** The E18 density run hit the shared bridge's port ceiling
  natively: `EXFULL` at `set_link_master`, commit `9460d899`; Linux 7.0 allows
  1,024 ports per bridge (`net/bridge/br_private.h:28-29`,
  `net/bridge/br_if.c:418 @ v7.0`)
  (`deliver/native-e18-bridge-capacity-falsification.md`).
- **User selection (binding).** Shared-memory virtio queues + virtio-vsock +
  Aya Rust eBPF forwarding in the kernel; the Rust control plane manages
  sockets, maps, activation and lifecycle. Forbidden: a userspace payload
  relay, with one exception — the leg-S kTLS↔vsock relay for VM backends,
  temporary, deleted when #303 lands (INB-1, approved 2026-10-11); kernel
  patches or a forked or patched kernel; TAP-based attachment; C eBPF. Native
  validation on qualified metal. A VMM fork is not a kernel fork: D13 rules
  the vendored Cloud Hypervisor fork in, and RESET-EXIT is a change to it.
  **The user's forwarding selection is the event-driven in-kernel
  forwarder (EVMOD-ADOPT, 2026-10-16, ADR-0197):** payload is forwarded by a
  loadable C module (`ovd_fwd`; an
  out-of-tree module, not a kernel patch — the kernel source stays
  unmodified), on both sides; Aya Rust eBPF stays for the guest's socket
  capture (cgroup socket hooks, `sock_release`). Rust-for-Linux on 7.0 has
  no socket abstractions (`vendors/linux/rust/kernel/net.rs:6`), so the
  module is C; the C-eBPF prohibition is unchanged.
- **Kernel.** Linux 7.0 is the pinned appliance kernel (KERNEL-7.0,
  2026-10-10). Every kernel claim in this design is read in `vendors/linux`
  at tag `v7.0` and cited `path:line @ v7.0`. Every spike of this design ran
  on Linux 7.0.
- **Inputs.** The user rulings in § *Approval record*; the spike findings
  under `docs/feature/netns-density-295/spike/` cited per fact below; the
  Quint specification `specs/quint/guest-flow-owner/` (§ *Formal protocol
  model*).

### Evidence classification

#### Proven facts (with measured boundary)

Native runs: qualified metal (AMD EPYC 8024P, no nesting), stock Ubuntu
`7.0.0-29-generic` host and guest; rows that name Lima also ran on
`7.0.0-34` aarch64. Linux 7.0 is the pinned kernel (KERNEL-7.0), so every row
ran on the pinned kernel line. **None ran through `overdrive serve` +
`overdrive deploy`.** Fact numbers are stable identifiers; numbers not listed
supported mechanisms this design does not contain.

Hazards: an `ESTABLISHED`-only attach refused 414 of 500 write-and-FIN flows (`h_strict`); no attach-time classification aborted 289–386 of 500 as `unclassified_eof` (`h_noseed`); no attach-time run stranded TCP early data (`h_nokick`); publishing "send shut" after the SHUTDOWN left aborted 270–300 of 300 clean flows (`h_lateshut`, the CLEAN-FULL-END race found and fixed in the module). A consumed `sk_err` reads as EOF (`net/ipv4/tcp.c:2794-2806 @ v7.0`) | [`spike/findings-ev-pair.md`](spike/findings-ev-pair.md); `spike-scratch/netns-density-295-ev-pair/`; metal host `7.0.0-38-generic`, CH-fork guest `7.0.0-29-generic` | The host pair ran on vsock loopback, not vhost; the destination-reset shape on vhost had the peer play the forwarder; datagram mode, kTLS halves, pending-cap exhaustion and a release with early data pending not tested; the module refused a reset TCP half and an empty-queue `0x3` vsock half with the half's errno (`ECONNRESET`, `EPIPE`, `ENOTCONN`), where the contract returns `ECONNABORTED` with the cause in `end_errno` (EVMOD-ATTACH-END; module code, checked in DELIVER) |
| P-72 | **V-EV-DGRAM: datagram mode.** 0, 1, 1,431, 4,096, 4,097 and 59,000 B datagrams and 10,000 mixed sizes, connected and unconnected, both ways at once: delivered once, whole and in order, empties included (4,050 in the mixed run), over loopback vsock with the module at both ends and over a real vhost device to an independent host parser. 6,079 partial-send resumes under a 64 KiB credit window, 0 lost, duplicated or corrupt; frames written in random 1–5,000 B pieces 1,200/1,200; datagrams queued before attach forwarded. Oversize consumed and counted, no desync; a bad magic or length aborts `FrameInvalid`. A 10 s stall in four positions: every datagram accounted for (sent = delivered + drops), drops only at UDP receive queues (`net/ipv4/udp.c:1721-1731 @ v7.0`), kernel memory flat. ICMP refusal and the D26 rule ended the association `SocketError` (111, 1). The `recvmsg4` rewrite restored the original reply source (200/200). Slot release: abort then discard then reconnect carried 0 stale datagrams; without the discard 1,018 reached the next association; a port-0 slot changed port at disconnect (`net/ipv4/udp.c:2209-2235`, `net/ipv4/af_inet.c:562-563 @ v7.0`). Found: a frame left incomplete at the peer's end hung the pair (fixed: abort `FrameInvalid`); a frame larger than a lowered vsock buffer can never be queued; `ENOBUFS` never surfaces without `IP_RECVERR` (`net/ipv4/udp.c:1195-1201 @ v7.0`; 1,086,869 qdisc drops, `err` 0). Per-datagram CPU below the Aya path at every size and population | [`spike/findings-ev-dgram.md`](spike/findings-ev-dgram.md); `spike-scratch/netns-density-295-ev-dgram/`; metal host `7.0.0-38-generic`, QEMU VM and CH-fork guest `7.0.0-29-generic` | The host-side module on a real vhost transport not run; the spike's ioctl and end ring stood in for `/dev/ovd_fwd`; IPv6, `UDP_SEGMENT` / GRO and a natural vsock RST in datagram mode not covered; per-association kernel memory below the noise floor |

### [REF] TCP capture correlation

`TCP-CORRELATION` is **APPROVED 2026-10-23**. The exact approved correction
adds the sixth guest program, the private pre-program-load staging-pin
exception to ADR-0159 and the bounded DISTILL work recorded below.

User ruling `TCP-CORRELATION-NO-WEAKEN` (2026-10-23) requires the replacement
to preserve admission below `GUEST_TCP_PENDING_MAX`, correct connection
identity and reset-before-accept. It expressly rejects retaining abandoned
correlation rows until a fixed map fills. The normative audit below removes
that relaxation: every transient belongs to a live handshake or accepted
child and has an exact consume-or-close cleanup.

The accepted event contract requires a TCP intake accept to yield
`OutboundCaptured { child, original_destination, cookie }`, but the accepted
program set names only `Connect4`, `Sendmsg4`, `Getpeername4`, `Recvmsg4` and
`SockRelease`. On Linux 7.0, `tcp_v4_pre_connect` invokes `connect4` before
`tcp_v4_connect` allocates an ephemeral local port
(`net/ipv4/tcp_ipv4.c:206-218`, `:301-308 @ v7.0`). The accepted child exposes
the application's allocated local port, but not the application's socket
cookie or the destination that `connect4` replaced. `sock_release` cannot fill
the gap: the verifier admits `src_port` only for post-bind programs, not for
`BPF_CGROUP_INET_SOCK_RELEASE` (`net/core/filter.c:8960-9002 @ v7.0`).

The successful guest-capture spike carried the missing post-allocation join
through a separate SockOps program: `connect4` stored the original destination
by application socket cookie; `BPF_SOCK_OPS_ACTIVE_ESTABLISHED_CB`, after
local-port allocation, used that cookie to publish the original destination by
local port; the intake owner consumed that row using the accepted child's peer
port
(`spike-scratch/netns-density-295-guest-vsock-capture/bpf/src/main.rs:169-313`,
`vfwd/src/owner.rs:1001-1017`). This ordering matches Linux 7.0: the active
established callback runs in `tcp_finish_connect`
(`net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:6753-6768 @ v7.0`) before the client sends the ACK
(`:6994-7022`), while the server child becomes accept-visible only when that
ACK completes the hashdance and queues the child
(`net/ipv4/tcp_minisocks.c:933-945`,
`net/ipv4/inet_connection_sock.c:1382-1442 @ v7.0`).
The earlier active/full-tuple proposal was independently reviewed and rejected:
an application release can precede passive establishment, while retaining
abandoned active rows introduces a below-quota refusal. The user explicitly
ruled that admission below the quota must be preserved; that proposed
relaxation is removed.

**Decision TCP-CORRELATION.** Keep the five accepted guest programs
and their meanings unchanged, and add one guest-only
`GuestProgram::TcpCorrelation` SockOps program. It is loaded and attached to
the guest root cgroup before `Connect4`, before READY. It uses a guest-internal
TCP option on the ACK that completes the local handshake, installs no socket
in a sockmap, parks no bytes and moves no payload. EVMOD-PAIR and the deletion
of the redirect machinery remain unchanged.

The option ABI is exactly 18 bytes: experimental kind `254`; length `18`;
magic/version `0x4f56`; application `SocketCookie` as BE `u64`; original IPv4
address in network order; original port as BE `u16`. It exists only on the
guest-local TCP handshake to `workload_addr:GUEST_TCP_INTAKE_PORT` and is not
a host wire or persisted format.

`Connect4` only records the accepted per-socket original destination and then
rewrites. After Linux allocates the ephemeral port,
`BPF_SOCK_OPS_TCP_CONNECT_CB` copies that origin into
`ACTIVE_CORRELATION`, `BPF_MAP_TYPE_SK_STORAGE` on that exact active socket,
and arms the SockOps write and parse callbacks.
`BPF_SOCK_OPS_ACTIVE_ESTABLISHED_CB` makes the storage eligible to emit and
precedes the final ACK. While the storage exists in that phase, each non-SYN
ACK reserves and writes the exact option. The first later non-SYN peer packet
deletes it; without such a packet it follows the active socket to destruction.
Application file release does not remove storage from the still-live orphaned
TCP socket, so an ACK retransmission cannot lose its metadata.

For an ordinary or syncookie handshake,
`BPF_SOCK_OPS_PASSIVE_ESTABLISHED_CB` loads and validates the current final ACK
with `bpf_load_hdr_opt(..., flags = 0)` and writes
`Ready { application_cookie, original_destination }` to
`CHILD_CORRELATION[child_cookie]`. For TCP Fast Open, passive establishment
runs on the data-bearing SYN and writes `Pending`; the child's parse callback
loads the later final ACK and changes that exact row to `Ready`. An absent,
malformed or duplicate option never creates `Ready`.

`KernelGuestOwnerIo` accepts the child and looks up its exact cookie. `Ready`
is lookup-and-deleted once and yields the already-approved
`OutboundCaptured`. A Fast Open `Pending` child reserves one
`GUEST_TCP_PENDING_MAX` place immediately and is held without an owner event;
its final-ACK callback submits a best-effort private wake, and the existing
event wait scans every held Pending row before blocking and after every poll
wake; the existing fixed one-second owner audit deadline is the quiescent
fallback. `Ready` then yields the event;
an absent row or a child that ends while pending is reset/dropped, releases
the place, emits no `GuestIoEvent`, opens no flow and sends no control message.
`SockRelease` deletes any child row for that exact cookie. A dropped wake can
delay classification only until the next event-wait scan, at most the audit
deadline when the owner is otherwise idle, but cannot lose it. No new public or
`pub(crate)` owner-event variant is added.

Linux and executed evidence pin the mechanism:

- `tcp_connect` invokes `BPF_SOCK_OPS_TCP_CONNECT_CB` after ephemeral-port
  allocation and before the SYN (`net/ipv4/tcp_output.c:4300-4305 @ v7.0`),
  and active establishment precedes the final ACK
  (`net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:6753-6768`, `:6994-7022`).
- Linux's header-option selftest loads the current final ACK specifically when
  syncookie mode has no saved SYN
  (`tools/testing/selftests/bpf/progs/test_tcp_hdr_options.c:458-478 @ v7.0`).
  A Fast Open child receives passive establishment on the SYN and changes to
  `TCP_ESTABLISHED` on the final ACK (`net/ipv4/tcp_fastopen.c:326-371`,
  `net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:7118-7291 @ v7.0`).
- Linux builds SYN options, including Fast Open, before BPF reservation. The
  program writes nothing on the SYN. On the stock guest
  `tcp_ecn=2`, so the ordinary final ACK uses the 12-byte timestamp and leaves
  28 of 40 option bytes for the exact 18-byte option
  (`net/ipv4/tcp_ipv4.c:3508-3511`,
  `net/ipv4/tcp_output.c:1148-1232 @ v7.0`).
- The bounded Aya probe `spike/findings-tcp-correlation-option.md` ran the
  final-ACK option on Linux `7.0.0-38-generic` with Aya eBPF 0.1.1 / Aya
  0.13.1: ordinary immediate close, forced syncookie, actual data-in-SYN Fast
  Open `Pending -> Ready`, direct rejection, post-handshake active-storage
  deletion and refused-connect socket-lifetime cleanup all held. The same run
  created the BTF-backed storage through Aya, removed its transient pin before
  program attach and reached `VERDICT=WORKS`. The existing v20 probe
  independently exercised socket-storage lifetime, syncookies, Fast Open and
  SockOps state callbacks at scale.

**Contract Shape — bounded-change.** The declared universe is one guest boot:

- the accepted per-application-socket origin fact, unchanged by owner flow end
  and removed only by `sock_release` / socket destruction;
- `ACTIVE_CORRELATION = { phase, application_cookie,
  original_destination }` as socket storage on each captured active TCP
  socket, from `TCP_CONNECT_CB` until its first post-handshake non-SYN peer
  packet or socket destruction;
- the immutable 18-byte option on each non-SYN ACK while that active storage
  exists;
- `CHILD_CORRELATION[child_cookie] = Pending | Ready {
  application_cookie, original_destination }` until classification or exact
  child `sock_release`; and
- the sixth BPF link and the one child currently being classified.

`ACTIVE_CORRELATION` is socket-local storage with `max_entries = 0` and no
fixed capacity: every value belongs to and is automatically removed with its
exact active socket. Aya 0.13.1 loads its BTF-backed legacy declaration by a
private bpffs staging pin. Setup creates the map and pin, lets
`EbpfLoader::allow_unsupported_maps().map_pin_path(..)` reuse it, then unlinks
the pin and staging directory before program load, attach or READY. The
running owner holds only FDs; no pin exists during service or teardown. Any
returned setup failure unlinks/closes the staging objects before returning; a
PID-1 death in that pre-READY window ends the VM, so no next owner can adopt
them. `CHILD_CORRELATION` is an ordinary preallocated, unpinned Aya hash map
with exactly 8,194 entries: at most
4,097 children in the intake accept queue for `listen(4096)`, at most 4,096
accepted Fast Open `Pending` children, and one spare classification entry.
`bind_tcp_intake` uses backlog 4,096 and enables `TCP_FASTOPEN` with backlog
4,096 so existing `MSG_FASTOPEN` behavior is not silently disabled. No active
collection, LRU, eviction, tuple conflict, runtime/persistent pin, adoption or
new timer exists. Sequential connections cannot accumulate child rows, so
correlation creates no admission bound below `GUEST_TCP_PENDING_MAX`.

The only allowed state deltas are:

1. `Connect4` records/replaces only that application socket's accepted origin,
   then rewrites. Failure to retain it returns 0 before rewrite, so Linux
   returns `EPERM` and creates no intake child
   (`kernel/bpf/cgroup.c:1649-1702 @ v7.0`).
2. At `TCP_CONNECT_CB`, `TcpCorrelation` creates that exact socket's active
   storage from the origin and arms write/parse callbacks. `Connect4` never
   owns SockOps arming. There is no active collection or capacity; a
   kernel/map defect remains fail-closed rather than guessing.
3. Active establishment makes the final non-SYN ACK writer eligible. Each ACK
   while the active storage is in its emit phase writes exactly kind `254`, length `18`, magic
   `0x4f56`, BE cookie, network-order IPv4 and BE port. It writes nothing on a
   SYN. Reserve/store failure writes no partial identity.
4. Ordinary/syncookie passive establishment validates the current ACK and
   atomically replaces/creates the exact child `Ready` row. Fast Open passive
   establishment creates `Pending`; its parse callback performs the same
   validation on the final ACK. It
   never infers identity from a port or tuple.
5. The active parse callback deletes its storage on the first non-SYN peer
   packet after emit; otherwise socket destruction removes it automatically.
   `sock_release` removes the accepted application origin as before but does
   not remove the active retransmission copy from a still-live orphaned TCP
   socket. Child `sock_release` deletes that exact child row.
6. Intake accept lookup-and-deletes `Ready` once. It holds and counts
   `Pending`; every event wait scans it before blocking and after a wake, with
   the next fixed audit as the idle fallback. Missing,
   malformed, ended or second-consume state resets/drops with no event.
7. `overdrive-init` teardown drops the unpinned runtime maps and BPF link. No
   correlation state survives owner death, guest boot or VM end.

Identity cannot alias: the full cookie and destination travel in the same
connection's final ACK and materialize under that connection's child cookie.
The active storage is neither port-keyed nor tuple-keyed and cannot alias
another socket; the exact socket lifetime is its cleanup.

`KernelGuestOwnerIo` owns the exact count of every accepted `CapturedConn`
from accept through successful `attach_outbound` or consuming `abort`/`close`,
including Fast Open children it still holds internally as `Pending`. It
therefore enforces the same 4,096-place total across internal Pending children
and already-emitted handles without changing `GuestOwnerIo`,
`GuestIoEvent` or the owner model. The owner's existing event-side quota check
remains a redundant guard for emitted handles.

**Normative no-weakening audit.** The replacement removes no accepted
`zero`, `never`, `must`, `exactly`, fail-closed or required outcome. D15's
per-socket original-peer restoration remains through `sock_release`;
`GUEST_TCP_PENDING_MAX` remains the first correlation-independent pending-flow
bound and keeps its reset outcome; reset/release before accept keeps exact
cookie/destination identity; missing/malformed metadata never opens a flow;
EVMOD-PAIR still parks early bytes only in the intake child's receive queue.
The only additive contract is the sixth pre-READY program, its guest-internal
18-byte final-ACK option ABI, the two exact transient state lifecycles, the
event wait's pending-child scans with the existing audit deadline fallback,
`TCP_FASTOPEN` on the intake, and ADR-0159's approved private
pre-program-load BTF/map create-pin-Aya-reuse-unlink staging exception. The
staging pin is absent before program load, attach and READY; no runtime pin or
adoption is permitted.

The exact setup contract becomes:

```rust
enum GuestProgram {
    TcpCorrelation,
    Connect4,
    Sendmsg4,
    Getpeername4,
    Recvmsg4,
    SockRelease,
}
```

`TcpCorrelation::as_str()` is `"tcp_correlation"`. Its load failure maps to
the existing `GuestTransportSetupError::ProgramLoad { program:
GuestProgram::TcpCorrelation, source }`; its attach failure maps to the
existing `ProgramAttach` variant with the same payload. No new setup-error,
wire, owner-event or flow-lifecycle variant is added. Every active-storage
BTF/create/staging-pin/reuse/unlink or child-map/ELF-map load failure is
represented as that same
`ProgramLoad { program: GuestProgram::TcpCorrelation, source:
aya::EbpfError::MapError(..) }`, preserving the exact typed cause rather than
encoding it in a diagnostic string. The intake `listen`/`TCP_FASTOPEN`
configuration remains within `bind_tcp_intake`; its failures map to the
existing `GuestTransportSetupError::IntakeBind { addr, source }`.

Rejected alternatives:

- Looking up the peer with socket diagnostics after `accept()` does not cover
  an application socket already reset and released, and the accepted event
  still requires its kernel cookie. It turns a capture fact into a timing
  guess.
- Encoding a correlation token in `SO_MARK` adds an unapproved mark protocol,
  changes the workload socket's mark, and requires a new collision,
  exhaustion and cleanup contract. It is neither the accepted five-program
  mechanism nor the measured spike path.
- Restoring the spike's passive-established sockmap parking branch would
  reintroduce machinery EVMOD-PAIR explicitly removed. The proposed passive
  callback only re-keys metadata under the accepted child's cookie; it never
  installs or parks the child.
- The reviewed SYN/saved-SYN/SK_STORAGE proposal is invalid: Fast Open consumes
  the SYN option space and syncookie children have no saved SYN. It also needs
  accepted-child storage whose load lifecycle was left unspecified. The
  replacement writes the current final ACK, uses socket storage only for the
  active lifetime where capacity-free ownership is necessary, and pins its
  create/reuse/unlink staging entirely before program attach and READY.

Bounded production fallout: the design-owned, Rust `pub(crate)`
`GuestProgram` enum and `GuestProgram::ALL`; `GuestTransportOps`' production
load/attach dispatch; the guest Aya object's private option ABI, active/child
storage/child map, BTF-backed create/reuse/unlink loader, parse callbacks and
private wake record; `bind_tcp_intake`'s exact
backlog and `TCP_FASTOPEN`; and the private `KernelGuestOwnerIo` pending-child
table/audit integration. No
language-level `pub` or cross-crate Rust type, host wire type, persisted
format, owner-event variant, flow lifecycle or model variable changes. The
exact guest setup contract and READY attachment set do change from five
programs to six.

**DISTILL authorization and validation.** Existing pre-authored
transport tests receive neutral body corrections only: the program list,
labels, setup order/call count and existing `ProgramLoad` / `ProgramAttach`
cases change from five to six. Those are not a new behavioral scenario. One
new parameterized Tier-3 correlation scenario is required because SockOps has
no meaningful `BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN` substitute:

- in the existing disposable guest-kit owner lane on Metal, the source-local
  `guest_flow::real_kernel` cell configures the production
  `KernelGuestTransportOps` / `KernelGuestOwnerIo`; ordinary application TCP
  connects to non-local destinations must yield `OutboundCaptured` values
  whose destinations and application `SO_COOKIE`s are exact, and a second
  take of an accepted child must yield no replay; active storage disappears
  after the first post-handshake peer packet or socket destruction, and the
  child map returns to baseline;
- the application closes immediately after `connect()` and before userspace
  accept; the passive callback must still preserve the exact cookie/destination;
- forced syncookie and actual data-in-SYN Fast Open variants drive the current
  final-ACK producer; Fast Open must pass through `Pending -> Ready`, consume
  one pending place while held and release it after classification;
- a direct, uncorrelated connection to the reserved intake drives the real
  passive producer with no correlation option and is reset with no
  `GuestIoEvent`, flow or control record;
- the existing integration wrapper runs that one added source-local cell. No
  seeded correlation state, raw-packet fixture, production branch or public
  test-support API is authorized.

This changes `guest_flow::real_kernel` from 7 to 8 cells and the in-guest lane
from 11 to 12 cells. It adds no new lane, model, benchmark or test-support
surface. DISTILL owns the exact executable body and the
roadmap's step-11-06 counts, correlation criterion and spike-source range
(`spike/findings-tcp-correlation-option.md` and its standalone Aya sources);
the scenario remains required before STEP 11-06 DELIVER resumes.

Every row is approved by the user on the date shown (§ *Approval record*).
"Open validations" are DELIVER-blocking proof obligations
(§ *Validation plan*), not conditions on the approval. An id missing from this
table is not a current decision (§ *Changed assumptions*).

A VM probe attempt whose dial returns `GuestDialError::Capacity` (for a probe dial: node flow slots only) or `GuestDialError::Quiesced` yields no sample: no `ProbeResultRow`, no startup-probe attempt consumed, no threshold advanced, the probe runs again at its next period, and one `probe.not_sampled` event (PROBE-NOSAMPLE-EVENT) per probe per period; every other `GuestDialError` is a probe failure with its `as_str` as detail. ### D15 re-derivation — pre-activation behaviour and READY

**READY meaning (ADR-0082 §D4) is unchanged.** READY means "guest platform
init, including guest network configuration, completed". Guest network
configuration is: the dummy device with `workload_addr/32`, the fwmark rule and
`net.ipv4.fwmark_reflect=1`, the guest capture programs loaded and attached,
the forwarder module loaded and its context opened and probed (EVMOD-LOAD,
EVMOD-GUEST-KIT), and the inbound vsock listener bound. READY waits
for exactly that and nothing on the host; it includes no listener-map seed.
The per-VM control session is not a READY precondition; host activation
requires it (G-V3), and a dial to an Active allocation whose control session
is not live returns `GuestDialError::NoSession`.

**Pre-activation and dial behaviour.** "Today" is the production attachment
this design replaces (per-VM TAP on a shared bridge, leg-S dialling the
workload address over it).

| Situation | Today (bridge / TAP attachment) | This design | Kernel-imposed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Guest application traffic before activation | None: the application starts at EXEC, after activation | Same | — |
| Remote client to a declared port before activation | Reaches leg-C (rule 4); leg-S's dial to the guest goes unanswered (TAP down) until leg-S's deadline | Reaches leg-C; leg-S's `GuestStreamDial::dial` returns `NotServing` at once (the address is not an Active VM lease); leg-C closes | Outcome for the remote client is the same (failure) |
| Host-local platform client (leg-S, VM probe runner) before activation | Unanswered (TAP down) | `dial` returns `GuestDialError::NotServing` at once; no flow is opened | **No** — a typed refusal instead of a wait. **D15-R1**: accepted by the user 2026-10-05, restated under INB-1 2026-10-11 |
| Dial to an Active VM allocation whose control session is not live | n/a | `dial` returns `NoSession` at once, with no state change; distinct from `NotServing` so that an operator can tell a lost session from an address that is not served | **No** — the owner cannot pair a flow without the session (INB-1) |
| Connect after activation while the guest application is not listening | Refused by the guest kernel (RST) | The guest's own connect to the application is refused by the guest kernel; the guest replies `Refused { errno: ECONNREFUSED }` and `dial` returns it; a probe reports unhealthy, and leg-S ends the remote client's connection as for any refused dial | Preserved; the host keeps no listener state, so there is no mirroring lag |
| Guest application listens but never accepts | The guest kernel completes the handshake while the backlog has room | Same: the guest's connect completes and `dial` returns `Ok`, so a TCP-connect probe is healthy while the backlog has room; once the backlog is full the guest's connect times out at `GUEST_INBOUND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` and `dial` returns `TimedOut { errno }` (P-49) | Preserved |
| Connect while node forwarding is quiesced | n/a (TAP down: unanswered) | `dial` returns `Quiesced` at once and opens no flow; guest-opened flows are refused by admission | Changed from unanswered to refused; same outcome class |
| Early bytes from a client before pairing completes | Delivered | Guest-opened flows: held in the source socket's own receive queue until the pair is attached and then delivered in order (P-71). Host-opened flows: the dialer writes only after `dial` returns the `GuestStream` (H-1); a remote client's bytes wait in leg-C's socket until then | Preserved |
| A peer resets or crashes on an established connection | The other side sees a TCP reset | The end crosses the VM boundary as the vsock `SHUTDOWN` flags, classified by the forwarder on each side (R2-END, EVMOD-END): `0x3` while any direction is open, or `RST`, aborts the other side with a reset; `0x2` is a clean half-close, completed after the last accepted byte without a deadline (R2-DRAIN) (P-69) | Preserved |
| Outbound guest `connect()` completes before the destination is reached | Yes: leg-F accepted the TPROXYed connection first; destination failure surfaced afterwards as a close | Yes: the guest TCP intake accepts first; destination failure surfaces as a reset after pairing is refused | Preserved (inherited from leg-F) |
| Bound on reaching a non-mesh destination | Kernel SYN retries (`tcp_syn_retries`, about 2 min), then close | Same: the host's destination connect is bounded only by the host kernel's SYN retries; a refusal or ICMP unreachable fails at once, an unresponsive destination after about 2 min; then reset. The flow holds one of the guest's pending TcpConnect places (`GUEST_TCP_PENDING_MAX`) and its quota slot meanwhile | Preserved. **D15-R3 = (b), APPROVED 2026-10-06** |
| Guest TCP / UDP to `127.0.0.0/8`, `169.254.0.0/16`, the host's own addresses, the gateway except port 53 | TCP: reached host services through leg-F's pass-through (no deny list). UDP: dropped by implicit martian handling (loopback) or routed (others) | Refused `HostInternal` (D26) | **No** — a security decision. **D26, APPROVED 2026-10-06** |
| Application binds a port in `61000–62024` on `workload_addr` or `0.0.0.0` | Succeeds | TCP bind on 61,000 and UDP bind on 61,001–62,024 fail `EADDRINUSE` (each holds an intake of that protocol, D25-BIND); a TCP bind on 61,001–62,024 or a UDP bind on 61,000 succeeds; no reserved port is ever handed out as an ephemeral port; a VM spec declaring any port of the range, either protocol, is refused at deploy (`ParseError::ListenerPortReserved`) | **Partly** — some guest ports must hold the intakes; the range is a choice. **D15-R2**, part of D25, APPROVED 2026-10-06; bind scope D25-BIND APPROVED 2026-10-06 |
| More than 1,024 concurrent UDP (socket, destination) pairs, or more than 4,096 outbound TCP flows pending pairing, in one VM | Unlimited | `EPERM` on the new destination (UDP) / reset (TCP), counted (D25) | **No** — pool sizes. D15-R2, APPROVED 2026-10-06 |
| A guest UDP association idle for 120 s | Unaffected | Ends; the next datagram opens a new association; a late reply to the old one is dropped (D25) | **No** — bounds slot lifetime. D15-R2, APPROVED 2026-10-06 |
| A guest application sends an empty UDP datagram | Delivered in order with its neighbours | Same: the forwarder delivers it once and in order with its neighbours (EVMOD-DGRAM, P-72) | Preserved |

### C4 — system context and containers

The diagrams show the VM path. Exec and process workloads keep leg-S's and
the probe runner's plaintext TCP connect to `workload_addr:port`, unchanged
(INB-1).

```mermaid
  Rel(fwd, ext, "Forwards non-mesh guest traffic to", "host TCP / UDP socket")
  Rel(fwd, dns, "Forwards guest DNS datagrams to", "UDP to gateway:53")
  Rel(svc, cp, "Rewrites VIP destinations of owner sockets for", "cgroup connect4 (ADR-0164)")
  Rel(nft, cp, "Rejects host-internal transmits of marked sockets from", "output rule (D26)")
```

Notes on the diagram:

- **Dial path (INB-1).** leg-S and the VM probe runner reach a VM port only
  through the owner's `GuestStreamDial`: the owner opens a host-initiated
  vsock STREAM to the guest's inbound port 1242 with a `TcpAccept` carrying
  peer `gateway:0`, the declared port and the live launch token; the guest
  connects to the application and answers `Paired`, `Refused { errno }` or
  `TimedOut { errno }` on the control session. The dialer holds the host
  vsock of a host-opened flow; the host forwarder watches it and does not
  forward it. leg-S relays kTLS ↔ vsock in userspace; it is deleted when
  #303 lands.
- **Guest gateway (GW-LOCAL, ADR-0152).** The gateway is the one host-local
  address of the guest prefix (one Overdrive-tagged `local <gateway>/32` route
  on `lo`), and guest DNS reaches the `DnsResponder` through it. No other
  address of the prefix is local, and no other route covers the prefix
  (INB-1); the host firewall refuses guest-prefix traffic that is not diverted
  to leg-C (ADR-0172), the gateway excluded. Spike evidence: with the
  gateway route as the only route in the prefix, an unbound UDP socket
  connected to `100.95.0.1:53` was answered from `100.95.0.1`, and TCP / UDP
  to other prefix addresses failed `ENETUNREACH` (Lima `7.0.0-38-generic`;
  [`spike/findings-prefix-route-lo.md` § "Case 6 — rules restored, route removed, GW-LOCAL kept"](spike/findings-prefix-route-lo.md#case-6--rules-restored-route-removed-gw-local-kept)).
- **Leg-B to a same-node VM address (LEGB-DIAL, [ADR-0190](../../product/architecture/adr-0190-leg-b-marks-and-loopback-binds-same-node-vm-dials.md)).** When the leg-B
  peer is inside `GUEST_NODE_PREFIX`, `HostMtlsEnforcement` sets `SO_MARK =
  MTLS_TPROXY_MARK` and binds `127.0.0.1:0` before `connect()`; for any other
  peer it sets neither. The marked lookup matches the existing `fwmark 0x1 →
  table 100` rule and its `local default dev lo` route; the bound source keeps
  the `RTN_LOCAL` result from choosing the destination as the source
  (`net/ipv4/route.c:2848-2868 @ v7.0`), which is not a host address and fails
  the lookup with `ENETUNREACH` (`net/ipv4/route.c:2729`, `:2766-2769 @
  v7.0`). The dial is delivered on `lo` and assigned to leg-C by the existing
  TPROXY rule for a registered `inbound_destinations` tuple. The node needs no
  default route and no prefix route. Contract and fail-closed table: §
  *[REF] Component — host mTLS enforcement leg-B dial (LEGB-DIAL)*.
- **Reset-exit fork (RESET-EXIT, ADR-0182).** The fork routes the guest-reset
  dispatch to the VMM exit path, so a guest PID-1 crash or reset ends the VMM
  and the driver observes an ordinary VMM exit. The VMM is the only holder of
  its `/dev/vhost-vsock` file (CID-NOCLAIM, ADR-0146), so the file's release
  at VMM exit (`vhost_vsock_dev_release`, `drivers/vhost/vsock.c:753 @ v7.0`)
  runs the orphan sweep (`drivers/vhost/vsock.c:767–768 @ v7.0`), which
  marks every host flow to that guest reset
  (`sk->sk_err = ECONNRESET`, `drivers/vhost/vsock.c:749 @ v7.0`; V-30).
- **Flow ends (R2-END, R2-DRAIN; EVMOD-ADOPT).** The in-kernel forwarder on
  each side forwards a clean end as `SHUT_WR` after the last accepted byte
  and aborts a pair with resets on any other end (ADR-0197, ADR-0183); it
  classifies a vsock end in its own callback and reports each pair's end as
  one record on the owner's control context (EVMOD-END, EVMOD-CTL,
  EVMOD-REC). There is no ring, classifier program or drain program.
- **Guest-neutral host side (HOST-NEUTRAL, ADR-0207).** Everything inside
  the host boundary acts the same way for every guest. The guest boundary is
  drawn for a Linux guest (`overdrive-init` and its guest kit); a guest that
  runs no Linux kernel is [GH #321](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/321).

`docs/product/architecture/c4-diagrams.md` and `brief.md` carry the
system-level view; this section is the feature's own.

### Contract impact matrix

Classes: **Replaced** (subject gone; the replacing ADR supersedes it) ·
**Retained** (holds as written) · **Revalidate** (principle kept;
topology-bound content re-pinned and re-proven) · **Correct** (states
something false; the correction is recorded). "Topology" = bridge, TAP,
guest netdevice, L2, nft-on-bridge or netns.

#### Evidence and ceilings

- **R18 / R19 (E14(a)–(e))** receipts stay as qualified evidence for the
  bridge/TAP topology. Their conclusions do not transfer; V-8 proves
  fail-closure for the vsock attachment.
- **`NetSlot` (4,096)** stays removed for VMs. **The bridge ceiling
  (~1,023)** does not apply: there is no bridge. **The CH Unix-muxer ceiling
  (1,023 per VMM)** is avoided by D2 / D13 (kernel vhost-vsock, no Unix
  socket backend).

| 10-02 native fault evidence (TAP deletion) | **Replace** | Faults: owner kill (host and guest; the host's control-context release aborts every pair, and no VMM child keeps the context, EVMOD-CTL), the `Forwarder` component recovery (every flow aborted, the old context closed before the new one opens), guest PID-1 crash ending the VMM (RESET-EXIT; the device release aborts every host pair), `serve` crash followed by boot reclamation (NO-SURVIVE), control-session loss without a VM fault, UDP slot released before `Paired`, a far reader that stops (the sender blocks within the per-flow bound); no link-detach injection (D19-LINKS). **Fault entry points (D-9, D-16):** control-session loss without a VM fault has no production stimulus through `serve` + `deploy`: in a deployed VM the session's guest end is held by the production `overdrive-init` (PID 1), which closes it only by exiting, and PID 1's exit ends the VM (RESET-EXIT); the owner closes the host end on a decode failure or a read error (§ *Control session*, "I/O", "Accept"), which only a defective `overdrive-init` or the VM's end produces, and at the allocation's teardown, which is not a fault. No entry point and no test-only guest is added to the production VM driver (the guest kit's scripted peer is PID 1 only on a VMM the fixture launches itself, and `deploy` never launches one). Its evidence is (i) the seeded-sim composed rig — the production owner, supervisor and action shim over `SimGuestFlowIo`, the session's close and a malformed message scripted at the seam, with § *Control session*, "Loss" as the oracle (every flow of that VM aborted on both sides, `NoSession` dials, activation waits, the next `ControlOpen` restores service) — and (ii) the in-guest session cells on the guest-kit lane, which run the production guest owner against a scripted host peer that closes the session or answers malformed, proving the guest side aborts every flow and reopens. Leg-F loss and the `Forwarder` component recovery have no production-reachable external stimulus on the appliance: only an Overdrive defect ends leg-F's accept task or fails the forwarder context, no foreign actor exists (CLAUDE.md, appliance threat model), and no test-only fault hook is added to `run_server` (`development.md` § "Production code is not shaped by simulation"). Their evidence is the seeded-sim composed rig — the production supervisor and owner, with the leg-F accept end scripted at `SimMtlsIntercept` and the context `Io` / inventory drift at `SimGuestFlowIo` (R5-61, the `quiescence` and `fwd_pair` drivers, `ForwarderRecoveryAbortsThenReopens`) — paired with Tier-3 proof of the kernel effects the recovery relies on: a context release resets every far end and aborts every vsock peer (R5-61 through `KernelFlowForwarder`; the `serve`-death cell, where process exit releases the context), and leg-F's repair on the real kernel — the worker-level Tier-3 cell `leg_f_repair_rebinds_transparent_listener` (below). **What ends leg F's accept task in production (D-9):** an `accept(2)` error on its listener — `shared_listener_task` returns the error and the task ends `TaskFailed { leg: F }` (`overdrive-worker` `mtls_intercept_worker.rs:1388`). The reachable errors leave the listener `LISTEN` with the pending connection still queued, because they fail before the connection is dequeued: descriptor exhaustion (`EMFILE` / `ENFILE` at `get_unused_fd_flags`, `include/linux/file.h:198-201`, through `FD_ADD` at `net/socket.c:2022 @ v7.0`) and socket allocation failure (`ENFILE` at `sock_alloc`, `net/socket.c:1965-1967 @ v7.0`, before `ops->accept` at `:1988`). **The cell's evidence:** stimulus `EMFILE` — the test lowers its own `RLIMIT_NOFILE` soft limit to its open-descriptor count, queues one TPROXY-captured connection, observes `TaskFailed { leg: F }` with the listener still `LISTEN` (`ss -ltn`), restores the limit, then drives the supervisor's repair port on the real `HostMtlsIntercept`. Oracle: the repair returns `Ok` — with no `EADDRINUSE`, which has teeth here because a second bind conflicts with a still-`LISTEN` `SO_REUSEADDR` socket (`inet_bind_conflict`, `net/ipv4/inet_connection_sock.c:177-181 @ v7.0`), so a repair that bound before releasing the old socket fails — the old descriptor is closed, the new listener is `LISTEN` on the same address with a new inode, and a new TPROXY-captured connection accepts on it. A `shutdown(SHUT_RD)` stimulus is not used: it moves the old socket out of `LISTEN` (`net/ipv4/tcp.c:3409-3414 @ v7.0`), so a bind-before-release repair also succeeds there (`inet_connection_sock.c:170-176`), and it is no production event. The cell runs in a test binary of its own (the lowered limit is process-wide) under `host-kernel-shared`. **Order within the cell:** every descriptor the stimulus needs exists before the limit is lowered — the client socket is created first (or the connection is opened from another process), because a socket created under the lowered limit fails `EMFILE` itself — and `ss -ltn` runs only after the limit is restored (spawning it needs pipes); the delayed `ss` still shows `LISTEN` because the worker's `SharedOwner` keeps the listener in its `leg_f_listener` slot after the task ends (`mtls_intercept_worker.rs:2479-2484`). The existing `mtls` Tier-3 suite proves only the first bind and accept |

| 10-05 attachment-capacity receipts | **Replace** | Bridge-era receipts do not carry over (D11); density measurements are the benchmark GH #326 (U-2) |

New steps (DELIVER owns IDs and order; the numbers are the references
DISTILL's pending markers and the attachment-cut step (DG-2) use):

K. **Forwarder module build and lane setup (EVMOD-BUILD; U-3 option (b))
   — scheduled before step 0, the first DELIVER step.** It lets FWD-PREREQ
   hold from the first commit, so the `serve` fixtures and the hooks run as
   DISTILL authored them. It depends on no other step: the C module includes only kernel
   headers and its own UAPI header, which is the SSOT of the frame and
   control constants (the Rust-side equality assertions against
   `overdrive_core::guest_transport::wire` live in `overdrive-fwd`, step 4);
   `kmod-build` and `kmod-load` are xtask orchestration and import no
   `overdrive-*` crate; and until step 4 `serve`'s phase-1 forwarder probe
   does not open the module, so nothing in steps 0–3 reads it. Contents:
   - `kmod/ovd_fwd/` as a buildable, unloadable module skeleton
     (EVMOD-LIFE with MODULE-REFCOUNT). It contains:
     - `Kbuild`;
     - `ovd_fwd.c`, GPL-2.0, with `module_init` and `module_exit`;
     - the misc device `/dev/ovd_fwd`, whose `file_operations.owner` is
       `THIS_MODULE`, so an open context holds a module reference;
     - `OVD_FWD_VERSION` returning `abi_version`;
     - the module's per-CPU workqueue;
     - `module_exit` in § *Module placement and lifetime*'s order:
       deregister the device, destroy the workqueue;
     - `MODULE_VERSION` taken from the tree-digest define, with an `#error`
       when it is absent;
     - `include/uapi/linux/ovd_fwd.h` (§ *Composition*, "Which module is
       loaded").

     Step 4 grows the source to the full EVMOD contract together with the
     tests that exercise it, including the per-socket references and rule
     5. This step adds no forwarding behaviour, because nothing before step
     4 can test it.
   - `cargo xtask kmod-build [--kernel-build-dir <dir>]`:
     `MO=<workspace>/target/kmod/<release>/`, `W=1`, `C=1` and
     `checkpatch.pl --strict`, and the whole-tree digest passed as the
     `MODULE_VERSION` define (sorted relative paths and contents of
     `kmod/ovd_fwd/`). No test greps the source; the module's `module_exit` and `THIS_MODULE` owner are checked by
     the DELIVER review and by V-EV-UNLOAD's real-kernel cell.
   - `cargo xtask kmod-load [--busy-ok]` (§ *Composition*, "`kmod-load`"):
     load when absent, accept a current module, and reload a stale idle
     one; a busy one is refused with the holder class.
   - The context half of V-EV-UNLOAD (§ *Validation plan*), with the
     placement that item pins. While a context is open, `refcnt` is 1 and
     `delete_module` is refused `EWOULDBLOCK`. Once it is closed, `refcnt`
     is 0 and the unload succeeds; a reload then opens a context and
     answers `OVD_FWD_VERSION`.
   - The build prerequisites of the development hosts — the running
     kernel's build tree (`/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build`) and `sparse` —
     in the Lima template and the `infra/metal` provisioning. They install
     build tools only; neither loads a module (EVMOD-LOAD).
   - `infra/metal/README.md`'s lane setup; the CI jobs that run `serve`
     tests (strict `kmod-load`); the mutants wrapper's `OVERDRIVE_KMOD_DIR`;
     the `overdrive-testing` and `guest_kit_prepare` module path from the
     workspace root.
   - The lefthook changes: pre-push's `kmod-prepare` before `nextest`, and
     pre-commit's `nextest-affected` script running `kmod-build` and
     `kmod-load --busy-ok` first (§ *Composition*, "The lanes that run
     it"). They land in this step and in no earlier commit, because
     `kmod-build` exists only from this step on.

   host loading by the image (development hosts already load it through
