| 5 | `RedirectRefused` and the cell's `drops` (A3) | A redirect into a vsock that left `ESTABLISHED` was dropped silently (T6) | The forwarder's send returns the error (`-EPIPE` once the peer shut its receive side, `net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:2176-2177 @ v7.0`) and the pair aborts | **Removed** |
| 6 | `FLOW_EVENT_RING`, the flow event record, `FlowCell`, `CellEpoch`, epochs (A2), `ring_lost` (A7), `ring_dropped` | A BPF ring buffer drops records when full, and slots are reused | One end record per pair, stored in the pair and queued when it ends; ids never reused (ADR-0202) | **Removed.** Replacement EVMOD-REC |
| 7 | `flow_end_classifier` (raw tracepoint on `vsock:virtio_transport_recv_pkt`), A4, A5 and its source check, A6, A-34, V-31-MV, A10 and its remainder | An established vsock RST reads as EOF (P-49), and the redirect had no callback of its own on the vsock | The forwarder's own `sk_state_change` sees every received SHUTDOWN and RST with the socket lock held, before the end is readable (`net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c:1443-1464`, `:1244-1253`, `:1661`, `:1705 @ v7.0`), and its `sk_error_report` sees the orphan sweep's `sk_err`; a TCP reset is seen by the TCP half's `sk_error_report` (`net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:4890-4902 @ v7.0`), which the forwarder needs because it stops reading a source after its FIN and a later reset reaches no `recvmsg` (P-69, hazard 16) | **Removed** (A10 and V-31-MV by the ruling). Replacement EVMOD-END (measured, P-69) |
| 9 | SEQPACKET from the guest, port 1241, request kind `3` `DatagramSeqpacket`, the host's matching of kinds 2 and 3, the UDP-SEQ length check and its `short` / `long` / `lt8` / `badmagic` / `oversize` counters, the `EMSGSIZE` buffer invariant, the split-send residual, V-32-MIX, A-39 (D4, UDP-SEQ; ADR-0148) | A stream verdict cannot see record boundaries, and a SEQPACKET send under credit pressure resends a whole record after a prefix (P-3, P-53) | The forwarder frames and unframes on one STREAM itself | **Removed** (EVMOD-DGRAM) |
| 10 | Guest framing and reassembly strparser cells, CELL-RECREATE, cell generations, K-B3 (P-41) | The redirect needed a framing hop, and emptied cells refilled from hidden queues | The slot socket's receive queue is the only queue; the guest owner discards it at an association's end | **Removed** (EVMOD-DGRAM) |
| 11 | The host verdict's frame strip, the `EmptyDatagram` notice and `empty_lost`, the owner-sent empty datagram, UE-1, UE-2, D15-R4 (UDP-EMPTY, ADR-0165) | A zero-length skb can be neither passed nor redirected (P-30, P-50) | The forwarder sends a zero-length datagram itself, in order | **Removed** (EVMOD-DGRAM) |
| 12 | The guest `lo` unframe TC program (`UnframeLo`, ADR-0150) | The host→guest redirect into the slot socket carried the frame | The forwarder sends the unframed payload on the slot socket | **Removed** (EVMOD-DGRAM) |
| 13 | V-3-DGRAM | The redirect's datagram queues were unbounded | A UDP source's receive queue is bounded and the kernel drops beyond it (`net/ipv4/udp.c:1721-1731 @ v7.0`) | **Moot** (EVMOD-DGRAM); the bound is measured by V-EV-DGRAM |
| 14 | `GUEST_INTAKE_RCVBUF`, T4(a), T4a-SRC, A-36 | `tcp_read_skb` hands each queued skb whole to the verdict (`net/ipv4/tcp.c:1778-1785 @ v7.0`), so an overlapping segment was forwarded twice | The forwarder reads with `tcp_recvmsg`, which copies from `copied_seq` (`net/ipv4/tcp.c:2731`, `:2767 @ v7.0`) | **Removed** |
| 15 | Guest drain-cell slots `GUEST_FLOW_SLOTS`, `GUEST_FLOW_CELL_LEN`, the guest cell array | One drain cell per guest flow | A pair's state is allocated at attach (248 B in the spike) | **Removed** |
| 19 | `GUEST_PROBE_SLOTS` (8) and `ParseError::ProbeCountExceeded` | A guaranteed guest drain slot per probe | A probe dial is quota-exempt; the cap bounds the node flow slots one allocation holds outside its quota | **Kept** (EVMOD-AB) |
| 20 | END-IDEMPOTENT, CLEAN-FULL-END (P-65) | A trailing RST or `0x3` after an end | The forwarder ignores transitions after a pair's or watch's end; an owner closes a flow's sockets only after its end record | **Kept** |
| 21 | H-1, TCPACCEPT-END, K-A4 | The request must not reach the target | An attached socket's bytes are payload, so the acceptor reads the request before attach | **Kept** (H-1 reads "before attach") |
| 22 | D20 `SO_LINGER{1,0}` on owner sockets | Owner death resets the far ends | The context's release aborts every attached pair; linger still covers owner sockets not yet attached | **Kept** |
| 23 | A-11 and the forwarder startup probe stages | The probe proved the program set | The probe proves the forwarder | **Replaced** (§ *Earned Trust*) |
| 24 | ADR-0068's kernel floor entries for the redirect: `sock_ops`, SK_SKB with strparser over vsock, TCX on guest `lo`, `fexit` / `fentry` and raw tracepoints, ring buffers, mmapable arrays | The redirect's programs | The forwarder module, built for the pinned kernel; guest capture keeps cgroup socket hooks and `sock_release` | **Replaced** in the floor by the step that ships the module |

Unchanged by the forwarder: the control session and its messages, ATTR-TOKEN
and ATTR-LIVE-CLAIM, the beacon, leases and CIDs, `GuestStreamDial` and its
errors, QHOLD, the quota's count of half-closed flows, policy and D26, D24 /
D24a, LEGB-DIAL, GW-LOCAL, the probe contracts, the guest capture programs
and the UDP slot sockets.

##### Spike pins and their disposition

The four contract-shaping spikes ran on Linux 7.0 (physical host
`7.0.0-38-generic`, guests and the host-role VM `7.0.0-29-generic`) and held
(P-69 to P-72). Each pin they returned, and where the contract answers it:

| Spike, pin | Pin | Disposition (where pinned) |
|---|---|---|
| EV-END 1 | "A TCP half needs no classifier" is falsified for a half whose source direction already ended: a later reset is seen only by `sk_error_report` | The TCP rule of § *End classification*, "TCP halves", already pinned; disposition table row 7 |
| EV-END 2, EV-PAIR 9.6 | A TCP reset's errno is `ECONNRESET`, or `EPIPE` in `CLOSE_WAIT` (`net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:4905-4930 @ v7.0`); both are a reset | § *End classification*, "TCP halves"; § *Failure projection* |
| EV-END 3 | Queue a watch's record before calling the original callback, in `sk_state_change` and `sk_error_report`; the sweep path takes no socket lock | § *End classification*, "Watch" |
| EV-END 3, EV-CTL 4.3 | An owner's abort of a watch: unspecified in the spike (the spike's `ABORT` did not touch the socket); a forwarder `SHUT_RDWR` makes the holder's `read` fail `ENOTCONN` in part of the trials | **WATCH-ABORT, approved by the user 2026-10-17:** an owner abort never touches `V_h`; only a context release shuts watched sockets; the holder takes its outcome from the watch after its read ends (§ *End classification*, "A watch ended by the owner"; EVMOD-STREAM-END; EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT) |
| EV-END 4 | `GuestStream` never infers a clean end from `read() == 0` | § *Owners' use*, "`GuestStream`" |
| EV-END 5 | Attach-time classification untested there | Measured by EV-PAIR (`h_noseed`, P-71) |
| EV-CTL 4.1, EV-PAIR 9.1 | Accept a TCP half in `CLOSE_WAIT` | Already pinned (§ *Control interface*, accepted states) |
| EV-CTL 4.2, EV-PAIR 9.3 | The spike modules refused a reset TCP half (`ECONNRESET`, `EPIPE`) and a vsock half in `CLOSING` (`ENOTCONN`, which is also the never-connected errno); the owner then aborted the flow (measured: `eg-rst` refused in ≥ 99 %, `eg-drst`'s host attach refused, P-71) | **User ruling 2026-10-17: an attach refused because a half has ended is a flow abort.** EVMOD-ATTACH-END gives the class its own errno, `ECONNABORTED`, with the half's own cause in `end_errno`, so it cannot be confused with a never-connected half (`ENOTCONN`, an owner defect) or with another refusal class (§ *Control interface*, "States attach and watch accept") |
| EV-CTL 4.4 | A holder's `close()` alone leaves the watch live | A `GuestStream` drop aborts the watch, then closes `V_h` (EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT) |
| EV-CTL 4.5 | Error precedence, `bad_side`, refused attaches consume ids | § *Control interface*, "Attach refusals" |
| EV-CTL 4.6 | Pin the TCP families accepted | § *Control interface*: `AF_INET` and `AF_INET6` (the hooks are family-agnostic; the owners create IPv4 only, § *Scope*) |
| EV-CTL 4.7 | kTLS installed after attach clobbers the saved callbacks | No owner installs a ULP on an attached socket (ADR-0200); unchanged. MODULE-REFCOUNT adds that a half which has a ULP at removal keeps its module reference for the boot (§ *Pair end*, "Stale invocations", rule 5) |
| EV-CTL 4.8 | `O_CLOEXEC` is load-bearing | Already pinned; the probe's `Version` stage checks `FD_CLOEXEC` on the context descriptor |
| EV-CTL 4.9 | The module's unload safety | The module is unload-safe by reference count (§ *Module placement and lifetime*; ADR-0198). Forced unload — the one bypass of the count — stays off wherever modules can be unloaded, and the appliance image kernel has no module unloading (ADR-0068 § 7), which makes it unconfigurable there. The probe makes no permanence check |
| EV-CTL 4.10 | Inventory counters are per context | § *Control interface* |
| EV-PAIR 9.2 | Seed the classification at attach | Already pinned (§ *Forwarding*, "Attach order") |
| EV-PAIR 9.4 | Record "this side shut its send" before the SHUTDOWN leaves | § *End classification*, CLEAN-FULL-END row |
| EV-PAIR 9.5 | The attach-time run is load-bearing for TCP halves | Already pinned |
| EV-PAIR 9.6 | An owner that reads, writes or shuts an attached socket turns a reset into a clean end | § *Forwarding*, "Owners never touch an attached socket" |
| EV-DGRAM D1 | An incomplete frame at the peer's end aborts `FrameInvalid` | § *Datagram mode*, "The peer's end with frames queued": the callback's class decides first — `PeerAbort` for an abort-class end (every production end), `FrameInvalid` only for a clean-class end that leaves a frame incomplete (no production producer), completion after the last whole frame otherwise (U-EV-9) |
| EV-DGRAM D2 | Slot sockets bind an explicit port; release is abort → discard → disconnect | § *Datagram mode*, "Guest slot release" |
| EV-DGRAM D3 | The vsock half's `buffer_size` ≥ `MAX_GUEST_DATAGRAM_FRAME` | § *Datagram mode*; attach refuses (`BufferTooSmall`) |
| EV-DGRAM D4 | The whole-frame wait keys on `vsock_stream_has_data` | § *Datagram mode* |
| EV-DGRAM | No `ENOBUFS` handling; `IP_RECVERR` stays off | § *Datagram mode* |
| Modeller U-EV-7 | No cause for an unclassified end | `AbortCause::Unclassified`, record cause `5` (§ *End classification*) |

Items the spikes did not run, and their class:
V-EV-CTL (h) the recovery order is a composition of measured facts (the
release completes before it returns; one context's release leaves another's
pairs running, P-70 § 3.8) and runs through the production owner in DELIVER
(V-8); V-EV-CTL (i) the holder's observation after an owner abort does not
shape a contract, because the holder's end is resolved from the watch
whatever its `read` returns; V-EV-CTL (j) the stale-invocation stress under
stock-kernel stress is V-EV-SAFE, a module-internal check in DELIVER (ADR-0204); the
widened-window attach race of V-EV-PAIR is a module-internal check in
DELIVER (the attach section's locks are read in the source, F9). The
attach of an ended half needs no further run: the user's ruling refuses it
and aborts the flow, the measured behaviour of both spike modules (P-70
§ 3.6, P-71); EVMOD-ATTACH-END changes only the errno the module returns for
the class, which is module code checked by the module suite in DELIVER.

##### Module placement and lifetime (EVMOD-LIFE, ADR-0198; EVMOD-BUILD, ADR-0203; EVMOD-LOAD, ADR-0205; EVMOD-GUEST-KIT, ADR-0206; EVMOD-SAFE, ADR-0204)

- **One module, `ovd_fwd`, on both sides.** Out-of-tree, loadable, C,
  GPL-2.0 (it calls GPL-only symbols such as `tcp_abort`,
  `net/ipv4/tcp.c:5141 @ v7.0`). Rust-for-Linux on 7.0 has no socket
  abstractions (`vendors/linux/rust/kernel/net.rs:6` declares only `phy`).
- **Unload-safe by reference count (EVMOD-LIFE; MODULE-REFCOUNT).** `ovd_fwd` has `module_init` and `module_exit`. It holds a
  module reference for every object through which the kernel can still call
  its text, so it unloads only when nothing can.

  How `delete_module` decides (`kernel/module/main.c @ v7.0`):
  - It refuses `-EBUSY` a module that is still initialising or already
    going (`:810-816`), and, permanently, a module that has an `init` and
    no `exit` (`:818-825`; an `ovd_fwd` built from this source always has
    an `exit`).
  - Otherwise `try_stop_module` (`:828`) removes the loader's base
    reference. If any other reference remains, `try_release_module_ref`
    puts it back (`:730-742`) and the syscall returns `-EWOULDBLOCK`
    (`EAGAIN`) without calling `exit` (`:744-751`).
  - Only at zero does it mark the module `GOING`, after which
    `try_module_get` fails (`:907-920`). It then calls `exit`
    (`:832-835`) and frees the module (`:847`).

  The holders, and when each releases its reference:

  | Holder | Taken | Released | What it keeps callable |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | An open forwarder context (the misc device's `file_operations.owner` is `THIS_MODULE`) | `misc_open` → `fops_get` → `try_module_get` (`drivers/char/misc.c:131`, `include/linux/fs.h:2336-2339 @ v7.0`) | `__fput`'s `fops_put` (`fs/file_table.c:474 @ v7.0`), after the context's `release` has returned (`:468-469`) and after epoll's entries on the file were removed (`:460`) | Every `ioctl`, `read`, `poll` and the release itself, which aborts every pair and watch and waits until the id table is empty (EVMOD-CTL) |
  | A hooked socket: each half of a pair and each watched `V_h` | `__module_get` (`kernel/module/main.c:898-904`) inside `OVD_FWD_ATTACH` / `OVD_FWD_WATCH`, before its overrides are installed (the caller's context reference keeps the module live) | `module_put` (`:923-932`) as the last statement of the pair's or watch's free work, once per hooked socket. That work runs after rule 5 of § *Pair end*, "Stale invocations", after the RCU grace period, and after `cancel_work_sync` (rule 3). A refused attach takes no reference, or releases the one it took before returning | The `sk_data_ready`, `sk_state_change` and `sk_error_report` overrides and the write-space wait-queue entry's function, entered from any kernel path; the pair's or watch's work item and free work |
  | A hooked TCP half that has a ULP installed when its overrides are removed (`inet_csk_has_ulp`, checked only on a TCP half: `sk_family` `AF_INET` / `AF_INET6` and `sk_protocol` `IPPROTO_TCP`, because the helper reads `inet_connection_sock` fields, `include/net/inet_connection_sock.h:347-350 @ v7.0`; a vsock or UDP half has no ULP; no Overdrive owner produces this, ADR-0200) | as above | Never: the reference is kept for the life of the boot, and the module logs the socket once. The ULP may have saved a copy of an override (kTLS: `net/tls/tls_sw.c:2693-2694`, called at `:2511-2516 @ v7.0`) | The saved copy |

  Work items hold no reference of their own. Every item belongs to a pair
  or watch whose socket references outlive it, and runs on the module's own
  per-CPU workqueue (EVMOD-WQ), never a system queue. The free work's
  return after its own `module_put` still runs module text. `module_exit`
  waits for it: `destroy_workqueue` drains every pending and running item
  (`kernel/workqueue.c:5962`, `:5979`, `:4183-4194 @ v7.0`). Besides the
  overrides, the module's only other entry from a socket is each hooked
  half's write-space wait-queue entry (rule 5), which is removed before the
  half's reference is dropped. The module registers no timer, notifier,
  `call_rcu` or `kfree_rcu` callback, and no procfs or sysfs entry beyond
  the module's own attributes, so nothing else can call it.

  **`module_exit`** runs only at zero references, so no context is open
  and no socket is hooked. In order, it deregisters the misc device
  (`misc_deregister`, `drivers/char/misc.c:284`), destroys the workqueue
  (the drain above), then frees the scratch pool — the reverse of
  `module_init`. It calls no `rcu_barrier()`, because the module queues no
  RCU callback of its own (`queue_rcu_work`'s callback is workqueue code,
  and a pending one holds its pair's socket references).

  **Forced unload stays off** wherever modules can be unloaded, because
  `delete_module(…, O_TRUNC)` under `CONFIG_MODULE_FORCE_UNLOAD` skips the
  count (`:714-721`, `:747-751`). The stock 7.0 kernels of the development
  and Tier-3 hosts have it off (P-70; the `7.0.0-29-generic`
  configuration).

  **The appliance image kernel**, host and guest, has no module unloading
  (`CONFIG_MODULE_UNLOAD` off, ADR-0068 § 7). On the appliance the module is
  loaded once at boot and nothing unloads it. `delete_module` is the
  not-implemented stub there (`kernel/sys_ni.c:92 @ v7.0`), forced unload
  cannot be selected (`kernel/module/Kconfig:140-142 @ v7.0`), and the
  reference calls are inline no-ops (`include/linux/module.h:722-736 @
  v7.0`). The appliance relies on not unloading; every kernel that can
  unload relies on the count. The requirement is asserted over the image
  kernel's `.config` when the image is built.

  **No permanence check.** `OVD_FWD_VERSION` reports the ABI version only.
  The probe reads neither a flag nor `/proc/modules`.

  **Rejected:**
  - Permanent, with no `module_exit`: a module change needs a kernel
    boot, which on the shared development VM ends every workspace's runs.
  - Built into the appliance kernel (ADR-0198).
  - A reference dropped at unhook: a saved kTLS pointer outlives the unhook.
    Rule 5 and the ULP check close that.

  The module's real-kernel unload cell is V-EV-UNLOAD (§ *Validation plan*).
- **Pair-state and unload safety (EVMOD-SAFE).** A pair's freed state is
  protected by the stale-invocation rules 1–4 of § *Pair end*, "Stale
  invocations" (ADR-0204), which hold only while no ULP saves a copy of an
  override (EVMOD-KTLS, ADR-0200). Rule 5 fixes when a hooked socket's
  module reference may be dropped.
- **Source.** `kmod/ovd_fwd/` at the repository root: `ovd_fwd.c`, the
  frame parser `ovd_fwd_frame.c` and `ovd_fwd_frame.h` (FRAME-PARSE, below;
  `Kbuild` links both objects into the one `ovd_fwd.ko`), `Kbuild`, and
  `include/uapi/linux/ovd_fwd.h`, the C SSOT of the control ABI and of the
  frame constants. Not under `crates/` (no crate builds it), not under
  `spike-scratch/`.
- **Build (EVMOD-BUILD).** `cargo xtask kmod-build --kernel-build-dir <dir>` runs the
  kernel's out-of-tree build (`make -C <dir> M=kmod/ovd_fwd modules`)
  against the build tree of one kernel release (Linux 7.0, ADR-0068) with
  `W=1`, `C=1` (sparse) and `checkpatch --strict` clean, and writes
  `<workspace>/target/kmod/<kernel-release>/ovd_fwd.ko`, under the
  repository checkout it runs in, never the shared cargo target directory
  (§ *Composition*, "Where the built module lives"). Kbuild's outputs go to
  that directory through `MO=` (`Makefile:137-139`, `:195 @ v7.0`), so
  `kmod/ovd_fwd/` holds sources only. The module's `version` modinfo
  field is the whole-tree digest `kmod-build` passes as a define (§
  *Composition*, "Which module is loaded"), the identity FWD-PREREQ's stale-module check
  compares. `finit_module` checks a module
  against the kernel it was built for through `same_magic`
  (`kernel/module/main.c:2593-2596 @ v7.0`): with `CONFIG_MODVERSIONS` that
  is `kernel/module/version.c:97-105 @ v7.0`, which for a module with CRCs
  compares the rest of `vermagic` after the release word, and the kernel
  checks the symbol CRCs (`version.c:75-94`, `:13-73`;
  `kernel/module/main.c:3340-3341`, `:1261-1262 @ v7.0`); without
  `CONFIG_MODVERSIONS` it is the `#else` stub that compares the whole
  `vermagic` (`kernel/module/internal.h:421-424 @ v7.0`) — so each root
  filesystem carries the build for its own kernel: the host image's
  against the host kernel's release and a guest's against its guest
  kernel's release, which differ today (host `7.0.0-38`, guest `7.0.0-29`
  in the spikes). Overdrive builds and publishes one module per kernel
  release it supports: the pinned appliance kernel (host and guest, ADR-0068
  § 4) and the stock 7.0 kernels its Tier-3 hosts and guest fixture run.
  xtask is the right home: it
  consumes kernel build artifacts and imports no `overdrive-*` crate
  (`.claude/rules/development.md`). The module is signed with the image's
  module-signing key when the pinned kernel enforces module signatures; no
  runtime signature policy is added (a root-level loader is outside the
  threat model).
- **Loading (EVMOD-LOAD).** Host: the appliance image loads it at boot, before
  `overdrive serve` starts; `serve` never loads modules, and nothing on the
  appliance unloads one. Development hosts: the lane setup loads the
  workspace's own build (`cargo xtask kmod-load`, which checks the loaded
  module's `version` and reloads a stale module while it is idle;
  § *Composition*, "Forwarder module as a lane prerequisite"). The Lima
  template and `infra/metal` provisioning load no module at boot, because
  they cannot know which workspace's build to load. A module change is a
  reload while the module is idle, never a reboot. Guest: `overdrive-init` loads it with `finit_module` from the
  fixed path `GUEST_FORWARDER_MODULE_PATH = "/lib/overdrive/ovd_fwd.ko"`
  (a core constant beside the guest's other paths) before READY, beside the
  vsock transport modules it already loads.
- **Who puts the module in a Linux guest (EVMOD-GUEST-KIT).** A
  module is bound to one kernel build, so a Linux guest kernel and its module
  are one Overdrive artifact, the **guest kit**: for each guest kernel
  release Overdrive supports, one kernel image, the `ovd_fwd.ko` that
  `cargo xtask kmod-build` built against that kernel's build tree, and the
  `overdrive-init` of the same Overdrive release, published together. The
  supported guest kits are the pinned appliance kernel's (ADR-0068 § 4) and,
  for Tier-3 only, the stock Linux 7.0 kernel the guest fixture boots, whose
  module the fixture's provisioning builds on the host it runs on.
  - **End state (the guest design).** The guest kernel is the pinned
    appliance kernel, and the image factory (#259) builds every guest root
    filesystem with `overdrive-init` and the kit's module at
    `GUEST_FORWARDER_MODULE_PATH`. No deploy can pair a guest kernel with a
    module of another kit.
  - **While VM specs name their own kernel and root filesystem.** BYO
    artifacts are an interim until the image factory
    ([#259](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/259)) delivers
    the guest image and `overdrive-init`, not the guest design. A VM
    spec's `kernel` must be the kernel image of a published guest kit, and
    its root filesystem carries that kit's `overdrive-init` and module at
    `GUEST_FORWARDER_MODULE_PATH` — the same contract under which the
    operator already bakes `overdrive-init` into the root filesystem
    ("the platform ships the binary and the contract"). Any other guest
    kernel is not supported and fails the VM's start before READY with a
    cause naming both releases (next bullet). `overdrive deploy` of a VM
    built from a kit runs the slice end to end; the Tier-3 walking skeleton
    runs on the fixture's kit.
  - **A guest that runs no Linux kernel** carries no `ovd_fwd` and no guest
    kit; it implements the same host-side protocol in its own image
    (HOST-NEUTRAL), and that hop is
    [GH #321](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/321).
- **A refused or missing module (EVMOD-GUEST-KIT).** `overdrive-init` makes
  the mismatch an observed fact: before `finit_module` it reads the module
  file's `vermagic` from its `.modinfo` section and the running release from
  `uname(2)`, and compares the module's release (the first word of
  `vermagic`, which is `UTS_RELEASE`, `include/linux/vermagic.h:41-42 @
  v7.0`) with the kernel's, on every kernel configuration. The kernel does
  not always compare the release. `check_modinfo` compares `vermagic`
  through `same_magic` (`kernel/module/main.c:2593-2596 @ v7.0`). With
  `CONFIG_MODVERSIONS` — which the appliance image's configuration does not
  exclude — that function is `kernel/module/version.c:97-105 @ v7.0`: for a
  module that carries CRCs it skips the release word and compares the rest,
  and the kernel checks the CRC of `module_layout` (`version.c:75-94`,
  refused `ENOEXEC` at `main.c:3340-3341`) and of every imported symbol
  (`version.c:13-73`, refused `EINVAL` at `main.c:1261-1262 @ v7.0`): a
  module of another release whose CRCs all match would load. Only without
  `CONFIG_MODVERSIONS` is `same_magic` the `#else` stub that compares the
  whole string (`kernel/module/internal.h:421-424 @ v7.0`).
  `overdrive-init`'s comparison is therefore the only release check on a
  `CONFIG_MODVERSIONS` kernel, not a diagnostic. A module of the same
  release but another build is refused by the kernel — the rest of
  `vermagic` or a CRC, or the whole string without `CONFIG_MODVERSIONS` —
  and reported
  as `ForwarderModuleLoad`. Three distinct failures, each a
  `GuestTransportSetupError` variant printed on the guest console, after
  which the guest exits before READY (the existing "guest exited before
  READY" start failure): `ForwarderModuleMissing { path }` (no file at the
  path); `ForwarderModuleRelease { module: KernelRelease, kernel:
  KernelRelease }` (the module was built for another kernel; the message
  names both and says that the VM's kernel and root filesystem must come
  from one guest kit); `ForwarderModuleLoad { source: std::io::Error }` (any
  other refusal of `finit_module`, a signature refusal under enforced module
  signing included). `KernelRelease` is an `overdrive-init`-private newtype
  (non-empty, at most 64 bytes, `__NEW_UTS_LEN`,
  `include/uapi/linux/utsname.h:15`, `:28 @ v7.0`; no whitespace or NUL;
  `FromStr` / `Display`). Deploy
  validation does not check the kernel: the API ingress does not read the
  node's kernel image, and the guest is the one owner that holds both facts
  — the running release and the module's — before any flow (ADR-0206,
  alternatives).
- **Version.** The control device reports its ABI version; the adapter
  refuses a different ABI (`ForwarderError::AbiMismatch`). No permanence
  flag or `/proc/modules` check exists (MODULE-REFCOUNT).

##### Sides and pairs

Every pair has exactly one `AF_VSOCK` `SOCK_STREAM` half. Half A is named
first at attach.

| Side | Flow kind | Half A | Half B | Mode | Attached by, when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Host | TcpConnect, non-mesh | V_h (accepted on 1240, request read) | D (TCP to the destination) | Stream | Host owner, after D's connect completed, before `Paired` |
| Host | TcpConnect, mesh | V_h | L (loopback TCP to leg-F) | Stream | Host owner, after L's connect completed, before `Paired` |
| Host | Datagram association | V_h (accepted on 1240, kind 2, request read) | H (connected UDP) | Datagram, UDP half B | Host owner, after H's `connect()`, before `Paired` |
| Host | TcpAccept (a dial) | V_h, held by the dialer | — | **Watch** | Host owner, when the dial's V_h connects, before the request is written |
| Guest | TcpConnect | I (intake child) | V_g (to host 1240) | Stream | Guest owner, on `Paired` |
| Guest | TcpAccept | V_g (accepted on 1242, request read) | C (to the application) | Stream | Guest owner, after C's connect completed, before `Paired` |
| Guest | Datagram association | S (UDP slot socket, connected to the application socket's address) | V_g (to host 1240, kind 2) | Datagram, UDP half A | Guest owner, on `Paired` |

The directions the evmod spike measured map onto these pairs: A (vsock
source to guest TCP target) is the guest's TcpAccept and TcpConnect inbound
direction, G (guest TCP source to vsock target) their outbound direction,
and the host role's `v2t` / `t2v` (P-68) the host pairs. No pair joins two
TCP sockets (the spike's T direction belonged to the removed parking cell).

##### Forwarding, per direction

- **Trigger.** Both halves are a source of one direction and the target of
  the other. The forwarder overrides `sk_data_ready`, `sk_state_change` and
  `sk_error_report` of both halves and keeps the originals. It does **not**
  override `sk_write_space`: its write-space trigger is an entry on each
  half's socket wait queue (`sk->sk_wq->wait`), added at attach with
  `add_wait_queue` and removed at the pair's end with `remove_wait_queue`
  (`kernel/sched/wait.c:18-27`, `:69-76 @ v7.0`). The socket's own
  `sk_write_space` (TCP `sk_stream_write_space`, which clears
  `SOCK_NOSPACE` only when writeable, `net/core/stream.c:34-51`; vsock and
  UDP `sock_def_write_space`, `net/core/sock.c:3617-3637`, or on a UDP
  socket its `sock_wfree` fast path `sock_def_write_space_wfree`,
  `:2675-2685`, `:3643-3660 @ v7.0`) wakes the queue with `EPOLLOUT`, and
  the entry's function, for a wake whose key carries `EPOLLOUT`,
  `EPOLLWRNORM` or `EPOLLWRBAND` (or has no key), marks the direction whose
  target this half is and queues the pair's work item. Why not an override:
  rule 5 of § *Pair end*, "Stale invocations" (a vsock or UDP socket's
  `sk_write_space` is also called by `sock_wfree` from preemptible process
  context with no lock). Each override and the entry's function record
  which directions need a run and queue the pair's one work item. The
  original `sk_data_ready` is not called (an attached socket has no
  userspace reader); on a pair's halves the originals of `sk_state_change`
  and `sk_error_report` are called first, as in the spike, because a pair's
  end record is queued by its work item after the abort actions, not in the
  callback. A watch is the exception (§ *End classification*, "Watch").
  A callback never sleeps and moves no byte; the vsock receive path calls it
  with the socket lock held (`net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c:1661`,
  `:1693`, `:1705 @ v7.0`). The entry's function runs with the wait-queue
  head's lock held and interrupts disabled (`kernel/sched/wait.c:104-108`,
  `:118-127 @ v7.0`), so it takes no lock of the module's that is taken
  with `spin_lock_bh` and touches only the pair's direction bits and
  `queue_work`.
- **Run.** Peek at most `FWD_CHUNK` (64 KiB) from the source with
  `MSG_PEEK | MSG_DONTWAIT`; send the peeked bytes to the target with
  `MSG_DONTWAIT | MSG_NOSIGNAL`; consume from the source exactly the bytes
  the target accepted (an `iov_iter_discard` receive). On `-EAGAIN` or a
  short send stop and wait for the target's write-space wake (its
  wait-queue entry); on an empty
  source stop and wait for its `sk_data_ready`. After `FWD_RUN_BUDGET`
  (256 KiB) in one direction requeue, so one pair cannot hold a worker.
  `FWD_CHUNK` and `FWD_RUN_BUDGET` are module constants, not contract; a
  change needs V-9's measurement.
- **Why it is bounded.** A peek returns no vsock credit; only a dequeue
  advances `fwd_cnt` and sends the credit update
  (`net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c:806-809`, `:536`, `:583`,
  `:654-655 @ v7.0`), and a TCP source's window stays closed while its bytes
  stay queued. A credit update and a TCP ACK that frees space wake the
  writer (`virtio_transport_common.c:1440-1441`; `include/net/tcp.h:770-776
  @ v7.0`), so the forwarder resumes without a timer.
- **Attach order (EVMOD-PAIR).** For each half in turn the forwarder takes
  the half's socket lock (`lock_sock`), then `sk_callback_lock` for writing,
  installs its overrides and sets `sk_user_data`, and **in the same
  section** reads the half's attach-time state. The half's write-space
  wait-queue entry is added under the socket lock after that section (a
  write-space wake carries no state the attach must classify; a wake before
  the entry exists is covered by attach's first run of each direction), so
  the module never takes a wait-queue head's lock inside `sk_callback_lock`
  or `vsock_table_lock`. The section reads: for TCP `sk_state`,
  `SOCK_DONE` / `RCV_SHUTDOWN` and `sk_err` (read with `READ_ONCE`, never
  `sock_error`, which would clear it); for vsock `sk_state`,
  `peer_shutdown`, `SOCK_DONE` and `sk_err`. For a vsock half the section
  also holds `vsock_table_lock` (`net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:247-248`), the
  lock the device release's orphan sweep runs under
  (`net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:453-471`, `drivers/vhost/vsock.c:721-750 @
  v7.0`), which sets `sk_err` without the socket lock. Lock order: the
  socket lock, then `vsock_table_lock`, then `sk_callback_lock`. The sweep
  holds the table lock when it calls `sk_error_report`, and an override
  that takes `sk_callback_lock` for reading would deadlock against an
  attach holding `sk_callback_lock` for writing while it waits for the
  table lock; the end re-check of EVMOD-SWEEP takes the table lock under
  the socket lock, in the same order. Every transition that
  changes this state runs under one of the held locks: vsock receive
  processing under `lock_sock` (`net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c:1661`,
  `:1705 @ v7.0`), TCP input queued to the backlog while the socket is owned
  and processed at `release_sock` with the overrides in place
  (`net/ipv4/tcp_ipv4.c:2318-2321 @ v7.0`), the orphan sweep under the table
  lock. So a transition is either in the attach-time state or seen by an
  override, never neither and never both unrecorded. The state check that
  refuses an ended half (EVMOD-ATTACH-END) is made in this same section,
  before anything is installed on that half. Half A is checked and hooked
  before half B is examined; a refusal on half B unhooks half A (the order
  of § *Pair end*, "Stale invocations") before the call returns, so a
  refused attach leaves neither half hooked (measured: after a refusal the
  other half could still be attached or watched, P-70 § 3.6). Every refusal
  of an ended half ends in the owner's abort of the flow, so an event half A
  received while briefly hooked has no reader it must reach. The attach-time state
  of each half is recorded as the bits and end it has acted on, and attach
  then queues one run of each direction, which forwards the queued bytes and
  carries out an end already present (§ *End classification*, "Ends present
  at attach").
- **Owners never shut before attach, and never touch an attached socket.**
  An owner neither shuts down nor writes a socket it will attach after
  reading that socket's request; this is what makes the attach-time
  classification unambiguous. Once attached, the owner neither reads, writes
  nor shuts the socket until it has read the pair's end record: a read that
  consumes a TCP half's `sk_err` makes the forwarder's next read return
  end-of-stream (`net/ipv4/tcp.c:2794-2806 @ v7.0`), turning a reset into a
  clean end (P-71 § 9.6). The only owner calls on an attached socket's
  pair are `abort` and `abort_all`.

##### End classification (EVMOD-END, ADR-0180)

The classification rule of R2-END is computed in the forwarder. For each vsock half the forwarder keeps the peer-shutdown bits it
has already acted on. In its `sk_state_change` override — called after every
received SHUTDOWN with its flags recorded in `peer_shutdown`
(`net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c:1443-1461 @ v7.0`) and after an
`RST` (`:1463-1464` → `virtio_transport_do_close`, `:1244-1253`) — it
compares `peer_shutdown` with them:

| Transition the callback sees | Class | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `SEND_SHUTDOWN` newly set, `RCV_SHUTDOWN` not set | Clean half-close of the peer's direction | Forwarded as EOF once the vsock's queue is empty (the reader sees end-of-stream only then, `net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:2326-2328 @ v7.0`) |
| `SEND_SHUTDOWN` newly set together with `RCV_SHUTDOWN` (`0x3`, or an `RST`) | Abort: the peer closed or reset with its direction open | Pair aborted |
| `RCV_SHUTDOWN` newly set, `SEND_SHUTDOWN` already acted on, and this side has shut its own send direction — the vsock half's own `sk_shutdown & SEND_SHUTDOWN`, read under its socket lock; `vsock_shutdown` sets it before the SHUTDOWN leaves, under the same lock (`net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:1203`, `:1216`, `:1221 @ v7.0`), so the peer's `0x3` cannot be classified before it. A forwarder flag published after the SHUTDOWN left is the defect EV-PAIR found (hazard `h_lateshut`: a clean flow aborted in 270 of 300, P-71) | The peer released a flow ended both ways (CLEAN-FULL-END) | None (END-IDEMPOTENT) |
| `RCV_SHUTDOWN` newly set while this side still sends | Abort: the peer stopped receiving | Pair aborted (a send would fail `-EPIPE`, `af_vsock.c:2176-2177 @ v7.0`) |
| `sk_err` set — the device release's orphan sweep (`drivers/vhost/vsock.c:746-750 @ v7.0`, reported through `sk_error_report`, no state change) | Abort, `SocketError { ECONNRESET }` | Pair aborted |
| Any transition after the pair's or watch's end | — | None |

The class is fixed per transition, in the callback, so once a half is
attached the forwarder never classifies from an accumulated state: `0x2`
followed later by `0x3` and a direct `0x3` are told apart. On the locked
receive path the class is recorded before the end is readable: the
transition and its callback run under the half's socket lock, which the
forwarder's run also holds while it reads the half.

**The orphan sweep is the one writer outside the socket lock (EVMOD-SWEEP,
F-S1).** `vhost_vsock_reset_orphans` stores `SOCK_DONE`,
`peer_shutdown = SHUTDOWN_MASK`, `sk_state = SS_UNCONNECTED` and
`sk_err = ECONNRESET` as four plain stores, then calls `sk_error_report`
(`drivers/vhost/vsock.c:746-750 @ v7.0`), holding only `vsock_table_lock`
(`net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:458`, `:471`). A run that reads the half between
the store of `peer_shutdown` (`:747`) and the store of `sk_err` (`:749`)
sees end-of-stream with `sk_err` still 0: the state stored at `:748`,
`SS_UNCONNECTED`, is the value 1 (`include/uapi/linux/net.h:49-50`), which
`recvmsg` reads as `TCP_ESTABLISHED` (`include/net/tcp_states.h:13`), so the
read passes the state check (`af_vsock.c:2522`) and reaches the wait loop;
the loop stops on the peer's SEND bit (`:2326-2328`) and, with no byte
queued and `sk_err` 0, the read returns 0 (`:2439-2442`). The class the
sweep's `sk_error_report` override will record is not yet recorded. The
stores carry no barrier, so on a weakly ordered CPU the run may see them in
any subset; every subset either reads as that end-of-stream, as
`-ECONNRESET`, or as no end. The same holds for the guest transport's reset
(`virtio_vsock_reset_sock`, `net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport.c:413-423`,
run through the same table-lock walk, `:442-443 @ v7.0`), whose run reads
`-ENOTCONN` from the state without `SOCK_DONE` (`af_vsock.c:2530-2531`).

The rule: **a run that reads an end — end-of-stream or an error — from a
vsock half whose class is not recorded takes `vsock_table_lock`
(`spin_lock_bh`) before acting, then reads the recorded class again and acts
on it.** Every store of the sweep and its `sk_error_report` call are inside
one hold of that lock, so the acquisition orders the run after a sweep that
was in progress when it read, on every architecture: the override has run
and recorded `SocketError { ECONNRESET }`, and the run aborts the pair with
that cause. A sweep that had not started on this socket when the run read
stored nothing the run saw. The nesting — socket lock held, then
`vsock_table_lock` — is the kernel's own order (`vsock_bind` →
`__vsock_bind`, `af_vsock.c:1106-1107`, `:863 @ v7.0`); the sweep never
takes the socket lock, so the two cannot deadlock. The re-check costs one
uncontended lock acquisition per vsock end that found no class, which
outside a sweep is no end at all.

Only an end whose class is still unrecorded after that re-check is
`Unclassified`: no writer in the kernel source produces it (every locked
path that sets `SEND_SHUTDOWN` in `peer_shutdown` without `sk_err` calls
`sk_state_change`, `virtio_transport_common.c:1253`, `:1461 @ v7.0`, and
both unlocked writers end in `sk_error_report` under `vsock_table_lock`), so
it is reachable only through a broken invariant of the forwarder itself.
The forwarder aborts the pair with its own cause, `Unclassified { side }`
(record cause `5`), and counts `unclassified_eof` as an alarm (U-EV-7). It
is not mapped to `PeerAbort`: a broken invariant keeps a cause no reachable
end uses. Measured 0 in every non-hazard run of P-69 and P-71 (including
1,280 pairs and 640 watches ended by a VMM kill, P-69); with the
attach-time seeding removed, 289 to 386 of 500 (hazard `h_noseed`, P-71).
The sweep window cannot be widened without changing the kernel, so the
re-check is discharged by the source reading above and the model, not by a
measurement: in `fwd_safe` the design's run takes the lock and
`NoUnclassifiedEnd` (part of `Safety`) holds (`fwd-safe-pair-safety-tlc`,
`fwd-safe-watch-safety-tlc`); the hazard `noSweepRecheck`, which omits the
re-check, violates it (`fwd-safe-hazard-no-sweep-recheck`, TLC); the runs
`SweepStoresBeforeErrReadRechecksUnderTableLock` and
`SweepErrVisibleFirstRechecksUnderTableLock` hold (§ *Formal protocol
model*). `NoUnclassifiedEof` is `fwd_pair`'s invariant, not `fwd_safe`'s.
`fwd_safe` models the vhost orphan sweep's two stores; the guest
transport's reset (`virtio_transport.c:413-423`, walked under
`vsock_table_lock` at `:442-443` and `:752-753 @ v7.0`) has the same shape
— `TCP_CLOSE` and `sk_err` stored, then `sk_error_report` — and is covered
by the same rule through the source reading above, not by a separate model
action.

**Ends present at attach.** An end that reached a half before its overrides
existed is in the attach-time state (§ *Forwarding*, "Attach order"), and is
classified once, there, by the table above with this side's send direction
open — which it always is at attach, because an owner never shuts a socket
before attaching it:

| Attach-time state of the half | Class | Effect of the first run |
|---|---|---|
| vsock: `peer_shutdown = SEND_SHUTDOWN` only, no `sk_err` | Clean half-close of the peer's direction | Queued bytes forwarded, then `shutdown(SHUT_WR)` on the target |
| vsock: `ESTABLISHED` with `RCV_SHUTDOWN` set (with or without `SEND_SHUTDOWN`), including `SOCK_DONE` with `peer_shutdown = SHUTDOWN_MASK` and bytes still queued (an `RST`, or `0x3`, that found data queued: `virtio_transport_do_close` leaves the state `ESTABLISHED` then, `:1249-1252`) | Abort | Pair aborted in the first run, after no byte: `PeerAbort { side }` |
| TCP: `CLOSE_WAIT` (`RCV_SHUTDOWN`, `SOCK_DONE`; `net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:4953-4960 @ v7.0`), no `sk_err` | Clean end of the peer's direction | Queued bytes forwarded, then `shutdown(SHUT_WR)` on the target |

This is the table's rule, not a second one: its only clean case with
`RCV_SHUTDOWN` requires that this side has shut its own send direction,
which cannot be true at attach. A `0x2` followed by `0x3` before attach is
therefore an abort, as a direct `0x3` is, and need not be distinguished. A
half that has **ended** — no connection left to forward — is not attached
at all: attach refuses it and the owner aborts the flow (EVMOD-ATTACH-END,
§ *Control interface*, "States attach and watch accept"). The shapes are
reachable: before the host attaches, the guest owner's close of
`V_g` (a pending intake child that reset, the pairing deadline, session
loss) sends `0x3` or `RST`; before the guest TcpConnect attaches on
`Paired`, the host forwarder may already have forwarded the destination's
FIN as `0x2` on `V_h` (the control session and the flow vsock are different
connections, so `Paired` and the `0x2` are not ordered), and may then abort
(`0x3`); a guest application that writes and half-closes before `Paired`
leaves its intake child in `CLOSE_WAIT`; an intake child, a destination or
an application reset before attach leaves its TCP half in `CLOSE` with
`sk_err` pending. Measured (P-71): the accepted rows (`CLOSE_WAIT`; vsock
`ESTABLISHED` with `SHUTDOWN_MASK` and queued data, aborted at attach 5,678
times) and the refused ended halves (an intake child reset before `Paired`,
refused in ≥ 99 % of `eg-rst`; a destination reset before the host attach,
`eg-drst`), each followed by the owner's flow abort with no clean EOF at a
far end.

**TCP halves.** A FIN makes `recvmsg` return 0 after every queued byte
(`net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:4953-4954`, `net/ipv4/tcp.c:2794-2795 @ v7.0`).
End-of-stream does not prove the end was clean: `tcp_recvmsg` tests
`SOCK_DONE` before `sk_err` (`net/ipv4/tcp.c:2794`, `:2797 @ v7.0`), so a
peer that sends a FIN and then a reset — a server closing with unread data —
reads as end-of-stream, and the reset is visible only through
`sk_error_report` (`tcp_done_with_error`, `net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:4890-4900
@ v7.0`) or a later send. The rule: **`sk_err` on a TCP half aborts the
pair while any direction of the pair is still open**, whatever its
`recvmsg` returned — seen by the half's `sk_error_report` override (an
`sk_err` already pending at attach refuses the attach instead,
EVMOD-ATTACH-END; it is read there with `READ_ONCE`). Once both directions have ended
the pair has already completed and the transition is ignored. A6's end
check has no subject. The rule is load-bearing: the forwarder stops reading
a source after its FIN, so a later reset reaches no `recvmsg`; without the
`sk_error_report` rule the pair stayed live and the far end stayed in
`CLOSE_WAIT` (hazard 16: 20 of 20 in each half-closed shape, P-69). The
record's errno for a TCP reset is `ECONNRESET`, or `EPIPE` when the half
was in `CLOSE_WAIT` (`tcp_reset`, `net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:4905-4930 @ v7.0`;
measured 200 and 200 at the host, 250 and 200 at the guest, P-69); owners
and `ForwardOutcome` consumers treat both as a reset.

**Watch (ADR-0216).** A dialled V_h (the `GuestStream`, held and read by
leg-S or the probe runner) is not forwarded (ADR-0214). The owner watches it: the forwarder
overrides only its `sk_state_change` and `sk_error_report`, applies the
table above (the watch is installed by the same locked section as an
attach, so an end present when the watch is installed is in its attach-time
state), and, in both overrides, **first queues the watch's end record** for
the first class of the guest's direction (`HalfClose` or `Aborted { cause }`)
**and then calls the socket's original callback** (the holder's wakeups are
otherwise unchanged). On the locked receive path the record is therefore
queued before the end is readable (the holder's `recvmsg` and `poll` take
the same socket lock, `net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:1280`, `:2518 @ v7.0`); on
the device release's orphan sweep, which sets `SOCK_DONE`, the peer bits,
the state and `sk_err` and then calls `sk_error_report` without the socket
lock (`drivers/vhost/vsock.c:725-750`, `net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:458-471 @
v7.0`), it is queued before the holder is woken. The end may be readable on
that path before the callback runs, so the holder never classifies from its
`read`: the owner resolves it (EVMOD-STREAM-END, § *[REF] Driving port —
guest stream dial*, "How an end is resolved").

**Locking on the callback paths (EVMOD-STREAM-END for the watch's order,
EVMOD-REC for the record queue; module-internal, checked by the DELIVER
review against the source).** A watch override runs in two
contexts: the vsock receive path, in process context under `lock_sock`,
and the orphan sweep, which holds `vsock_table_lock` with
`spin_lock_bh` — bottom halves disabled, atomic, no socket lock
(`net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:458`, `:471 @ v7.0`). So queueing a record
never sleeps, never allocates (the record is preallocated with the watch,
ADR-0202) and never takes the socket lock: it takes only the context's
record-queue lock, a spinlock taken with `spin_lock_bh` on every path
(the override, the pair's work item, `OVD_FWD_ABORT` / `ABORT_ALL` /
`PAIR_STATE`, `read` and `poll`) that also guards the context's id table
(§ *Pair end*, "Stale invocations", rule 4), removes the watch's id and
inserts the record, releases the lock, wakes the context's
own wait queue (the owner's readiness), and only then calls the socket's
original callback. The release of the record-queue lock happens before
the original callback's wakeup of the holder, and the owner takes records
under the same lock, so a holder woken by the original callback, which
then asks the owner, finds the record. The pair overrides on TCP halves
run in softirq context (TCP input with the socket not owned,
`net/ipv4/tcp_ipv4.c:2318-2321`; `tcp_fin` calls `sk_state_change`,
`net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:5004`; `tcp_done_with_error` calls `sk_error_report`,
`:4900 @ v7.0`); they record which directions need a run and queue the
pair's work item, and never touch the record queue, whose pair records the
work item queues in process context. The
opposite order (original first) held 1,200 of 1,200 on the locked path
(hazard 8, P-69), where the lock orders the reader either way, and is
rejected for the sweep path. Measured with this order: the record was
present at the holder's observation in 6,640 of 6,640, including 640 on the
sweep path; an aborted dial read as EOF at the holder in 2,000 of 2,000
(P-69), which is why the read's return is never the classification.
`GuestStream`'s contract is `Ok(0)` for a classified half-close and
`Err(ConnectionReset)` for an abort.

**A watch ended by the owner (U-EV-3; WATCH-ABORT, approved by the user
2026-10-17, ADR-0211).** `OVD_FWD_ABORT` on a watch id, or `abort_all`, queues the
watch's record (`Aborted { Detached }`), then restores the watch's two
callbacks and clears `sk_user_data` (the order of § *Pair end*, "Stale
invocations"), then drops the forwarder's file reference — and **never
touches the holder's socket**: no shutdown, no state change, nothing sent
on the vsock. The holder's descriptor and its socket stay as they were. The
guest learns of the abort from the owner, not from the socket: the owner
sends `Abort { flow }` on the control session while it is live, and the
holder's close of `V_h` when it drops the stream sends `0x3` with the host's
direction open, which the guest's pair classifies as an abort
(EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT, § *Owners' use*, "`GuestStream`"). The spike's `ABORT`
of a watch behaved this way (P-70 § 3.8, § 4.3).

**Only the context's release shuts watched sockets.** At release no owner
remains to tell the guest or the holder, so the release shuts every live
watch's `V_h` with `shutdown(SHUT_RDWR)` (the guest sees `0x3` with its
direction open and classifies an abort) and queues no record. After that
shutdown the holder's `read` returns 0 or fails `-ENOTCONN`:
`vsock_shutdown` clears `SOCK_DONE` (`net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:1220 @
v7.0`), and once the socket has left `ESTABLISHED` without it `recvmsg`
returns `-ENOTCONN` rather than 0 (`:2522-2531`; 0 is returned only while
the state is `ESTABLISHED`, `:2545-2548`); a write fails `EPIPE`. Measured
after the forwarder's `SHUT_RDWR`: `ENOTCONN` in 10 of 400 (`0x3`), 4 of
400 (`close()`) and 1,916 of 4,096 (the parallel run), the rest 0 (P-70
§ 3.5). **Whatever the holder's read returns after it ends — EOF or an
error — the holder takes its outcome from the watch** (EVMOD-STREAM-END). A watch
ended by the guest's own classified end shuts nothing: the holder still
holds an open direction (a guest half-close leaves the host's direction to
the holder).

##### Pair end

- **Stream mode.** A clean end of a source (TCP end-of-stream; vsock
  end-of-stream classified a clean half-close) is forwarded as
  `shutdown(SHUT_WR)` on the target after the last byte the target accepted
  (ADR-0183); a vsock `SHUT_WR` sends SHUTDOWN `0x2`
  (`net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c:1084-1097 @ v7.0`) and never
  overtakes accepted bytes (T3, P-56). The pair **completes** when both
  directions ended cleanly.
- **Abort.** The pair aborts on: an error from any `recvmsg` or `sendmsg`
  of either half, or `sk_err` reported by a half's `sk_error_report`
  (`SocketError { side, errno }`; on a vsock half whose class was not
  recorded, only after the `vsock_table_lock` re-check of EVMOD-SWEEP, which
  turns an orphan sweep or transport reset in progress into its recorded
  `SocketError { ECONNRESET }`); a vsock half classified abort
  (`PeerAbort { side }`); an invalid or incomplete datagram frame
  (`FrameInvalid { side }`); an end-of-stream whose class is still not
  recorded after that re-check (`Unclassified { side }`, an alarm); the owner's `abort` (`Detached`); the
  release of the context (no record). The abort action: `tcp_abort(sk,
  ECONNABORTED)` on each TCP half still open, which sends a reset
  (`net/ipv4/tcp.c:5087-5141 @ v7.0`); `shutdown(SHUT_RDWR)` on the vsock
  half, which the peer's forwarder or watch classifies abort; nothing to
  send on a UDP half.
- **Order of a pair's end.** In the pair's work item: on each half, with
  the half's socket lock held (`lock_sock`, rule 5), remove its write-space
  wait-queue entry (`remove_wait_queue`), then, under `sk_callback_lock`
  for writing, restore the saved callbacks and clear `sk_user_data` (the
  pattern of `drivers/nvme/host/tcp.c:1917-1922 @ v7.0`), noting for a TCP
  half whether a ULP is installed (rule 5); then, for an abort, the abort
  action above (so its wakeups reach the restored callbacks); then drop the
  file references; then, in one section under the context's record-queue
  lock, remove the pair's id from the context's table and queue its one end
  record (ADR-0202; none when the context is being released); last, queue
  the pair's free work (rules 3 and 4 below). The owner, on reading the
  record, clears linger on a cleanly completed TCP
  socket it holds (D20), closes its descriptors and releases the flow's
  quota place and node flow slot.
- **Stale invocations (EVMOD-SAFE, ADR-0204).** An override may still be
  running, or be entered, on another CPU while its pair ends, and a control
  call by id (`OVD_FWD_ABORT`, `OVD_FWD_ABORT_ALL`, `OVD_FWD_PAIR_STATE`)
  may race the pair's own end, and the module may be unloaded once nothing
  references it. Five rules, internal to the module, make that harmless:
  1. The overrides find their pair only through `sk_user_data`, read with
     acquire semantics (`smp_load_acquire`) inside `rcu_read_lock()`; a pair
     found is processed (a spurious run is harmless). The one other path
     from a socket to a pair is the half's write-space wait-queue entry,
     embedded in the pair: its function runs only under the wait-queue
     head's lock (`kernel/sched/wait.c:104-108`, `:118-127 @ v7.0`), and the
     pair's end removes the entry under that same lock
     (`remove_wait_queue`, `:69-76`) before it queues the free work, so no
     entry function holds the pair once the removal has returned. The only
     path that does not start at a socket is the context's id table
     (rule 4).
  2. A pair's end restores the callbacks before it clears `sk_user_data`, on
     each half under `sk_callback_lock` for writing: each callback pointer
     back to its saved original with `WRITE_ONCE`, then `sk_user_data`
     cleared with a release store (`smp_store_release`). Not
     `rcu_assign_pointer(…, NULL)`: for a constant `NULL` it is a plain
     `WRITE_ONCE` with no release barrier (`include/linux/rcupdate.h:575-576
     @ v7.0`). An override that reads `NULL` therefore sees the restored
     original and calls the socket's current callback of the same kind
     (`READ_ONCE`), which is the original — never itself — so an event
     racing the removal still reaches the socket's reader.
  3. The pair's state is freed in this order: an RCU grace period that
     follows the removal, then the completion of the pair's work item, then
     the free. A pair's end runs inside the pair's own work item (§ *Pair
     end*, "Order of a pair's end"), which cannot cancel or wait for itself,
     so the end does not free: it marks the pair ended first, and its last
     step — after the id has left the context's table (rule 4) — queues the
     pair's free work with `queue_rcu_work`, which runs only after a full
     grace period (`kernel/workqueue.c:2639-2664 @ v7.0`); it touches the
     pair no further. After the grace period no override can still hold the
     pair (rule 1 reads it inside `rcu_read_lock()`), no wait-queue entry
     function can (its entry was removed before, rule 1), and no control call can
     reach it (its id left the table before the free work was queued), so
     nothing can queue its work item again. The free work then calls
     `cancel_work_sync` on the pair's work item, which returns with the item
     neither pending nor running only "as long as there aren't racing
     enqueues" (`kernel/workqueue.c:4477-4498`, the caveat at `:4481-4484 @
     v7.0`) — which these rules exclude. It waits for the ending run and any
     run an override or a control call queued earlier, each of which finds
     the pair ended and does nothing, and only then frees the state. The end
     record is not part of the freed state while it is queued; it is freed
     when the owner reads it (ADR-0202).
  4. **The control path by id.** The context's id table maps each live id to
     its pair or watch and is guarded by the context's record-queue lock
     (the spinlock of "Locking on the callback paths", taken with
     `spin_lock_bh`). `OVD_FWD_ABORT` and `OVD_FWD_ABORT_ALL` look each id up
     and, while still holding the lock, mark the abort requested (cause
     `Detached`) and `queue_work` the pair's work item; `OVD_FWD_PAIR_STATE`
     looks the id up and copies the pair's counters (`READ_ONCE`) while
     holding the lock. None of them dereferences a pair after releasing the
     lock. The pair's end, in its work item, removes the id from the table
     and queues the end record in **one** section under that lock, then
     wakes the context's wait queue (inside the section), then queues the
     free work. So a control call either found the id and finished with the
     pair before that section — any work it queued is waited for by the free
     work's `cancel_work_sync` — or finds no id and returns `ENOENT` (the
     record is queued or was read). An `OVD_FWD_ABORT` of a pair returns
     only once its record is queued (EVMOD-REC): it waits on the context's
     wait queue and re-checks by id under the lock, never through the pair.
     Ids are never reused within a context, so a stale id never names a
     later pair. A watch's end belongs to the path that removes its id under
     the lock — the watch's override on the guest's classified end, an
     owner's `OVD_FWD_ABORT` / `ABORT_ALL`, or the release — and that path
     queues the watch's record (none at release) in the same section; the
     watch's overrides are then removed (by that path in process context,
     or by the watch's work item when the path is an override), and its free
     work, with the same grace-period order, is queued only after that. A
     path that finds the id already removed does nothing more. The context's
     release runs at the file's last `fput`, so no control call is in flight
     on it; it requests the end of every live id as `ABORT_ALL` does, with
     no record, waits until the table is empty, and frees the context only
     after that.

  5. **A hooked socket's module reference is dropped only when no module
     text can be running or entered on its behalf (MODULE-REFCOUNT,
     2026-10-20).** The whole of an override's text counts, its prologue
     and epilogue included, not only its `rcu_read_lock` section. The
     module is entered from a socket in two ways, each closed by its own
     mechanism:
     - **The overrides** (`sk_data_ready`, `sk_state_change`,
       `sk_error_report`; a watch's `sk_state_change` and
       `sk_error_report`). Each is invoked from one of three caller
       classes:
       - **lock:** a caller that owns the socket lock — the vsock receive
         path (`net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c:1661`, `:1705 @
         v7.0`), TCP backlog processing in `release_sock`;
       - **rcu:** a caller inside a region a vanilla RCU grace period waits
         for — an `rcu_read_lock` section, preemptible or not, or a region
         with bottom halves, preemption or interrupts disabled
         (`include/linux/rcupdate.h:671-675`, `:687-691 @ v7.0`): TCP input
         with the socket not owned (`net/ipv4/tcp_ipv4.c:2318-2321`), the
         orphan sweep under `spin_lock_bh`, UDP receive under
         `ip_local_deliver_finish`'s `rcu_read_lock`
         (`net/ipv4/ip_input.c:240-242`) and ICMP-error delivery in softirq;
       - **work:** the forwarder's own work item, including the error
         reports its own sends cause.

       So rule 2's removal is done, on each half, with the half's socket
       lock held (`lock_sock`, then `sk_callback_lock` for writing, in
       process context: the pair's work item, or for a watch the aborting
       `ioctl`, the release or the watch's work item). A **lock** caller
       that loaded the old pointer has therefore returned before the
       removal, and no caller can load it afterwards. The free work runs
       after a vanilla RCU grace period, which waits for every **rcu**
       caller, and after `cancel_work_sync` (rule 3), which waits for the
       **work** caller.
     - **The write-space wait-queue entry** (pairs only). `sk_write_space`
       is never overridden, because it has a fourth caller class that
       neither mechanism above covers — **wfree:** `sock_wfree`, for a
       socket without `SOCK_USE_WRITE_QUEUE` (vsock and UDP; TCP sets it,
       `net/ipv4/tcp.c:477 @ v7.0`), calls `sk->sk_write_space` when a
       transmit skb is freed, holding no socket lock, outside any RCU
       section and with bottom halves enabled (`net/core/sock.c:2675-2693 @
       v7.0`), from preemptible process context: the host's vhost worker
       (`drivers/vhost/vsock.c:95-103`, `:252`), the guest's virtio-vsock
       transmit work (`net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport.c:342-361`), both via
       `virtio_transport_consume_skb_sent`
       (`net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c:475-491`; the vsock
       transmit skb's destructor is `sock_wfree`, set at `:288-289` through
       `skb_set_owner_w`, `net/core/sock.c:2716-2726 @ v7.0`), and a NIC driver freeing a UDP
       transmit skb (`net/core/dev.c:3464-3470`;
       `drivers/net/virtio_net.c:6304-6315`, `:6336-6345`, `:7097 @
       v7.0`). A task preempted in an override's prologue or epilogue
       there is waited for by neither the socket lock nor a vanilla grace
       period. The socket's own `sk_write_space` wakes the wait queue
       instead, and the entry's function runs only with the wait-queue
       head's lock held and interrupts disabled
       (`kernel/sched/wait.c:104-108`, `:118-127 @ v7.0`); the pair's end
       removes the entry with `remove_wait_queue` under that lock
       (`:69-76`) before the free work is queued. Once the removal has
       returned, no entry function is running or can be entered, whatever
       its caller's class.

     The free work runs on the module's own workqueue and calls
     `module_put` as its last statement, once per hooked socket. A **TCP**
     half (`sk_family` `AF_INET` / `AF_INET6`, `sk_protocol`
     `IPPROTO_TCP`) that has a ULP installed at its removal
     (`inet_csk_has_ulp`, `include/net/inet_connection_sock.h:347-350 @
     v7.0`) keeps its reference for the boot, and the module logs it: the
     ULP may have saved a copy of an override, which no removal can
     withdraw. The check is made on TCP halves only: the helper reads
     `inet_connection_sock` fields, which a vsock or UDP socket does not
     have, and neither can carry a ULP. `module_exit`'s `destroy_workqueue`
     waits for the free work's return after its `module_put`.

     **Excluded by precondition:** `sk_error_report` is also called from
     process context with no lock when an error-queue completion is
     delivered — a `MSG_ZEROCOPY` completion (`net/core/skbuff.c:1868-1878
     @ v7.0`) and a transmit timestamp through `sock_queue_err_skb`
     (`:5468-5485`). Neither reaches a hooked socket: the forwarder never
     sends with `MSG_ZEROCOPY` or a timestamping control message, a watched
     socket's holder sends the same way, and no owner sets `SO_ZEROCOPY` or
     transmit timestamping on a socket it attaches or watches (no crate
     sets either today). Attach and watch refuse a half that already has
     `SOCK_ZEROCOPY` set or any `SOF_TIMESTAMPING_TX_RECORD_MASK` bit in
     `sk_tsflags` with `ESOCKTNOSUPPORT`, which the owner reads as the
     existing `ForwarderError::UnsupportedSocket` (no new variant). That
     refusal is partial: an owner can still set either option after the
     attach, so the owner obligation stands, and the DELIVER review checks
     both it and the refusal.
     An invocation path outside these classes is a module defect.

  Rule 2's "the current callback is the original" holds only because no
  other subsystem holds a saved copy of an override (ADR-0200: no ULP on an
  attached socket); rule 5 keeps the text alive for a copy that exists
  anyway. The DELIVER review of the module step checks the following against
  the source: the order of rule 2, the free order of rule 3, the id-table
  locking of rule 4, and for rule 5: the socket lock at removal; no
  assignment to `sk_write_space` anywhere in the module, and the
  write-space wait-queue entry removed before the free work is queued;
  `module_put` placement; the ULP check guarded by `sk_family` `AF_INET` /
  `AF_INET6` and `sk_protocol` `IPPROTO_TCP` before `inet_csk_has_ulp` is
  called; no `MSG_ZEROCOPY` or timestamping send in the module; the
  attach- and watch-time `ESOCKTNOSUPPORT` refusal of a half with
  `SOCK_ZEROCOPY` or a transmit-timestamping bit in `sk_tsflags`; and no
  `SO_ZEROCOPY` or transmit-timestamping option set by an owner on a socket
  it attaches or watches, before or after the attach. The module's Tier-3 suite runs V-EV-SAFE, with
  control calls on ending ids among its stimuli, and V-EV-UNLOAD
  (§ *Validation plan*).
- **Measured propagation** (P-68, final build): a close, kill or RST at
  either end reaches the other far end in well under a millisecond typical
  (cut-A p50 0.37 ms, max 202 ms; rst-T p50 0.23 ms; 23 of 23 close, kill
  and RST shapes ended with no live pair).
- **A read-shutdown-only peer.** A TCP application that calls
  `shutdown(SHUT_RD)` and keeps its socket open sends nothing
  (`net/ipv4/tcp.c:3113-3114 @ v7.0`); once its receive buffer is full its
  zero window stops the forwarder, and the flow looks exactly like a stalled
  reader (cut-T: 2 of 5 stayed open, 2.6 MB held, no leak). It is what a
  direct TCP connection to that application does. **Owner policy: none.**
  No deadline, probe or abort: the flow holds its quota place until the
  application reads, closes or resets, or the flow is aborted by
  quiescence, teardown, control-session loss or the VM's end (ADR-0183: a
  slow reader is backpressure; ADR-0208: it holds only its own quota).

##### Datagram mode (EVMOD-DGRAM, ADR-0201)

- **One connection.** A datagram association is one vsock STREAM (kind `2`
  `DatagramStream`, port 1240) carrying the frame of ADR-0149 both ways.
- **UDP half → vsock half.** Peek one datagram with `MSG_TRUNC` to learn its
  length; a datagram longer than `MAX_GUEST_DATAGRAM_PAYLOAD` is consumed and
  counted `dgram_oversize`, not sent; otherwise send the 8-byte header and
  the payload, keeping a per-direction count of the current frame's bytes
  already accepted and resuming there; consume the datagram only after its
  whole frame was accepted.
- **vsock half → UDP half.** Peek the 8-byte header and pass it, with the
  queued-byte count, to the frame parser (below); a bad magic or a
  declared length above the bound aborts the pair (`FrameInvalid`); wait
  until the whole frame is queued, keyed on the queued-byte count
  (`vsock_stream_has_data`, exported GPL, `net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:1030-1037
  @ v7.0`), so no payload peek repeats while a frame accumulates; send the
  payload as one datagram — zero bytes for an empty one — and consume the
  frame after the send. A send that returns `-EAGAIN` waits for the UDP
  socket's write-space wake on its wait queue (§ *Forwarding, per
  direction*, "Trigger"). With `sk_write_space` left as
  `sock_def_write_space`, a connected UDP socket (`SOCK_RCU_FREE`,
  `net/ipv4/udp.c:329 @ v7.0`) keeps `sock_wfree`'s fast path, which wakes
  the queue inside `rcu_read_lock` (`net/core/sock.c:2675-2685 @ v7.0`).
  Resuming was measured with the `sk_write_space` override (P-72
  § 8); the wait-queue trigger is checked by V-EV-SAFE's full-target cases
  (§ *Validation plan*).
- **The vsock half's buffer holds the largest frame.** Datagram-mode attach
  refuses a vsock half whose `buffer_size` (`include/net/af_vsock.h:71 @
  v7.0`) is below `MAX_GUEST_DATAGRAM_FRAME` (59,008 B) with `EMSGSIZE`
  (`ForwarderError::BufferTooSmall { side }`, an owner defect); the owners
  never set `SO_VM_SOCKETS_BUFFER_SIZE` (default 256 KiB,
  `net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:199`). A smaller buffer can never queue a large
  frame: with 32,768 B the pair stayed live and the peer's write never
  finished (P-72 § 8).
- **The peer's end with frames queued (EV-DGRAM D1; U-EV-9).** The end's
  class is fixed first, in the vsock half's callback (§ *End
  classification*), and decides the cause:
  - **An abort-class end** (`0x3` with a direction open, or an `RST`) aborts
    the pair `PeerAbort { side }` in the callback, whatever frames are
    queued, whole or partial. Every production end of a datagram vsock is of
    this class: the guest slot release and the host's abort both shut the
    vsock both ways (§ *Pair end*, the abort action), and no owner
    half-closes a datagram vsock (U-EV-5). So after a production end the run
    never meets an incomplete frame.
  - **A clean-class end** (`0x2` only; no production producer): the run
    sends every whole frame still queued, in order, and the pair completes
    after the last one is sent (`Completed`); if a frame is left incomplete
    — a partial header or a partial payload — the pair aborts
    `FrameInvalid { side }`. The forwarder reads `peer_shutdown &
    SEND_SHUTDOWN` before the queued-byte count, so an incomplete frame is
    never waited on after the end.
  This last branch is not a defence against a reachable state; it is the
  forwarder's one correct effect for an input the class table admits — the
  other effects are a pair that waits for ever (reproduced with an
  independent peer, `trunc_fix=0`: the pair ended only on the owner's
  detach) or a frame dropped while the association reports a clean end.
  Measured with the rule: `kind=2 cause=3 side=1` at once, `dg_trunc` 1, in
  both environments (P-72 § 8).
- **No `ENOBUFS` handling; `IP_RECVERR` stays off.** A UDP send whose packet
  a qdisc drops returns success and counts `SndbufErrors` unless
  `IP_RECVERR` is set (`net/ipv4/udp.c:1195-1201 @ v7.0`; 1,086,869 qdisc
  drops, `err` 0, the pair kept running, P-72 § 8). The owners never set
  `IP_RECVERR` on a pair's UDP half, so a qdisc drop is UDP loss, not an
  association's end.
- **End.** A UDP half has no end of stream. The pair ends when the vsock
  half's peer ends its direction (the association is over: `Completed` for a
  classified half-close once every whole frame is sent, `Aborted { PeerAbort
  }` otherwise; the bullet above), on a socket
  error (a connected UDP socket's ICMP-reported `ECONNREFUSED`, or the D26
  rule's `EPERM`: `SocketError`, which the host owner reports as
  `DestinationUnreachable`, D26-PINS), or on the owner's abort.
- **Guest slot release.** The guest owner aborts the pair, then discards
  the slot socket's receive queue without reading payload
  (`recvmsg(MSG_DONTWAIT | MSG_TRUNC)` into an empty buffer until `EAGAIN`),
  then disconnects the slot socket and returns the slot (U-2, slot release,
  idle release). The order is load-bearing: without the discard, 1,018
  queued datagrams of one association reached the next association's peer;
  with it, none (P-72 § 7). A datagram the application sends while the
  association ends may be discarded, which UDP permits; the next one starts
  a new association.
- **Slot sockets bind an explicit port.** Each slot socket is bound to its
  own `GUEST_UDP_SLOT_BASE + n` (as § *Guest adaptation contract* pins),
  never port 0: `__udp_disconnect` unhashes the socket and clears its port
  unless the bind set `SOCK_BINDPORT_LOCK` (`net/ipv4/udp.c:2209-2235`,
  `net/ipv4/af_inet.c:562-563 @ v7.0`), so an autobound slot changes its
  port at disconnect (59,778 → 57,681, P-72 § 7), and the slot's address
  keys the capture programs' maps.
- **Bound.** Datagrams wait in the source UDP socket's receive queue; once
  it is full the kernel drops new ones (`net/ipv4/udp.c:1721-1731 @ v7.0`),
  as for an unforwarded socket.
- **Order and empties.** Every datagram, an empty one included, is delivered
  once and in order (measured: the strict-order check held across 4,050
  empties in the mixed run, P-72 § 1).
- **Frame parser (FRAME-PARSE, ADR-0201).** The host and the guest forwarder interpret a frame
  header received on a vsock half only through one pure C function in its
  own source file. It allocates nothing, takes no lock, touches no socket
  and calls no kernel API; it reads only `buf[0 .. min(buf_len, 8)]`, never
  a byte past its input; it checks the declared length against
  `MAX_GUEST_DATAGRAM_FRAME` (in 64-bit arithmetic, so the header-plus-length
  sum cannot wrap) and against `avail` before using it; and it returns a
  typed outcome. Nothing else in the module interprets bytes received from
  the peer. The UDP → vsock direction builds a header from the length
  `MSG_TRUNC` reported and parses nothing; TCP stream payload is never
  parsed.

  Files: `kmod/ovd_fwd/ovd_fwd_frame.c` and `kmod/ovd_fwd/ovd_fwd_frame.h`.
  The `.c` includes only the `.h`; the `.h` includes only `<linux/types.h>`
  and the module's UAPI header `include/uapi/linux/ovd_fwd.h` (the one
  SSOT of the frame magic, header length and bounds, ADR-0149), so the same
  file compiles in the kernel build (EVMOD-BUILD; `W=1`, sparse, checkpatch
  clean) and in userspace.

  The frame constants of the UAPI header, each the C mirror of one
  `overdrive_core::guest_transport::wire` constant (ADR-0149):

  ```c
  /* include/uapi/linux/ovd_fwd.h — frame constants */
  #define OVD_FWD_FRAME_MAGIC        0x4f564431U  /* "OVD1": the header's first 4 bytes, read big-endian; DATAGRAM_FRAME_MAGIC */
  #define OVD_FWD_FRAME_HDR_LEN      8U           /* magic + BE __u32 payload length; DATAGRAM_FRAME_HEADER_LEN */
  #define OVD_FWD_FRAME_MAX_PAYLOAD  59000U       /* MAX_GUEST_DATAGRAM_PAYLOAD */
  #define OVD_FWD_FRAME_MAX          59008U       /* OVD_FWD_FRAME_MAX_PAYLOAD + OVD_FWD_FRAME_HDR_LEN; MAX_GUEST_DATAGRAM_FRAME */
  ```

  The header asserts `OVD_FWD_FRAME_MAX == OVD_FWD_FRAME_MAX_PAYLOAD +
  OVD_FWD_FRAME_HDR_LEN` at compile time. The `overdrive-fwd` UAPI mirror
  carries the four values and asserts at compile time that each equals its
  core constant (the byte order of the magic included), beside its layout
  assertions, so the Rust codec, the C parser and the module cannot
  disagree on a frame bound. Where this section says
  `MAX_GUEST_DATAGRAM_FRAME`, the C side reads `OVD_FWD_FRAME_MAX`.

  ```c
  /* kmod/ovd_fwd/ovd_fwd_frame.h */
  enum ovd_fwd_frame_outcome {
  	OVD_FWD_FRAME_NEED_MORE = 0,
  	OVD_FWD_FRAME_COMPLETE  = 1,
  	OVD_FWD_FRAME_OVERSIZE  = 2,
  	OVD_FWD_FRAME_INVALID   = 3,
  };

  enum ovd_fwd_frame_outcome ovd_fwd_frame_parse(const __u8 *buf,
  					       __u32 buf_len,
  					       __u64 avail,
  					       __u32 *need,
  					       __u32 *len);
  ```

  - **Inputs.** `buf`/`buf_len`: the bytes at the stream head the caller
    holds (the module passes its peek of at most 8 header bytes); `buf` may
    be `NULL` only when `buf_len` is 0. `avail`: the bytes queued at the
    stream head, `avail >= buf_len` (the module passes
    `vsock_stream_has_data`). `need` and `len` are never `NULL` and are
    written on every return.
  - **Outcomes, decided in this order.**
    1. `avail < buf_len` → `INVALID` (a caller precondition; no production
       call reaches it, because the module never peeks more than is queued).
    2. `buf_len < 8` → `NEED_MORE`, `*need = 8`, `*len = 0`; no byte is
       inspected, so a partial header is never rejected early.
    3. The magic is not `OVD1` → `INVALID`, `*need = 0`, `*len = 0`.
    4. The declared length `n` has `8 + n > MAX_GUEST_DATAGRAM_FRAME` →
       `OVERSIZE`, `*need = 0`, `*len = n`.
    5. `avail >= 8 + n` → `COMPLETE`, `*need = 8 + n`, `*len = n` (`n = 0`
       is the empty datagram).
    6. Otherwise → `NEED_MORE`, `*need = 8 + n`, `*len = n`.
  - **The module's use.** `COMPLETE` → consume the 8 header bytes, send
    `*len` payload bytes as one datagram, consume them after the send.
    `NEED_MORE` → keep `*need` in the direction's state and wait until the
    queued-byte count reaches it (the partly queued frame resumes there, with
    no payload peek repeated); at a clean-class end with `NEED_MORE`
    outstanding the pair aborts `FrameInvalid { side }` (the end bullet
    above). `INVALID` and `OVERSIZE` → abort `FrameInvalid { side }`
    (ADR-0149); the two are separate outcomes only so the tests can compare
    them with the Rust codec's `BadMagic` and `Oversize`.
  - **Verification obligations (owned by DISTILL and DELIVER; their tests
    are not designed here).**
    (a) The shipped `ovd_fwd_frame.c` itself is compiled into a userspace
    Rust test crate with the `cc` crate behind a thin FFI wrapper (test
    support); no copy or port of the parser is tested in its place. The
    userspace build also enforces purity: a kernel API call does not link.
    (b) A default-lane proptest **differential** against the Rust codec of
    ADR-0149 in `overdrive-core` (`DatagramFrame`, `DatagramFrameError`):
    over arbitrary buffers and arbitrary split points, and over Rust-encoded
    datagram sequences delivered in arbitrary chunks, the C parser and the
    codec agree on accept or reject (`COMPLETE` ↔ `decode` of the frame's
    `8 + n` bytes is `Ok`; `INVALID` ↔ `BadMagic`; `OVERSIZE` ↔ `Oversize`
    with the same length; `NEED_MORE` ↔ fewer bytes than the frame), on the
    payload length, and on every datagram boundary. That the parser reads
    nothing past its input is checked by a sanitizer build of the same file
    in the fuzz lane, with the input allocated to exactly `buf_len` bytes.
    (c) A coverage-guided `cargo-fuzz` target on the same FFI entry point,
    with arbitrary `buf` and `avail`, runs in the nightly soak with
    [GH #322](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/322).
    The module's Tier-3 suite (the truncated-frame and partial-frame
    shapes above) remains the composed check through real vsock.

##### kTLS (EVMOD-KTLS, ADR-0200)

The production path puts kTLS on no socket the forwarder joins (§ *Sides and
pairs*); leg-C's kTLS socket stays with leg-S's userspace relay over a
watched `GuestStream` (ADR-0186) until #303, and after #303 the guest's kTLS
socket reaches the host through a loopback TCP peer that carries
ciphertext (§ *Guest-mTLS boundary*). Attach and watch refuse a TCP socket
with an upper layer protocol installed (`inet_csk_has_ulp`,
`include/net/inet_connection_sock.h:349 @ v7.0`) with
`ForwarderError::UpperLayerProtocol`, and no owner installs a ULP on an
attached socket. No TLS-record-aware peek, `close_notify` mapping or hook
order is needed. The rejected alternative — forwarding leg-S in the kernel
