with a control-buffer peek (`net/tls/tls_sw.c:1844-1860`, `:2062 @ v7.0`) —
would need its own contract-shaping spike before acceptance.

##### Workqueue (EVMOD-WQ)

The forwarder runs every pair on one per-CPU workqueue (`WQ_PERCPU`,
`include/linux/workqueue.h:405 @ v7.0`), with no per-pair choice. Measured
(P-68 item 3): an unbound queue (`WQ_UNBOUND`, `:372`) helped one large flow
by 1.1–1.4× and was worse wherever flows were many or messages small (0.041
against 0.106 GiB/s at 64 peers and 1 KiB; −14 % at 16,384 peers and 64 KiB).
No production caller knows at attach that a flow will be large, so no
option is offered.

##### Memory and backpressure bounds

- **Per direction of a stalled flow** (the far reader stopped): the source's
  receive queue (a vsock source: at most its buffer, 256 KiB by default,
  `net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:199`, `:939 @ v7.0`; a TCP source: its receive
  buffer) + the target's send queue (TCP: its send buffer; vsock: limited by
  the peer's credit) + at most one `FWD_CHUNK` of scratch while a run is in
  progress. It does not grow with the stall's length. The owners do not set
  socket buffer sizes; TCP buffers autotune up to `net.ipv4.tcp_rmem` and
  `tcp_wmem`'s maxima.
- **Measured** (P-67, P-68): default buffers — guest pipeline 2.6–2.8 MiB
  (vsock source to TCP), up to 8 MiB (TCP autotune), 0.25–1.7 MiB (TCP
  source to vsock); host role 4.69 and 0.65 MiB; with 64 KiB buffers
  0.12–0.51 MiB; unreclaimable slab rise ≤ 0.6 MiB across 3 s and 10 s
  stalls. The sockmap control queued 160 MiB in 0.36 s. P-67's and P-72
  § 8's resume times and throughput / core-s / p99 figures were measured with
  the `sk_write_space` override and belong to that trigger; they are
  re-measured with the wait-queue entry under V-9's benchmark (GH #326).
  Through the entry a vsock target wakes only when `sock_writeable` holds, so
  the resume waits for a later `sock_wfree`; V-EV-SAFE has full-target resume
  cases for a TCP, a vsock and a UDP target and checks correctness only.
- **The forwarder's own memory:** about 248 B per pair (spike) plus a
  scratch pool of `FWD_CHUNK` buffers, one per concurrently running work
  item (`pool_miss` 0 at 16,384 pairs with 8 buffers on 4 vCPUs); one queued
  end record per ended, unread pair.
- **Per node:** the per-flow bound × the node flow capacity
  (`GUEST_FLOW_MAX_PAIRS`); V-9's benchmark (GH #326) measures it at density. At 16,384 peers the
  spike measured 2.76 GiB of unreclaimable slab (Aya 2.79) and 16,466 kernel
  tasks.

##### Control interface (EVMOD-CTL, ADR-0199; EVMOD-REC, ADR-0202)

The C UAPI header `include/uapi/linux/ovd_fwd.h` is the SSOT; the Rust
mirror lives in `overdrive-fwd` with `const` size and offset assertions and
a Tier-3 round-trip test. The pairs' lifetime (the context and its release)
is EVMOD-CTL; the end record, `read` and `poll` are EVMOD-REC.

- **Device.** One misc character device, `/dev/ovd_fwd`, mode `0600`,
  owner root (the image sets it; the guest's `overdrive-init` runs as root).
- **Context (EVMOD-CTL).** Each `open()` is a forwarder context, opened
  `O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC | O_NONBLOCK` by `KernelFlowForwarder::open`; every
  pair and watch belongs to the context that created it. The context's
  release — the last `close()` of its file, or the exit of its process —
  aborts every live pair and watch of the context before it returns (TCP
  halves reset, vsock halves `SHUT_RDWR`, a watched `V_h` included — the
  only operation that shuts a watched socket (WATCH-ABORT) — overrides
  restored, references dropped) and queues no record. `O_CLOEXEC` keeps the
  descriptor out of every child the owner's process spawns (`serve` spawns
  the VMMs), so no child can hold the context past the owner; a user task's
  last `fput` runs the release before `close()` returns to userspace
  (`fs/file_table.c:528-530 @ v7.0`). A watched `V_h`'s holder keeps its own
  descriptor.
- **Ids.** `u64`, from 1, never reused within a context.
- **Operations** (`ioctl` unless stated):

| Operation | Input | Result | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OVD_FWD_VERSION` | — | `abi_version: u32` | — |
| `OVD_FWD_ATTACH` | `fd_a: i32`, `fd_b: i32`, `mode: u32` (`0` stream, `1` datagram with UDP half A, `2` datagram with UDP half B), `flags: u32` (0) | `id: u64`; on error `bad_side: u8` and `end_errno: u16` (non-zero only with `ECONNABORTED`) | `EBADF` / `ENOTSOCK`; `ESOCKTNOSUPPORT` (a half of an unsupported kind for the mode, or not exactly one vsock STREAM half, or a half with `SOCK_ZEROCOPY` set or any `SOF_TIMESTAMPING_TX_RECORD_MASK` bit in `sk_tsflags`, `include/net/sock.h:1005`, `include/uapi/linux/net_tstamp.h:59-63 @ v7.0`; § *Pair end*, rule 5, "Excluded by precondition"); `EPROTONOSUPPORT` (a TCP half with a ULP); `ECONNABORTED` (a half that has ended, EVMOD-ATTACH-END; `end_errno` carries its cause); `ENOTCONN` (a half that never connected, listens, or whose own send this side shut — an owner defect); `EBUSY` (`sk_user_data` already set: attached or watched elsewhere); `EMSGSIZE` (datagram mode: the vsock half's `buffer_size` below `MAX_GUEST_DATAGRAM_FRAME`); `EINVAL` (one socket twice, unknown mode or flag bits) |
| `OVD_FWD_WATCH` | `fd: i32` | `id: u64`; on error `end_errno: u16` | as attach, for one vsock STREAM half |
| `OVD_FWD_ABORT` | `id: u64` | `0` once the id's record is queued, or `ENOENT` when the id is not live (its end record is queued or was read). The id is looked up, and the abort requested, only under the context's record-queue lock (§ *Pair end*, "Stale invocations", rule 4). For a pair: the abort is carried out by the pair's work item (the abort action, § *Pair end*); for a watch: record, unhook, reference dropped, **the socket untouched** (WATCH-ABORT, ADR-0211) | — |
| `OVD_FWD_ABORT_ALL` | — | the number of ids aborted, each as `OVD_FWD_ABORT` does; returns once every one of their records is queued | — |
| `OVD_FWD_INVENTORY` | — | of this context only: `live_pairs: u32`, `live_watches: u32`, `queued_ends: u32`, cumulative counters (`attached`, `completed`, `aborted` by cause, `unclassified_eof`, `dgram_oversize`) | — |
| `OVD_FWD_PAIR_STATE` | `id: u64` | per direction: `source_end: u8` (0 none, 1 clean, 2 abort), `target_shut: u8`, `moved: u64`, copied under the context's record-queue lock while the id is live (rule 4) | `ENOENT` |
| `read()` | buffer of `n × 32` bytes | whole end records, oldest first; `EAGAIN` when none (non-blocking) | `EINVAL` for a buffer shorter than one record |
| `poll()` | — | `EPOLLIN` while a record is queued | — |

- **Request numbers (IOCTL-NUMBERS).** The module's UAPI header
  `include/uapi/linux/ovd_fwd.h` defines them (it is the SSOT; step 4 mirrors
  them in `overdrive-fwd/src/uapi.rs` with equality assertions). Magic `0xB9`,
  unused in `Documentation/userspace-api/ioctl/ioctl-number.rst @ v7.0`; numbers
  in the order of the table above: `OVD_FWD_VERSION` = `_IOR(0xB9, 0x00, struct
  ovd_fwd_version)`, `OVD_FWD_ATTACH` = `_IOWR(0xB9, 0x01, struct ovd_fwd_attach)`,
  `OVD_FWD_WATCH` = `_IOWR(0xB9, 0x02, struct ovd_fwd_watch)`, `OVD_FWD_ABORT` =
  `_IOW(0xB9, 0x03, __u64)`, `OVD_FWD_ABORT_ALL` = `_IO(0xB9, 0x04)`,
  `OVD_FWD_INVENTORY` = `_IOR(0xB9, 0x05, struct ovd_fwd_inventory)`,
  `OVD_FWD_PAIR_STATE` = `_IOWR(0xB9, 0x06, struct ovd_fwd_pair_state)`.
  `abi_version` is `1` (`OVD_FWD_ABI_VERSION`).

- **States attach and watch accept (EVMOD-PAIR, U-EV-1;
  EVMOD-ATTACH-END, ADR-0210).** Attach accepts a half that is still connected even when its
  peer has already ended its direction, so such an end is carried out by the
  first run; it refuses a half that has **ended** — whose connection is gone
  — and the owner aborts the flow (user ruling 2026-10-17: "attach
  reset/closed errnos are a flow abort"). Checked in the locked section of
  § *Forwarding*, "Attach order", `sk_err` first:

| Half | Accepted | First run | Refused `ECONNABORTED` — ended; the owner aborts the flow | Refused `ENOTCONN` — an owner defect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TCP | `ESTABLISHED`; `CLOSE_WAIT` (FIN received), each with no `sk_err` | Forwards the queued bytes; carries out a FIN as a clean end | `sk_err` pending (a reset received, before or after a FIN: `tcp_reset` leaves `CLOSE` with `ECONNRESET`, or `EPIPE` when the half was in `CLOSE_WAIT`, `net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:4905-4931 @ v7.0`); `end_errno` = the pending error, read with `READ_ONCE` and never consumed (`sock_error` would clear it) | `LISTEN`, `SYN_SENT`, `SYN_RECV`, `CLOSE` without `sk_err` (never connected, or an error the owner consumed), and every state in which this side has shut its send (`FIN_WAIT1`, `FIN_WAIT2`, `CLOSING`, `LAST_ACK`, `TIME_WAIT`) |
| vsock STREAM | `ESTABLISHED` with any `peer_shutdown` bits and no `sk_err` (including `SHUTDOWN_MASK` with bytes still queued) | Forwards the queued bytes; classifies the end by § *End classification*, "Ends present at attach" | `sk_err` set — the orphan sweep, `ECONNRESET` (`drivers/vhost/vsock.c:746-750 @ v7.0`), checked before the state because the sweep writes `SS_UNCONNECTED` (1) into `sk_state` (`:748`), the value of `TCP_ESTABLISHED` (`include/uapi/linux/net.h:49-50`, `include/net/tcp_states.h:13 @ v7.0`); or `CLOSING`, set only by `virtio_transport_do_close` on an `RST`, or on `0x3` with an empty queue, of a connected socket (`net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c:1249-1252 @ v7.0`); `end_errno` = `sk_err`, else `ECONNRESET` | `LISTEN`, `SYN_SENT`, an unconnected socket (`TCP_CLOSE` without `SOCK_DONE`), and a socket on which this side has shut its send |
| UDP (datagram mode) | connected (`sk_state` `ESTABLISHED`), with or without a pending `sk_err` (a connected UDP socket stays usable after an ICMP error) | Forwards queued datagrams; aborts on `sk_err` (`SocketError`) | — | unconnected |

  **Why its own errno.** The class is a flow event, not an owner defect, so
  it must not share an errno with one: `ENOTCONN` is also the never-connected
  errno, and a half's pending `sk_err` may be any errno, so returning it
  directly could collide with another refusal class. `ECONNABORTED` is used
  by no other refusal, and the half's own cause travels in `end_errno`; the
  adapter maps it to `ForwarderError::HalfEnded { side, errno }`. The errno
  the module returns is module code, checked by the module suite in DELIVER,
  and the kernel facts the class rests on are cited above. A refused ended half is never hooked, so no end record follows; the
  owner's abort is the flow's only end (§ *Failure projection*, "Owner
  response to an ended half at attach").

  **Measured.** `ESTABLISHED` and `CLOSE_WAIT` TCP halves and `ESTABLISHED`
  vsock halves with any peer bits were accepted and carried out in every
  shape of P-71 (961,995 of 962,000 trials; the 5 failures were the
  harness's own `connect()` before any attach); the `CLOSE_WAIT` acceptance
  is load-bearing (an `ESTABLISHED`-only rule refused 414 of 500
  write-and-FIN flows, hazard `h_strict`). Ended halves were refused and the
  flow aborted with no clean EOF at any far end (`eg-rst` refused in ≥ 99 %;
  `eg-drst`'s host attach refused when the destination's reset preceded it;
  P-71 § 5, § 7).
- **Address families.** A TCP half may be `AF_INET` or `AF_INET6` (the hooks
  are family-agnostic; IPv6 TCP was accepted, P-70 § 3.6); the owners create
  IPv4 sockets only (§ *Scope — IP family, UDP, in and out*).
- **Attach refusals (EV-CTL pin 4.5).** Checked in this order, the first
  failing check deciding the errno: `EBADF` / `ENOTSOCK` (each half in
  turn); `EINVAL` (one socket twice, unknown mode or flags); `ESOCKTNOSUPPORT`;
  `EPROTONOSUPPORT`; the state check, half A then half B, `ECONNABORTED` or
  `ENOTCONN` by the table above; `EBUSY`; `EMSGSIZE`. `bad_side` names the
  first offending half, and half B for a same-socket `EINVAL`. A refused
  attach changes nothing on either half (the other half can still be
  attached or watched) and consumes an id: ids are never reused and not
  necessarily consecutive. Measured: the seven classes the spike module had
  are pairwise distinct, and the precedence holds (P-70 § 3.6; 42 of 42).

- **End record (EVMOD-REC)** (32 bytes, native byte order; it never leaves the machine):

| Offset | Size | Field | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8 | `id` | the pair or watch |
| 8 | 1 | `kind` | `1` pair completed · `2` pair aborted · `3` watch: guest half-close · `4` watch: aborted |
| 9 | 1 | `cause` | kinds 2 and 4: `1` peer abort · `2` socket error · `3` frame invalid · `4` detached · `5` unclassified (an alarm, § *End classification*); else `0` |
| 10 | 1 | `side` | causes 1–3 and 5: `0` half A, `1` half B; else `0` |
| 11 | 1 | reserved | `0` |
| 12 | 2 | `errno` | cause 2: the errno, non-zero; else `0` |
| 14 | 2 | reserved | `0` |
| 16 | 8 | `moved_ab` | bytes accepted by half B from half A (payload bytes in datagram mode) |
| 24 | 8 | `moved_ba` | bytes accepted by half A from half B |

  Every id produces exactly one record unless its context is released
  first. The record's storage is allocated with the pair, so queueing it
  cannot fail. Measured (P-70 § 3.3, § 3.4, § 3.8): the layout and offsets
  above; 16,384 pairs ending at once in six storm shapes gave one record per
  id, 0 lost and 0 duplicated; 1,000,001 ids strictly increasing with one
  record each; `read` of a buffer shorter than one record `EINVAL`, of 100
  bytes three whole records; `ABORT` of a live id returns with its
  `Detached` record queued.
- **Attach takes a file reference to each half** (`sockfd_lookup`) and
  drops it at the pair's end; the owner keeps its own descriptors until it
  reads the pair's end record (it needs them to clear linger and, in the
  guest, to discard a slot socket's queue).

##### [REF] Driven port — `FlowForwarder` (EVMOD-PORT)

```rust
// overdrive_core::guest_transport::forwarder — pure data and the port trait;
// no I/O. One SSOT for the host owner, `overdrive-init`, the adapters and
// the sims.

/// A forwarded pair or a watched vsock, named by the forwarder context that
/// created it. Never reused within one context.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct ForwardId(/* private */ std::num::NonZeroU64);
impl ForwardId {
    pub fn new(raw: u64) -> Result<Self, ForwardIdError>; // 0 → Zero
    pub const fn get(self) -> u64;
}
// FromStr / Display (decimal) / Serialize / Deserialize matching them;
// proptest roundtrip mandatory.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum ForwardIdError {
    #[error("forward id is zero")] Zero,
    #[error("forward id is not a decimal integer")] NotDecimal,
}

/// The generation of an owner's forwarder context: 1 for the first context
/// an owner opens, + 1 for each later open in the same process (only the
/// host's `Forwarder` recovery opens a later one). A `ForwardId` names a
/// pair only together with the generation it was issued in. Observation
/// only (QPROJ-8); no kernel ABI carries it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct ForwarderGeneration(/* private */ std::num::NonZeroU64);
impl ForwarderGeneration {
    pub const FIRST: Self;
    pub fn new(raw: u64) -> Result<Self, ForwardIdError>; // 0 → Zero
    pub const fn get(self) -> u64;
    /// The next generation; `None` only at `u64::MAX`.
    pub const fn next(self) -> Option<Self>;
}
// FromStr / Display (decimal) / Serialize / Deserialize matching them;
// proptest roundtrip mandatory.

/// The half of a pair, in attach order.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PairSide { A, B }
impl PairSide { pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PairMode {
    /// Both halves stream sockets (one vsock STREAM, one TCP).
    Stream,
    /// One vsock STREAM half carrying ADR-0149 frames and one connected UDP
    /// half, named by `udp` (ADR-0201).
    Datagram { udp: PairSide },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AbortCause {
    /// The vsock half's peer closed or reset with a direction open, or
    /// stopped receiving while this side still sent (EVMOD-END).
    PeerAbort { side: PairSide },
    /// A `recvmsg` / `sendmsg` of that half failed (a TCP reset, `EPIPE`, the
    /// device release's `ECONNRESET`, a UDP `ECONNREFUSED` or `EPERM`).
    SocketError { side: PairSide, errno: KernelErrno },
    /// Datagram mode: a frame with a bad magic or an oversized length, or a
    /// frame left incomplete when the vsock peer ended its direction with a
    /// clean-class end (`0x2`; an abort-class end is `PeerAbort`).
    FrameInvalid { side: PairSide },
    /// The owner's `abort` or `abort_all`.
    Detached,
    /// An end-of-stream on that vsock half whose class was never recorded:
    /// a broken invariant (record cause 5), counted `unclassified_eof`.
    Unclassified { side: PairSide },
}
impl AbortCause { pub const fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str; }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ForwardOutcome {
    /// Pair: both directions ended cleanly.
    Completed,
    /// Watch: the guest's direction ended with a clean half-close.
    GuestHalfClose,
    /// Pair or watch.
    Aborted { cause: AbortCause },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ForwardEnd {
    pub id: ForwardId,
    pub outcome: ForwardOutcome,
    /// Bytes accepted by half B from half A, and by half A from half B
    /// (payload bytes in datagram mode; zero for a watch).
    pub moved_ab: u64,
    pub moved_ba: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SourceEnd { Clean, Abort }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct DirectionState { pub source_end: Option<SourceEnd>, pub target_shut: bool, pub moved: u64 }
/// Read-only state of a live pair (the conformance pairing's accessor).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PairState { pub a_to_b: DirectionState, pub b_to_a: DirectionState }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct ForwarderInventory {
    pub live_pairs: u32, pub live_watches: u32, pub queued_ends: u32,
    pub attached: u64, pub completed: u64, pub aborted: u64,
    pub unclassified_eof: u64, pub dgram_oversize: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AbortResult { Aborted, AlreadyEnded }

/// The forwarder of one side, through one context. `S` is the adapter's
/// socket handle: `dyn std::os::fd::AsFd` for the kernel adapter, the sim's
/// socket type for the sim. Every method is synchronous and non-blocking.
pub trait FlowForwarder<S: ?Sized>: Send + Sync {
    /// Earned Trust (§ *Earned Trust*). Kernel adapter: the probe stages.
    fn probe(&self) -> Result<(), ForwarderError>;
    fn attach(&self, a: &S, b: &S, mode: PairMode) -> Result<ForwardId, ForwarderError>;
    fn watch(&self, vsock: &S) -> Result<ForwardId, ForwarderError>;
    fn abort(&self, id: ForwardId) -> Result<AbortResult, ForwarderError>;
    fn abort_all(&self) -> Result<u32, ForwarderError>;
    /// The oldest queued end record, `None` when none is queued.
    fn take_end(&self) -> Result<Option<ForwardEnd>, ForwarderError>;
    fn pair_state(&self, id: ForwardId) -> Result<Option<PairState>, ForwarderError>;
    fn inventory(&self) -> Result<ForwarderInventory, ForwarderError>;
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ForwarderOp { Open, Version, Attach, Watch, Abort, AbortAll, Read, Inventory, PairState }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ForwarderProbeStage {
    DeviceOpen, Version, StreamRoundTrip, HalfClose, PeerAbortClassified,
    Backpressure, DatagramRoundTrip, WatchClassified, ContextRelease, Cleanup,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ForwarderProbeObservation {
    BytesDiffer, NothingReceived, TailTruncated, WrongOutcome, SenderNotBlocked,
    DatagramSplit, FarEndNotReset, ResidueRemains { pairs: u32 },
    /// The context descriptor lacks `FD_CLOEXEC` (EV-CTL pin 4.8).
    ContextInheritable,
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum ForwarderError {
    #[error("the flow forwarder device cannot be opened")]
    DeviceAbsent { #[source] source: std::io::Error },
    #[error("forwarder ABI {found} is not the expected {expected}")]
    AbiMismatch { expected: u32, found: u32 },
    #[error("socket {side:?} is not a supported kind for this pair")]
    UnsupportedSocket { side: PairSide },
    #[error("socket {side:?} carries an upper-layer protocol")]
    UpperLayerProtocol { side: PairSide },
    #[error("socket {side:?} is not connected")]
    NotConnected { side: PairSide },
    /// EVMOD-ATTACH-END: the half was connected and has ended (a
    /// pending reset error, a vsock `CLOSING` or the device release's
    /// sweep); `errno` is its cause (`end_errno`). Not an owner defect: the
    /// owner aborts the flow.
    #[error("socket {side:?} has already ended: errno {errno}")]
    HalfEnded { side: PairSide, errno: KernelErrno },
    #[error("socket {side:?} is already attached or watched")]
    AlreadyHooked { side: PairSide },
    #[error("vsock socket {side:?} has a buffer smaller than the largest datagram frame")]
    BufferTooSmall { side: PairSide },
    #[error("forwarder operation {op:?} failed")]
    Io { op: ForwarderOp, #[source] source: std::io::Error },
    #[error("a forwarder end record failed to decode")]
    EndDecode { field: ForwardRecordField },
    #[error("forwarder probe stage {stage:?} failed")]
    Probe { stage: ForwarderProbeStage, #[source] source: Box<ForwarderError> },
    #[error("forwarder probe stage {stage:?} observed {observed:?}")]
    ProbeMismatch { stage: ForwarderProbeStage, observed: ForwarderProbeObservation },
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ForwardRecordField { Id, Kind, Cause, Side, Errno, Reserved }
```

`KernelErrno` is the wire newtype of § *Wire contracts*. Adapters:

- **`overdrive-fwd::KernelFlowForwarder`** — a new crate, `crate_class =
  "adapter-host"`, depending on `overdrive-core`, `nix` and `thiserror` only
  (no async runtime), so both `overdrive-control-plane` and the static
  `overdrive-init` link it. It opens `/dev/ovd_fwd` with `O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC
  | O_NONBLOCK` in `KernelFlowForwarder::open() -> Result<Self,
  ForwarderError>`; the type is not `Clone`, and dropping it closes the
  context (ADR-0199). It implements `FlowForwarder<dyn AsFd>`,
  and exposes the context's descriptor for the owners' event loops
  (`fn readiness_fd(&self) -> BorrowedFd<'_>`, inherent). It holds the
  `#[repr(C)]` mirrors of the UAPI.
- **`overdrive-sim::SimFlowForwarder`** — implements
  `FlowForwarder<SimSocket>` over the sim sockets the owners' seams use;
  it is the named arbiter of the forwarder's kernel facts (the queues, the
  per-direction state, the classification and the end records), scripted
  per test (a peer's `0x2` / `0x3` / RST, a reader that stops, a socket
  error, a context release); its Tier-3 pair is V-EV-END and V-EV-CTL.

Contract of the port:

- **Preconditions.** `attach`: exactly one half is a vsock STREAM and, in
  `Stream`, the other is a TCP socket, in `Datagram { udp }` the named half
  a UDP socket; each half in a state the control interface's accepted-state
  table admits (a half whose peer already ended its direction is admitted);
  neither half carries a ULP; neither is attached or watched; the caller has
  not shut either half's send direction. `watch`: one vsock STREAM in an
  admitted state. Every violation is a typed error and changes nothing. A
  half that has ended is not a precondition violation the caller could
  avoid — the peer ended it — and returns `HalfEnded { side, errno }`, which
  the caller handles as the end of the flow.
- **Postconditions.** `attach` returns a live id; the forwarder holds a
  reference to both halves and has queued one run per direction. `abort`
  returns `Aborted` and the id's record (`Detached`) is queued before it
  returns, or `AlreadyEnded` when the id's record was already queued or read.
  `abort_all` aborts every live id of the context. `take_end` returns each
  id's record once.
- **Edge cases.** An id of another context, or unknown, is `AlreadyEnded`
  for `abort` and `None` for `pair_state`. A pair whose both sources have
  already ended cleanly when attached completes in its first run; one with a
  vsock half whose peer sent `0x3` or an `RST` while bytes were still queued
  aborts in its first run; one with a half reset before attach, or a vsock
  half in `CLOSING`, is refused `HalfEnded`. A watch on a vsock whose guest
  direction already ended queues its record at once. `abort` of a watch
  queues its record, unhooks it and drops the forwarder's reference, and
  changes nothing on the socket (WATCH-ABORT); only the context's release
  shuts a watched vsock. In datagram mode a vsock half whose
  `buffer_size` is below `MAX_GUEST_DATAGRAM_FRAME` is `BufferTooSmall`. An
  `Unclassified` outcome is a broken invariant: the owner handles it as an
  abort and reports it as an alarm.
- **Observable invariants.** At most one record per id; no record after the
  context's release; `live_pairs + live_watches` equals the ids attached or
  watched minus the records queued or read; the forwarder never shuts a
  target before its source's clean end and never forwards a byte past the
  first abort.

##### Owners' use of the forwarder

- **Host owner** (`overdrive-control-plane::guest_network`) opens one
  context at `converge_shared` and holds it for its life (ADR-0151, ADR-0159),
  replacing it only by the `Forwarder` recovery of "Context lifetime and
  owner failure" below:
  it attaches each TcpConnect and datagram pair before sending `Paired`,
  watches each dial's V_h, waits on the context's readiness descriptor with
  its other inputs, and on each end record releases the flow (quota place
  and node flow slot), closes its descriptors (clearing linger first on a
  completed TCP flow) and records the close cause. Quiescence's first hold
  calls `abort_all` and ends every stream as EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT pins
  (below); teardown and control-session loss abort each affected id. An
  attach or watch refused `HalfEnded` ends the flow at once (§ *Failure
  projection*, "Owner response to an ended half at attach"). There is no
  flow-event ring, drain step, counter read or audit-tick read for flows.
- **Guest owner** (`overdrive-init`) checks and loads the module
  (EVMOD-GUEST-KIT), opens one context and runs `version` before READY;
  attaches each TcpConnect pair on `Paired`, each TcpAccept pair before
  sending `Paired`, each datagram pair on `Paired`; reads end records in its
  event loop; keeps a pending intake child unattached and observes it only
  for its error (`EPOLLERR` / `EPOLLHUP`) until `Paired`; on an `Abort {
  flow }` for a paired flow aborts its pair (`abort`).
- **`GuestStream` (EVMOD-STREAM-END).** The host owner answers every end a
  stream observes on `V_h` from its own end of the watch or the watch's
  record, never from the socket call's return; the rule, its order and its
  results are pinned once, in § *[REF] Driving port — guest stream dial*,
  "How an end is resolved".
- **An owner abort of a stream (EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT, under
  WATCH-ABORT).** Quiescence's first hold, the allocation's teardown,
  control-session loss and the `Forwarder` recovery end every open stream
  of the affected allocations in one owner step: (a) `abort(watch)` — the
  record is queued and `V_h` is untouched; (b) `Abort { flow }` on the
  control session while it is live (U-5), so the guest owner aborts its
  pair for the flow at once — resetting the guest application's connection
  and shutting `V_g`, which reaches `V_h` as `0x3` and changes nothing the
  stream reports; (c) the node flow slot and, for `Relay`, the quota place
  are released; (d) the stream is marked ended by the owner, and every
  pending and later `read`, `write` and `shutdown_write` returns
  `Err(ConnectionAborted)` without waiting for `V_h`: the owner wakes a
  call parked on `V_h`'s readiness through the stream's I/O, which is the
  owner's own adapter (`GuestStreamIo`), so a holder blocked in `read`
  (leg-S's relay, an HTTP probe) returns at once. With the session lost no
  `Abort` is sent: session loss already aborts every flow at the guest
  (DG-5-F); at teardown the VM is ending. This keeps
  `QuiescedHoldsNoFlow`: after the first hold no host flow, dial or stream
  is open, and the guest's pair ends on the `Abort` or at the holder's
  close, whichever comes first.
- **A dropped `GuestStream`** aborts its watch, then closes `V_h`, in one
  step; the close sends `0x3` (`virtio_transport_common.c:1288-1295 @
  v7.0`), which the guest's pair classifies as an abort with a direction
  open, or as CLEAN-FULL-END after both directions ended cleanly. A
  `close()` alone would leave the watch live and the guest unaware, because
  the forwarder holds its own file reference (P-70 § 4.4: `live_watches=1`
  after the close, the far end saw nothing until the `ABORT`). A stream the
  owner already ended has no live watch, and its drop only closes `V_h`.
- **Release point (EVMOD-AB).** The host releases a forwarded
  flow's places when it reads its end record, and a dial's when its stream
  is dropped or aborted; no host place waits for the guest's final close.

##### Context lifetime and owner failure (EVMOD-CTL, ADR-0199; U-EV-4)

- **One context per owner, held by value.** `KernelFlowForwarder` is not
  `Clone`; the host owner holds it as a field it alone owns, and lends only
  `readiness_fd()` (a `BorrowedFd` for its own event loop). `overdrive-init`
  holds the guest's. No context descriptor is duplicated, sent or inherited
  (`O_CLOEXEC`).
- **In-process recovery of the host `Forwarder` component** — the only path
  that replaces a context while `serve` runs — runs inside one ADR-0124
  recovery under its quiescence hold, in this order:
  1. `quiesce()`: the first hold latches admission and aborts every flow,
     dial and stream on the node (G-V5, `QuiescedHoldsNoFlow`). The owner
     calls `abort_all()` on the current context; then, in the same step,
     takes every end record queued in that context (`take_end` until it
     returns `None` or an error; an error ends the reads) and applies each as an ordinary dispatch would (§ *Failure
     projection*): a `Completed` pair's TCP socket has its linger cleared
     (D20) and closes cleanly, so a pair that completed before the recovery
     and whose record was still unread is not turned into a reset; every
     other record closes as its row says (the `Aborted { Detached }` records
     `abort_all` itself queued end their flows with cause `OwnerAbort`).
     Every flow still in its table
     after that — a dial or stream with no forwarded pair, or a pair whose
     record was not read because `abort_all` or `take_end` failed — ends
     with cause `OwnerAbort`:
     the owner closes the flow's descriptors (TCP with `SO_LINGER{1,0}`,
     D20), releases its quota place and node flow slot, and ends every dial
     and `GuestStream` with the quiescence result (`Quiesced`). A held
     `GuestStream` whose watch has already ended (`guest_end: Some(_)`) is
     ended the same way, as an owner abort (D-3: its `dials` entry leaves at
     the owner's abort; U-R1): `Abort { flow }` is written while the session
     is live (the guest discards an `Abort` for a flow id it no longer holds;
     ids are never reused), and the stream resolves later calls by the
     order of "How an end is resolved" — the owner's own end first — while
     what it already returned to the holder and its `end()` class stay as
     they were. After this step the owner's flow table is empty and no id of
     the old context is referenced by it.
  2. Repair (`converge_shared` for `Forwarder` only): the owner takes the
     old `KernelFlowForwarder` out of its field and drops it, which closes
     its descriptor; the release aborts every pair and watch `abort_all`
     did not reach (an `Io` failure included) and queues no record. Only
     then does the repair call `KernelFlowForwarder::open()` and `probe()`;
     a successful open advances `forwarder_generation` (QPROJ-8); a failure
     is a failed attempt of the same recovery (UP-7).
  3. Audit: the new context's `inventory()` shows no live pair, watch or
     queued end, and the owner's flow table is empty.
  4. `restore(hold)`: admission reopens when the count reaches zero.
  Step 1 reads every record the old context queued before its release; the
  release in step 2 queues none, so no record of the old context is left
  unread for a flow the owner still holds. No path opens a second context while
  the first is open, so no pair forwards without an owner.
- **Every other end of the host owner is the end of `serve`.** The owner is
  not replaced in-process: the supervisor's end in any form is already a
  fail-stop of `serve` (`SupervisorReturned`, `SupervisorFailed`,
  `SupervisorPanicked`, `SupervisorCancelled`,
  `crates/overdrive-control-plane/src/lib.rs:1518-1533`), as are the
  leaked-hold and foreign-hold causes. At the process exit the context's
  release aborts every pair (far ends reset), the owner's own descriptors
  close (linger reset on D, H-5), every control session's host socket closes
  (the guest observes EOF, K-A5), dial futures end with the process, and no
  claim, session, flow or dial survives into the next process, whose boot
  reclaims every VM it does not supervise (NO-SURVIVE). This is why
  `owner_flows` needs no owner-death action: the owner's death is the end
  of every behaviour the model describes, and the restart is `cid_lease`'s
  reclamation.
- **The guest owner** is PID 1; its death panics the guest kernel and ends
  the VM (RESET-EXIT), and the host side aborts every pair on the device
  release's `sk_err`.

##### Failure projection

| Outcome | Owner's response | Close cause |
|---|---|---|
| Pair `Completed` | Release; clear linger on the TCP half; close | `PeerEof` |
| `Aborted { PeerAbort }` | Release; close (the forwarder already reset the TCP half) | `PeerReset` |
| `Aborted { SocketError }` on the destination half of a datagram association (`ECONNREFUSED`, `EPERM`) | Release; close | `DestinationUnreachable` (D26-PINS) |
| `Aborted { SocketError }` otherwise (`ECONNRESET` and `EPIPE` alike — a TCP reset in `CLOSE_WAIT` reports `EPIPE`, `net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:4905-4930 @ v7.0` — and `ECONNRESET` from the device release included) | Release; close | `PeerReset` |
| `Aborted { FrameInvalid }` | Release; close; counted | `FrameInvalid` |
| `Aborted { Unclassified }` | Release; close; a structured `warn` event naming the pair, side and context, beside the `unclassified_eof` counter (an alarm: unreachable under the design) | `PeerReset` |
| `Aborted { Detached }` | The owner's own abort; release already decided by its cause | the abort's cause |
| `attach` or `watch` refused `HalfEnded { side, errno }` (EVMOD-ATTACH-END) | Not a defect: the flow ended before it was attached. The owner ends it by the table below, closes its descriptors (each TCP half with `SO_LINGER{1,0}`, D20, so its far end reads a reset), releases its places and counts `forwarder_attach_ended` | `PeerReset` |
| `attach` refused (`UnsupportedSocket`, `UpperLayerProtocol`, `NotConnected`, `AlreadyHooked`, `BufferTooSmall`) | An owner defect: refuse the flow (`Refused(IntakeUnavailable)` host-side), close its sockets, count `forwarder_attach_refused` | `OwnerAbort` |
| `Io` on the context (`read`, `ioctl`), or an audit drift between the owner's flow table and `inventory` | A failure of the `Forwarder` component: the supervisor's recovery (ADR-0124) in the order of "Context lifetime and owner failure" below | each flow's abort cause (`OwnerAbort`) |

**Owner response to an ended half at attach (EVMOD-ATTACH-END).**
Each row is the flow's existing end before `Paired` (or, for the guest's
attach on `Paired`, an abort of a flow the host has already attached), so
no new message or phase is added:

| Side, kind, when | Ended half | Owner's step | What the far side sees |
|---|---|---|---|
| Host TcpConnect or datagram, before `Paired` | `D` / `H` (the destination reset after the connect) or `V_h` (the guest closed `V_g`) | Ends the flow as every flow it closes before `Paired`: closes `V_h` and `D` / `H`, sends `Abort { flow }` while the session is live (U-5), releases the quota place and node slot | Guest: `V_g` ends with `0x3` and the guest resets its intake child; destination: reset by `D`'s linger |
| Host dial (watch of `V_h`) | `V_h` (the orphan sweep: the VMM exited) | The dial returns `Unreachable { errno }` (the `end_errno`, `ECONNRESET`), as for a VMM exit with the dial in flight | — |
| Guest TcpConnect, on `Paired` | `I` (the intake child reset) or `V_g` (the host already aborted) | Closes `I` (linger) and `V_g` | Host: its attached pair classifies the `0x3` on `V_h` with a direction open as `PeerAbort` and resets `D` |
| Guest TcpAccept, before `Paired` | `C` (the application reset after accepting) | Writes `Refused { errno: end_errno }`, closes `C` (linger) and `V_g` | Host: the dial returns `Refused { errno }` |
| Guest TcpAccept, before `Paired` | `V_g` (the host ended its dial) | Closes `C` (linger) and `V_g`; sends nothing (a reply would be discarded as late, U-5) | — |
| Guest datagram association, on `Paired` | `V_g` (the host already aborted) | The slot release of § *Datagram mode*: discard, disconnect, return the slot | Host: already ended |

A pending intake child's error before `Paired` is the guest owner's own
input: it watches the child for `EPOLLERR` / `EPOLLHUP` and aborts the flow
on it without attaching; the race in which the reset lands after that check
and before the attach is the `I` row above.

##### Earned Trust — the forwarder probe

`KernelFlowForwarder::probe`, run on the host first by `probe_forwarder` in
boot phase 1 (step 1, before any boot effect, on a context it opens and
releases; D-8), then by `open_forwarder` on every context the owner serves
from (boot step 9, and each `Forwarder` repair), over the vsock loopback
transport (CID 1, which delivers through
`virtio_transport_recv_pkt` like vhost, `net/vmw_vsock/vsock_loopback.c:142
@ v7.0`), one `ForwarderProbeStage` each: `DeviceOpen`; `Version` (the ABI
version, and `FD_CLOEXEC` on the context descriptor, `ContextInheritable`
otherwise; no permanence check, MODULE-REFCOUNT); `StreamRoundTrip` (a vsock STREAM pair and a loopback TCP
pair attached, bytes both ways byte-exact); `HalfClose` (a tail after
`SHUT_WR` delivered, then end-of-stream, then `Completed`);
`PeerAbortClassified` (closing the vsock peer with a direction open yields
`Aborted { PeerAbort }` and a reset at the TCP far end); `Backpressure` (a
target whose reader does not read stops the sender with the source queue
within its buffer); `DatagramRoundTrip` (0, 1 and 59,000-byte datagrams and
an empty one, in order); `WatchClassified` (`0x2` → `GuestHalfClose`, `0x3`
with a direction open → `Aborted`); `ContextRelease` (a second context
closed with a live pair: its TCP far end is reset); `Cleanup` (inventory
zero). The guest runs `DeviceOpen` and `Version` before READY. The gold test
injects each failure a stage exists to catch — the module absent, a module
of another ABI, an inheritable context descriptor, the vsock loopback
transport absent, a peer that resets where the stage expects a clean end —
and requires the refusal to name the stage; a probe that passes under its
own failure fails the test. Three layers: subtype (`FlowForwarder::probe`),
structural (the boot-order test: phase 1's forwarder probe before
`compose_vm_driver`, the veth provisioning and every other boot effect, and
no forwarder context open when phase 1 returns), behavioural (the gold
test).

##### Lifecycle Gate Ownership impact

The forwarder adds no gate. G-V1's promise is "forwarder context opened and
probed"; G-V7's guest network configuration includes the module loaded from
`GUEST_FORWARDER_MODULE_PATH` and its ABI version checked
(READY's meaning is unchanged; a missing module, a module of another kernel
release and any other refusal are `GuestTransportSetupError`'s
`ForwarderModuleMissing`, `ForwarderModuleRelease` and
`ForwarderModuleLoad`, each the existing pre-READY start failure;
EVMOD-BUILD, EVMOD-LOAD and EVMOD-GUEST-KIT add no gate, they name who supplies the
module the existing precondition already needs); G-V5's `Forwarder` repair closes the old
context before opening the new; G-V9's owner is the side
holding the direction's target, here the forwarder under that owner's
context, and its promise is no half-close before the last accepted byte and
every other end an abort, with the forwarder's
classification and end record as its inputs. Forwarding backpressure is flow control
inside `Paired` and gates nothing (§ *Lifecycle Gate Ownership*).

##### Source, build and test

- **Where:** `kmod/ovd_fwd/` (C module and UAPI header); `crates/overdrive-fwd`
  (adapter, UAPI mirror); `overdrive-core` (`guest_transport::forwarder`);
  `overdrive-sim` (`SimFlowForwarder`).
- **Build and checks:** `cargo xtask kmod-build` (`W=1`, `C=1` sparse,
  `checkpatch.pl --strict` clean); the Rust mirror's `const` layout
  assertions; mutation testing does not cover the C module
  (`.claude/rules/testing.md`: C kernel code is outside cargo-mutants).
- **Tier-3:** the forwarder probe's gold test and the module's own suite
  (the evmod battery shapes — stall, long, slow, cycles, burst, bidir, eof,
  tiny, fault injection, cut, rst, kill, tight buffers, and the unload cell
  V-EV-UNLOAD — run against `ovd_fwd` through `KernelFlowForwarder`) on the host role in
  Lima and in a native metal microVM guest (`cargo xtask metal run`,
  `kvm-tests`); the composed paths through `overdrive serve` +
  `overdrive deploy` (V-6, V-8, V-9).
- **Seeded sim:** the owners over `SimFlowForwarder`; its facts are paired
  with the module's Tier-3 suite, whose shapes are those of V-EV-END,
  V-EV-CTL, V-EV-PAIR and V-EV-DGRAM (P-69 to P-72) with their hazard
  variants as negative controls (`h_lateshut`, `h_noseed`, `h_strict`,
  hazards 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16, the truncated-frame and no-discard controls),
  plus V-EV-SAFE.

#### [REF] Driving port — guest stream dial `GuestStreamDial`

Decisions: INB-1, ADR-0173, ADR-0174.

A host platform client reaches a TCP port of a VM only through a flow the
guest-flow owner opens over vsock. No workload address of the guest prefix
is host-local (INB-1; only the gateway is, GW-LOCAL, ADR-0152): no host socket listens for one, and a host-local
`connect()` to a workload address is refused by the constant guest-prefix
rules (ADR-0172).
Two production clients exist: leg-S of the inbound mTLS intercept, for a VM
backend (§ *leg-S over vsock*), and the VM probe runner (§ *VM probe
runner*). Each dispatches on the target: an address inside the node guest
prefix goes through this port; any other address keeps today's plaintext TCP
connect, unchanged.

```rust
// overdrive_core::guest_transport::dial

/// INB-1 (ADR-0173): opens a host-initiated TCP connection to a declared
/// listen port of an Active VM allocation, carried by one host-opened vsock
/// flow. Production impl: the guest-flow owner
/// (`overdrive-control-plane::guest_network`); sim impl:
/// `overdrive-sim::SimGuestStreamDial`. A required constructor argument of
/// every consumer (leg-S, the VM probe runner); never defaulted. The
/// `purpose` parameter is PROBE-NOSAMPLE surface (ADR-0187, approved
/// 2026-10-13); the rest of the signature is INB-1
/// (approved 2026-10-11).
#[async_trait::async_trait]
pub trait GuestStreamDial: Send + Sync {
    async fn dial(
        &self,
        target: std::net::SocketAddrV4,
        purpose: DialPurpose,
    ) -> Result<GuestStream, GuestDialError>;
}

/// PROBE-NOSAMPLE (ADR-0187): what a
/// dial is for. It decides only whether the dial counts against the target
/// allocation's flow quota; every other step of `dial` is the same.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DialPurpose {
    /// leg-S relaying a client connection. Takes a node flow slot and counts
    /// against the allocation's flow quota, like every other flow.
    Relay,
    /// The VM probe runner. Takes a node flow slot; does not count against
    /// the allocation's flow quota. Each probe task holds at most one dial
    /// in flight, so the exemption is bounded by the probe count the
    /// allocation's spec declares (at most `GUEST_PROBE_SLOTS`).
    /// In every other respect a probe stream is a relay stream:
    /// `shutdown_write` half-closes it, and its drop aborts its watch and
    /// releases the node slot at once [EVMOD-AB].
    Probe,
}
impl DialPurpose { pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; }

/// The host end of a paired host-opened flow: the connected host vsock
/// `V_h`, owned until the stream is dropped. The holder (leg-S's relay, the
/// probe runner) reads and writes the bytes itself; the forwarder moves none
/// of them. The owner **watches** `V_h` (`FlowForwarder::watch`, set up
/// when `V_h` connects, before the request is written) [EVMOD-END,
/// EVMOD-STREAM-END], so the guest's end of its direction is classified by the
/// forwarder's callback, not by the socket call that observed it.
///
/// - Every end the stream observes on `V_h` — a `read` of 0, any `read`
///   error (`ENOTCONN` and `ECONNRESET` included), any `write` error — is
///   resolved from the watch, in this order: the owner's own end of the
///   watch (`Err(ConnectionAborted)`); else the watch's end record
///   (`GuestHalfClose` → `Ok(0)` for a read; `Aborted { .. }` →
///   `Err(ConnectionReset)`); else the record is in flight (only the
///   orphan sweep makes an end readable before its callback) and the call
///   waits for it. A read's return is never the classification
///   [EVMOD-STREAM-END].
/// - An owner abort (quiescence's first hold, the allocation's teardown,
///   control-session loss, the `Forwarder` recovery) ends the stream at
///   once: the watch's record is queued and `V_h` is untouched
///   [WATCH-ABORT]; the owner writes `Abort { flow }`
///   to the guest while the session is live; every pending and later
///   `read`, `write` and `shutdown_write` returns `Err(ConnectionAborted)`
///   without waiting on `V_h` [EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT].
/// - Move-only. Dropping it aborts the watch, then closes `V_h` (the guest
///   receives `0x3`), in one step; a stream the owner already ended only
///   closes `V_h` [EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT]. The node flow slot and (for
///   `Relay`) the quota place are released at the drop or the owner's
///   abort, whichever comes first [EVMOD-AB].
#[must_use]
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct GuestStream { /* private: target, io: Box<dyn GuestStreamIo> */ }
impl GuestStream {
    /// Constructed by a `GuestStreamDial` implementation only.
    pub fn new(target: std::net::SocketAddrV4, io: Box<dyn GuestStreamIo>) -> Self;
    /// The address `dial` was called with.
    pub fn target(&self) -> std::net::SocketAddrV4;
    /// `Ok(n > 0)`: guest application bytes, in order. `Ok(0)`: the
    /// guest's direction ended with `GuestStreamEnd::HalfClose` (resolved
    /// from the watch's record) and every byte before it was read.
    /// `Err(ConnectionReset)`: the guest's direction ended with `Abort`.
    /// `Err(ConnectionAborted)`: the owner ended the stream
    /// [EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT].
    pub async fn read(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize>;
    /// `Ok(n)` while the host→guest direction is open, also after the guest
    /// half-closed its own. After `shutdown_write`: `Err(BrokenPipe)`.
    /// Any `V_h` write error is `Err(ConnectionReset)` unless the owner
    /// ended the stream, which is `Err(ConnectionAborted)`
    /// [EVMOD-STREAM-END, EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT].
    pub async fn write(&mut self, buf: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize>;
    /// Ends the host→guest direction cleanly: the guest receives a vsock
    /// SHUTDOWN with flags 0x2 and half-closes the application connection.
    /// A second call returns `Ok(())` and sends nothing. After an owner
    /// abort: `Err(ConnectionAborted)`. The same for both purposes
    /// [EVMOD-AB].
    pub async fn shutdown_write(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()>;
    /// The classified end of the guest→host direction, once it has ended:
    /// `None` until then, then fixed for the stream's life. An owner abort
    /// reports `Some(Abort)`. Resolved as the reads are [EVMOD-STREAM-END].
    pub fn end(&self) -> Option<GuestStreamEnd>;
}

/// The I/O behind a `GuestStream`: the owner's vsock adapter in production
/// (which resolves every end from the watch and is woken by the owner on
/// an owner abort, EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT), an in-memory pipe in
/// `overdrive-sim`. Same four operations, same contract as the
/// `GuestStream` methods that delegate to it.
#[async_trait::async_trait]
pub trait GuestStreamIo: Send + std::fmt::Debug {
    async fn read(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize>;
    async fn write(&mut self, buf: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize>;
    async fn shutdown_write(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()>;
    fn end(&self) -> Option<GuestStreamEnd>;
}

/// R2-END: how the guest ended its direction of the flow, as the watch's
/// end record reports it [EVMOD-REC, EVMOD-STREAM-END].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum GuestStreamEnd {
    /// The guest sent a vsock SHUTDOWN with flags 0x2 (SEND only): the guest
    /// application half-closed its connection (record `GuestHalfClose`).
    HalfClose,
    /// The guest sent 0x3 while a direction was open, or an RST; or the VM
    /// ended (the device release's `sk_err`); or the owner ended the stream
    /// (record `Aborted { cause }`, or the owner's own end).
    Abort,
}
impl GuestStreamEnd { pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; }

// `KernelErrno` is the errno newtype of § *Wire contracts* (never 0).

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum GuestDialError {
    /// The guest's connect to the application failed (its `Refused` reply);
    /// `ECONNREFUSED` when nothing listens on the port.
    #[error("the guest refused the connection: errno {errno}")]
    Refused { errno: KernelErrno },
    /// The guest's connect to the application did not complete within
    /// `GUEST_INBOUND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` (its `TimedOut` reply), e.g. a full
    /// listen backlog.
    #[error("the guest's connect to the application timed out: errno {errno}")]
    TimedOut { errno: KernelErrno },
    /// No pairing reply within `GUEST_DIAL_PAIRING_DEADLINE` from a VM whose
    /// VMM is still running (a VMM exit ends the dial `Unreachable`).
    #[error("no pairing reply from the guest within the pairing deadline")]
    PairingDeadline,
    /// The address is not the workload address of an Active VM allocation,
    /// or the port is not one of its declared TCP listen ports; also the
    /// result of an in-flight dial that the allocation's teardown ended.
    #[error("no Active VM allocation serves this address and port")]
    NotServing,
    /// The allocation is Active but its control session is not live as the
    /// owner observes it, so no pairing reply could be delivered; also the
    /// result of an in-flight dial ended by the session loss the owner
    /// observed.
    #[error("the VM's control session is not live")]
    NoSession,
    /// Node forwarding is quiesced (ADR-0169); also the result of an
    /// in-flight dial that the first quiescence hold ended.
    #[error("node forwarding is quiesced")]
    Quiesced,
    /// The VM or its vsock device is gone while the owner still holds the
    /// session live: the vsock connect failed (`ENODEV` when no device holds
    /// the CID), or the VMM exited with the dial in flight and the device
    /// release reset V_h (`ECONNRESET`), or another connect or I/O error of
    /// V_h before pairing.
    #[error("the VM is unreachable over vsock: errno {errno}")]
    Unreachable { errno: KernelErrno },
    /// The node's flow-slot capacity is exhausted, or, for a
    /// `DialPurpose::Relay` dial, the allocation's flow quota is. A
    /// `DialPurpose::Probe` dial is never refused for the allocation quota
    /// (PROBE-NOSAMPLE).
    #[error("guest flow capacity exhausted")]
    Capacity,
}
impl GuestDialError { pub const fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str; }
```

The two INB-1 deadlines, `GUEST_INBOUND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` (1.5 s) and
`GUEST_DIAL_PAIRING_DEADLINE` (3 s, compile-time asserted to exceed the
former), are declared in § *Wire contracts*.

`GUEST_DIAL_PAIRING_DEADLINE` is the opener's pairing deadline for every
TcpAccept flow; `FLOW_PAIRING_DEADLINE` keeps bounding datagram
associations. The 1.5 s margin covers the guest's accept, request read and
reply; with the owner's deadline at or below the guest's timeout the owner
abandons dials the guest can still answer (V-28 Q4 used 1.5 s / 3 s; the
Quint hazard `owner-flows-hazard-owner-deadline-shorter` violates
`DialDeadlineAfterGuestReply` and `NoPairedAfterDialEnded`).

**Contract of `dial`:**

- **Preconditions:** none on the caller beyond holding the port. Every
  `target` is accepted; an address outside the guest prefix, the gateway,
  port 0 and an undeclared port are answered `NotServing`, never a panic.
- **Order of decision** (the owner, in the target CID's serialized order,
  M-7): (1) `target.ip()` is not the `workload_addr` of a lease whose CID is
  Active, or `target.port()` is not in that lease's `listen_ports()` (the
  PORT-295-C TCP projection) → `NotServing`; (2) node forwarding quiesced →
  `Quiesced`; (3) the CID's control session not live → `NoSession`; (4) the
  node's flow-slot capacity (`GUEST_FLOW_MAX_PAIRS`) full, or, for
  `DialPurpose::Relay` only, the allocation's flow quota
  (`GUEST_FLOW_MAX_PAIRS_PER_ALLOCATION`) full → `Capacity`. A
  `DialPurpose::Probe` dial takes a node flow slot and no quota slot
  (PROBE-NOSAMPLE); the probe runner holds one dial in flight per declared
  probe and a spec declares at most `GUEST_PROBE_SLOTS` (8) probes across
  its roles, so an allocation holds at most `GUEST_PROBE_SLOTS` probe dials
  (D-UP-12, approved 2026-10-14; § *Core vocabulary*). A
  dial's flow holds a node flow place; its `V_h` is watched, not paired
  (EVMOD-END), and the watch's `ForwardId` keys its one end record
  (EVMOD-REC). Steps 1–4 and the registration of
  the dial slot are one step relative to quiescence, teardown and
  control-session loss (U-1), so each of those finds every registered dial.
  Steps 1–4 return immediately and change nothing: no slot, no socket, no
  quota slot, no message (Quint `owner_flows` `TypedRefusalChangesNothing`
  for steps 1–3). Step 4's `Capacity` — node flow slots for both purposes,
  the allocation quota for `Relay` and its exemption for `Probe` — and the
  release of the slot and quota slot on cancellation and teardown are
  discharged by the seeded-sim scenario R5-53 against the production owner;
  the Quint dial model has no capacity bound.
- **Opening** (after registration): claim a host-origin `FlowId`;
  non-blocking `connect()` of a host vsock STREAM to (CID,
  `GUEST_INBOUND_PORT`); a connect failure → `Unreachable { errno }` (the
  kernel reports `ENODEV` when no device holds the CID,
  `drivers/vhost/vsock.c:290 @ v7.0`) and the slot is removed. On connect,
  write the TcpAccept request: `client` = the lease's guest gateway with
  port 0 (the guest kernel picks the port, ADR-0174, V-28 Q3),
  `listen_port` = `target.port()`, `launch` = the CID's live launch token
  (ATTR-TOKEN). Before writing the request the owner watches `V_h`
  (`FlowForwarder::watch`, EVMOD-END); the forwarder moves none of its
  bytes. A watch refused `HalfEnded { errno }` ends the dial `Unreachable {
  errno }` (EVMOD-ATTACH-END): from the orphan sweep (the VMM exited, which
  resets the control session too) with no message, as a VMM exit during the
  dial does; from any other end of `V_h` before the request was written (a
  guest close of `V_g`, which no guest path produces before it read the
  request) as a `V_h` I/O error, with `Abort { flow }` while the session is
  live (below).
- **A gone VM.** While the VMM has exited but the owner has not yet
  observed the control session's loss, step 3 passes and the vsock connect
  fails → `Unreachable { errno: ENODEV }`. Once the owner has observed the
  session loss, step 3 answers `NoSession`.
- **Outcome:** the guest's pairing reply on the control session decides it:
  `Paired` → `Ok(GuestStream)`; `Refused { errno }` → `Refused { errno }`;
  `TimedOut { errno }` → `TimedOut { errno }`. No reply by
  `GUEST_DIAL_PAIRING_DEADLINE` after the request was written, from a VM
  whose VMM is still running → `PairingDeadline`. Every error closes the host vsock (the guest sees the
  end of V_g and tears down its half, K-A4) and releases the slot and its
  quota slot (a `Relay` dial's) before the result returns.
- **`Abort` when the owner ends the dial before `Paired`.** When the owner
  ends a host-opened flow before `Paired` — at the pairing deadline, on a
  dropped `dial` future, or on a V_h write or I/O error (`Unreachable {
  errno }`) — and the CID's control session is live, it sends `Abort { flow
  }` on the control session in the same step that closes V_h, as for every
  other flow closed before `Paired` (§ *Per-kind total orders*, U-5) and as when
  the host aborts an open host-opened flow. The guest closes its half of a
  flow it holds and discards an `Abort` for a flow id it does not yet hold
  (U-5; the close of V_h reaches that flow instead). With the session not
  live no `Abort` is sent (session loss already aborts every flow on both
  sides, DG-5-F). No `Abort` is sent when V_h fails with `ECONNRESET` from
  the device-release sweep: the same sweep resets the control session, and
  the owner then observes the session loss (Quint `VmStop`: `toGuestAbort`
  unchanged; the run asserts it is empty). A vsock connect failure
  (`ENODEV`) opens no flow and sends nothing. Quint `owner_flows`
  `HostDialDeadline`, `DialCancel` and `HostAbortAccept`.
- **In-flight aborts:** quiescence, teardown and control-session loss abort
  a registered dial like any flow (DG-5-F), closing V_h and releasing its
  slot and quota slot. The dial reports the cause with the admission result
  of that cause: the first quiescence hold → `Quiesced`; teardown of the
  allocation → `NotServing`; the session loss the owner observed →
  `NoSession`. None of these owner-initiated ends returns `Unreachable`.
  `Unreachable` comes only from V_h itself, which is not owner-initiated: a
  VMM exit resets the host vsock through the device-release orphan sweep
  (`sk_err = ECONNRESET`, `drivers/vhost/vsock.c:746-750 @ v7.0`), before
  the owner has observed the session's loss; the dial returns
  `Unreachable { errno: ECONNRESET }`, never `PairingDeadline`.
- **Late replies:** a `Paired`, `Refused` or `TimedOut` for a dial that has
  already returned — including one the owner ended at the pairing deadline
  or on a dropped future after sending `Abort` — is discarded and counted
  (`guest_flow.control_discarded`, U-5), gets no reply, and never yields a
  stream (`NoPairedAfterDialEnded`; `LatePairedForClosedHostFlowIsDiscarded`,
  `PairingDeadlineFiresOnlyAfterGuestTimeoutAndLateReplyIsDiscarded`).
- **Cancellation:** dropping the `dial` future before it completes aborts
  the dial exactly as a `PairingDeadline` does (vsock closed, `Abort { flow
  }` sent while the session is live, slot and quota slot released, a late
  reply discarded; Quint
  `DroppedDialFutureEndsLikeThePairingDeadline`). No slot outlives its
  future.
- **Concurrency:** dials are independent; none blocks the owner's event
  loop or another dial, and none waits on another CID.

**Contract of `GuestStream`:**

Each clause names the decision it rests on.

- **How an end is resolved (EVMOD-STREAM-END, under WATCH-ABORT; the one
  home of this rule).** Every end the stream observes on
  `V_h` — a `read` of 0, any `read` error (`ENOTCONN`, `ECONNRESET`), any
  `write` error — is resolved from the watch, never from the socket call's
  return: the stream asks the owner, which takes every queued end record
  and answers, in this order: (1) the owner's own end of the watch, when
  the owner ended it — `Err(ConnectionAborted)` (the watch's `Detached`
  record is taken and discarded); (2) the watch's record, when the owner has
  read it — `GuestHalfClose` gives `Ok(0)` for a read, `Aborted { .. }`
  gives `Err(ConnectionReset)`; (3) otherwise the record is in flight, and
  the call waits for it on the owner's readiness. Only the device release's
  orphan sweep can make an end readable before its callback ran: it stores
  the peer bits, the state and `sk_err` before it calls `sk_error_report`,
  without the socket lock (`drivers/vhost/vsock.c:746-750 @ v7.0`), so a
  holder reading then gets the queued bytes and then end-of-stream (read
  between `:747` and `:749`) or `-ECONNRESET`
  (`net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:2326-2328`, `:2439-2442`; U-EV-11, EVMOD-SWEEP),
  and the callback queues the record before it wakes anyone (§ *End
  classification*, "Watch"); case (3) waits for it. An aborted dial reads EOF at
  the holder in 2,000 of 2,000 (P-69), which is why a read's return is never
  the classification.
- **Reads.** `Ok(n > 0)`: guest application bytes in order. `Ok(0)`: the
  guest direction ended with `GuestStreamEnd::HalfClose` and every byte
  before it has been read. `Err(ConnectionReset)`: the guest direction
  ended with `Abort` (a guest `0x3` with a direction open, an RST, the VM's
  end). `Err(ConnectionAborted)`: the owner ended the stream
  (EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT).
- **Writes.** `Ok(n)` while the host→guest direction is open, also after
  the guest half-closed its own direction. After `shutdown_write`:
  `Err(BrokenPipe)`. A `V_h` write error is `Err(ConnectionReset)` unless
  the owner ended the stream (`Err(ConnectionAborted)`): the guest stops
  receiving only by an abort, or after the host shut its own direction,
  after which the stream does not write (EVMOD-STREAM-END).
- **`shutdown_write`.** Sends a vsock SHUTDOWN with flags 0x2
  (`net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:1179-1222`,
  `net/vmw_vsock/virtio_transport_common.c:1084-1097 @ v7.0`); the guest's
  pair forwards it to the application as a half-close after the last byte
  the application accepted. A second call returns `Ok(())` and sends
  nothing; after an owner abort, `Err(ConnectionAborted)`. The same for both
  purposes (EVMOD-AB).
- **`end`.** `None` until the guest direction has ended; then the class,
  fixed for the stream's life, resolved as above. An owner abort reports
  `Some(Abort)`.
- **Owner abort (EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT, under WATCH-ABORT).** Quiescence's
  first hold, the allocation's teardown, control-session loss and the
  `Forwarder` recovery end every open stream of the affected allocations in
  one owner step: `abort(watch)` queues the watch's record and leaves `V_h`
  untouched; `Abort { flow }` is written on the control session while it is
  live, so the guest aborts its pair at once (resetting the application's
  connection and shutting `V_g`, which reaches `V_h` as `0x3` and changes
  nothing the stream reports); the node flow slot and (for `Relay`) the
  quota place are released; every pending and later `read`, `write` and
  `shutdown_write` returns `Err(ConnectionAborted)` at once, the owner
  waking a call parked on `V_h` through the stream's I/O. With the session
  lost no `Abort` is sent (session loss aborts every guest flow, DG-5-F).
- **Drop (EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT).** Dropping the stream aborts its watch, then
  closes `V_h`, in one step; the close sends SHUTDOWN 0x3
  (`virtio_transport_common.c:1288-1295 @ v7.0`), which the guest's pair
  classifies as an abort while a direction is open, or as CLEAN-FULL-END
  after both directions ended cleanly. A `close()` alone would leave the
  watch live and the guest unaware: the forwarder holds its own reference
  to `V_h` (P-70 § 4.4). A stream the owner already ended only closes
  `V_h`. Close cause `StreamDropped`; bytes the holder had not read are
  discarded with the vsock. The node flow slot and (for `Relay`) the quota
  place are released at the drop (EVMOD-AB).
- **Cancellation.** A `read`, `write` or `shutdown_write` future dropped
  before it completes consumes no byte and changes no state.

**Observable invariants.** Every `Ok(stream)` was preceded by the guest's
`Paired` for that flow id on the session of the CID's current launch, and
the flow holds its node flow slot (`GUEST_FLOW_MAX_PAIRS`) and (for
`Relay`) counts against the allocation's quota from registration until the
host releases it — at the stream's drop or the owner's abort (EVMOD-AB;
half-closed streams count, `DrainingFlowHoldsItsSlot`). A dial's one
watch is live from the dial's connect of `V_h` until its end record is
queued — by the guest's end, the owner's abort or the stream's drop — and
no watch outlives the stream's drop (`NoLiveWatchAfterDrop`). No outcome the stream
reports is taken from a socket call's return (`HolderOutcomeFromWatch`).
A dial that returns an error leaves no slot, socket, watch or quota slot. `GUEST_DIAL_PAIRING_DEADLINE >
GUEST_INBOUND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` (`DialDeadlineAfterGuestReply`). Every
TcpAccept request a dial writes carries peer gateway:0, the target port and
the live launch token.

**Telemetry.** `guest_dial.failed { alloc?, target, error }`
(`GuestDialError::as_str`); `guest_dial.paired { alloc, cid, target }`.

#### [REF] Owner and provisioner — `overdrive-control-plane::guest_network`

Decisions: D7, D8; gates G-V1 to G-V7.

The owner's use of the forwarder — attach, watch, end records, release,
recovery — is § *[REF] vsock data path — the in-kernel event-driven
forwarder (EVMOD)*, "Owners' use of the forwarder", "Context lifetime and
owner failure" and "Failure projection"; the owner flow rules T1–T6 below
state the owner's own steps around it. The owner is guest-neutral: nothing
below varies by guest kind (HOST-NEUTRAL, ADR-0207).

```rust
pub trait GuestNetworkProvisioner: Send + Sync {
    /// Registers `plan.alloc`'s CID as Provisioned with the lease's launch
    /// token (`plan.assignment().launch()`, ATTR-TOKEN): its control session
    /// is accepted when its `ControlOpen` carries that token; its flow
    /// requests carrying that token are refused `NotActive`; connections
    /// carrying any other token are closed unattributed. Binds nothing.
    async fn provision(&self, plan: &GuestNetworkPlan) -> Result<()>;
    /// The only Provisioned → Active edge. Requires the CID's control session
    /// to be live; then marks the CID Active, after which guest-opened flows
    /// are admitted and `GuestStreamDial::dial` serves the CID's declared
    /// ports. Binds nothing. Idempotent on an Active CID (`Activated`).
    /// `Err(PostconditionMismatch { operation: ForwardingActivate, .. })` when
    /// the CID is unknown or Retiring. Serialized with quiescence by the
    /// existing sequencer, and with this CID's session events and dial
    /// admissions by the per-allocation order (M-7).
    async fn activate(&self, plan: &GuestNetworkPlan) -> Result<ForwardingActivation>;
    /// Marks the CID Retiring, closes its control session, aborts every flow
    /// of the CID — guest-opened flows, datagram associations, in-flight
    /// dials and open `GuestStream`s — and converges on absence. Returns `Ok`
    /// only when no flow or control session of the CID remains; a failure to
    /// abort or remove a flow returns `Err` as today and teardown is retried
    /// by the existing reclaim path, the lease staying Retiring (ADR-0133,
    /// CleanupPending ADR-0141). `pool.release` runs only after `Ok` and after
    /// the VMM has exited.
    async fn teardown(&self, plan: &GuestNetworkPlan) -> Result<()>;
}

pub enum ForwardingActivation {
    Activated,
    /// Node forwarding is quiesced; retry under the EXEC claim (ADR-0131).
    QuiescenceLatched,
    /// The guest's control session is not yet live; retry under the EXEC
    /// claim within the same budget as `QuiescenceLatched`.
    ControlSessionPending,
}

pub trait SharedGuestNetworkOwner: GuestNetworkProvisioner + GuestStreamDial {
    /// Owner placement (D24), fd budget, and the guest prefix configuration
    /// checks (D8-PREFIX-CFG, D8-PREFIX-VIP), from one `host_facts()`
    /// snapshot; the host owner's body is `probe_guest_flow_startup` over its
    /// own seam (D-8, § *Composition*), which `run_server` also runs before
    /// the owner exists. After those checks it runs the forwarder probe on
    /// a context of its own (`GuestFlowIo::probe_forwarder`: open, every
    /// `ForwarderProbeStage`, release; the `Cleanup` stage leaves inventory
    /// zero), so a missing or mis-built module refuses before any boot
    /// effect → `GuestNetworkError::Forwarder { source }`. An address
    /// configured on any root-namespace interface inside the guest prefix →
    /// `GuestNetworkError::GuestPrefixOverlapsNodeAddress`; any range of the
    /// configured service VIP range overlapping the guest prefix →
    /// `GuestNetworkError::GuestPrefixOverlapsVipRange` (checked first, so a
    /// node that would fail both names the VIP range). The production owner
    /// is constructed with the configured `VipRange` as a mandatory
    /// parameter — the same `config.vip_range` value the service VIP
    /// allocator and `ServiceBackendsResolve::new` receive; no default.
    /// Runs before any boot effect (*Composition* step 1). Changes nothing
    /// that outlives it: the probe's context is released before return, on
    /// `Ok` and on `Err`.
    async fn probe_startup(&self) -> Result<()>;
    /// Verifies no process-scoped owner object (listener, link, map, socket)
    /// survives from a previous run. It does not inspect the gateway route
    /// (GW-LOCAL), a node-global object `converge_shared` converges (H-4).
    async fn sweep_stale(&self) -> Result<()>;
    /// At boot: opens and probes the owner's serving forwarder context
    /// (`KernelFlowForwarder::open`, `probe`; EVMOD-CTL), binds the flow and
    /// control listeners, then converges the gateway route
    /// (GW-LOCAL): keep an identical Overdrive-tagged `local <gateway>/32
    /// dev lo` route, replace a tagged one whose attributes differ, add a
    /// missing one. No other route covers the guest prefix and no other
    /// address of it is made local. Idempotent: re-running after a crash at
    /// any point reaches the same state. Nothing removes the route. When a
    /// runtime recovery calls it as its repair, it converges only that
    /// recovery's component and never writes the route; for the
    /// `Forwarder` component it closes the old context before it opens and
    /// probes the new one (EVMOD-CTL). The listeners bind the owner's
    /// configured ports (`VsockListenPort`, PORTS-CONFIG) at boot, once per
    /// process; a listener repair neither closes nor binds: it re-spawns the
    /// accept task on the held listening socket after `bind_listener`
    /// confirms it is still listening (§ *Composition*, "Repair").
    async fn converge_shared(&self) -> Result<()>;
    /// PORTS-CONFIG (ADR-0218). `None` until this owner's first
    /// `converge_shared` returns `Ok`; from then on `Some` of the ports its
    /// stream and control listeners bound, the same value for the rest of
    /// the process (a listener repair keeps the held socket, so its port
    /// never changes). Reads only.
    fn flow_ports(&self) -> Option<GuestFlowPorts>;
    /// Non-repairing. Reports damage of the process-owned shared components
    /// and of the shared firewall state; the `Forwarder` component is
    /// damaged when its context fails `Io` or its `inventory()` disagrees
    /// with the owner's flow table. Not audited: the gateway route (only
    /// boot writes it).
    async fn audit_shared(&self) -> std::result::Result<SharedGuestNetworkAudit, SharedGuestNetworkAuditError>;
    /// QHOLD (ADR-0169). Increments the node's quiescence hold count and
    /// returns the new hold. The hold that takes the count from 0 to 1
    /// latches admission `Quiesced` (new flows refused `Quiesced`, dials
    /// answered `GuestDialError::Quiesced`) and aborts every live flow on the
    /// node — guest-opened flows, datagram associations, in-flight dials and
    /// open `GuestStream`s; a later hold only increments the count.
    /// `unconfirmed` reports per-allocation flow-abort failures at return.
    /// Infallible: per-allocation failures are classified, never returned.
    /// The hold is issued by this owner's own `QuiescenceLedger` (D-UP-4).
    async fn quiesce(&self) -> (QuiescenceHold, ForwardingQuiescence);
    /// QHOLD. Redeems `hold` at this owner's ledger and decrements the count.
    /// At zero: clears the latch (admission and dials reopen) → `Reopened`.
    /// Above zero: changes nothing else → `StillQuiesced`. Aborted flows are
    /// not restored. The caller (the supervisor) calls it only after its own
    /// repair and a clean audit.
    /// `Err(ForeignHold)` (D-UP-4 and PD-1, approved 2026-10-14): `hold`
    /// was issued by
    /// another ledger. The count, the latch and this owner's leaked count are
    /// unchanged, so forwarding stays as quiesced as it was (fail-closed);
    /// the foreign hold is dropped unredeemed and counts as leaked at the
    /// ledger that issued it. Never a panic.
    async fn restore(&self, hold: QuiescenceHold) -> Result<ForwardingRestore, QuiescenceRestoreError>;
}

pub struct ForwardingQuiescence { pub unconfirmed: std::collections::BTreeMap<AllocationId, GuestNetworkError> }

/// QHOLD: one outstanding quiescence of node forwarding. Not `Clone`; built
/// only by `QuiescenceLedger::issue`; consumed only by the `redeem` of the
/// ledger that issued it (reached through `restore`). It holds a shared
/// reference to its issuing ledger's state (an `Arc` to the ledger's private
/// inner), which is how a drop reaches that ledger: dropped unredeemed, it
/// increments that ledger's leaked count (one atomic increment; no I/O, no
/// lock, nothing awaited). The owner's hold count stays raised, so
/// forwarding stays quiesced until the process ends.
#[must_use]
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct QuiescenceHold { /* private: Arc<the issuing ledger's inner>, redeemed flag */ }

/// QHOLD capability (D-UP-4 and PD-2, approved 2026-10-14; public in
/// `overdrive-control-plane` so the sim owner uses it). Issues and redeems the
/// `QuiescenceHold`s of one owner and counts those dropped without a redeem.
/// Not `Clone`: each owner constructs and holds exactly one; a ledger is
/// never shared between owners.
pub struct QuiescenceLedger { /* private: Arc<inner { leaked: AtomicU32 }> */ }
impl QuiescenceLedger {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    /// A new hold bound to this ledger (it clones this ledger's inner `Arc`).
    pub fn issue(&self) -> QuiescenceHold;
    /// Consumes `hold` without counting a leak when this ledger issued it
    /// (identity: `Arc::ptr_eq` of the hold's inner and this ledger's);
    /// returns it unchanged otherwise.
    pub fn redeem(&self, hold: QuiescenceHold) -> Result<(), QuiescenceHold>;
    /// Holds of this ledger dropped without a redeem; never decreases.
    pub fn leaked(&self) -> u32;
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ForwardingRestore {
    /// The count reached zero: admission and dials reopened.
    Reopened,
    /// Other holds remain; nothing reopened.
    StillQuiesced,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum QuiescenceRestoreError {
    /// The hold was issued by another owner's ledger (a composition defect:
    /// one supervisor is composed with one owner).
    #[error("quiescence hold was issued by another owner's ledger")]
    ForeignHold,
}
impl QuiescenceRestoreError { pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; }
```

The ledger keeps its inner state alive as long as any hold of it exists, so
a hold dropped after its owner is dropped still increments a valid counter
(that no one reads). The owner's hold count and latch are the owner's, not
the ledger's: `quiesce` issues then increments, `restore` redeems then
decrements; `flow_observation().leaked_quiescence_holds` is the owner's
ledger's `leaked()`. A process-wide forgery of a hold that reopens an owner's
forwarding is unrepresentable: only that owner's ledger issued holds it
redeems, and the ledger is reachable only inside the owner.

Activation returns `QuiescenceLatched` while the hold count is above zero.
The runtime supervisor (RUN-295-B) is the only caller of quiesce and
restore: each component's recovery takes one hold, repairs with
`converge_shared` only while it holds, audits, and restores with its own
hold. No repair — of the firewall (`IpRules` / `IpSets`) included — runs
without a hold. A boolean latch is not used: the first recovery's restore
would reopen forwarding while a second recovery is still repairing.

**A recovery ends only by restore or fail-stop (D-UP-3, approved
2026-10-14; UP-7 governs).** A repair `Err` and a failed post-repair audit
are failed attempts within the recovery's budget (ADR-0124). The recovery
keeps its `QuiescenceHold` across them and either repairs within its budget
and restores, or reaches the budget's fail-stop still holding it. No
recovery returns, and none is dropped, while it holds a hold: the supervisor
ends a recovery only through `restore` or through the fail-stop of `serve`
(process exit). A `restore` that returns `Err(ForeignHold)` ends the
recovery by ADR-0124's typed fail-stop of `serve` at once, cause
`SharedGuestNetworkFailStopCause::ForeignQuiescenceHold` (PD-1, approved
2026-10-14); forwarding stays quiesced until then.

**Leaked hold → fail-stop (QHOLD).** A hold is leaked when it is dropped
unredeemed. Because no recovery path drops one, a leak is an Overdrive
defect, and the leaked-hold count bounds the effect of these defect classes:
(1) an early return (`?`, `return`, `break`) out of a recovery between
`quiesce` and `restore`; (2) a recovery future dropped by anything but the
supervisor's own shutdown cancellation — a `select!` arm that loses, a
timeout wrapper, an `abort()` of a recovery task; (3) a hold moved into a
value that is dropped or overwritten (a replaced map entry, a dropped
struct); (4) a panic that unwinds, in a profile that unwinds (the release
profile aborts on panic, `panic = "abort"`, `Cargo.toml:284`, which ends the
process instead). The supervisor reads the owner's leaked-hold count at
every audit tick. A count above zero is an exhausted recovery: the
supervisor takes ADR-0124's typed fail-stop of `serve` at once, cause
`SharedGuestNetworkFailStopCause::LeakedQuiescenceHold` (beside
`RecoveryDeadlineExceeded`). Forwarding stays quiesced until then; the
supervised restart converges on boot (*Composition*, step 8 included).

**Shutdown cancellation (D-UP-3).** `serve`'s shutdown stops the supervisor
task through its cancellation token; a recovery in progress is dropped with
it and its hold is dropped unredeemed, which increments the ledger's leaked
count. That drop is not a defect and is not classified as one: the only
reader of the count is the supervisor's audit tick, which runs in the
cancelled task and never runs again, so no fail-stop cause is recorded and
the shutdown exit is unchanged. Forwarding stays quiesced until the process
exits (the safe direction: nothing reopens unrepaired), and the next boot's
owner starts with a count of 0 and converges (*Composition*). The
