```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize,
         rkyv::Archive, rkyv::Serialize, rkyv::Deserialize)]
pub struct ProbeResultRowV2 {
    pub alloc_id: AllocationId,
    pub probe_idx: ProbeIdx,
    pub role: ProbeRole,
    pub status: ProbeStatus,
    /// Observation time shown to operators; does not decide the merge.
    pub last_observed_at_unix_ms: u64,
    pub inferred: bool,
    /// The producer's run sequence for `(alloc_id, role, probe_idx)`.
    pub run_seq: ProbeRunSeq,
    /// The producer's observed streak of `status` ending with this run.
    pub same_status_runs: SameStatusRuns,
}

pub type ProbeResultRow = ProbeResultRowV2;       // re-pointed at V2 (:206)
pub type ProbeResultRowLatest = ProbeResultRowV2; // re-pointed at V2 (:211)

pub enum ProbeResultRowEnvelope {                 // :224
    V1(ProbeResultRowV1), // discriminant 0, unchanged
    V2(ProbeResultRowV2), // discriminant 1, appended
}
```

- **Up-conversion.** `From<ProbeResultRowV1> for ProbeResultRowV2` copies
  every field and sets `run_seq = ProbeRunSeq::FIRST` and
  `same_status_runs = SameStatusRuns::ONE`. Reason: a V1 row can
  only belong to an allocation of an earlier `serve` process, which boot
  reclamation reclaims before any probe runs
  (`crates/overdrive-control-plane/src/vm_reclamation_boot.rs:110-140`), so
  it is never counted toward a live allocation. `into_latest()` maps
  `V1(v1) => Ok(v1.into())`, `V2(v2) => Ok(v2)`; `latest()` wraps `V2`.
- **Version-bump procedure.** `.claude/rules/development.md` § "rkyv schema
  evolution" → "Version-bump procedure", all six steps in one commit:
  the variant appended (never reordered), both aliases re-pointed,
  `latest()` and `into_latest()` updated, the `From` impl, and the
  fixtures. `known_discriminants()` becomes `&[0, 1]` and
  `discriminant_offset_from_end()` (`:252-254`, today `56`) is re-pinned,
  measured on a canonical V2 archive, together with the test's
  `GOLDEN_DISCRIMINANT_OFFSET_V1`
  (`crates/overdrive-core/tests/schema_evolution/probe_result_row.rs:37`)
  and a new V2 offset constant (R5-PROBE-V2).
- **Layer policy.** Observation layer: an undecodable row is logged and
  skipped (`ObservationStoreError::Envelope`; ADR-0048 § 3), as for V1
  today; convergence proceeds on the surviving rows.
- **API JSON unchanged.** `ProbeResultRowJson` and its
  `From<&ProbeResultRow>` (`crates/overdrive-control-plane/src/api.rs:803-866`)
  do not carry `run_seq` or `same_status_runs`; the CLI and API output is
  byte-identical.
- `last_observed_at_unix_ms` stays the raw V1 field (renaming or retyping it
  is not part of this decision).

**Merge (LWW by run sequence).** For a key `(alloc_id, role, probe_idx)` —
one writer, its probe task — a written row replaces the stored row iff no
row is stored, the stored row is undecodable (ADR-0048 § 3, unchanged), or
its `run_seq` is strictly greater than the stored row's. An equal or smaller
`run_seq` is dropped: no state change, no `SubscriptionEvent`. The
observation time does not decide the merge, so a backward wall-clock step
loses no row. The contract is the `ObservationStore::write_probe_result`
rustdoc (`crates/overdrive-core/src/traits/observation_store.rs:2150-2208`,
today "LWW resolution on `last_observed_at_unix_ms`"), restated on
`run_seq`, and both merging implementers follow it in the same commit:

| Adapter | Function | Today |
|---|---|---|
| `LocalObservationStore` (`adapter-host`) | `apply_probe_result_lww`, `crates/overdrive-store-local/src/observation_backend.rs:1374-1395` | `incoming.last_observed_at_unix_ms > prior_row.last_observed_at_unix_ms` |
| `SimObservationStore` (`adapter-sim`) | `PeerState::apply_probe_result`, `crates/overdrive-sim/src/adapters/observation_store.rs:520-536` | the same comparison |

The restated postconditions, as the trait rustdoc text (replacing the
`# Postconditions` "LWW resolution on `last_observed_at_unix_ms`" bullets and
completing the failed-write case, which today says only that a failed
transaction emits no event):

```rust
// overdrive_core::traits::observation_store::ObservationStore::write_probe_result
/// # Postconditions
/// - On `Ok(())` the merge outcome is durable: a later
///   [`Self::list_probe_results_for_alloc`] returns the written row iff no
///   row, or an undecodable row, was stored at `(alloc_id, role, probe_idx)`,
///   or the written row's `run_seq` is strictly greater than the stored
///   row's. `last_observed_at_unix_ms` does not decide the merge.
/// - An accepted write emits exactly one live [`SubscriptionEvent::Row`]
///   carrying [`ObservationRow::ProbeResult`], after the durable commit. A
///   write whose `run_seq` is equal to or smaller than the stored row's
///   changes no state and emits no event.
/// - On `Err(_)` the call changed no state and emitted no
///   [`SubscriptionEvent`]: the row stored at the key is the row stored
///   before the call, and a later write is merged against that row.
```

The `Err` clause is the store's half of PC-3 (a run that writes no row
leaves the store unchanged): R5-PROBE-COUNT discharges it for
`SimObservationStore` (`inject_write_failure`), R5-PROBE-MERGE's
failed-write case for `LocalObservationStore`.

Other `ObservationStore` implementations delegate the write
(`crates/overdrive-sim/src/invariants/terminal_contention.rs:270-279`) or are
test doubles. `list_probe_results_for_alloc` is unchanged: one row per
`(role, probe_idx)`, the merge winner.

#### [REF] Guest adaptation contract — `overdrive-init` + guest programs

Decisions: D6, D10, D15.

This is the guest side of a **Linux** guest: `overdrive-init`, its capture
programs and the guest kit's `ovd_fwd` (EVMOD-GUEST-KIT). `overdrive-init`
loads `ovd_fwd`, opens its context and attaches each pair (§ *[REF] vsock
data path*, "Module placement and lifetime", "Owners' use of the
forwarder"). A guest that runs no Linux kernel implements the same
host-side protocol in its own image (HOST-NEUTRAL;
[GH #321](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/321)).

- **Guest intake model (D25, APPROVED 2026-10-06; finding H-2).**

  | Item | Contract |
  |---|---|
  | TCP intake | One listener on `workload_addr:GUEST_TCP_INTAKE_PORT` (61,000); every captured outbound `connect()` is rewritten to it |
  | UDP slot sockets | `GUEST_UDP_SLOTS` (1,024) UDP sockets, slot n bound to its own explicit port `workload_addr:GUEST_UDP_SLOT_BASE + n` (61,001–62,024) from boot, never port 0 (EVMOD-DGRAM: a port-0 bind loses its port at disconnect) |
  | Reservation | All intakes bound before READY **without** `SO_REUSEADDR` / `SO_REUSEPORT`; `net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports` set to `guest_reserved_ports()`, so no reserved port is handed out as an ephemeral port. An application bind on `workload_addr` or `0.0.0.0` fails `EADDRINUSE`, deterministically, only on a port holding an intake of that protocol: TCP 61,000; UDP 61,001–62,024 (D25-BIND). A TCP bind on 61,001–62,024 or a UDP bind on 61,000 succeeds. No application socket can share an intake |
  | Slot identity | One slot per (application socket cookie, original destination). A socket sending to N destinations holds N slots. `overdrive-init` holds the slot-ownership table (`slot → (cookie, destination)`), read from the kernel slot map |
  | Slot release | Every slot of a released socket (not only the last); or a slot idle for `GUEST_DATAGRAM_SLOT_IDLE` (120 s) in both directions; a lost `sock_release` report is recovered by the level-triggered audit (slots whose cookie no longer exists). Release order: abort the pair (or close V_g before `Paired`) → discard the slot socket's receive queue without reading payload → disconnect the slot socket → return the slot (EVMOD-DGRAM, P-72). Never re-associated; late `Paired` → `Abort` |
  | Event dispatch | Every readiness event is dispatched by flow id or slot index, never by raw descriptor number |
  | Pool sizes | Pending TcpConnect flows `GUEST_TCP_PENDING_MAX` = 4,096 (= the per-allocation quota); UDP slots 1,024. Both count against the per-allocation quota (4,096) while in use. The guest has no per-flow slot pool: the forwarder allocates a pair's state at attach (EVMOD-AB) |
  | Clean full end | The guest forwarder completes a pair only after both directions ended cleanly (its own `0x2` sent on V_g after the last accepted byte, and the host's `0x2` received; P-65; ADR-0180); the owner closes V_g after the end record. A close with a direction open is an abort. A SHUTDOWN or RST after a pair's end is a no-op (END-IDEMPOTENT) |
  | Exhaustion | `GUEST_TCP_PENDING_MAX` pending → the new outbound TCP connection is reset (application sees `ECONNRESET`), counted `guest_tcp_pending_exhausted`. No free slot → the capture program refuses the application's `connect()` / `sendmsg()` to a new destination with `EPERM`, counted `guest_udp_slot_exhausted`. Existing flows are unaffected |
  | Deploy validation | A spec whose `[[listener]]` declares a port (either protocol) in `guest_reserved_ports()` is refused at deploy: `ParseError::ListenerPortReserved` at the TOML ingress, `AggregateError::Validation { field: "listeners[].port", .. }` at the API ingress (§ *Core vocabulary*). A spec whose startup, readiness and liveness probes together exceed `GUEST_PROBE_SLOTS` (8) is refused: `ParseError::ProbeCountExceeded` at the TOML ingress, `AggregateError::Validation { field: "probes", .. }` at the API ingress (D-UP-12) |

- **Kernel command-line token:**
  `overdrive.transport=vsock2,addr=<workload_addr>,dns=<gateway>,launch=<LaunchToken>,beacon=<port>,stream=<port>,control=<port>`.
  Exactly one token; fields in that order; no extra fields. `beacon`,
  `stream` and `control` are the host listener ports this node bound
  (GUEST-PORTS, ADR-0217; PORTS-CONFIG, ADR-0218), decimal: the VM driver
  writes `beacon` from its own intake's `bound_port()` and `stream` /
  `control` from the assignment's `flow_ports()`. A port field that is not a
  decimal `u32`, lies in 0..=1023, is `u32::MAX` or repeats another port
  field is `TokenMalformed { field }`, refused before any guest setup step
  (the existing pre-READY exit). `launch` is the
  assignment's `LaunchToken` (32 lowercase hex characters, ATTR-TOKEN);
  `overdrive-init` writes it in its `ControlOpen`, in every flow request it
  opens, and in READY, and checks it on every `TcpAccept` request.
- **Guest network configuration** (before READY): `lo` up; a dummy device up
  with `<workload_addr>/32`; `ip rule fwmark <platform mark> lookup local`;
  `net.ipv4.fwmark_reflect=1` (so the guest kernel's own reset toward a
  transparent client address is routed back at once, P-36);
  `net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports` = `guest_reserved_ports()` and every
  intake bound (D25); IPv6 stays disabled; resolver `nameserver <gateway>`;
  the guest capture programs loaded and every attachment linked; the
  forwarder module checked and loaded from `GUEST_FORWARDER_MODULE_PATH`, its
  context opened and its `DeviceOpen` and `Version` probe stages passed
  (EVMOD-LOAD, EVMOD-GUEST-KIT); inbound vsock listener bound on
  (`VMADDR_CID_ANY`, `GUEST_INBOUND_PORT`).
- **Guest image.** Carries the guest kit's `overdrive-init` and `ovd_fwd`
  for its kernel (EVMOD-GUEST-KIT), the capture programs, and the
  socket-diagnostics support the slot audit uses.
- **TcpAccept, guest side (INB-1).** On an inbound vsock connection V_g:
  read the 32-byte request; a launch token other than its own closes V_g
  with no message (ATTR-TOKEN); end-of-stream on V_g after the request means
  the host already closed it (TCPACCEPT-END, P-38) — the flow ends with no
  C and no message. Otherwise create C with `SO_LINGER{1,0}`,
  `IP_TRANSPARENT` bound to the request's `client` (the gateway with port 0;
  the guest kernel picks the port, V-28 Q3) and the platform `SO_MARK`;
  non-blocking `connect()` to `workload_addr:listen_port`, bounded by
  `GUEST_INBOUND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`. Connected → attach V_g–C, send `Paired`
  (an attach refused `HalfEnded` ends the flow by § *[REF] vsock data path*,
  "Owner response to an ended half at attach"). Failed → send
  `Refused { errno }` with the connect's errno (`ECONNREFUSED` when nothing
  listens). Not connected by the timeout → send
  `TimedOut { errno: ETIMEDOUT }`. Either failure closes C and V_g. If the
  flow was closed meanwhile (an `Abort`, session loss, the end of V_g), C is
  closed and nothing is sent (U-1).
- **Flow end (guest).** The guest owner applies § *Owner and provisioner*'s
  flow-end rules and owner flow rules to its own flows; the guest forwarder
  classifies each end of V_g: a host vsock SHUTDOWN 0x2 → `SHUT_WR` on I or
  C after the last accepted byte; 0x3 while a direction is open, or RST →
  abort, resetting I or C; the guest owner learns each from the pair's end
  record.
- **Typed setup failures.** `overdrive-init` exits before READY on any of:

  ```rust
  // overdrive-init (binary), rendered to the console; the host sees the
  // existing "guest exited before READY" start failure.
  enum GuestTransportSetupError {
      TokenMissing,
      TokenDuplicate,
      TokenMalformed { field: TransportTokenField },   // Version, Addr, Dns, Launch, Beacon, Stream, Control (GUEST-PORTS), Extra
      DummyDevice { source: std::io::Error },
      AddressAdd { source: std::io::Error },
      FwmarkRule { source: std::io::Error },
      FwmarkReflect { source: std::io::Error },
      ProgramLoad { program: GuestProgram, source: aya::EbpfError },
      ProgramAttach { program: GuestProgram, source: aya::programs::ProgramError },
      InboundListenerBind { source: std::io::Error },
      /// D25: reserving `guest_reserved_ports()` failed.
      ReservedPorts { source: std::io::Error },
      /// D25: binding an intake on a reserved port failed.
      IntakeBind { addr: std::net::SocketAddrV4, source: std::io::Error },
      /// EVMOD-GUEST-KIT: no module file at `GUEST_FORWARDER_MODULE_PATH`.
      ForwarderModuleMissing { path: std::path::PathBuf },
      /// EVMOD-GUEST-KIT: the module was built for another kernel release;
      /// the message names both and says that the VM's kernel and root
      /// filesystem must come from one guest kit.
      ForwarderModuleRelease { module: KernelRelease, kernel: KernelRelease },
      /// EVMOD-GUEST-KIT: any other refusal of `finit_module` (a same-release
      /// build the kernel refuses by `vermagic` or a CRC, a signature
      /// refusal under enforced module signing).
      ForwarderModuleLoad { source: std::io::Error },
      /// The forwarder context could not be opened or failed its `DeviceOpen`
      /// / `Version` probe stages (EVMOD-CTL, EVMOD-LIFE).
      Forwarder { source: ForwarderError },
  }
  enum GuestProgram { Connect4, Sendmsg4, Getpeername4, Recvmsg4, SockRelease }
  ```

  No new beacon message is added.
- **UDP slot release** follows § *Per-kind total orders* and the intake model
  above: every slot of a released socket, its queued datagrams discarded
  without reading payload, a released slot never re-associated. An
  association ended by `Refused`, `Abort`, the pairing deadline or its pair's
  end record discards the queue the same way, keeps its slot and is not
  re-associated until the application sends again (U-2).
- **Non-blocking connects.** The guest's connect to the application (TcpAccept)
  is non-blocking and never delays another flow.
- **No payload in guest userspace.** On each flow vsock connection
  `overdrive-init` writes or reads exactly one 32-byte request; on the control
  session one 24-byte `ControlOpen`, then only 8-byte messages.
- **Order.** Every exchange follows § *Per-kind total orders*.
- **Abort visibility (G-CRASH).** Intake children and application
  connections (C) carry `SO_LINGER{1,0}` from creation; a clean close clears
  it first. The linger serves the guest owner's abort path only: every abort
  the guest owner takes resets I or C, and the guest forwarder resets them
  itself when it aborts a pair — including when the host owner dies, whose
  context release shuts every host flow vsock both ways, which the guest
  forwarder classifies as an abort (EVMOD-CTL, EVMOD-END). A vsock
  end-of-stream is never turned into a FIN unless it was classified a clean
  half-close. A guest
  owner death is not an abort path: the guest owner is PID 1, and its death
  panics the guest kernel (`kernel/exit.c:929-930 @ v7.0`) before its files
  are released (`exit_files`, `kernel/exit.c:971 @ v7.0`), so no guest
  linger runs; the VM ends (RESET-EXIT) and the host owner aborts its side.
  After a `serve` crash the VM keeps running until the next boot's
  reclamation kills it (NO-SURVIVE, #312).
- **Programs.** The capture programs are Aya Rust in `overdrive-bpf`,
  embedded in the guest image; the forwarder is the guest kit's `ovd_fwd`.
- **Conformance observation (guest flow owner).** `overdrive-init` is a
  binary; its guest flow owner (control session, flow table, UDP slot pool)
  runs over the guest-owner seam the seeded-sim lane uses (DG-5). The
  accessor is a normal, read-only method of that owner type, compiled into
  the binary; the types are items of the binary crate, and the in-crate
  driver is a `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "integration-tests"))]` module in
  the binary's `src/`, driving the owner in-process:

  ```rust
  // overdrive-init (binary) — read-only, compiled in the binary
  impl GuestFlowOwner {   // DG-5
      pub(crate) fn guest_observation(&self) -> GuestSideObservation;
  }

  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub struct GuestSideObservation {
      /// The guest owner holds a control-session connection it has not
      /// observed lost (D-UP-8, approved 2026-10-14): true from the dispatch
      /// that starts its connect until the dispatch that observes the loss
      /// (DG-5-F). The owner holds at most one such connection.
      pub session: bool,
      /// Host-opened (TcpAccept) flows the guest holds, by host-origin flow id.
      pub accepted: BTreeMap<FlowId, GuestAcceptPhase>,
      /// Paired TCP flows the guest holds (either opener), by flow id, each
      /// with its attached pair; per-direction state through
      /// `FlowForwarder::pair_state` (EVMOD-PORT). A flow leaves the map in
      /// the dispatch that reads its pair's end record.
      pub flows: BTreeMap<FlowId, ForwardId>,
      /// TcpConnect flows the guest opened that are not yet Paired; their
      /// intake children are unattached and observed only for an error.
      pub awaiting_paired: BTreeSet<FlowId>,
      /// Every UDP slot, by the slot socket's bound address
      /// (`workload_addr:GUEST_UDP_SLOT_BASE + n`).
      pub slots: BTreeMap<SocketAddrV4, SlotObservation>,
      /// Cumulative attaches the forwarder refused `HalfEnded`, each ended
      /// by the guest owner as a flow abort (EVMOD-ATTACH-END; QPROJ-8).
      /// Never decremented.
      pub forwarder_attach_ended: u64,
      /// Cumulative attaches the forwarder accepted (`Ok`), raised in the
      /// dispatch that made the call (QPROJ-8, `attRes`). Never decremented.
      pub forwarder_attached: u64,
      /// The last end record the guest owner consumed in a dispatch (its
      /// pair's `take_end`, EVMOD-REC): depth 1, replaced at each
      /// consumption, `None` until the first (D-11).
      pub last_consumed_end: Option<ForwardEnd>,
      /// Cumulative end records the guest owner consumed. Never decremented.
      pub consumed_ends: u64,
  }

  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub enum GuestAcceptPhase {
      /// V_g accepted, request read and token matched; V_g unattached and
      /// observed only for its end; the connect to the application is issued
      /// or pending.
      Accepted,
      /// (V_g, C) attached and `Paired` sent in one dispatch (EVMOD-PAIR).
      Paired { pair: ForwardId },
  }

  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub struct SlotObservation {
      /// The (application socket, original destination) owning the slot.
      pub owner: Option<(SocketCookie, SocketAddrV4)>,
      /// The slot's current association, if any.
      pub association: Option<FlowId>,
      /// The association's datagram pair (S, V_g) is attached (EVMOD-DGRAM).
      pub attached: Option<ForwardId>,
  }
  ```

  `ForwardId` is the core forwarder id (EVMOD-PORT). `SocketCookie` is the
  `overdrive-init`-private newtype pinned in DG-5.

  **The guest's session (D-UP-8, approved 2026-10-14).** The guest owner
  holds at most one control-session connection. It opens another only in a
  dispatch after the one that observed the loss of the connection it held
  (DG-5-F), and it holds none while its VM is down (the owner does not
  exist; the VM's next start runs a fresh owner). A second first-connect to
  the control port from the same CID — the racing connect of L-3 (R5-18) —
  is not the guest owner's: any guest process can open an `AF_VSOCK` socket
  to the host's `GUEST_FLOW_CONTROL_PORT` (1243), and a workload that read the launch token from
  the kernel command line can present it. The host owner's one-live-session
  rule (L-3) governs it; the guest owner's `session` is unaffected by it.
  In the model the guest's session is the guest-side variable `gSess` of
  `owner_flows`, and the racing connect is its own action,
  `WorkloadOpenSession(c)`. Rejected: deriving `session` from the host's
  `sess` table (it counts a dead session live after `VmStop`, and none after
  `HostSessionLoss` while the guest still holds its flows).

  **Real-kernel reach of the guest side (D-UP-18).** No driving port is
  missing: `configure_guest_transport(token, &mut KernelGuestTransportOps)`
  and `GuestFlowOwner` over `KernelGuestOwnerIo` and `KernelFlowForwarder`
  are reachable from source-local `#[cfg(all(test, feature =
  "integration-tests"))]` real-kernel tests in the binary (the placement the
  conformance drivers use) and from the microVM walking skeleton (P6-S13).
  Which lane carries each check is DISTILL's.

  Contract of `guest_observation`:

  - **Preconditions:** none. Infallible; callable on a constructed owner at
    any time, before and after the control session.
  - **Postconditions:** an owned copy of the owner's session flag, flow
    tables and slot table. The call accepts, routes, releases and closes
    nothing and changes no state.
  - **Consistency point:** between two owner steps. An owner step is one
    dispatch of the owner's serialized event handling (a control message, a
    readiness event, an accept, a forwarder end record, an
    application-leg event, a timer).
  - **Edge cases:** before the session opens, `session = false` and every
    table is empty except `slots`, which lists every slot with
    `owner = None`. A slot with an `owner` and no `association` has not
    started pairing; `attached` being `Some` implies `association` is
    `Some`. A flow the
    guest ended (closed, aborted, refused, timed out, or a V_g torn down in
    its accept queue) is absent. After the session ends, `session = false`
    and the tables hold only what the owner has not yet ended.
  - **Observable invariants:** a `FlowId` in `awaiting_paired` is in
    neither `accepted` nor `flows`; an `accepted` entry in
    `Paired { pair }` is in `flows` with the same `pair`; a repeated call
    with no intervening owner step returns an equal value.

#### [REF] Composition — production entry points

**Boot** (`run_server` → `run_server_with_obs_and_drivers`):

1. **Startup checks (phase 1 of the owner's two-phase boot, D-8).** Owner cgroup placement (D24), fd budget, no range of
   `vip_range` overlapping the guest prefix (D8-PREFIX-VIP) and no node
   interface address inside it (D8-PREFIX-CFG), all from one
   `GuestFlowIo::host_facts()` snapshot. They need only the seam and two
   configured values, never the owner's late ports (the resolve, the mTLS
   worker), so `run_server` runs them over the boot's `GuestFlowIo` with
   `probe_guest_flow_startup` (below) before the owner exists: after the
   ADR-0028 cgroup preflight and the control-plane slice enrolment (the
   placement check observes that enrolment) and before the probe-runner
   gate and `compose_vm_driver`, so before the beacon bind (step 2) and the
   load-balancer veth provisioning from `vip_range` (step 3). After those
   four checks phase 1 runs the forwarder probe
   (`GuestFlowIo::probe_forwarder`): it opens a context of its own, runs
   every `ForwarderProbeStage` and releases the context before it returns,
   on `Ok` and on `Err` (the `Cleanup` stage leaves inventory zero), so a
   missing or mis-built module refuses before any boot effect
   (ADR-0205, ADR-0159). Phase 1 leaves nothing behind. Refusal:
   `health.startup.refused`, reason `guest_network.probe`. The owner is
   composed at step 5 over the same `GuestFlowIo` instance and is not
   probed again before step 9. On the supplied-owner path
   (`run_server_with_obs_and_drivers`, below) step 1 is the supplied
   owner's `probe_startup()`, first in the boot. Only the owner's
   composition waits for step 5 — the resolve and the enforcement it takes
   need the CA identity of step 3 — and nothing that phase 1 checks needs
   either, so the two-phase split exists only for the composition.
2. `compose_vm_driver` over `adapters.vm` (NO-OVERRIDE-SEAMS, below):
   `Vmm::probe` (today's stages; DG-1) and `CgroupAccounting::probe` on
   `adapters.vm.cgroup_accounting`, then the beacon listener bind
   (`BeaconIntake::bind(adapters.vm.beacon, config.vsock_ports.beacon())`,
   passed to `VmDriver::new`, DG-4; the intake reports the bound port,
   PORTS-CONFIG). A failed probe leaves the node without a `Vm` driver when
   `adapters.vm.capability` is `Optional` and refuses boot (`vmm.probe`)
   when it is `Required`. The probe runner, the exec gate and the VM driver
   take `adapters.boot.clock`, the one clock of the boot. Guest forwarding does not depend on its outcome: the owner opens,
   probes, audits and repairs the forwarder and binds its listeners on
   every node (on the appliance the pinned Cloud Hypervisor fork
   is always present, ADR-0161, ADR-0068).
3. CA, identity (as today), then the dataplane through
   `adapters.boot.dataplane.compose(plan)` (NO-OVERRIDE-SEAMS, below), which
   returns the probed dataplane and the node's `host_ipv4`. With the default
   interface names, the host composer provisions ADR-0061's load-balancer
   veth pair `ovd-veth-cli` / `ovd-veth-bk` in the root namespace: gateways
   from `vip_range` (disjoint from the guest prefix by step 1) and the route
   `<vip_range> dev ovd-veth-cli`.
4. `GuestAddressPool::new(GUEST_NODE_PREFIX, GUEST_NODE_GATEWAY, entropy)`
   (DG-9) — `entropy` is `adapters.boot.entropy` (`OsEntropy` in
   production), which draws the launch tokens (ATTR-TOKEN).
5. Enforcement (`adapters.boot.mtls.enforcement.enforcement(deps)` with the
   boot's `IdentityMgr` as `deps.identity`, `GUEST_NODE_PREFIX` as
   `deps.guest_prefix`, LEGB-DIAL, and the boot's unbound `OwnerDial` as
   `deps.guest_dial`, LEGS-DIAL; production's factory builds
   `HostMtlsEnforcement::new` over them) and resolve probes;
   `MtlsInterceptWorker::new` (its four ports, no dial; the intercept is
   `adapters.boot.mtls.intercept`); `AppState`. The owner's ports take the mTLS
   worker (forwarded-outbound registration); the enforcement reaches the
   owner through the `OwnerDial`. This is phase 2 of the owner's boot (D-8):
   `compose_guest_network(ports, io, dial)` builds the worker over the
   enforcement and the owner over the step-1 `GuestFlowIo`, and binds the
   boot's one `OwnerDial` to the owner (D-13, below), so every component is
   constructed with its required arguments and none is defaulted or
   optional. The construction shape inside it is the crafter's.
6. `vm_reclamation_boot::converge` — kills every VM the new process does not
   supervise (NO-SURVIVE; VM survival across a `serve` restart is #312).
   Each reclaimed VMM's vhost-vsock file is released at its exit, before its
   cgroup is removed, and before any `assign` (`AssignAfterReclaim`).
7. `sweep_stale()`.
8. `mtls_worker.start_shared_owner()`: leg-F (registered mesh only), leg-C,
   the constant rules — 1, 4, 6, 7; 5 and 8 on the constant guest prefix
   (output reject / prerouting drop of guest-prefix traffic not diverted to
   leg-C, R5-43), after the leg-C divert, so the divert still sees every
   packet of its connections; the host-internal rules (D26: the marked
   `gateway:53` accept and the marked non-unicast / loopback / link-local
   reject) first in that output chain, ahead of every `accept` (D26-PINS
   F-1, P-47) — with `inbound_destinations` converged to empty. The table is
   written, and every later replacement of it is made, in one nft
   transaction (D26-PINS F-2). **A failure refuses boot (QHOLD,
   ADR-0184):** `health.startup.refused`, reason `mtls.shared_owner`,
   `ControlPlaneError::MtlsBoot(MtlsBootError::SharedOwner { source })`,
   before forwarding opens; the supervised restart converges on boot.
9. `converge_shared()`: the owner's serving forwarder context
   (`open_forwarder`: `KernelFlowForwarder::open` and `probe`, so no context
   is used before it passed; the module itself is loaded by the host image
   before `serve` starts, EVMOD-LOAD) and the flow and control listeners,
   bound on `config.vsock_ports.flow_stream()` / `.flow_control()`; from this
   call's first `Ok` the owner reports the bound ports (`flow_ports()`,
   PORTS-CONFIG), and `run_server` reads them once into the action shim's
   state. Then the gateway route (GW-LOCAL): one Overdrive-tagged (`proto
   GUEST_PREFIX_ROUTE_PROTOCOL`) `local <gateway>/32 dev lo` route, kept if
   identical, replaced if its attributes differ, added if missing, never
   removed. A failure refuses boot (`health.startup.refused`, reason
   `guest_network.converge`; `Netlink { operation: LocalRouteConverge }`).
   This is the only `converge_shared` call that writes the route. No other
   route covers the guest prefix (LEGB-DIAL).
10. DNS bind (ADR-0116), probe, serve.
11. Supervisor.
12. `open_after_boot()`.

**The owner's two-phase boot (D-8).** The guest-flow
owner cannot exist at step 1: its ports need the mTLS worker, which needs
the enforcement port (the CA identity of step 3) and the resolve built at
step 5. Its startup checks need neither, so they are a function of the seam
and run first; the owner is built later over the same seam:

```rust
// overdrive_control_plane::guest_network — crate-private
/// Phase 1 (Composition step 1): every `probe_startup` check over one
/// `io.host_facts()` snapshot — `GuestPrefixOverlapsVipRange` first, then
/// `GuestPrefixOverlapsNodeAddress`, `OwnerCgroupPlacement`, `FdBudget` —
/// then `io.probe_forwarder()` (`GuestNetworkError::Forwarder { source }`).
/// Leaves nothing behind: the probe's context is released before return.
/// `HostSharedGuestNetworkOwner::probe_startup` is this
/// function over the owner's own seam, `vip_range` and `node_prefix`, so the
/// two cannot disagree.
pub(crate) async fn probe_guest_flow_startup(
    io: &dyn GuestFlowIo,
    vip_range: &VipRange,
    node_prefix: Ipv4Net,
) -> Result<(), GuestNetworkError>;
```

Phase 2 is `compose_guest_network(ports, io, dial)` at step 5 (§ *Owner
and mTLS-worker composition (D-UP-16)*) over the `io` phase 1 checked. The
structural boot-order test pins phase 1 — its forwarder probe included —
before `compose_vm_driver` and every other boot effect, no forwarder
context open when phase 1 returns, and `compose_guest_network` after it; no
boot path composes an owner whose seam phase 1 did not check. The probe
context is not the serving context: the serving context is opened at step
9, so a forwarder module is proven usable before boot has changed
anything, and the context the owner serves from is still probed before it
is used.

**Entry points and the supplied owner (D-8).**

- `run_server(config, adapters)` (production; the composition root
  passes `adapters`, NO-OVERRIDE-SEAMS) takes the owner's seam from
  `adapters.guest_flow` and creates the boot's `OwnerDial::unbound()`, runs
  phase 1 over that seam, the probe-runner gate (over `adapters.probers`
  and the dial) and `compose_vm_driver` over `adapters.vm`, then the
  crate-private `boot_server` with `adapters.boot` and
  `GuestNetworkSource::Composed { io, dial }`, which composes at step 5.
  Neither `run_server` nor `boot_server` constructs an adapter over a host
  resource or a store: both compose driver and owner objects (the
  `VmDriver` in `compose_vm_driver`, the `DriverRegistry`, the owner, the
  workflow engine) over the ports they are given, and obtain the CA and
  the mTLS enforcement only through the supplied factories (STORES-IN).
- The in-crate composed rig (`shared_network_test_ports::composed`, T-8)
  boots the same way over `SimGuestFlowIo`: phase 1 over its seam, then
  `boot_server` with `GuestNetworkSource::Composed`. It builds no
  owner over a separately built worker, so D-UP-16's postcondition holds in
  the rig.
- `run_server_with_obs_and_drivers` keeps its supplied
  `Arc<dyn SharedGuestNetworkOwner>` parameter: it is the owner's driven
  port, for owner-level doubles (`TestOwnerProcess` over `TestSharedOwner`,
  the FHOLD-CHECK supervisor mapping) that script the owner's answers. It
  takes the boot-wide group `BootAdapters` (below); it has no `obs` or
  `vm_host_state` parameter and no adapter field of `ServerConfig`;
  `BootAdapters` carries the stores and the CA too
  (STORES-IN), so on this path as well the boot opens and constructs
  nothing: its caller passes `StoreAdapters::open(&config)` (or simulation
  view and journal stores beside an `IntentStoreAdapter::open` over its
  temporary directory) and `CaAdapters::host()` (or one over
  `SimCaFactory`), and the boot builds the CA over `boot.entropy` and runs
  the view-store probes and the CA's generate-or-adopt exactly as on the
  composed path. It takes no `NodeAdapters`, because it composes neither a
  VM driver (its caller builds the registry, with whatever `Vmm`,
  `BeaconIo` and `CgroupAccounting` that caller's `VmDriver` holds) nor the
  owner (supplied), and `config.vsock_ports` is not read on it (the
  supplied owner and the caller's `VmDriver` bound their own ports; the
  action shim reads the supplied owner's `flow_ports()` as on the composed
  path). Step 1 there is the supplied owner's `probe_startup()`, first in the boot;
  the enforcement takes the supplied owner as its `guest_dial`
  (LEGS-DIAL). D-UP-16's
  postcondition is not claimed on that path (no `compose_guest_network`
  runs), and no test that asserts the owner ↔ worker composition, the
  forwarded-outbound registration or a leg-S / probe dial uses it.

**No production branch on VM capability.**
Production boot is the same on every node: the owner's startup probe
includes the forwarder probe, `converge_shared` opens the serving forwarder
context and binds the flow and control listeners, and `audit_shared` and
the supervisor audit and repair `Forwarder`, `FlowListeners` and
`ControlListener` unconditionally. On the appliance the pinned Cloud
Hypervisor fork is always present and probes healthy (ADR-0161, ADR-0068);
a node whose `Vm` driver is not composed (a non-appliance host) still
requires the forwarder module (ADR-0205) and serves no VM: a `[vm]` deploy
fails at dispatch for the absent capability, as today. No state that only a
test configuration produces is given a production branch
(`development.md` § "Ground the premise"; design.md § "Correct, and no more
than correct").

**Driven adapters of `run_server` (NO-OVERRIDE-SEAMS, ADR-0219).** `run_server`
receives every driven adapter it composes the node over as one required
parameter, built by the composition root. `overdrive serve` passes the host
adapters; a test passes simulation adapters or host adapters it names.
Neither `run_server` nor the `boot_server` it delegates to constructs an
adapter over a host resource or a store (STORES-IN: no carve-out — the persistent stores and the workload-identity
CA come from the composition root too; the CA as a `CaFactory` the boot
calls over its one entropy). What they do build is composition over the
supplied ports: `compose_vm_driver` builds the `VmDriver` (a `Driver`
implementation) over `adapters.vm`, `run_server` builds the
`DriverRegistry` over it, and the boot obtains the CA and the mTLS
enforcement through the supplied factories. `ServerConfig` carries configuration only: no field of it
carries or swaps an adapter, and no field injects a fault. Removed from `ServerConfig`: `clock` (and its
`SystemClock` default in `ServerConfig::new`), `kek`, `dataplane_override`,
`mtls_intercept`, `guest_dns`, `mtls_identity_override`,
`dataplane_probe_fault`, `mtls_probe_fault` and `vm_override` (DG-4); no
guest-flow seam field exists (`GuestFlowIoOverride`, `sim_vsock` and
`guest_flow_io_override` do not exist). D-UP-16's
"`ServerConfig` gains no field for the owner's seam" holds. Removed
from `run_server`'s body: the second `SystemClock` (`lib.rs:2864`, which
ignored `config.clock`: the probe runner, the exec gate and the VM driver
ran on a different clock from the convergence loop), the construction of
`TokioTcpProber`, `HyperHttpProber`, `RealCgroupAccounting`,
`RealVmHostState`, the observation store
(`observation_wiring::wire_single_node_observation`), `OsEntropy` (three
sites: the workflow engine, the CA, the address pool), the workflow
engine's `TcpTransport`, `HostMtlsEnforcement` and `EbpfDataplane` (with
its veth provisioning and probe), and the `host_ipv4` fallback keyed on
`dataplane_override`'s presence (`host_ipv4_with_override_fallback`,
`lib.rs:2752-2761`, `:3682-3685`, deleted with its unit tests). Removed
from `boot_server`'s body (STORES-IN): `LocalIntentStore::open`
(`lib.rs:3433-3437`), `RedbViewStore::open` (`:3453-3459`), the journal's
`redb::Database::create` and `RedbJournalStore::new` (`:3744-3750`),
`RcgenCa::new` with its `OsEntropy` (`:3778-3779`) and
`RootKeyAeadCodec::new` (`:3789`). What stays in `boot_server` is building
the CA through the supplied `CaFactory` over the boot's entropy, and using
and probing the adapters, at today's positions: the view store's Earned-Trust
probe and bulk load inside each `runtime.register` (ADR-0035 § 5), and
the workload-identity CA's generate-or-adopt with its Earned-Trust probes
(`ca_boot::boot_ca`: KEK resolve (a), envelope decrypt (b); then
`bootstrap_node_intermediate`) over the supplied CA, codec, intent store
and KEK, refusing as today with `ControlPlaneError::CaBoot`. The
composition root wires; the boot probes and adopts before first use
(wire → probe → use), so every composition — host or test — runs those
probes.
Configuration that stays in `ServerConfig`: `bind`, `data_dir`,
`operator_config_dir`, `tick_cadence`, `node`, `vip_range`, `dataplane`,
`dataplane_pin_dir`, `dataplane_cgroup_attach_path` and `vsock_ports`.
`ServerConfig::new()` takes no argument (the fields keep today's defaults);
`ServerConfig` derives `Debug` and stays without `Default`.

**What decides the composition.** The mTLS worker, its enforcement and
resolve, the DNS task owner and the shared-network supervisor are composed
on every boot, whichever adapters are passed (ADR-0138; no `compose_mtls`
branch exists, as banned by
`required_serve_ports_source_scan.rs:86-92`). No branch of the boot keys on
which adapter a field holds: the dataplane is whatever the composer
returns, and the node address `ServiceMapHydrator` registers local backends
with (`host_ipv4`) is the address the composer resolved on its own client
interface — on the host composer `resolve_iface_ipv4(client_iface)` after
provisioning, a failure refusing the boot as today; on a simulation
composer the value it was built with. The `Vm` driver is composed when its
probes pass; when they fail, `VmCapability` decides between "no `Vm`
driver" and refusal.

```rust
// overdrive_control_plane — public
/// The driven adapters `run_server` composes over. Every field required;
/// no `Default`, no builder (`development.md` § "Port-trait dependencies").
pub struct NodeAdapters {
    /// The adapters both boot paths compose over (`run_server` and the
    /// supplied-owner path).
    pub boot: BootAdapters,
    /// The cgroupfs adapter: the workloads-slice bootstrap, the
    /// `CgroupManager` and the VM driver use it. `overdrive serve` passes the
    /// handle its ADR-0054 probe accepted (the probed handle is the used
    /// handle).
    pub cgroup_fs: Arc<dyn CgroupFs>,
    pub probers: ProbeAdapters,
    pub vm: VmAdapters,
    pub guest_flow: GuestFlowAdapter,
}

/// The adapters `boot_server` composes over, on both boot paths.
pub struct BootAdapters {
    /// The one clock of the boot: convergence loop, `TickContext`, probe
    /// runner, exec gate, VM driver, workflow engine, node-health writer,
    /// streaming handlers, supervisor. `SystemClock` in production.
    pub clock: Arc<dyn Clock>,
    /// The workflow engine's RNG, the workload-identity CA's key generation
    /// and the address pool's launch tokens. `OsEntropy` in production.
    pub entropy: Arc<dyn Entropy>,
    /// The workflow engine's `ctx.call` transport. `TcpTransport` in
    /// production.
    pub transport: Arc<dyn Transport>,
    /// The workload-identity CA's KEK (ADR-0063). `SystemdCredsKeyring` in
    /// production.
    pub kek: Arc<dyn Kek>,
    /// The observation store. In production the `LocalObservationStore`
    /// `observation_wiring::wire_single_node_observation(&config.data_dir)`
    /// opens (`NodeAdapters::host` derives the path from the configuration
    /// it is given, so the host bundle cannot disagree with it; a test that
    /// replaces this field keeps it over the same `data_dir` or a
    /// simulation store).
    pub observation: Arc<dyn ObservationStore>,
    /// The VM host state boot reclamation reads (composed whether or not a
    /// `Vm` driver is). `RealVmHostState` over the cgroup root,
    /// `/run/overdrive/vm` and `clone_index_dir(&config.data_dir)` in
    /// production (S-VM-84: `clone_index_dir` stays the one derivation both
    /// sites call).
    pub vm_host_state: Arc<dyn VmHostState>,
    /// The node's persistent stores (STORES-IN). In production
    /// `StoreAdapters::open(config)`.
    pub stores: StoreAdapters,
    /// The workload-identity CA's factory and codec (STORES-IN). In
    /// production `CaAdapters::host()`. The boot builds the CA over this
    /// bundle's `entropy`, then runs its generate-or-adopt.
    pub ca: CaAdapters,
    pub dataplane: Arc<dyn DataplaneComposer>,
    pub mtls: MtlsAdapters,
    /// ADR-0138. `HostGuestDnsFactory` in production.
    pub guest_dns: Arc<dyn GuestDnsFactory>,
}

/// The transparent-mTLS adapters (ADR-0138, ADR-0219).
pub struct MtlsAdapters {
    /// `HostMtlsIntercept` in production.
    pub intercept: Arc<dyn MtlsIntercept>,
    /// `HostMtlsEnforcementFactory` in production.
    pub enforcement: Arc<dyn MtlsEnforcementFactory>,
}

/// The node's persistent stores (STORES-IN, ADR-0219). Opened by the
/// composition root over `config.data_dir`; `boot_server` opens nothing.
/// Not `Clone`: one `StoreAdapters` serves one boot. Every boot opens its
/// stores from disk (`StoreAdapters::open` or `NodeAdapters::host`), so a
/// restart or crash test reopens the files the previous server released and
/// reruns `LocalIntentStore::open`'s boot-validation walks, as a new
/// process does (`rust.md`'s reopen-after-generation-bump precedent). For
/// the intent store, a boot over the previous boot's live handle is
/// unrepresentable: `IntentStoreAdapter` has private fields, only `open`,
/// and no `Clone`. `views` and `journal` are public `Arc` fields, so a
/// caller could build a second boot's `StoreAdapters` from the first boot's
/// `Arc`s by struct literal. The type does not prevent that; it is a caller
/// error, and every restart and crash test reopens through
/// `StoreAdapters::open` or `NodeAdapters::host` (DISTILL handoff (11)).
/// Production opens them once per process.
pub struct StoreAdapters {
    /// The intent store and the file it was opened from.
    pub intent: IntentStoreAdapter,
    /// The reconciler view store (ADR-0035). `RedbViewStore` over
    /// `<data_dir>/reconcilers/memory.redb` in production; `SimViewStore`
    /// in a simulated test. The boot probes and bulk-loads it in each
    /// `runtime.register`, as today.
    pub views: Arc<dyn ViewStore>,
    /// The workflow journal (ADR-0066). `RedbJournalStore` over
    /// `<data_dir>/workflow-journal.redb` in production; `SimJournalStore`
    /// in a simulated test.
    pub journal: Arc<dyn JournalStore>,
}
impl StoreAdapters {
    /// The host stores over `config.data_dir`, in this order: the intent
    /// store (`IntentStoreAdapter::open`, which creates `data_dir` when
    /// missing, so the two opens after it never depend on another
    /// component having created it), the view store
    /// (`RedbViewStore::open(&config.data_dir)`), the journal
    /// (`redb::Database::create(<data_dir>/workflow-journal.redb)` then
    /// `RedbJournalStore::new`).
    /// Err, first failure in that order, each the error `boot_server`
    /// returns for it today: the intent open's
    /// `ControlPlaneError::Internal` ("open LocalIntentStore"),
    /// `ControlPlaneError::ViewStoreBoot(ViewStoreBootError::Open { path,
    /// source })`, the journal create's `ControlPlaneError::Internal`
    /// ("create workflow-journal redb"). A file opened before the failure is
    /// closed by drop; the files themselves stay (they are the node's
    /// durable state, created idempotently). Effects: only the three files
    /// under `data_dir` (and `data_dir` itself).
    pub fn open(config: &ServerConfig) -> Result<Self, ControlPlaneError>;
}

/// The node's intent store (Phase-1 single mode: `LocalIntentStore` over
/// redb) and the path of its file. Concrete, not `Arc<dyn IntentStore>`:
/// `AppState.store` and the listener-fact rebuild take the concrete store,
/// and `LocalIntentStore` over a temporary directory is already the store
/// every test runs (`testing.md` § "Store composition"); no simulation
/// intent store exists to substitute. The path travels with the store, so
/// the CA boot's refuse-to-start remediations, the listener-fact rebuild and
/// `HydrationContext::intent_redb_path` name the file that was opened, not a
/// path re-derived from the configuration. Not `Clone`, for the reason
/// `StoreAdapters` is not; the boot shares the store through
/// `store().clone()` of the `Arc`.
pub struct IntentStoreAdapter { /* private: store: Arc<LocalIntentStore>, path: PathBuf */ }
impl IntentStoreAdapter {
    /// `LocalIntentStore::open(<data_dir>/intent.redb)`; creates `data_dir`
    /// when missing. Err: `ControlPlaneError::Internal` ("open
    /// LocalIntentStore"), as `boot_server` returns today.
    pub fn open(data_dir: &Path) -> Result<Self, ControlPlaneError>;
    pub fn store(&self) -> &Arc<LocalIntentStore>;
    /// The file `open` opened.
    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path;
}

/// The workload-identity CA's factory and the codec that seals its root key
/// under the KEK (ADR-0063, STORES-IN). The boot calls `factory.build` once,
/// over `BootAdapters.entropy`, so the CA's key generation always draws
/// from the boot's one entropy: a test that replaces `entropy` by struct
/// update cannot leave a CA keyed to another source (the representability
/// rule `NodeAdapters::host(&ServerConfig, ..)` applies to `data_dir`). The
/// built CA holds no root; the boot's `ca_boot::boot_ca` /
/// `bootstrap_node_intermediate` generate or adopt the persistent root and
/// the node intermediate over `BootAdapters.stores.intent` and
/// `BootAdapters.kek`, after its Earned-Trust probes. Each boot builds its
/// own CA: `RcgenCa` caches the root it adopted (`RaceOnceCell`).
/// `NodeAdapters` / `BootAdapters` are not `Clone`.
pub struct CaAdapters {
    /// `RcgenCaFactory` in production; `SimCaFactory` or a test-local
    /// factory in a test.
    pub factory: Arc<dyn CaFactory>,
    /// `RootKeyAeadCodec` (the only codec; `boot_ca` takes it concretely).
    pub root_key_codec: Arc<RootKeyAeadCodec>,
}
impl CaAdapters {
    /// `RcgenCaFactory` (over the workload CA trust-domain subject
    /// `boot_server` uses today, `spiffe://overdrive.local/overdrive/ca`)
    /// and `RootKeyAeadCodec::new()`. Infallible; no I/O.
    pub fn host() -> Self;
}

// overdrive_core::traits::ca — public, beside `Ca`
/// Builds the workload-identity CA over the entropy the boot supplies
/// (the precedent of `MtlsEnforcementFactory`: an adapter whose inputs
/// are known only to the boot is supplied as a factory).
pub trait CaFactory: Send + Sync {
    /// Called exactly once per boot, by `boot_server`, before
    /// `ca_boot::boot_ca`. Postcondition: the returned CA draws every key
    /// it generates from `entropy` and holds no root until `boot_ca` (or
    /// `bootstrap_node_intermediate`) installs one; two calls return two
    /// independent CAs. Infallible and effect-free: no I/O, no clock read.
    fn build(&self, entropy: Arc<dyn Entropy>) -> Arc<dyn Ca>;
}
// overdrive_host::ca — public
/// `build` returns `RcgenCa::new(entropy, subject)`.
pub struct RcgenCaFactory { /* private: subject */ }
impl RcgenCaFactory { pub fn new(subject: SpiffeId) -> Self; }
// overdrive_sim::adapters::ca — public
/// `build` returns `SimCa::new(entropy)`.
pub struct SimCaFactory;

/// The probe runner's probers (ADR-0054 § 7). `TokioTcpProber` and
/// `HyperHttpProber` in production.
pub struct ProbeAdapters {
    pub tcp: Arc<dyn TcpProber>,
    pub http: Arc<dyn HttpProber>,
}

/// The VM driver's driven ports (DG-4), the cgroup accounting probed beside
/// the VMM (ADR-0082 § D8 "Composition") and the composition root's
/// statement of whether this node requires VM capability.
pub struct VmAdapters {
    /// `CloudHypervisorVmm` in production; `SimVmm` in a simulated-VM test.
    pub vmm: Arc<dyn Vmm>,
    /// `VsockBeaconIo` in production; `SimBeaconIo` with `SimVmm`. A
    /// simulated VMM with a real beacon (or the reverse) is a caller error
    /// the type does not prevent; DG-4's "the two travel together" is a
    /// documented precondition of this struct.
    pub beacon: Arc<dyn BeaconIo>,
    /// `RealCgroupAccounting` in production. It rides the VM driver's
    /// composition gate (probed with the VMM, the same `VmCapability`
    /// classification), so it belongs to this group.
    pub cgroup_accounting: Arc<dyn CgroupAccounting>,
    pub capability: VmCapability,
}

/// What a failed `Vmm::probe` or `CgroupAccounting::probe` (or the
/// `/dev/kvm` group read or the clone-staging setup after them) means at
/// boot step 2. The probes run unconditionally either way (Earned Trust).
/// Why `Required` exists although `overdrive serve` never passes it:
/// ADR-0219, Decision.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum VmCapability {
    /// The node boots without a `Vm` driver and logs
    /// `driver.vm.not_composed`; a `[vm]` deploy fails at dispatch
    /// (ADR-0083 § D8's "capability absence"). `overdrive serve` passes this
    /// (today's production behaviour).
    Optional,
    /// The boot refuses: `health.startup.refused`, reason `vmm.probe`,
    /// `ControlPlaneError::VmmBoot` (ADR-0083 § D8's "substrate lie"). A
    /// root whose VMM is a double it constructed passes this.
    Required,
}
impl VmCapability { pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; } // "optional" | "required"

/// The guest-flow owner's seam (`GuestFlowIo`, crate-private, § *Owner
/// and provisioner*). Opaque: outside the crate only the host seam can be
/// named, so every out-of-crate `serve` runs the production listeners and
/// forwarder (PORTS-CONFIG: no simulated seam is swapped in).
pub struct GuestFlowAdapter(/* private: Arc<dyn GuestFlowIo> */);
impl GuestFlowAdapter {
    /// `HostGuestFlowIo::new()`. Infallible; touches no kernel state. The
    /// in-crate composed rig does not go through `run_server`; it calls
    /// `boot_server` with `GuestNetworkSource::Composed` over
    /// `SimGuestFlowIo` (below), so no other constructor exists.
    pub fn host() -> Self;
}

impl NodeAdapters {
    /// The host bundle — the composition `overdrive serve` runs — over the
    /// configuration it will boot (every path is derived from
    /// `config.data_dir`, so the bundle and the boot cannot name two
    /// directories), with the two adapters the binary boundary chooses
    /// passed in: `cgroup_fs` (the handle its ADR-0054 probe already
    /// accepted: the caller probes first, as `serve` does) and `kek`
    /// (`SystemdCredsKeyring` in `serve`; C1-AMEND). Every other field is the
    /// host adapter named in its docstring above, `capability` is
    /// `VmCapability::Optional` and `guest_flow` is `GuestFlowAdapter::host()`.
    /// Order (STORES-IN): the infallible adapters (clock, entropy,
    /// transport, probers, VM ports, dataplane composer, mTLS adapters,
    /// guest-DNS factory, `RealVmHostState` over `config.data_dir`), then
    /// `StoreAdapters::open(config)`, then the observation store;
    /// `ca` is `CaAdapters::host()`.
    /// It is the one place the host adapters are named, so `serve` and every
    /// test that runs the production composition (the D-17 `kvm-tests` lane,
    /// the CLI lanes) use one list; a test replaces a field by struct update
    /// and so names each adapter it does not take from the host.
    /// Err: the first failing open, the error the boot returns for it today
    /// (`StoreAdapters::open`'s three, then the observation store's). Effects:
    /// the node's durable files under `config.data_dir` only; no kernel
    /// state. Precondition: nothing in this process still holds the same
    /// `data_dir`'s redb files (a restart or crash test shuts the first
    /// server down, or kills it with `kill_for_test`, which releases every
    /// handle, and drops any handle it opened itself before calling this
    /// again). A held file is redb's open refusal, returned as the error above.
    pub fn host(
        config: &ServerConfig,
        cgroup_fs: Arc<dyn CgroupFs>,
        kek: Arc<dyn Kek>,
    ) -> Result<Self, ControlPlaneError>;
}

pub async fn run_server(
    config: ServerConfig,
    adapters: NodeAdapters,
) -> Result<ServerHandle, ControlPlaneError>;

/// The supplied-owner path (above). `boot` carries the observation store,
/// the VM host state, the stores and the CA; preconditions: `drivers` and
/// `guest_network_exec` were built over `boot.clock` (the boot's one
/// clock), and `boot.stores` / `boot.observation` / `boot.vm_host_state`
/// are over `config.data_dir` or simulations.
pub async fn run_server_with_obs_and_drivers(
    config: ServerConfig,
    boot: BootAdapters,
    drivers: Arc<DriverRegistry>,
    shared_guest_network: Arc<dyn SharedGuestNetworkOwner>,
    guest_network_exec: GuestNetworkExecWiring,
    vm_cgroups: CgroupManager,
) -> Result<ServerHandle, ControlPlaneError>;
/// Its single-driver convenience sibling, the same change.
pub async fn run_server_with_obs_and_driver(
    config: ServerConfig,
    boot: BootAdapters,
    driver: Arc<dyn Driver>,
    shared_guest_network: Arc<dyn SharedGuestNetworkOwner>,
    guest_network_exec: GuestNetworkExecWiring,
    vm_cgroups: CgroupManager,
) -> Result<ServerHandle, ControlPlaneError>;

/// Boot step 3's dataplane block (ADR-0052, ADR-0061: provision →
/// construct → probe), behind a port because its production construction
/// has host effects that must follow the boot's startup checks.
#[async_trait::async_trait]
pub trait DataplaneComposer: Send + Sync {
    /// Called once per boot, at step 3.
    /// Ok: a dataplane that passed its Earned-Trust probe, and the node's
    /// address on `plan.config.client_iface`.
    /// Err: the `ControlPlaneError` the boot returns for that failure today
    /// — `DataplaneBoot(Provision | Construct | Probe)`, or the client
    /// interface's address-resolution error. Nothing the call created
    /// survives an Err (a constructed dataplane is dropped, which detaches
    /// its programs and unpins its maps, as today).
    async fn compose(&self, plan: DataplanePlan<'_>) -> Result<ComposedDataplane, ControlPlaneError>;
}

pub struct DataplanePlan<'a> {
    pub config: &'a DataplaneConfig,
    pub vip_range: &'a VipRange,
    /// `config.dataplane_pin_dir`, or `overdrive_dataplane::DEFAULT_PIN_DIR`.
    pub pin_dir: &'a Path,
    /// `config.dataplane_cgroup_attach_path`, or
    /// `overdrive_dataplane::DEFAULT_CGROUP_ATTACH_PATH`.
    pub cgroup_attach_path: &'a Path,
}

pub struct ComposedDataplane {
    pub dataplane: Arc<dyn Dataplane>,
    pub host_ipv4: Ipv4Addr,
}

/// Production: provisions the veth pair when the configured interfaces are
/// the default names (ADR-0061 § 1), constructs `EbpfDataplane` with
/// `plan.pin_dir` and `plan.cgroup_attach_path`, runs its probe, then
/// resolves `host_ipv4` from `plan.config.client_iface`. Infallible
/// constructor; touches nothing until `compose`. On a probe `Err` the
/// constructed `EbpfDataplane` is dropped before `compose` returns (its
/// `Drop` detaches the programs and unpins the maps).
pub struct HostDataplaneComposer { /* private: integration-tests-only probe fault */ }
impl HostDataplaneComposer {
    pub const fn new() -> Self;
    /// `integration-tests` only (`#[cfg(feature = "integration-tests")]`,
    /// the gate of `EbpfDataplane::set_probe_fault` it calls; absent from
    /// production builds). The production composer, except that `compose`
    /// arms `fault` on the `EbpfDataplane` it constructs (`set_probe_fault`)
    /// before running its probe, so the probe returns `fault` and `compose`
    /// takes its real `Err` path: `DataplaneBoot(Probe { source: fault })`,
    /// the dataplane dropped. A fault on the adapter itself, not a
    /// `ServerConfig` field (NO-OVERRIDE-SEAMS): it is the real-kernel
    /// evidence for the composer's `Err` path (S-BDB-14). `compose` takes
    /// the fault out of its slot (it is consumed by the one boot), held in a
    /// `parking_lot::Mutex` (`rust.md` § "Concurrency & async"; no lock
    /// poisoning, so a taken fault can never be read back as "no fault").
    pub fn with_probe_fault(fault: DataplaneError) -> Self;
}
```

```rust
// overdrive_core::traits::mtls_enforcement — public, beside `MtlsEnforcement`
/// What the boot supplies the enforcement: values that exist only inside
/// the boot.
pub struct MtlsEnforcementDeps {
    /// The boot's `IdentityMgr` (the held SVIDs and the trust bundle).
    pub identity: Arc<dyn IdentityRead>,
    pub limits: MtlsLimits,
    /// `GUEST_NODE_PREFIX` (LEGB-DIAL).
    pub guest_prefix: Ipv4Net,
    /// The boot's `OwnerDial` (LEGS-DIAL).
    pub guest_dial: Arc<dyn GuestStreamDial>,
}

pub trait MtlsEnforcementFactory: Send + Sync {
    /// Called once per boot, at step 5, before the enforcement's probe
    /// (`run_server` probes what this returns: wire → probe → use).
    /// Postcondition: the returned enforcement dials leg S through
    /// `deps.guest_dial` for a guest-prefix target (LEGS-DIAL) and enforces
    /// `deps.limits`. Production's enforcement reads `deps.identity`; a
    /// factory may build its enforcement over another `IdentityRead` (the
    /// former `mtls_identity_override` use: a `TestPki`-rooted identity,
    /// whose SVID must still chain to its bundle, because the production
    /// relying-party verifier stays active).
    fn enforcement(&self, deps: MtlsEnforcementDeps) -> Arc<dyn MtlsEnforcement>;
}
```

`HostMtlsEnforcementFactory` (`overdrive-dataplane`, beside
`HostMtlsEnforcement`; infallible `new()`) returns
`HostMtlsEnforcement::new(deps.identity, deps.limits, deps.guest_prefix,
deps.guest_dial)`. `SimMtlsEnforcementFactory` (`overdrive-sim`) returns a
`SimMtlsEnforcement::new(deps.identity, deps.limits, deps.guest_dial)`
whose probe can be scripted to fail. `SimDataplaneComposer` (`overdrive-sim`,
beside `SimGuestDnsFactory`, which already implements a port this crate
declares, ADR-0138) returns a `SimDataplane` with the `host_ipv4` it was
built with (`Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST` for every test that injected
`SimDataplane` before, where the `lo` / `lo` or unprovisioned client
interface resolved to loopback or failed into the fallback), or a scripted
`DataplaneBoot` refusal. Their scripting methods are DISTILL's test
support. Since `compose_guest_network(ports, io, dial)`'s caller now builds
the enforcement through the factory with the same `dial`, the composition's
D-13 binding holds for every factory that meets its postcondition.

**`overdrive serve` and the CLI entry points (probe before the bundle; no
env seam).** The CLI has one entry function and production is a
call of it:

```rust
// overdrive_cli::commands::serve — public
/// `ServeArgs` gains `vsock_ports: NodeVsockPortConfig` (§ "Node vsock
/// ports"); its other fields are unchanged.
pub async fn run(args: ServeArgs) -> Result<ServeHandle, CliError>;
// = run_with_adapters(args, Arc::new(RealCgroupFs::new()),
//       |config, fs| NodeAdapters::host(config, fs,
//           Arc::new(SystemdCredsKeyring::new())))

/// Builds the `ServerConfig` from `args` (`bind`, `data_dir`,
/// `operator_config_dir` = `config_dir`, `vsock_ports`, the rest
/// `ServerConfig::new()`), then, in this order:
/// 1. probes `cgroup_fs` (ADR-0054); on `Err` emits `health.startup.refused`
///    (reason `cgroup_fs.probe`, typed `cause`, `adapter`) and returns
///    `CliError::ProbeRefused { cause }` — `adapters` is never called, so a
///    refused probe opens no store and creates no file;
/// 2. calls `adapters(&config, cgroup_fs)` — the probed handle is the one
///    the bundle carries;
/// 3. `run_server(config, bundle)`.
/// An `Err` from step 2 or 3 is mapped as `run_server`'s errors are today:
/// `ViewStoreBoot` emits `health.startup.refused` first; every error
/// becomes `CliError::Transport { endpoint, cause }`.
pub async fn run_with_adapters<F>(
    args: ServeArgs,
    cgroup_fs: Arc<dyn CgroupFs>,
    adapters: F,
) -> Result<ServeHandle, CliError>
where
    F: FnOnce(&ServerConfig, Arc<dyn CgroupFs>) -> Result<NodeAdapters, ControlPlaneError>;
```

A test passes its cgroupfs adapter and a builder that calls
`NodeAdapters::host(config, fs, Arc::new(SimKek::for_boot()))` and replaces
the fields it simulates by struct update. This keeps production's order
(probe, then open) in the test entry point too, and the builder receives
the same `&ServerConfig` the boot gets, so the bundle's paths cannot
disagree with it. `run_with_adapters` replaces `run_with_dataplane`,
`run_with_kek`, `run_with_kek_and_vm_override` and
`run_with_dataplane_and_vm_override`. It is not
feature-gated (it carries no test-only behaviour: `run` is a call of it).
The stale `run_with_kek` docstring claiming `compose_mtls =
dataplane_override.is_none()` goes with it.

**PROBE-ROOT-ENV.** The `OVERDRIVE_TEST_PROBE_ROOT`
environment variable (`serve.rs:44`, read by `build_probe_adapter`,
`serve.rs:365-371`) is removed with `build_probe_adapter` and its `mutants:
skip` comment: production `run` constructs `RealCgroupFs::new()` (probe
root `/sys/fs/cgroup`) unconditionally. `serve_probe_refusal.rs` passes a
failing cgroup adapter through `run_with_adapters` — `RealCgroupFs::new()
.with_probe_root(<a path under a regular file>)`, the real adapter's
existing probe-root constructor (`overdrive-host`, already exercised by
`overdrive-worker`'s `probe_with_custom_root.rs`), so the refusal still
comes from the real probe's `create_dir_all` failure — and asserts as
today: `CliError::ProbeRefused`, the `health.startup.refused` event with
its typed cause, no preflight event, and now also that the builder was
never called. The test loses `#[serial(env)]`, its `EnvGuard` and its
`unsafe` env mutation (how its event capture is scoped is DISTILL's test
support).

**How each removed test seam is replaced.**

| Removed | Users today | Replacement |
|---|---|---|
| `dataplane_override: Some(SimDataplane)` | the CLI `run_with_dataplane` callers and every control-plane, sim and conformance fixture listed in the DISTILL handoff (11) | `boot.dataplane = SimDataplaneComposer` built over the `SimDataplane` with `host_ipv4` `127.0.0.1` |
| `dataplane_override: None` (real dataplane) | `run_with_kek` callers; the S-BDB fixtures that configure their own interfaces | `boot.dataplane = HostDataplaneComposer::new()` (in `NodeAdapters::host`); `dataplane_pin_dir` / `dataplane_cgroup_attach_path` stay configuration |
| `dataplane_probe_fault: Some(msg)` | S-BDB-14 only (`backend_discovery_bridge/boot_composition.rs:849`) | S-BDB-14 keeps its real-kernel boot: `boot.dataplane = HostDataplaneComposer::with_probe_fault(DataplaneError::LoadFailed(msg))` (below) with the fixture's veth pair and `dataplane_pin_dir`; it asserts, as today, the `DataplaneBoot(Probe { LoadFailed(_) })` refusal, the `health.startup.refused` event with reason `dataplane.probe`, and that the `SERVICE_MAP` pin under the pin directory is gone after `run_server` returns — the evidence for `DataplaneComposer::compose`'s "nothing the call created survives an Err" on the production composer. A scripted `SimDataplaneComposer` refusal is the simulated-boot counterpart for tests that never construct a real dataplane; it carries no pin evidence. (`EbpfDataplane::set_probe_fault` alone does not cover the pin removal: its only use, `unconnected_udp_reply_hardening.rs:409`, checks that the typed error passes through intact.) |
| `mtls_probe_fault: Some(msg)` | none in the tree | a `SimMtlsEnforcementFactory` whose enforcement's probe is scripted to fail; `run_server`'s existing `mtls.probe` refusal (`MtlsBootError::Probe`) is the only refusal path. DISTILL decides whether a cell for it is added |
| `mtls_identity_override: Some(read)` | none in the tree | a test factory that builds `HostMtlsEnforcement::new(read, deps.limits, deps.guest_prefix, deps.guest_dial)` |
| `vm_override: Some(VmOverride { vmm, beacon })` | S-VM-13, S-VM-51, S-VM-75, the CLI VM lanes, `lib.rs` compose tests | `vm: VmAdapters { vmm, beacon, cgroup_accounting, capability: Required }` |
| the `ServerConfig::new` `SystemClock` default | every fixture that did not set `clock` | the fixture names its clock: `NodeAdapters::host`'s `SystemClock`, or `SimClock` |
| the stores and the CA `boot_server` opened and constructed (STORES-IN) | every boot (no test substituted them) | `boot.stores` / `boot.ca` from `NodeAdapters::host` (host bundles), or on the supplied-owner path `StoreAdapters::open(&config)` and `CaAdapters::host()`; a test may pass `SimViewStore`, `SimJournalStore` or a `CaAdapters` over `SimCaFactory` where it chooses to |
| `OVERDRIVE_TEST_PROBE_ROOT` (CLI env, PROBE-ROOT-ENV) | `serve_probe_refusal.rs` | `run_with_adapters` with a `RealCgroupFs::new().with_probe_root(..)` whose probe fails (above) |

Every in-crate test of the deleted `host_ipv4_with_override_fallback` is
deleted with it (`development.md` § "Deletion discipline"); the
`compose_vm_driver` tests take `VmAdapters`.

**Node vsock ports (PORTS-CONFIG; ADR-0218).** The
three node-global host vsock listener ports are node configuration. The
constants `BEACON_VSOCK_PORT` (1234), `GUEST_FLOW_STREAM_PORT` (1240) and
`GUEST_FLOW_CONTROL_PORT` (1243) remain only as the production defaults.

```rust
// overdrive_core::guest_transport — public
/// How one node-global host vsock listener's port is chosen.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum VsockListenPort {
    /// Bind exactly this port. Valid only above `LAST_RESERVED_PORT`
    /// (1023) and below `VMADDR_PORT_ANY` (`u32::MAX`); checked by
    /// `NodeVsockPortConfig::new`.
    Fixed(VsockPort),
    /// Bind `VMADDR_PORT_ANY` (`-1U`, `include/uapi/linux/vm_sockets.h:109
    /// @ v7.0`): the kernel picks a port above `LAST_RESERVED_PORT` from a
    /// per-network-namespace counter seeded at random
    /// (`net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c:787-788 @ v7.0`, shared with outbound
    /// auto-bind, `:251-259`): it tries up to `MAX_PORT_RETRIES` (24, `:229`)
    /// consecutive candidates and fails `EADDRNOTAVAIL` when all of them are
    /// bound (`:792-810 @ v7.0`). The caller never assumes which port it gets; it
    /// reads it back from the owner.
    KernelAssigned,
}

/// The three node-global listeners.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum NodeVsockListener { Beacon, FlowStream, FlowControl }
impl NodeVsockListener { pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; } // "beacon" | "flow_stream" | "flow_control"

/// The node's configured vsock listener ports. Validated at construction.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct NodeVsockPortConfig { /* private: beacon, flow_stream, flow_control */ }
impl NodeVsockPortConfig {
    /// Err, first match in this order: a fixed port in 0..=1023 →
    /// `Reserved`; a fixed `u32::MAX` → `PortAny`; fixed and
    /// kernel-assigned ports mixed → `Mixed`; two equal fixed ports →
    /// `Collision` (listeners in `NodeVsockListener` order).
    pub fn new(beacon: VsockListenPort, flow_stream: VsockListenPort,
               flow_control: VsockListenPort) -> Result<Self, NodeVsockPortConfigError>;
    /// All three `KernelAssigned` (what tests configure).
    pub const fn kernel_assigned() -> Self;
    pub const fn beacon(&self) -> VsockListenPort;
    pub const fn flow_stream(&self) -> VsockListenPort;
    pub const fn flow_control(&self) -> VsockListenPort;
}
/// `Fixed(1234)`, `Fixed(1240)`, `Fixed(1243)`.
impl Default for NodeVsockPortConfig { fn default() -> Self; }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum NodeVsockPortConfigError {
    #[error("vsock port {port} for the {listener} listener is in the reserved range 0-1023")]
    Reserved { listener: NodeVsockListener, port: u32 },
    #[error("vsock port 4294967295 (VMADDR_PORT_ANY) is not a fixed port for the {listener} listener; use VsockListenPort::KernelAssigned for a kernel-assigned port")]
    PortAny { listener: NodeVsockListener },
    #[error("vsock listener ports must be all fixed or all kernel-assigned")]
    Mixed,
    #[error("the {first} and {second} listeners are both configured on vsock port {port}")]
    Collision { first: NodeVsockListener, second: NodeVsockListener, port: u32 },
}

/// The ports the guest-flow owner's listeners are bound on (built by the
/// owner from its two binds' results).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct GuestFlowPorts { /* private: stream, control */ }
impl GuestFlowPorts {
    /// Err: either port in 0..=1023 or `u32::MAX` (`OutOfRange`), or the
    /// two equal (`Equal`). A bound port always passes (the kernel never
    /// assigns those values and the configuration refuses them).
    pub fn new(stream: VsockPort, control: VsockPort) -> Result<Self, GuestFlowPortsError>;
    pub const fn stream(&self) -> VsockPort;
    pub const fn control(&self) -> VsockPort;
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum GuestFlowPortsError {
    #[error("vsock port {port} is not a valid guest-flow listener port")]
    OutOfRange { port: u32 },
    #[error("the guest-flow stream and control ports are both {port}")]
    Equal { port: u32 },
}
```

- **Configuration surface (NODE-CONFIG-LOADER, user ruling 2026-10-20).** `ServerConfig.vsock_ports:
  NodeVsockPortConfig` (required field; the argument-free
  `ServerConfig::new()` sets `Default`). The value is validated when it is
  constructed (`NodeVsockPortConfig::new`), so an invalid port set cannot
  reach `run_server` and the boot has no port-validation refusal. The CLI
  carries it as `ServeArgs.vsock_ports: NodeVsockPortConfig` (a required
  field of the CLI library's argument struct, copied into
  `ServerConfig.vsock_ports` by `run_with_adapters`); the `overdrive`
  binary's `main` passes `NodeVsockPortConfig::default()`, and every CLI
  test fixture passes `NodeVsockPortConfig::kernel_assigned()` — the
  mechanism by which a CLI-driven `serve` test reaches kernel-assigned
  ports. #295 adds no configuration-file section and no command-line flag:
  `overdrive serve` reads no node configuration file today (the
  `[dataplane]` parser, `dataplane_config::parse_dataplane_section`, has no
  production caller; `serve` boots on `ServerConfig::new()`'s
  `DataplaneConfig::single_node_veth()` default). Loading the operator node
  configuration file, a `[vsock]` section included, is out of #295's scope
  and is GH #327 (ADR-0218, "Deferred to GH #327"). In #295 production
  always runs the defaults.
- **Bound-port accessors (the owners).** `BeaconIo::bind(&self, port:
  VsockListenPort) -> Result<VsockPort, io::Error>` returns the port the
  bind took (`getsockname`, `vsk->local_addr`, `af_vsock.c:824`,
  `:1133-1138 @ v7.0`); `BeaconIntake::bind(io, port)` keeps it and
  `BeaconIntake::bound_port(&self) -> VsockPort` reports it;
  `BeaconIntakeError::Bind { port: VsockListenPort, source }`. A second
  `BeaconIo::bind` call returns the first bind's port whatever `port` it
  passes (the argument is not consulted after the first bind): the beacon
  is bound once per process by `compose_vm_driver`, so a second call has no
  production caller, and a typed refusal would be an error variant for a
  state no path reaches.
  `GuestFlowIo::bind_listener(&self, listener, port: VsockListenPort) ->
  Result<VsockPort, FlowIoError>` returns the bound port (on a listener the
  seam already holds, the held socket's port; § "Repair", below);
  `SharedGuestNetworkOwner::flow_ports(&self) -> Option<GuestFlowPorts>`:
  `None` until the owner's first `converge_shared` returns `Ok`, then the
  ports its two listeners bound, constant for the process. `run_server`
  reads it once after step 9 (`unreachable!` on `None` after an `Ok`
  converge: the trait's postcondition). `ServerHandle::vsock_ports(&self)
  -> BoundVsockPorts` (public, read-only) reports both owners' values:

  ```rust
  // overdrive_control_plane — public
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub struct BoundVsockPorts {
      /// `None` when `run_server` composed no `Vm` driver (`Optional`
      /// capability absent) or on the supplied-owner path.
      pub beacon: Option<VsockPort>,
      pub flow: GuestFlowPorts,
  }
  ```

  A test that configured `kernel_assigned()` reads the ports here (or from
  the owner and intake in-crate) and never assumes a number.
- **Repair.** The owner's seam holds each listening
  socket for the process's life, apart from its accept task. What ends a
  listener's accept task in production is an `accept(2)` error that fails
  before the connection is dequeued (descriptor exhaustion,
  `include/linux/file.h:198-201 @ v7.0` through `net/socket.c:2022 @ v7.0`;
  socket allocation, `net/socket.c:1965-1967 @ v7.0`), which leaves the socket
  listening. A listener repair (`FlowListeners`, `ControlListener`) calls
  `bind_listener` on the held socket, which checks it is still listening
  (`SO_ACCEPTCONN`, `net/core/sock.c:1993-1995 @ v7.0`; set by
  `vsock_listen`, `af_vsock.c:1941 @ v7.0`) and returns its bound port with
  no close and no bind; the owner then spawns a new accept task on it. The
  port therefore never changes and no close-to-bind window exists. A
  rebind path is not built: nothing on the appliance closes or un-listens a
  held listener (the owner never shuts it, and no other actor exists), so a
  held socket found not listening is an Overdrive defect, reported as a
  failed attempt of that component's recovery (`FlowIoError`, ADR-0124's
  bound then fail-stop). The beacon listener is bound once per process.
- **Restart.** A restart reads the configuration again; kernel-assigned
  ports may differ. Every VM of the previous process is reclaimed at step 6
  before the first `assign` (NO-SURVIVE), so no running guest carries a
  previous process's ports.
- **Who uses the ports.** The VM driver writes the beacon port its intake
  bound and the flow ports carried in the allocation's
  `GuestTransportAssignment` onto the guest's kernel command line
  (GUEST-PORTS, ADR-0217; § *Guest adaptation contract*). Nothing else
  reads a port constant: the probe runner and leg S dial guest ports
  (`GUEST_INBOUND_PORT`, guest-side, unchanged), not host listeners.

**Forwarder module as a lane prerequisite (FWD-PREREQ).** `serve` never loads `ovd_fwd` (EVMOD-LOAD; on the appliance
the host image loads it). On a test host the lane's setup loads it, once per
kernel boot, as a declared prerequisite: `cargo xtask kmod-build` (with no
`--kernel-build-dir`, the module for the running kernel's
`/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build`, V-EV-BUILD) then `cargo xtask kmod-load`
(an `xtask` build/dev orchestration step; it imports no `overdrive-*`
crate). On Lima: `cargo xtask lima run -- cargo xtask kmod-build` and
`cargo xtask lima run -- cargo xtask kmod-load`; on metal the same two
steps through `cargo xtask metal run --`, listed in the lane setup of
`infra/metal/README.md` before `guest-kit-prepare`.

- **Which module is loaded.** Every Conductor
  workspace shares the one Lima VM, so "an `ovd_fwd` is loaded" does not
  mean "this workspace's `ovd_fwd` is loaded". The module's identity is its
  **version**: `MODULE_VERSION` is a digest of the whole `kmod/ovd_fwd/` tree.
  `kmod-build` hashes the tree's files (sorted relative paths and contents)
  and passes the hex digest to the module build as a define; the source uses
  it for `MODULE_VERSION` and fails to compile (`#error`) without it. The
  reason: workspaces that share the one Lima VM can have different
  `ovd_fwd` builds loaded, and a digest tells builds of different sources
  apart with no hand-kept bump to forget (ADR-0203). `MODULE_VERSION` is
  `MODULE_INFO(version, ..)` (`include/linux/module.h:277-280 @ v7.0`), so
  the field is in the module's `.modinfo`, and the loaded module exposes it as
  `/sys/module/ovd_fwd/version` (`MODINFO_ATTR(version)`,
  `kernel/module/main.c:607 @ v7.0`, listed at `:1059`; the attribute
  exists only when the field does, `:590-593`). Every check reads the
  version back from a module's `version` field. Any source edit changes the
  digest, so it is detected as stale.
- **Where the built module lives (workspace-scoped).**
  `kmod-build` writes `<workspace>/target/kmod/<kernel-release>/ovd_fwd.ko`,
  where `<workspace>` is the root of the repository checkout the command
  runs in — never the cargo target directory. The cargo target directory
  is shared: in the Lima VM `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is `~/.cargo-target-lima`
  (`infra/lima/overdrive-dev.yaml:457`) for every Conductor workspace, so a
  `.ko` there would be overwritten by whichever workspace built last. The
  workspace root is distinct per workspace (each is virtiofs-mounted at its
  own host path) and is the tree whose `kmod/ovd_fwd/` source was built. Both
  spellings — `xtask::guest_kit_prepare::forwarder_module_path` and the
  `overdrive-testing` lookup (`guest_kit.rs`, today
  `cargo_target_dir(..)`-based) — take the workspace root, not
  `cargo_target_dir`, and the S-12 drift guard covers the pair. Under
  `cargo xtask mutants` the mutated tree is a scratch copy without
  `target/`, so the wrapper exports `OVERDRIVE_KMOD_DIR` = the original
  tree's `<workspace>/target/kmod`, which the `overdrive-testing` lookup
  reads first — the precedent of `OVERDRIVE_BPF_OBJECT` (`testing.md`
  § "Mutation testing"). This is test support and xtask only; no production
  crate reads it.
- **`kmod-load` (MODULE-REFCOUNT).** It loads this workspace's
  `<workspace>/target/kmod/<uname -r>/ovd_fwd.ko`. Load and unload are the
