  kernel's own atomic calls, and their return codes are the verdicts
  (`.claude/rules/rust.md`, "Check-and-act must be atomic"). The one
  separate read, `initstate` after an `EBUSY`, only classifies the `EBUSY`: it
  tells a module that finished unloading (back to step 1) from one still
  present. Any `EBUSY` on a present module is busy/retry, with no retry of
  its own:
  1. **Load.** It calls `finit_module`. `Ok` means the module was absent
     and is now loaded: done.
  2. **Compare.** On `EEXIST` it compares `/sys/module/ovd_fwd/version`
     with the `.ko`'s `version` modinfo field. Equal is success.
  3. **Unload a stale module.** When the two differ, it calls
     `delete_module("ovd_fwd", O_NONBLOCK)`. The kernel's reference check is
     the idle test.
     - `0`: the stale module was idle and is now gone. Return to step 1;
       the `.ko` is now loaded.
     - `ENOENT`: another process unloaded it first. Return to step 1.
     - `EWOULDBLOCK` / `EAGAIN` (references held, `kernel/module/main.c:744-751
       @ v7.0`), or any `EBUSY` while `/sys/module/ovd_fwd/initstate`
       (`kernel/module/main.c:964-986 @ v7.0`) reads `coming`, `going` or
       `live` (`:810-816`): the module is busy. `kmod-load` fails with "`ovd_fwd` is busy; retry when its
       holders are gone", naming both versions and the holder class:
       - **an open forwarder context:** a process with `/dev/ovd_fwd` open,
         found among `/proc/<pid>/fd` links and named by pid and `comm` (a
         `serve` test of this or another workspace);
       - **socket references still being freed, or a context reference not
         visible in `/proc`:** `/sys/module/ovd_fwd/refcnt`
         (`kernel/module/main.c:889-896 @ v7.0`) is above zero while no
         process has the device open in an fd table. These are pairs or
         watches of a released context whose free work has not run yet,
         which clear within an RCU grace period; or an open file of the
         device held outside every fd table (a descriptor in flight in an
         `SCM_RIGHTS` message, an io_uring fixed file), which clears when
         its holder drops it. If they persist, a socket that had a ULP
         installed after attach holds a reference for the boot (rule 5),
         and the module has logged that socket as a defect.
     - `EBUSY` and the `initstate` read fails with `ENOENT`: a `going`
       module finished unloading between the two calls. The module is gone;
       return to step 1.

     `kmod-load` never names a reboot as the remedy.

  Steps 1–3 are bounded to two passes. If the second `finit_module` finds
  another workspace's build loaded again, `kmod-load` reports busy/retry
  with the versions it read. It is never softened by `--busy-ok` and never
  names a reboot.

  With `--busy-ok` (the hooks' form, below) a busy stale module (the
  `EWOULDBLOCK` / `EBUSY` case) prints the same message and exits 0, leaving the stale verdict to the `serve`
  fixtures. Every other outcome is the same as the strict form.
  **Cost:** workspaces whose `ovd_fwd` sources differ still contend on the
  one Lima VM. Each workspace's setup reloads its own build whenever the
  module is idle, so a run can find the other workspace's build loaded
  between two of its `serve` tests and fail a later fixture as stale.
  Rerunning `kmod-load` is the remedy. No run of any workspace is
  interrupted.
- **The fixture's check.** Before it boots, a `serve` test's fixture reads
  `/sys/module/ovd_fwd/version` and the `version` modinfo field of the
  `.ko` built from its own workspace (the path above). The outcomes:
  - no built `.ko`: a missing prerequisite naming `cargo xtask kmod-build`;
  - no loaded module: a missing prerequisite naming `cargo xtask kmod-load`;
  - unequal values: the stale prerequisite. Its remedy is `cargo xtask
    kmod-load`, which reloads the module once it is idle.

  So a
  missing or foreign module is never read as a boot regression, and a test
  runs only against a loaded module whose `version` equals that of the
  module built from its own workspace's source (two workspaces whose
  trees are byte-identical share a loaded module).
- **The lanes that run it.** Every `serve` test, VM or not, runs the real
  phase-1 forwarder probe. CI runs the two steps (strict `kmod-load`) in
  every job that runs `serve` tests (the integration and mutation lanes);
  each CI job boots a fresh VM, so stale is not reachable there. The
  lefthook hooks run them too, in the lenient form: pre-push gains a
  `kmod-prepare` command, ordered before `nextest` (pre-push runs its
  commands in order), whose script runs `cargo xtask lima run -- cargo
  xtask kmod-build` then `cargo xtask lima run -- cargo xtask kmod-load
  --busy-ok`; pre-commit's `nextest-affected` script runs the same two
  commands before its `nextest` invocation (pre-commit runs its commands in
  parallel, so a separate command would race it). The hooks therefore load
  an absent module (so a push never fails ~75 `serve` tests on a missing
  prerequisite), reload a stale idle one after any edit under
  `kmod/ovd_fwd/`, and never fail on a busy one: the stale
  verdict is then the fixtures', which fail only when a `serve` test
  actually runs, so a commit or push whose affected set has no `serve`
  test is not blocked by another workspace's module.

A non-VM `serve` test still converges the node-global gateway `/32` route
on `lo` and writes the node-global `overdrive-mtls` table
(`start_shared_owner`), so its test binary stays a whole-binary member of
`host-kernel-shared` (`testing.md` § "Node-global kernel state requires a
catch-all nextest group"); PORTS-CONFIG removes only the vsock-port
collision. Every out-of-crate `serve` test binds the real flow and control
listeners (`GuestFlowAdapter::host()`), and the real beacon whenever it
passes `VsockBeaconIo` and its `Vm` driver is composed; with
`NodeVsockPortConfig::kernel_assigned()` none of them collides with another
`serve` on the host, whichever workspace runs it.

**`overdrive deploy` → `Action::StartAllocation`:**

1. `pool.assign(alloc, listen_ports, flow_ports)` → `GuestTransportAssignment`
   (`workload_addr`, `gateway`, CID = `GUEST_CID_BASE + lease offset`,
   `LaunchToken`, and the owner's bound `GuestFlowPorts` the action shim read
   at boot, PORTS-CONFIG): next-fit from the cursor (M-9), the launch token drawn with
   the lease (ATTR-TOKEN); the existing exhaustion refusal when no offset is
   free. Within one `serve` process lease uniqueness gives CID uniqueness
   (`CidUnique`).
2. `provision` → CID Provisioned.
3. `spec.transport = Some(..)`.
4. `driver.start`: `Vmm::create(config, cid)`: CH with
   `--vsock cid=…,backend=vhost-kernel` and the transport token (carrying
   `launch=` and, GUEST-PORTS / ADR-0217, `beacon=` from the driver's
   intake and `stream=` / `control=` from the assignment); the VMM opens `/dev/vhost-vsock` itself (ADR-0146). No
   Overdrive process holds a copy of that file, so its last close at VMM exit
   runs the orphan sweep and resets every host flow of the guest (V-30
   Q2c/Q2d). A device the VMM cannot open makes it exit before READY: the
   existing pre-READY VMM-exit start failure.
5. Guest: network configuration, control session opened (`ControlOpen` with
   the launch token; the owner claims the session only on a matching token),
   READY (carrying the launch token; the driver accepts it only on a match).
6. Running row written.
7. `mtls_lifecycle.start_alloc`: inbound elements, capability →
   intercept-live (`managed_guest_ips` does not exist; the guest-prefix rules
   use the constant prefix, ADR-0172).
8. `activate_guest_network` under `exec.claim_release()`; retried on
   `QuiescenceLatched` / `ControlSessionPending`.
9. `driver.release_for_exit_emission` (EXEC).

**Teardown, reclaim and stop:** retire → `driver.stop` (VMM exits; the last
close of its vhost-vsock file resets the guest's host flows) →
`mtls_lifecycle.stop_alloc` → `provisioner.teardown` → `pool.release`
(ADR-0133). `driver.stop` returns after the launch's beacon session and its
claim are released, and `teardown` after the control session and its claim
are, so neither claim outlives the lease (ATTR-TOKEN, § *Control session*).
Each ends its launch's live token in the same per-CID step, so a connection
of the launch read afterwards takes no claim (ATTR-LIVE-CLAIM). The lease is
released only after the VMM has exited and `teardown` returned `Ok`
(`LeaseOutlivesVmm`), so a CID is never leased again while a VMM or a flow
of the earlier lease exists.

**Guest reset (RESET-EXIT, ADR-0182).** The vendored fork routes the guest
reset to the VMM exit path. A guest PID-1 crash under `panic=1` or a triple
fault ends the VMM with no guest `EXIT` record; the driver sees a pre- or
post-READY VMM exit and classifies it a failure by the absence of that
record, never by the exit status (§ *VMM backend contract*), and the
lifecycle charges the restart budget; the guest's host flows are reset by
the orphan sweep. The same CID and launch token never run a second boot.
In the step that observes the VMM exit the driver ends the launch's
liveness and releases its beacon claim (D-UP-9, approved 2026-10-14;
§ *Beacon intake*), so the claim does not wait for `driver.stop`.

**Shutdown** (graceful or not) never removes the gateway route or the
constant firewall rules: they stay while `serve` is down; the next boot
converges them. The release of the host's forwarder context aborts every
host pair and the host's file teardown closes every host flow vsock; each
guest forwarder classifies the `0x3` as an abort and the guest keeps running
until the next boot's reclamation.

#### [REF] Ownership of descriptors and kernel objects

| Object | Created by | Held by | Removed by | Crate (class) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/dev/vhost-vsock` file of one VM (CID = `GUEST_CID_BASE + lease offset`) | the VMM (fork, `backend=vhost-kernel`, its Landlock rule for the device) | the VMM only; no Overdrive process holds a copy | VMM exit (last close: the orphan sweep resets the guest's host flows) | launched by `overdrive-host` (adapter-host) |
| vhost worker | the VMM (`VHOST_SET_OWNER`) | VMM | VMM exit | launched by `overdrive-host` (adapter-host) |
| Beacon listener (`CID_ANY`, the node beacon port; default 1234, ADR-0218) and sessions | VM driver | VM driver | driver shutdown; session end | `overdrive-worker` (adapter-host) |
| Flow listener and control listener (the node stream and control ports; defaults 1240 and 1243, ADR-0218), control sessions | owner `converge_shared` (boot step 9 only; a repair re-spawns accept on the held listener, § *Composition*, "Repair") | owner, for the process's life | owner shutdown (listeners); teardown (sessions) | `overdrive-control-plane` (adapter-host) |
| Host vsock of a host-opened flow | owner, in `GuestStreamDial::dial` | the owner until `Paired`; then the `GuestStream` holder (leg-S, the probe runner); the owner keeps the flow's registration and the watch | the holder's drop (which aborts the watch first); an owner abort leaves the socket untouched (WATCH-ABORT) and the socket closes at the holder's drop; only the context's release shuts it | `overdrive-control-plane`; held in `overdrive-worker` |
| Host pair sockets | owner | owner (as `PairSocket` handles of `GuestFlowIo`, DG-3; the seam adapter holds the descriptors) | owner, after the pair's end record | `overdrive-control-plane` |
| Host forwarder context (`/dev/ovd_fwd`, `O_CLOEXEC`) and its pairs and watches | `KernelFlowForwarder::open` at boot `converge_shared` (and the `Forwarder` repair) | owner, by value (EVMOD-CTL) | context release: drop or process exit, which aborts every live pair and watch | `overdrive-fwd` (adapter-host), held by `overdrive-control-plane` |
| Host forwarder module `ovd_fwd` | the host image at boot (EVMOD-LOAD); on a development host, `cargo xtask kmod-load` | the kernel, with one module reference per open context and per hooked socket (EVMOD-LIFE, MODULE-REFCOUNT) | on the appliance never (no module unloading; machine reboot); on a development host `kmod-load`'s reload of a stale idle module, refused while any reference is held | `kmod/ovd_fwd` (no crate) |
| Gateway `local` route on `lo` (GW-LOCAL) | owner boot `converge_shared` only | kernel (node infrastructure; persists across `serve` restarts) | never removed; never written at runtime; converged at every boot (H-4) | via `overdrive-netlink` |
| Owner egress socket mark + host-internal reject rule (D26); guest-prefix output reject / prerouting drop of traffic not diverted to leg-C (ADR-0172) | `mtls_worker.start_shared_owner()` with the other constant rules | kernel | converged with the constant rule set (ADR-0125) | via `overdrive-netlink` (nft) |
| Guest capture programs and links, the guest forwarder context and its pairs, pair sockets, dummy device, rule | `overdrive-init` | `overdrive-init` | guest exit | `overdrive-init` (binary) |
| Guest forwarder module `ovd_fwd` (the guest kit's) | `overdrive-init`, `finit_module` (EVMOD-LOAD, EVMOD-GUEST-KIT) | the guest kernel, with its module references (EVMOD-LIFE) | never unloaded (guest exit) | guest kit |

#### [REF] Lifecycle

- **Allocation (owner, per CID):** `Provisioned → Active → Retiring → absent`.
  `activate` is the only Provisioned → Active edge. Quiescence latches node
  admission; it does not change per-CID state.
- **Control session (per CID):** `Absent ⇄ Live`; loss aborts every flow of
  the CID, host-opened ones included (DG-5-F).
- **Flow:** `Requested → Paired → Closed`; a Paired flow's directions are
  the forwarder's (`pair_state`); `Closed` (clean or aborted) is terminal and
  is reached at the pair's end record or the owner's abort.
- **Host-opened flow:** `AwaitingReply → Paired (held by the GuestStream) →
  Closed`; a refusal before registration creates nothing.
- **Quiescence (node):** a hold count; admission is latched `Quiesced` iff
  the count is above zero; a leaked hold keeps it above zero until the
  supervisor's fail-stop.
- **Drain to zero (teardown):** close the control session → abort every
  flow, dial and stream of the CID (each pair's or watch's `abort`, its
  record queued before it returns) → close sockets → read back the owner's
  table and the forwarder's inventory (no live pair or watch of the CID) →
  return `Ok` → lease released after the VMM has exited. A failure to abort or remove a flow returns `Err` and
  teardown is retried, the lease staying Retiring.
- **Crash / restart (D19):** owner death releases the forwarder context,
  which aborts every host pair, and closes every host flow; guests receive
  0x3 and abort their flows; remote far ends the dying owner
  holds are reset through `SO_LINGER{1,0}` (H-5). The gateway route
  (GW-LOCAL) and the constant firewall rules survive. Next boot:
  boot reclamation kills every VM the new process does not supervise
  (NO-SURVIVE, #312); `sweep_stale` verifies no process-scoped object
  remains; `start_shared_owner` converges the rules (failure refuses boot,
  ADR-0184); `converge_shared` opens and probes a forwarder context and
  converges the gateway route.
  No process-scoped object is adopted.
- **Guest reset:** the VMM exits (RESET-EXIT); the allocation sees a VMM
  exit; the lease is released after it.

#### [REF] Typed error taxonomy and who branches

The forwarder's errors are `ForwarderError` (§ *[REF] Driven port —
`FlowForwarder`*), carried by `GuestNetworkError` through one `#[from]`
variant `Forwarder { source: ForwarderError }` (never flattened to
`Internal`, `.claude/rules/rust.md`); the forwarder's per-flow outcomes are
§ *[REF] vsock data path*, "Failure projection". The guest's setup errors,
`GuestTransportSetupError` with the three EVMOD-GUEST-KIT variants and
`Forwarder { source: ForwarderError }`, are pinned in § *Guest adaptation
contract*; `KernelRelease` is an `overdrive-init`-private newtype.

**`GuestNetworkError`** (ADR-0122, revalidated):

- Kept: `PoolExhausted`, `ExecGateNotBootClosed`, `AdmissionCapReached`,
  `LeaseRetiring`, `Netlink { operation, source }`, `Io { operation, source }`,
  `PostconditionMismatch { operation, expected, observed }`,
  `ScratchCleanupIncomplete`, `StartupProbeCleanup`.
- `Tcx { … }` is removed; the forwarder's errors are `Forwarder { #[from]
  source: ForwarderError }`.
- Added: `Wire { operation, source: FlowWireError }`,
  `FdBudget { required: u64, available: u64 }`,
  `OwnerCgroupPlacement { owner: PathBuf, attach_point: PathBuf }` (D24: the
  owner's cgroup is not at or below the `connect4` attach path; the root
  cgroup never is),
  `GuestPrefixOverlapsNodeAddress { prefix: Ipv4Net, interface:
  InterfaceIndex, address: Ipv4Net }` (D8-PREFIX-CFG: the node's network
  configuration, which the operator owns, places an interface address
  inside the guest prefix; checked by `probe_startup` before any boot
  effect; startup refuses, naming the address and the interface),
  `GuestPrefixOverlapsVipRange { prefix: Ipv4Net, vip_range: Ipv4Net }`
  (D8-PREFIX-VIP: a range of the configured service VIP range, which the
  operator owns, overlaps the guest prefix; checked by `probe_startup`
  before any boot effect; startup refuses, naming the range).

**`GuestDialError`** (§ *Driving port — guest stream dial*) is returned to
the dialer only; it never enters `GuestNetworkError`.

**`SharedGuestNetworkFailStopCause`** (core) gains `LeakedQuiescenceHold`
(QHOLD: a hold of the owner's ledger was dropped unredeemed — an Overdrive
defect, D-UP-3) and `ForeignQuiescenceHold` (PD-1, approved 2026-10-14:
`restore` returned `QuiescenceRestoreError::ForeignHold`, a composition
defect). The enum has no `as_str` labels and gains none: the fail-stop
request carries the typed cause, its consumers match on the variant, and no
consumer needs a string label.

**`ParseError`** (core, TOML ingress) gains `ProbeCountExceeded { count,
max }` (D-UP-12, approved 2026-10-14; § *Core vocabulary*).

**`GuestNetworkOperation`:** `PoolAssign`, `StartupProbe`, `SharedAudit`,
`CleanupComplement`, `ForwarderOpen`, `ForwarderInventory`,
`FlowListenerBind`, `ControlListenerBind`, `ControlSessionAccept`,
`LocalRouteConverge` (the gateway route, GW-LOCAL), `LocalDeliveryCheck`,
`OwnerPlacementCheck`, `GuestPrefixConfigCheck`, `FlowAccept`,
`FlowRequestRead`, `ControlMessageWrite`, `HostPeerConnect`,
`GuestInboundConnect`, `PairAttach`, `PairAbort`, `ForwardingActivate`,
`ForwardingQuiesce`, `ForwardingRestore`.

**`GuestNetworkFact`:** `Forwarder { generation: ForwarderGeneration, live_pairs: u32, live_watches: u32 }`,
`FlowListener { port: VsockPort, bound: bool }`,
`ControlSession { alloc, cid, live: bool }`,
`AllocationForwarding { alloc, cid, pairs: u32 }`,
`CleanupComplement`,
`ScratchCleanupComplement`, `StartupProbe { stage: ForwarderProbeStage }`,
`SharedComponent`.

**`SharedGuestNetworkComponent`:** `Forwarder` (the context: an `Io` failure,
or the owner's flow table against the forwarder's `inventory()` —
Overdrive's own drift), `FlowListeners`, `ControlListener`, `LegF`, `LegC`,
`IpRules`, `IpSets`, `Dns`, `Supervisor`. The gateway route is not a
component: boot writes it and nothing changes it at runtime. Absent:
`Bridge`, `TcxLink`, `EndpointMap`, `CounterMap`, `BpffsPin`, `BridgeGuard`,
`LocalRoute`, `SockOpsLink`, `DrainCounterLink`, `UnframeLink`,
`IntakeListeners`.

| Failure | Typed form | Who branches | Projection |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fd budget / owner placement / node address inside the guest prefix / VIP range overlapping the guest prefix / the forwarder probe (boot step 1, phase 1, D-8) | `FdBudget`, `OwnerCgroupPlacement`, `GuestPrefixOverlapsNodeAddress`, `GuestPrefixOverlapsVipRange`, `Forwarder { source: ForwarderError::DeviceAbsent | AbiMismatch | Probe | ProbeMismatch | .. }` | `run_server` | `health.startup.refused`, reason `guest_network.probe`; no boot effect has run and no forwarder context is left open |
| Boot step 8: the shared mTLS table write fails (QHOLD, ADR-0184) | `ControlPlaneError::MtlsBoot(MtlsBootError::SharedOwner { source })` | `run_server` | `health.startup.refused`, reason `mtls.shared_owner`; boot refuses before forwarding opens; the supervised restart retries |
| Boot `converge_shared` fails (the serving forwarder context's open or probe, listener bind, gateway route) | `GuestNetworkError::Forwarder { source: ForwarderError::Probe | ProbeMismatch | DeviceAbsent | AbiMismatch | .. }`, `Io { FlowListenerBind | ControlListenerBind }`, `Netlink { LocalRouteConverge }` | `run_server` | `health.startup.refused`, reason `guest_network.converge` |
| A guest-opened connection whose first record carries another launch's token (ATTR-TOKEN) | `guest_flow.connection_closed_unattributed { cause: StaleLaunch }` (owner); `vm_beacon.connection_closed_unattributed { cause: StaleLaunch }` (VM driver) | owner / VM driver | Connection closed; no control message, no refusal, no claim, no effect on any allocation |
| A pair or watch ends (EVMOD-REC) | `ForwardEnd { outcome }` | owner / `overdrive-init` | § *[REF] vsock data path*, "Failure projection" |
| The guest's forwarder module is missing, built for another kernel release, or refused by `finit_module` (EVMOD-GUEST-KIT) | `GuestTransportSetupError::ForwarderModuleMissing { path }`, `ForwarderModuleRelease { module, kernel }`, `ForwarderModuleLoad { source }` | `overdrive-init` → VM driver | Guest console names the cause (both releases for a mismatch, and that kernel and root filesystem must come from one guest kit); guest exits before READY; existing start failure |
| An attach or watch refused because a half has ended (EVMOD-ATTACH-END) | `ForwarderError::HalfEnded { side, errno }` | owner / `overdrive-init` | Flow abort by § *[REF] vsock data path*, "Owner response to an ended half at attach"; counted `forwarder_attach_ended` |
| A forwarder context `Io` failure or an inventory drift | `GuestNetworkError::Forwarder { source }` / `SharedGuestNetworkAuditError { component: Forwarder, .. }` | supervisor | ADR-0124 recovery of `Forwarder` in the order of "Context lifetime and owner failure" |
| An attach or watch refused for an owner defect (`UnsupportedSocket`, `UpperLayerProtocol`, `NotConnected`, `AlreadyHooked`, `BufferTooSmall`) | `ForwarderError::*` | owner / `overdrive-init` | Flow refused (`Refused(IntakeUnavailable)` host-side), sockets closed, `guest_flow.attach_refused` |
| An end record with cause `Unclassified` (EVMOD-END) | `AbortCause::Unclassified { side }` | owner / `overdrive-init` | Flow aborted (`PeerReset`); `guest_flow.unclassified_end` at `warn` (an alarm) |
| `Paired` / `Refused` / `TimedOut` / `Abort` for an unknown or closed flow (U-5) | `guest_flow.control_discarded` | owner / `overdrive-init` | Discarded; no reply (SLOT-ABORT excepted) |
| Host platform client dial refused or failed (INB-1) | `GuestDialError` | leg-S / VM probe runner | leg-S: leg C reset, `MtlsEnforcementError::GuestDial`; probe: `Capacity` (node flow slots; a probe dial is exempt from the allocation quota) / `Quiesced` → no sample (no `ProbeResultRow`, no run number consumed, event `probe.not_sampled` with `reason` `node_capacity` / `quiesced`; PROBE-NOSAMPLE, PROBE-RUN-COUNT, PROBE-NOSAMPLE-EVENT), every other variant → unhealthy with the variant as detail. No allocation state changes |
| Host-internal destination | `FlowRefusal::HostInternal` | owner | Flow-local refusal; counted |
| Spec declares a listener port in the reserved guest range (D25) | `ParseError::ListenerPortReserved` (TOML ingress) / `AggregateError::Validation { field: "listeners[].port" }` (API ingress) | `overdrive deploy` / the submit handler | Deploy refused before any intent write; nothing is placed |
| Spec's startup, readiness and liveness probes together exceed `GUEST_PROBE_SLOTS` (D-UP-12) | `ParseError::ProbeCountExceeded` (TOML ingress) / `AggregateError::Validation { field: "probes" }` (API ingress) | `overdrive deploy` / the submit handler | Deploy refused before any intent write; nothing is placed |
| Leaked quiescence hold (QHOLD; an Overdrive defect, D-UP-3) | `SharedGuestNetworkFailStopCause::LeakedQuiescenceHold` | supervisor | ADR-0124 typed fail-stop of `serve` at the next audit tick; forwarding stays quiesced until then. A hold dropped by the supervisor's shutdown cancellation is not classified (no audit tick follows; the shutdown exit is unchanged) |
| `restore` of a hold another ledger issued (D-UP-4, PD-1) | `QuiescenceRestoreError::ForeignHold` → `SharedGuestNetworkFailStopCause::ForeignQuiescenceHold` | supervisor | ADR-0124 typed fail-stop of `serve` at once; the owner's count and latch unchanged (fail-closed) |
| Beacon listener bind fails at composition (DG-4) | `BeaconIntakeError::Bind` | `compose_vm_driver` | `health.startup.refused`, reason `vm_driver.beacon_bind` |
| vsock device setup fails at launch (the VMM cannot open `/dev/vhost-vsock`) | existing pre-READY VMM-exit start failure | VM driver → shim | Non-terminal start failure; retire, then release the lease after the VMM exited |
| Guest reset (RESET-EXIT) | existing pre-READY `VmGuestExitUnreported` or post-READY `WorkloadCrashedImmediately` (no guest `EXIT` record; the VMM's exit status is not read) | VM driver → lifecycle | A failure; the restart budget is charged |
| Guest setup fails before READY | `GuestTransportSetupError` (guest console) → existing "guest exited before READY" | VM driver → shim | Existing start failure |
| Activation: quiesced / control session pending | `ForwardingActivation::{QuiescenceLatched, ControlSessionPending}` | shim | Retry under the EXEC claim (ADR-0131 budget) |
| Activation of an unknown or Retiring CID | `GuestNetworkError::PostconditionMismatch { operation: ForwardingActivate, .. }` | shim | Activation-failure projection (`WorkloadNetnsProvisionFailed`, stage `guest_network_activate`) |
| Forwarded registration fails | any `MtlsInterceptInstallError` | owner | `Refused(IntakeUnavailable)` |
| Audit finds a damaged component | `SharedGuestNetworkAuditError{component, source}` | supervisor | ADR-0124 recovery under a hold / fail-stop |
| Per-flow refusal or failure | `FlowRefusal`, `FlowCloseCause`, `ForwardOutcome` | **nobody in the allocation lifecycle** | Flow-local only |
| Malformed request / control message | `FlowWireError` | owner / `overdrive-init` | `Refused(Malformed)` / session closed |
| Oversize datagrams and pair outcomes | `ForwarderInventory` (`dgram_oversize`, `aborted`, `unclassified_eof`) | audit (observability) | Counters only |

Per-flow failures and dial results never delay, advance or revoke allocation
`Running`, READY, intercept-live or Service `Stable`.

#### [REF] Restart decision — one predicate for `WorkloadLifecycle` and its accessor (RESTART-SSOT, GH #324)

**Defect (current code).** `WorkloadLifecycle` is the single restart
authority (ADR-0087). It places a successor for a failed allocation while
`attempts < RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING` (`overdrive-reconcilers/src/workload_lifecycle.rs:1116-1119`),
and always when the failed row is a platform reclamation
(`is_platform_reclaimed`, ADR-0083) or a new desired generation is pending
(`view.observed_generation < desired.generation`, ADR-0073). The rule is
spelled out three times inside the reconciler (`:369`, which also omits the
generation exemption; `:425-431`; `:1116-1119`). The runtime's accessor
`ReconcilerRuntime::restart_status_for_alloc`
(`overdrive-control-plane/src/reconciler_runtime.rs:460-470`) computes a
fourth copy: `attempts + 1 < RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING`, which is false at
`attempts = RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING − 1` while the reconciler restarts, and
it ignores both exemptions. Its boundary unit test
(`reconciler_runtime.rs:1815-1846`) pins the wrong value. The operator's
`overdrive deploy` stream (`streaming.rs:397-414`, the Job stream) renders
its `.1` as `will_restart`; for a Job that value is wrong in a second way:
the reconciler finalizes a Job's first natural exit, a crash included,
before its restart branch is reached (`workload_lifecycle.rs:1035-1057`),
so no Job crash is ever placed again, while the accessor reports
`will_restart: true` for the first four. The fix lands
in #295 (user, 2026-10-18: fix the accessor, do not work around it) and
closes [GH #324](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/324).

**The predicate (`overdrive-reconcilers`, crate root, beside
`RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING`).**

```rust
/// Whether `WorkloadLifecycle` places a successor for a failed allocation.
#[must_use]
pub const fn restart_decision(
    attempts: u32,
    platform_reclaimed: bool,
    generation_replacement: bool,
) -> bool;
```

- **Postcondition.** Returns
  `attempts < RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING || platform_reclaimed || generation_replacement`.
  `true`: the reconciler places a successor for this allocation (the
  backoff deadline and the guest-attachment cap may delay that placement;
  they never change the decision). `false`: the restart budget is spent and
  the reconciler finalizes the allocation (`FinalizeFailed` with
  `BackoffExhausted` or, for a liveness kill,
  `ServiceFailed { LivenessProbeFailed }`, ADR-0087 D4).
- **Inputs, as the reconciler reads them.** `attempts` is
  `view.restart_counts[failed.alloc_id]`, 0 when absent (the restarts
  already charged to the lineage; a reclaim or a generation replacement
  carries it to the successor unchanged, `:1214-1221`).
  `platform_reclaimed` is `overdrive_core::is_platform_reclaimed(failed)`.
  `generation_replacement` is `view.observed_generation < desired.generation`.
- **Edge cases.** `attempts = RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING − 1` → `true` (the
  value #324 got wrong). `attempts ≥ RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING` → `false`
  unless an exemption holds. `u32::MAX` attempts with either exemption →
  `true`. Whether a row is a restart candidate at all (a natural Job exit,
  an operator stop with no new generation, a stop intent) is not this
  predicate's question; those branches are decided before it, unchanged.
- **Call sites — the only places the ceiling is compared.** Each of the
  reconciler's three ceiling checks (`:369`, `:426`, `:1116`) is replaced by
  a call to `restart_decision` with that site's row and view, the `:369`
  next-wake site passing its `restart_pending` as `generation_replacement`
  (so the next-wake boundary reports a restart for a lineage a pending
  generation replaces).
  `restart_after_failure` below calls it. No other expression in
  `overdrive-reconcilers` or `overdrive-control-plane` compares a value
  against `RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING`; the DELIVER reviewer rejects one.

**The failed-allocation decision (`overdrive-reconcilers::workload_lifecycle`,
re-exported at the crate root).**

```rust
/// Whether `WorkloadLifecycle` places a successor (`RestartAllocation`) for
/// the current allocation `failed` of a workload of kind `kind`.
#[must_use]
pub fn restart_after_failure(
    kind: WorkloadKind,
    run_desired: bool,
    failed: &AllocStatusRow,
    attempts: u32,
    generation_replacement: bool,
) -> bool;
```

- **Meaning.** `true` exactly when one `WorkloadLifecycle::reconcile` over
  this workload, with `failed` as its current allocation (the module's
  `current_alloc`, the numerically greatest attempt suffix), past the backoff
  deadline and below the guest-attachment cap, emits
  `RestartAllocation { alloc_id: failed.alloc_id, .. }`. Backoff, the cap and
  attempt-suffix exhaustion (`next_allocation_attempt` returning `None`,
  `:1204-1206`, unreachable below `u32::MAX` placements) delay a `true`
  decision; they never change it. A `false` decision means the reconciler
  places no successor *of `failed`* on this row: it finalizes it, waits for
  it, keeps it stopped, or (clause 4) places a fresh lineage with
  `StartAllocation`, which carries no restart count of `failed`.
- **Inputs, as the reconciler reads them.** `run_desired` is
  `desired.job.is_some() && !desired.desired_to_stop`; `attempts` and
  `generation_replacement` as for `restart_decision`.
- **Postcondition (total), in the reconciler's own order (`reconcile_inner`,
  `workload_lifecycle.rs:787-1239`).** Every clause names the line whose
  branch it equals.
  1. `false` when `!run_desired`: the Stop branch (`:787-810`) and the
     Absent branch (`:839-855`) emit only `StopAllocation` for `Running`
     rows, for every row class.
  2. `false` when `failed.state == AllocState::Draining`: the reconciler
     returns before any placement while the current row is `Draining`
     (`:953-955`), with or without a pending generation; it decides once
     the row reaches `Terminated` or `Failed`. (`is_restartable` matches
     `Draining`, `:1606-1610`, so this clause is checked first — clause 4
     alone would wrongly reach clause 5.)
  3. `false` when `kind == WorkloadKind::Job` and `failed` is a natural exit
     (`is_natural_exit`: `Terminated` or `Failed`, not intentionally
     stopped, not platform-reclaimed, `:1614-1633`). This equals both Job
     branches: the terminal-claim fence (`:882-895`, a natural exit already
     finalized `Completed` / `Failed`, no pending generation) and the
     natural-exit finalize (`:1035-1057`, which has no generation guard).
  4. `false` when `failed` is not a restart candidate: neither
     `is_restartable(failed)` nor `generation_replacement &&
     is_operator_stopped(failed)` (the filter at `:1090-1092`). This covers
     a `Running` row (`:930-943`: nothing, or under a pending generation a
     `StopAllocation`, not a successor), a `Pending` or `Suspended` row, an
     operator stop with no pending generation (the veto at `:1013-1015`),
     and a `SystemGc` stop (excluded from `active_allocs_vec`, `:908-909`;
     a resubmit gets a fresh `StartAllocation` at `:1241-1344`).
  5. otherwise
     `restart_decision(attempts, is_platform_reclaimed(failed), generation_replacement)`
     (`:1093-1239`): `false` emits `FinalizeFailed` once (or nothing when
     the row already carries `BackoffExhausted` or
     `ServiceFailed { LivenessProbeFailed }`, `:1130-1140`); `true` places
     the successor.
- **Where the accessor's single row equals the reconciler's whole row
  set.** The reconciler reads every row of the workload; the decision takes
  only the current one. Two reconciler checks read other rows, and neither
  can differ in a production lineage: (a) "any active row is `Running`"
  (`:930-931`) — a successor is minted only when no active row is `Running`
  (both placement branches sit behind `:932`), and a row reaches `Running`
  only as its own allocation's start, so a non-current row is never
  `Running` while the current one is not; (b) "any active row is a Job
  natural exit" (`:1035-1037`) — a Job's natural exit finalizes the Job
  and fences its lineage (`:882-895`), so every non-current row of a Job
  lineage is intentionally stopped or platform-reclaimed, neither of which
  is a natural exit. Regression obligation 4 generates lineages of that
  shape.
- **One source per clause.** The reconciler's branches call the same
  `is_natural_exit`, `is_restartable`, `is_operator_stopped` and
  `restart_decision` this function calls; clause 2 and the reconciler's
  `:953` guard both read `AllocState::Draining` on the current row. No
  clause is spelled a second time, and `restart_after_failure` is defined
  in `workload_lifecycle.rs` beside the branches it mirrors.
- **Edge cases.** A platform-reclaimed Job row is not a natural exit and is
  placed again (DD-1). A Job's operator stop under a pending generation is
  placed again (ADR-0073), as the reconciler does. A Service row already
  finalized `BackoffExhausted` is a restart candidate: `false` without a
  pending generation, `true` with one (a `Redeploy` of an exhausted Service
  places it again and the successor keeps the count, `:1214-1221`).

**The accessor (`overdrive-control-plane::reconciler_runtime`, replaces the
current signature, single cut).**

```rust
impl ReconcilerRuntime {
    /// `(attempt_index, will_restart)` for the failed allocation `failed`.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn restart_status_for_alloc(
        &self,
        target: &TargetResource,
        kind: WorkloadKind,
        run_desired: bool,
        failed: &AllocStatusRow,
        desired_generation: u64,
    ) -> (u32, bool);

    /// The 1-indexed attempt number of `alloc_id` in its lineage.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn attempt_index_for_alloc(
        &self,
        target: &TargetResource,
        alloc_id: &AllocationId,
    ) -> u32;
}
```

- **Preconditions.** `kind` is the workload's kind as the reconciler's
  `hydrate_desired` reads it (`WorkloadLifecycleState.workload_kind`);
  `run_desired` is `hydrate_desired`'s `job.is_some() &&
  !desired_to_stop`; `failed` is the workload's current allocation's latest
  observed row (the LWW winner the reconciler's `hydrate_actual` reads into
  `WorkloadLifecycleState.allocations`, selected by `current_alloc`, below);
  `desired_generation` is the value at
  `workloads/<id>/generation` decoded by `TxnOp::decode_counter` (absent →
  0), which `hydrate_desired` reads into `WorkloadLifecycleState.generation`.
  These are the inputs the decision needs: the Job rule needs the kind,
  clause 1 the intent, `platform_reclaimed`, the `Draining` check and the
  candidate filter come from the row, `generation_replacement` from the
  generation and the view.
- **Postconditions.** With the `WorkloadLifecycle` view of `target` (the
  default view when none is held — `attempts` 0, `observed_generation` 0),
  `attempts = view.restart_counts[failed.alloc_id]` (0 when absent):
  `.0 = attempts.saturating_add(1)`;
  `.1 = restart_after_failure(kind, run_desired, failed, attempts, view.observed_generation < desired_generation)`.
  `attempt_index_for_alloc` returns
  `view.restart_counts[alloc_id].saturating_add(1)`, 1 when absent — the
  current accessor's `.0`, for callers that render only the index. It reads
  any allocation the view has issued, including a successor whose dispatch
  has written no row yet (the view is written through before dispatch).
- **The current allocation.** The module's existing private
  `current_alloc(allocs: &[&AllocStatusRow]) -> Option<&AllocStatusRow>`
  (`workload_lifecycle.rs:1406-1412`, the numerically greatest
  `mint_alloc_id` suffix) becomes `pub` and is re-exported at the crate root
  under the same name, so a caller selects `failed` with the reconciler's own
  rule. One definition; no copy.
- **Consistency point.** Both read the in-memory view the last tick wrote
  through (fsync first, `development.md` § "Reconciler I/O", step 7 → 8);
  neither reads a store.
- **Callers.** `streaming.rs:399` (the Job stream's `AttemptFailed` event)
  calls `restart_status_for_alloc` with `WorkloadKind::Job`, the
  workload's `run_desired`, the event allocation's row and the workload's
  generation; how the streaming handler
  reads them is internal,
  under `.claude/rules/rust.md` § "Errors" (a failed read is not absorbed
  into a default). `streaming.rs:439`, `:493` and `:545` render only the
  index and call `attempt_index_for_alloc`. The `cid_lease` conformance
  driver projects `retry` from `restart_status_for_alloc` (QPROJ-2W).
- **Wire and display.** `JobSubmitEvent::AttemptFailed { will_restart, .. }`
  keeps its shape; only its value becomes the reconciler's decision.

**Regression obligations (DISTILL; the RESTART-SSOT step of § *Roadmap
impact*).**

1. Ceiling boundary: a failed row at `attempts = RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING − 1`
   — `restart_decision` and `restart_status_for_alloc(..).1` are `true`, and
   one `WorkloadLifecycle::reconcile` past the backoff deadline emits
   `RestartAllocation`; at `attempts = RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING` both are
   `false` and `reconcile` emits `FinalizeFailed`. The current boundary test
   (`reconciler_runtime.rs:1815-1846`), which pins the defect, is replaced.
2. Platform-reclaim exemption: a row with `StoppedBy::PlatformReclaimed` at
   `attempts ≥ RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING` — `true` from both, and `reconcile`
   emits `RestartAllocation` with the successor's count unchanged.
3. Generation-replacement exemption: `observed_generation <
   desired.generation` at `attempts ≥ RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING` — `true` from
   both, and `reconcile` places the successor without waiting for backoff.
4. Agreement property (proptest over all three `WorkloadKind` variants,
   `Job`, `Service` and `Schedule` (`workload_spec.rs:323-331`), `attempts ∈ 0..=2 ×
   CEILING`, the generation flag, `run_desired` — including a stop intent
   and an absent aggregate — and a current row of every class: crash-class
   (`Terminated` / `Failed` with an exit), start-rejected (`Failed`),
   liveness-killed, platform-reclaimed, operator-stopped, `SystemGc`-stopped,
   `Draining`, `Running`, `Pending`, a Job natural exit, and a row already
   finalized `BackoffExhausted`; earlier rows of the lineage drawn from
   intentionally stopped and platform-reclaimed rows, the shape the
   "single row" paragraph above proves production produces):
   `restart_status_for_alloc(..).1` is `true` exactly when one `reconcile`
   past the backoff deadline and below the attachment cap emits
   `RestartAllocation { alloc_id: failed.alloc_id, .. }`. A mutation of the
   predicate's `<`, of either `||` arm, of the `Draining` clause, of the
   `run_desired` clause or of the Job clause fails it. Every kind is
   generated with every row class, so a mutation of clause 3's
   `kind == Job` into `kind != Service` (equal on `Job` and `Service`) fails
   on a `Schedule` row.
5. Job stream: a Job's crash produces `AttemptFailed { will_restart: false }`
   followed by its terminal `Failed` (today `true`), through the in-process
   `overdrive deploy` stream of the production handler.

**Defect RESTART-GEN-CRASH — a generation replacement placed but not yet
started is lost at a `serve` crash. Not fixed in #295: it is
[GH #325](https://github.com/overdrive-sh/overdrive/issues/325) (user
ruling 2026-10-18, § *Approval record*). No test or model run against
production has shown it yet.** When the reconciler places a successor for a pending
generation it stamps `observed_generation = desired.generation` in the
emitting tick's view (`workload_lifecycle.rs:1211-1213`; the fresh-placement
branch likewise, `:1340-1342`), and the runtime writes that view through
before it dispatches the action (`development.md` § "Reconciler I/O", step
7 before step 9). The dispatch writes the successor's first row only when
the successor starts or fails: `RestartAllocation` provisions the successor
before it touches the predecessor (`action_shim/mod.rs:2707-2716`), and no
dispatch path writes a `Pending` row (no `AllocState::Pending` write in
`overdrive-control-plane/src`). A `serve` crash in that window — a real
Overdrive failure (CLAUDE.md § "Overdrive runs on its own appliance OS":
"a crash mid-sequence") — leaves the predecessor as the current row and the
generation already observed. Then:
- `Redeploy` of a **stopped** workload: the current row is the operator stop,
  `restart_pending` is false, and the operator-stop veto (`:1013-1015`)
  places nothing, forever (until another `overdrive workload restart`);
- `Redeploy` of an **exhausted** Service: the current row is
  `BackoffExhausted` at the ceiling, no exemption holds, and the idempotency
  guard (`:1130-1140`) places nothing, forever.
The operator's restart was acknowledged (`RestartWorkloadResponse`) and is
silently dropped — the `reconcilers.md` "marker stamped on the emit path"
shape (the stamp records "placement emitted", the docstring and the veto
treat it as "placement happened"). A crash-class or platform-reclaimed
predecessor is unaffected: its row is still a restart candidate after the
crash, so the reconciler places it again with the same count.

What #295 does with it (user ruling 2026-10-18): nothing in production. #295
pins no contract for the fix and changes no View field; the shape of the fix
is #325's to design. The `cid_lease` model keeps the behaviour #325 is to
deliver (a `Redeploy`'s placement leased at a `serve` crash is placed again)
as the run `RedeployLeasedAtServeCrashIsPlacedAgain` and keeps today's
behaviour as the hazard `crashLosesPlacedGeneration`, both **pending #325**:
neither is checked against production in #295. The run is replayed only on
the separate main `lease_conf_325`, by a `#[quint_test]` marked
`#[ignore = "pending #325"]`; the conformance main `lease_conf_ok` excludes
the window (§ *Per-module projection and action map*, `cid_lease` item 9),
so no randomized trace replays a state production handles differently.
When #325 lands, that change removes the exclusion, merges `lease_conf_325`
into `lease_conf_ok` and activates the test.

#### Sim counterparts (adapter-sim)

- `SimSharedGuestNetworkOwner` implements the owner traits above; scripts
  `ForwardingActivation` (all three), `ForwardingQuiescence`,
  `ForwardingRestore` (`Reopened` / `StillQuiesced`) over a hold count with
  a leaked-hold count, audit damage, teardown failures and the
  `OwnerCgroupPlacement` startup refusal; records calls in order. It issues
  and redeems its holds through its own `QuiescenceLedger` (D-UP-4, approved
  2026-10-14): the ledger is public in `overdrive-control-plane` (PD-2,
  approved 2026-10-14), so the sim,
  which is another crate, needs no test-only constructor; a hold it issued
  never reopens a production owner (that owner's `restore` returns
  `ForeignHold`). Its leaked-hold count is its ledger's `leaked()`.
- `SimGuestStreamDial` (new, `overdrive-sim`, `pub`): implements
  `GuestStreamDial` for consumers outside the owner crate (leg-S, the VM
  probe runner). Per target it scripts `Ok` with an in-memory `GuestStream`
  whose guest side the test drives (bytes, a `HalfClose` end, an `Abort`
  end, an owner abort), or any `GuestDialError` variant, immediately or
  after a delay, and may script a different outcome per `DialPurpose`; it
  records every dial in order with its `target` and `purpose` and reports
  stream drops and `shutdown_write` calls. It names only `overdrive-core` types (rule 1 of
  the sim-placement rule), so it unifies in every crate.
- `SimVmm` scripts pre-READY exits (no new `VmmProbeError` variant, DG-1)
  and a guest reset, which ends the simulated VMM (RESET-EXIT); `create`
  takes the CID; the simulated device is held by the VMM process until it
  exits.
- The sim mTLS intercept models `register_forwarded_outbound` with its
  intercept-live precondition and atomic claim, and the shared table as the
  two states one nft transaction leaves, absent or complete, with a scripted
  failed table write that leaves the state as it was — at boot step 8 it
  refuses boot (ADR-0184).
- The owner seam's sim (`SimGuestFlowIo`, DG-3, source-local) delivers
  accepted guest-opened connections with a peer CID and a first record (so
  a seeded run can deliver a connection a previous launch of the same CID
  left queued, P-37), scripts vsock connect outcomes for dials (`ENODEV`,
  `ECONNRESET`), pairing replies (`Paired`, `Refused { errno }`,
  `TimedOut { errno }`). The forwarder's kernel facts — a pair's end record
  and its cause, the attach refusals, and the context's `inventory()` — are
  arbitrated by `SimFlowForwarder` (§ *[REF] Driven port — `FlowForwarder`*;
  Tier-3 pair: the adapter-equivalence scenario of that section, and R5-57
  for node flow-slot occupancy, D-UP-17).
- **Accept order in the seam sims (D-UP-19).** The kernel's accept queues
  are FIFO; the sims' are not. `SimGuestFlowIo`, `SimBeaconIo` and
  `SimGuestOwnerIo` hold each pending connection — with its peer CID and
  its buffered first record — outside the listener's accept queue and
  release it into the queue at the step that accepts it, so the queue
  never holds two connections when an accept runs and the driver chooses
  the accept order. Contract: a sim delivers queued connections to the
  owner in any order the driver chooses, FIFO included, and every
  per-connection fact it reports on accept (peer CID, the buffered first
  record or none, a dead peer's failure at the first I/O, K-A2′) is the
  fact the kernel reports for that connection. Why that is sound: the owner
  observes no connection before accepting it — listener readiness says only
  that some connection is queued, and no per-connection fact is readable
  before `accept` returns it — so the owner's behaviour on an accepted
  connection depends only on the accept sequence and those per-connection
  facts. The kernel's FIFO sequence is one of the sequences the sim can
  produce, so every property checked over the sim's orders holds over the
  kernel's. The sim also produces orders the kernel cannot (a connection a
  dead launch queued, accepted after one the next launch queued later); no
  invariant depends on accept order, so those orders only add coverage.
  Sim and kernel are kept consistent on the per-connection facts by R5-59
  (accept-path adapter equivalence: the host seams against a scripted guest
  peer in a microVM, the guest seam in a microVM) and, for the dead-peer facts,
  R5-41 (the K-A2′ shape through `serve`, microVM).
- The sim pool is the production pool (the pool is not a port), with
  seeded entropy (`SimEntropy`) for launch tokens (ATTR-TOKEN).
- `SimMtlsResolve` (existing) drives the owner's single resolution, including
  scripted VIP-branch outcomes (D24a).
- `SimGuestAttachmentView` is the attachment-view sim.
- `SimFlowForwarder` is the forwarder port's sim. The owner's flow state
  machine runs under seeded simulation through `GuestFlowIo` (DG-3) and
  `FlowForwarder`, printing the seed and retaining the triggering sequence.
  No test hand-installs a production effect.
- **Conformance arbiters.** The sim read surfaces the Quint conformance
  drivers project from, each paired with its Tier-3 scenario, are pinned in
  § *Conformance observation surface and action map*.

#### [REF] Conformance observation surface and action map

**Status: approved by the user 2026-10-09** (QPROJ-1 to QPROJ-7; rulings
U-QP-1 and U-QP-2). The projections of the INB-1, R2-END, R2-DRAIN,
CID-NOCLAIM, RESET-EXIT, QHOLD and NO-SURVIVE contracts are recorded under
those decision ids, approved by the user 2026-10-11; the forwarder's
projection (QPROJ-8) under the EVMOD-* ids, approved 2026-10-17. Driver
placement is backed by
`docs/research/testing/conformance-driver-placement-research.md`.

**Why.** `.claude/rules/design.md` § "Pin the observable projection the
conformance driver reads" requires, for every Quint module the design
carries, the production owner's accessor that yields each compared variable
and the driving port each action maps onto. This section pins both for the
six state-machine modules of `specs/quint/guest-flow-owner/`
(`owner_flows`, `fwd_pair`, `flow_quota`, `cid_lease`, `quiescence`,
`udp_slots`); the projection of `specs/quint/probe-count/` is
pinned with its model (§ *Formal protocol model* → *Probe-run counting*).
Every variable of every module is either
projected from a pinned source below or classified (ghost, model-only,
model-internal, stimulus, hazard-only). No driver projects from its own
bookkeeping, a constant, or a sim field not pinned as an arbiter. The ADRs
are unchanged by this section: every item below is an interface contract of
a decision they record.

**Owner field (S-7; orchestrator lint ruling 2026-10-19, per `testing.md`
§ "Per-driver checklist" as written).** Every driver holds its production
owner — or the production composition containing it — directly, as a
non-`Option` field set at construction (checklist item 2). A read marked
`// conformance-lint: sim-arbiter-ok` may feed a projected variable when the
arbiter is named below, but it never stands in for the owner field and
never makes a driver without one pass item 2. The `overdrive-init` drivers
(`fwd_pair` guest side, `udp_slots`, `owner_flows` guest side) therefore
hold `GuestFlowOwner` directly; a `GuestProcess`-style wrapper may remain as
test support for the guest process's lifecycle beside that field, never as
the only path to the owner. A guest owner's death is driven as the host
owner's is (S-3): the seam's process exit, then the owner's runtime
dropped, the owner field kept and never called or projected again. While
`GuestFlowOwner::new` is a DELIVER step-5 RED scaffold such a driver
panics at construction, which is its RED; it carries
`#[ignore = "pending DELIVER step 5"]` until then (`testing.md` § "RED
acceptance scaffolds and activation").

##### QPROJ-1 — Where each driver runs and what may feed `State`

- **Placement follows the owner.** A module, or one side of a module, whose
  protocol belongs to one production owner is replayed by a source-local
  conformance module in that owner's crate — `#[cfg(all(test, feature =
  "integration-tests"))] mod quint_conformance` beside the owner — that
  replays traces through quint-connect, references the spec in place
  (`specs/quint/guest-flow-owner/<module>.qnt`), and runs through `cargo
  xtask lima run --`. The owners' socket effects sit behind private effect
  seams (DG-3, DG-5; `overdrive-init` is a binary with no library target),
  and the forwarder behind the core `FlowForwarder` port, so only a
  source-local driver can build the production
  owner over its seam's sim implementation without widening any cross-crate
  API (precedent: D-295-DISTILL-12A, `with_allocation_io` is `#[cfg(test)]`
  and source-local).

  | Module (conformance main, `REC = true`) | Owner under test | Driver crate | Played by the driver (stimulus) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `cid_lease` (`lease_conf_ok`) | `GuestAddressPool` with the VM driver's launch and stop, and boot reclamation (`vm_reclamation_boot::converge`) | `overdrive-control-plane` | placement intent, the VMM processes (`SimVmm`: exit, guest reset, orphans of the previous process), `serve` crash and restart |
  | `owner_flows` (`flows_conf`) — host side | host guest-flow owner (`HostSharedGuestNetworkOwner`) and the dial (`GuestStreamDial`) | `overdrive-control-plane` | the guest (connections, first records, its replies), VM start / exit, the dialer's calls |
  | `owner_flows` (`flows_conf`) — guest side (`gf`) | guest flow owner of `overdrive-init` (`GuestFlowOwner`, driven in-process) | `overdrive-init` | the host owner (V_h, its request, `Abort`, its close), the guest application |
  | `owner_flows` (`flows_beacon_conf`) | `VmDriver` beacon intake | `overdrive-worker` | the guest, lease and owner lifecycle (`Provision`, `Teardown`, `Release`) |
  | `fwd_pair` (`pair_conf`) — host side / guest side | each owner over `SimFlowForwarder` | `overdrive-control-plane` / `overdrive-init` | the other owner, both far ends, the far readers, the kernel's per-half socket facts (through `SimFlowForwarder`) |
  | `flow_quota` (`quota_conf`) | host guest-flow owner's admission and flow end | `overdrive-control-plane` | the guests of three allocations, far ends, drain completion |
  | `udp_slots` (`slots_conf`) — guest side / host side | guest slot pool / host datagram associations | `overdrive-init` / `overdrive-control-plane` | the other side, applications |
  | `quiescence` (`quiesce_conf`) | host owner with the runtime shared-network supervisor | `overdrive-control-plane` | component damage, crash, restart; boot step 8 through `SimMtlsIntercept` |
  | `probe_count` (`probe_streak_conf`, `specs/quint/probe-count/`) | the probe runner and `ServiceLifecycle` under the reconciler runtime | `overdrive-control-plane` | probe outcomes (the Sim `GuestStreamDial`), looks, the driver port's stop outcome, clock steps |

  Each driver names exactly one main — the one in its row — in
  `Config::nondet`, every `#[quint_test]` and every `#[quint_run]`. The
  other mains of a module (`flows_ok`, `flows_one`, `flows_sess`,
  `flows_beacon`, the `fwd_pair` model-checking mains, `quota_ok`,
  `lease_ok`, `lease_live`, `lease_five`, `quiesce_ok`, `quiesce_live`,
  `slots_ok`, `slots_live`, `probe_streak` and every hazard main) are
  model-checking mains: they record no step, so no driver replays them. The
  conformance mains' configurations cover them: `flows_conf` is `core2` (the
  core with two host-opened flows, on which every core and `core2` run
  replays), `quiesce_conf` joins `quiesce_ok`'s crash with `quiesce_live`'s
  unbounded repair failures, `lease_conf_ok` is the five offsets of the
  `/29` test pool, and the others equal their model-checking instance.

  A two-owner module is replayed once per side. The side under test is
  projected; the other side's actions are stimulus taken from the trace,
  and its outputs are consumed by the driver as the trace's next step
  dictates. A driver never re-implements an owner's rules.
- **Trace modes and the step record (D-UP-1, approved 2026-10-14; spike
  QT1, `spike/findings-qt1-conf-step.md`, WORKS).** The pinned
  `quint-connect` 0.1.2 generates `#[quint_test]` traces with `quint test …
  --out-itf` and no `--mbt` (`src/trace/generator/test.rs:25-43`), so those
  traces carry no `mbt::actionTaken` / `mbt::nondetPicks`; a driver whose
  `Config::nondet` is empty fails every named run with ``Missing
  `mbt::actionTaken` variable in the trace`` (`src/driver/step.rs:24-75`).
  Every stateful module that is a conformance target therefore declares
  `conf_step`, a sum-typed, model-only, write-only state variable: its tag
  is the exact action name a driver's `switch!` arm matches, its value the
  record of the action's parameters by parameter name (the unit value for
  none); a wrapper that only picks a parameter records the action it takes.
  No guard, effect or property reads it. It changes only on a conformance
  main — one recording main per driver, so one per module except
  `owner_flows`, which has `flows_conf` (host and guest drivers) and
  `flows_beacon_conf` (the VM driver), because the beacon instance enables
  only the VM driver's actions (D-UP-20; PD-6, approved 2026-10-14); on
  every other main — model-checking,
  liveness, hazard — it keeps its initial value, so no TLC or Apalache check
  carries it in its state space, and, being write-only, it leaves every
  other variable's behaviours identical on both kinds of main. Every driver:
  - sets `Config { nondet: &["<main>::<module>::conf_step"], .. }` — one
    path element, the fully qualified ITF variable name, where `<main>` is
    the conformance main and `<module>` the module that declares
    `conf_step` (the mains import modules with `.*`; an `as X` import would
    put the alias in that place, and no main uses one);
  - names that same main in every `#[quint_test(main = ..)]` and
    `#[quint_run(main = ..)]` (a driver pointed at a non-recording main
    decodes every step as the initial action and diverges at step 1, QT1);
  - projects its `State` by matching the spec's qualified variable names
    (`<main>::<module>::<var>`), not bare names: the ITF state record is
    keyed by qualified names, so a plain field-named deserialisation fails
    and `Config::state` cannot select several qualified variables (QT1
    caveat 1);
  - pins each named run with `#[quint_test(.., max_samples = 1)]`: a named
    run is deterministic, so each further sample regenerates the same trace
    (QT1 caveat 4); `#[quint_run]` keeps a sample count and the seed printed
    on failure.
  Alternatives rejected: re-expressing the named runs through `step` (adds
  no `mbt::*` under the 0.1.2 generator); forking `quint-connect` to pass
  `--mbt` to `quint test` (unverified support, a second maintenance
  surface); `#[quint_run]` alone (testing.md requires both trace modes);
  recording on every main (measured: `owner-flows-safety-tlc` grows from
  11.3 M to over 22.9 M distinct states). This applies to both subsystems,
  `specs/quint/guest-flow-owner/` and `specs/quint/probe-count/`.
- **Sources of `State`.** Exactly three: (a) a public read-only owner
  observation accessor named in QPROJ-2 to QPROJ-6; (b) a sim arbiter's
  read accessor for a driven-port fact the owner does not hold, each paired
  with a Tier-3 item (QPROJ-7); (c) the caller's own observation of a
  driving-port call it issued — that it is still pending, or what it
  returned — only where a table below names it. Never a driver-owned map of
  owner state, a constant, or a sim field not pinned as an arbiter.
- **Identity relabelling.** Model identifiers (allocation `a`, generation
  `gen`, connection `c` / `b`, flow `f` / `h` / `i`, slot `s`, socket `k`,
  destination `d`, offset `o`, component `C1` / `C2`) map to production
  identities (`AllocationId`, `LaunchToken`, connection keys, `FlowId`,
  socket cookie, `SocketAddrV4`, lease CID, `SharedGuestNetworkComponent`)
  through a bijection the driver fixes when it creates the stimulus or first
  sees the production identity (for a dial: the host-origin `FlowId` the
  owner writes in the `TcpAccept` request the seam holds). The bijection
  relabels; it is never a source of state. A production identity with no
  pre-image fails the comparison.
- **Variables not compared.** Every variable a table below does not compare
  is one of: *ghost* — it exists to state an invariant and is a function of
  the compared trajectory and the action taken, so a divergence surfaces in
  the compared variables or in the action's enabledness; *model-only* — an
  in-flight wire message set or another fact no participant holds as state
  (a control message written and not yet consumed, a vsock operation in
  flight); the driver plays its delivery as the next step of the trace, so
  a message production did not write fails the step that releases it;
  *model-internal* — state inside one atomic production operation, compared
  only at states where that operation is not in progress; *stimulus* —
  state of what the driver plays (applications, far ends, placement intent,
  the peer owner, fault budgets); *hazard-only* — constant in the design
  instances.
- **Linearization and stepping.** Every owner observation accessor returns a
  state between two steps of each CID's serialized order (M-7) and of
  quiescence, never mid-step. A seam's sim implementation holds each effect
  the owner issues (connect, bind, listen, an attach, watch or abort on the
  forwarder, a close) and each input event (accept, readiness, an end
  record on the forwarder context) until the driver releases it, and
  reports when every owner task waiting on it is
  parked with nothing undelivered; the driver compares only then. Those
  stepping methods are test support (DISTILL's); the read accessors below are
  the contract.
- **Visibility.** The owner observation accessors (QPROJ-2 to QPROJ-6) are
  real, read-only production methods: `pub` (`pub(crate)` inside the
  `overdrive-init` binary), compiled in every build, each returning an owned
  value snapshot, mutating nothing and holding no lock across the return.
  They are interface contracts like any other public method and are
  documented as such — QPROJ-2 and QPROJ-3 in § *Owner and provisioner*,
  QPROJ-5 in § *Guest adaptation contract*, QPROJ-4 and QPROJ-6 below — with
  the discipline of
  `.claude/rules/development.md` § "Trait definitions specify behavior"
  (preconditions, postconditions, edge cases, the consistency point the
  snapshot reflects, observable invariants). Sim arbiters of public driven
  ports are `pub` in `overdrive-sim` (adapter-sim test API, precedent
  D-295-DISTILL-10). Sim arbiters behind private seams are source-local
  `#[cfg(test)]` beside the seam in the owner's crate.
- **Sim placement and the crate graph.** `overdrive-sim` has normal
  dependencies on `overdrive-control-plane` and `overdrive-worker`, and both
  owner crates take `overdrive-sim` as a dev-dependency. A test module inside
  an owner crate is therefore a second copy of that crate next to the one
  `overdrive-sim` links, so a sim type that names the *owner crate's own*
  types does not unify with the production owner under test. The rule: (1) a
  sim that implements an `overdrive-core` trait and names only
  `overdrive-core` types lives in `overdrive-sim` and unifies in every crate;
  (2) a sim of a trait defined in a third crate that is a normal dependency
  of both the owner and `overdrive-sim` unifies (Cargo links one copy of that
  crate); (3) a sim of an owner's own I/O seam, or one whose signatures name
  the owner crate's types, lives in the owner crate beside the seam. QPROJ-7
  assigns every sim by this rule. `overdrive-sim`'s adapters that name
  `overdrive-control-plane` types (`SimMtlsInterceptLifecycle`, the guest
  network, guest DNS, view-store and journal adapters) are not used by any
  in-crate driver. No workspace crate depends on `overdrive-init`, so no
  second copy arises there; the binary's guest owner uses its own synchronous
  `GuestClock` and `SimGuestClock` (DG-5), so it takes no `overdrive-sim`
  dev-dependency.
- **Rejected.** (1) Drivers in `tests/conformance` over `#[doc(hidden)] pub`
  seams with public socket sims: widens the owner's cross-crate surface
  into a socket and BPF fault framework
  (C-295-G's rejected alternative), and cannot reach `overdrive-init`. (2) A
  `#[cfg(feature = "integration-tests")] pub mod` harness in each owner
  crate, like `e18_test_support`: still exports a test-only owner
  constructor over a private seam, a production-crate hook surface, for no
  gain over the source-local module. (3) Projection from driver
  bookkeeping: compares the model with itself. (4) `#[cfg(test)]
  pub(crate)` observation accessors: a hook compiled only into tests, outside
  the documented contract, that production code cannot share and that no
  contract review covers.
- **Consequence for DISTILL.** Every guest-flow-owner conformance driver
  lives in its owner's crate; none lives in `tests/conformance`
  (`.claude/rules/testing.md` § "Root-level system conformance"). Action
  names in each driver's `switch!` are the spec's, exactly.

##### QPROJ-2 — Pool lease observation (`GuestAddressPool`, `overdrive-control-plane`)

The accessor is `GuestAddressPool::lease_observation() ->
GuestLeaseObservation { next_fit, leases: BTreeMap<AllocationId,
GuestLeaseView { cid, state, launch }> }`, pinned with its contract
(preconditions, postconditions, consistency point, edge cases, invariants) in
§ *Owner and provisioner*, "Conformance observation (owner accessors)". The
projection relies on three of its properties: `leases` holds exactly the
Admitted and Retiring leases at one pool-lock acquisition, never inside an
`assign` walk; at most one lease per CID (CID-NOCLAIM: lease uniqueness is CID
uniqueness within one `serve` process); a pool built after a `serve` restart
reports no lease of the previous process (NO-SURVIVE).

Consumers: `cid_lease` (`lease`, `cursor`, `al`); `alloc` (`Retiring` /
`Absent`) and `gen` of `owner_flows`.

##### QPROJ-2W — Workload placement decision (`WorkloadLifecycle`, T-5)

`WorkloadLifecycle` (`overdrive-reconcilers`) is the production owner of
whether a workload is placed, kept stopped or placed again; the pool only
holds the lease the reconciler's actions take and return. The `cid_lease`
driver reads the reconciler's decision inputs through the reconciler's own
production hydration and the runtime's restart-budget accessor, and drives
placement only through the runtime's convergence tick. Every surface below
exists in the tree except the restart-budget accessor's signature, which
RESTART-SSOT pins (§ *Restart decision*, GH #324).

| Surface | Signature | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Driving port: one convergence tick | `reconciler_runtime::run_convergence_tick_with_guest_network_provisioner_for_test(state: &AppState, reconciler_name: &ReconcilerName, target: &TargetResource, now: Instant, tick_n: u64, deadline: Instant, provisioner: &dyn GuestNetworkProvisioner) -> Result<(), ConvergenceError>` (`reconciler_runtime.rs:1421`) | the production tick (`run_convergence_tick_inner`: hydrate, `reconcile`, view write-through, `action_shim::dispatch`) with only the accepted guest-network driven port substituted; `reconciler_name` = `workload_lifecycle_canonical_name()`, `target` = the workload's `workloads/<id>` target |
| Driving port: operator verbs | `handlers::submit_workload`, `handlers::stop_workload`, `handlers::restart_workload` (`handlers.rs:264`, `:842`, `:941`), each called in-process with `State(app_state)` | the intent writes `overdrive deploy`, `overdrive job stop` and `overdrive workload restart` make, with every side effect of the handler (listener-fact eviction, enqueue) |
| Accessor: desired placement | `reconciler_runtime::hydrate_desired_for_test(reconciler: &AnyReconciler, target: &TargetResource, state: &AppState) -> Result<AnyState, ConvergenceError>` (`reconciler_runtime.rs:1727`), the `WorkloadLifecycle` arm projected to `WorkloadLifecycleState { job, desired_to_stop, generation, .. }` (`overdrive-reconcilers/src/workload_lifecycle.rs:1818`) | the same `AnyReconciler::hydrate_desired` dispatch the tick runs, over the composition's `HydrationContext`: the reconciler's own reading of the stop sentinel and generation |
| Accessor: observed allocation rows | `reconciler_runtime::hydrate_actual_for_test(reconciler: &AnyReconciler, target: &TargetResource, state: &AppState) -> Result<AnyState, ConvergenceError>` (`reconciler_runtime.rs:1745`), the `WorkloadLifecycle` arm's `allocations: BTreeMap<AllocationId, AllocStatusRow>` | the reconciler's own reading of the latest row of each allocation; supplies the `failed` row of the restart-budget accessor |
| Accessor: restart decision | `ReconcilerRuntime::restart_status_for_alloc(target: &TargetResource, kind: WorkloadKind, run_desired: bool, failed: &AllocStatusRow, desired_generation: u64) -> (u32, bool)` (RESTART-SSOT; replaces the current `(target, alloc)` signature at `reconciler_runtime.rs:460`) | `.1` = `restart_after_failure(..)`, the reconciler's own decision procedure: whether it places a successor of the current allocation |
| Accessor: restart count | `ReconcilerRuntime::attempt_index_for_alloc(target: &TargetResource, alloc_id: &AllocationId) -> u32` (RESTART-SSOT) | `view.restart_counts[alloc_id] + 1` (1 when absent), including an issued allocation with no row yet |
| Accessor: current allocation | `overdrive_reconcilers::current_alloc(allocs: &[&AllocStatusRow]) -> Option<&AllocStatusRow>` (RESTART-SSOT: the existing private fn at `workload_lifecycle.rs:1406` made `pub`, re-exported) | the reconciler's own choice of the current allocation among `hydrate_actual`'s rows |

Contract the projection relies on: `hydrate_desired` reads intent at one
`IntentStore` snapshot and returns `job: None` only when the workload's
aggregate is absent; `desired_to_stop` is true exactly while the stop
sentinel exists; `generation` is the value the reconciler compares with its
view's `observed_generation`; `hydrate_actual`'s `allocations` holds the
latest row of each allocation of the workload; `restart_status_for_alloc`
reads the in-memory view the last tick wrote through, so it is read only
after the step's tick returned, and it decides with `restart_after_failure`
and `restart_decision`, the functions the reconciler's own branches call, so
the projected `retry` and the reconciler's placement cannot disagree on any
input. The
composition registers `WorkloadLifecycle` in its `ReconcilerRuntime` and
spawns neither `spawn_convergence_loop` nor `spawn_interest_router`: every
tick is a driver step, so no wakeup the model does not show places a
workload.

Consumer: `cid_lease` (`al(a).st` `wait` / `done` / `failed`,
`al(a).retry`, `al(a).ex`, `att`).

##### QPROJ-3 — Host guest-flow owner observation (`HostSharedGuestNetworkOwner`, `overdrive-control-plane`)

The accessor is `HostSharedGuestNetworkOwner::flow_observation() ->
GuestOwnerObservation`, pinned with its types and contract in § *Owner and
provisioner*, "Conformance observation (owner accessors)". It is the only
host owner accessor the drivers read; every fact below is a field path of
its value:

| Fact | Field path |
|---|---|
| QHOLD hold count, leaked holds, admission latch | `quiescence_holds`, `leaked_quiescence_holds`, `admission` |
| listener tasks | `flow_listeners_running` |
| per CID: allocation, launch token, phase | `cids[cid].alloc`, `.launch`, `.phase` (`Provisioned` / `Active` / `Retiring`) |
| control session holder, unread control connections | `cids[cid].session`, `.unread` |
| guest-opened TCP flows (U-1), their phase and pair | `cids[cid].guest_flows[key]`: `GuestFlowPhase`; once `Paired { pair }`, the pair's per-direction state is `FlowForwarder::pair_state(pair)` (QPROJ-8) |
| host-opened flows (INB-1 dials and open `GuestStream`s) and their purpose | `cids[cid].dials[flow]`: `DialObservation { purpose, phase }`, `phase` = `DialPhase::AwaitingReply` / `Paired { watch, guest_end, host_shut }` (D-UP-17); an entry leaves only at the owner's abort, the stream's drop, or a typed error or dropped future before `Paired`, never at the watch record's read (D-3) |
| datagram associations | `cids[cid].datagrams[flow]`: `AssociationObservation { phase }`, `phase` = `AwaitingPaired` / `Paired { pair }` |
| flows counted against the allocation's quota, half-closed included; a flow's release | `cids[cid].held_flows`: `guest_flows` + `datagrams` + the `Relay` dials (D-UP-17); a flow's release is its absence from its table and the drop of `held_flows` in the dispatch that read its end record (EVMOD-AB) |
| node flow-slot occupancy | not an owner fact: the forwarder's, read from `FlowForwarder::inventory()` of the `SimFlowForwarder` arbiter (QPROJ-8, D-UP-17); the oracle of the node-cap scenario is the public refusal (`GuestDialError::Capacity`, `FlowRefusal::Capacity`). No owner accessor is added |

The projection relies on the contract's edge cases: a flow, dial,
association or CID the owner no longer holds is absent; a dial that returned
a typed error is absent (a typed refusal changes no owner state, INB-1); a
CID in `Retiring` stays until `teardown` returns `Ok`, after which the pool
(QPROJ-2) reports `Retiring` until `release`.

##### QPROJ-4 — VM driver beacon observation (`VmDriver`, `overdrive-worker`)

```rust
// overdrive_worker — public, read-only, compiled in production
impl VmDriver {
    pub fn beacon_observation(&self) -> BeaconObservation;
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct BeaconObservation {
    /// CIDs with a live launch (started, not stopped) and its token.
    pub live: BTreeMap<GuestCid, LaunchToken>,
    /// Holder of each CID's beacon claim (READY released).
    pub claims: BTreeMap<GuestCid, BeaconConnKey>,
    /// Accepted beacon connections whose first line is not yet read.
    pub unread: BTreeSet<BeaconConnKey>,
}

// `BeaconConnKey` is `overdrive_core::vm::beacon::BeaconConnKey` (DG-4).
```

Contract of `beacon_observation`:

- **Preconditions:** none. Infallible; callable at any time on a constructed
  driver, including before any `start`.
- **Postconditions:** an owned copy of the driver's live-launch table and
  beacon-claim state, taken without holding a lock on return; no beacon
  connection is accepted, read, claimed or closed by the call, and no state
  changes.
- **Consistency point:** between two per-CID beacon steps (ATTR-LIVE-CLAIM):
  a connection's live-launch recheck and its claim are one step, so a claim
  is never reported as taken on a connection whose recheck is still pending.
- **Edge cases:** a driver that has started nothing returns three empty
  collections. A CID stopped by `VmDriver::stop` or whose VMM exited — a
  guest reset included (RESET-EXIT) — is absent from `live`. A connection
  whose READY line was read and whose claim was refused is in neither
  `unread` nor `claims`.
- **Observable invariants:** each `BeaconConnKey` appears at most once across
  `claims` values and `unread`; a repeated call with no intervening beacon
  step returns an equal value.

##### QPROJ-5 — Guest flow owner observation (`overdrive-init`)

`overdrive-init` is a binary; its guest flow owner (control session, flow
table, UDP slot pool) runs over the guest-owner seam `GuestOwnerIo` (DG-5),
driven in-process by `dispatch_next`. The accessor is
`GuestFlowOwner::guest_observation() -> GuestSideObservation`, pinned with
its types and contract in § *Guest adaptation contract*, "Conformance
observation (guest flow owner)". Its fields are the projection sources:

| Fact | Field path |
|---|---|
| the guest owner holds a control-session connection it has not observed lost (D-UP-8) | `session` |
| host-opened (TcpAccept) flows the guest holds | `accepted[flow]`: `GuestAcceptPhase::Accepted` / `Paired { pair }` |
| paired TCP flows (either opener) and their pair | `flows[flow]`: the `ForwardId`; per-direction state through `FlowForwarder::pair_state` (QPROJ-8) |
| guest-opened TcpConnect flows not yet `Paired` | `awaiting_paired` |
| UDP slots | `slots[addr]`: `SlotObservation { owner, association, attached }` |

`SocketCookie` is the `overdrive-init`-private newtype pinned in DG-5.

##### QPROJ-8 — Forwarder observation (`FlowForwarder`, both sides)

The forwarder facts `fwd_pair` projects are read through the port's own
read-only methods (§ *[REF] Driven port — `FlowForwarder`*):
`pair_state(id) -> Option<PairState>` (per direction `source_end`,
`target_shut`, `moved`), `take_end()` as the owner reads end records (the
driver observes the records the owner consumed, in order, through the
owner's dispatch), and `inventory()`. In the seeded and conformance lanes
the adapter is `SimFlowForwarder`, the named arbiter of the forwarder's
kernel facts (`// conformance-lint: sim-arbiter-ok`), paired with V-EV-END,
V-EV-CTL and the module's Tier-3 suite through `KernelFlowForwarder`; the
far readers' delivered units and the socket queues are the Sim sockets'
facts, named arbiters paired with the same runs. Model-only, never
projected: `loss`, `lost`, `tcls`, `ucls`, `fwdAfterEnd`, `trail`,
`faults`, `sdrop` / `rdrop` / `fdrop`, `conf_step`.

**Context-generation variables (U-EV-8).**

| Variable | Class and source |
|---|---|
| `gen` (the generation of the context the owner holds) | O, host: `flow_observation().forwarder_generation: ForwarderGeneration` — the number of serving forwarder contexts the host owner has opened in this process (phase 1's probe context is not counted, D-8): 1 after boot step 9's open, incremented by each `Forwarder` repair's successful `KernelFlowForwarder::open()`, never decremented. Guest: constant 1 (the guest owner opens one context for its life and is never repaired in-process), projected as 1 |
| `oldCtx` (a released context still holding pairs or still open) | S: `SimFlowForwarder`'s context table, the named arbiter of the device's open contexts — the kernel's fact, which the owner no longer holds once it has dropped the context. Tier-3 pair: P-70 § 3.2 and § 3.8 (release completes before it returns; another context's pairs are unaffected), kept in the module's suite |
| a pair's `cgen` (the generation of the context that attached it) | O: the host flow table records, per flow, the generation in force when it attached the flow, read through `flow_observation()` as `GuestFlowPhase::Paired { pair, generation }`, `AssociationPhase::Paired { pair, generation }` and `DialPhase::Paired { watch, generation, .. }`; guest: 1 |
| `att`, `clsAt`, `ncls`, `snap` (attach-time and per-transition classification bookkeeping) | model-only: ghosts stating `AttachTimeEndClassifiedOnce` and `ClassFixedAtTransition`; discharged by P-69 and P-71 and the module suite's `h_noseed` and hazard 2 controls |
