| `fwdOld` (a unit forwarded by a pair of a released context) | model-only: ghost of `NoPairOfReleasedContextForwards`; discharged by `oldCtx` (S, above) and the release measurements |
| `unclassified` | O: `FlowForwarder::inventory().unclassified_eof` (above) |
| `rstOpen` (a reset arrived with a direction open) | model-only: ghost of `ResetNeverEndsClean`; the projected outcome is the pair's end record (`take_end`) |
| `holderReadAfterAbort` | model-only: ghost of `NoHolderReadAfterWatchAbort`; the projected facts are the dial's phase and the `GuestStreamEnd` its stream delivered (DG-15) |

`forwarder_generation` and the `generation` fields of the three phases are
new read-only observation surface on the host owner (§ *Owner and
provisioner*, `flow_observation`), the accessor the design pins for these
variables (`.claude/rules/design.md` § "Pin the observable projection").
Its contract: at a consistency point of the owner, every `generation` in a
`Paired` phase equals `forwarder_generation` (the recovery empties the flow
table before it opens the next context, § *Context lifetime and owner
failure*); a repeated call with no intervening owner step returns an equal
value. This is the production check of `NoPairOfReleasedContextForwards`
at the owner's boundary; the kernel half (no pair of a released context
still forwards) is the arbiter's.

**Ended-half, watch and stream variables (EVMOD-ATTACH-END,
EVMOD-STREAM-ABORT).** One row per state variable, record field and derived
definition of `fwd_pair` that these contracts declare (§ *Formal protocol
model*, items T-1 to T-9), named as the spec names them. A derived definition is not projected; it is computed from
the projected variables it reads, so a driver compares it only through
them.

| Spec name (T-item) | Class and source |
|---|---|
| `tcpErr(s)` — state variable: a TCP half's pending reset error, `"0"`, `"ECONNRESET"` or `"EPIPE"` (T-1) | S: `SimFlowForwarder`'s per-half `sk_err` of the TCP half, the named arbiter of the kernel's socket state. Tier-3 pair: P-69 hazard-16 shapes (`g-rst-hg-only`, `r-rst-gh-only`) in the module's suite. The projected outcome is O: the pair's end record as the owner consumed it, `ForwardEnd { outcome: Aborted { cause: SocketError { side, errno } } }`, which is `pr(s).cause` / `pr(s).errno` |
| `tcpSt(t, s)` — derived definition over `tcpErr(s)`, the far writer's FIN and this side's own FIN (`est`, `closeWait`, `ended`, `defect`; T-3, T-4) | not projected (derived); its inputs are projected (`tcpErr` above, `dir(d).wfin` and `dir(d).dstShut` by the `fwd_pair` map) |
| `vs(s).st` — the vsock half's state, `est` or `closing` (T-4) | S: `SimFlowForwarder`'s per-half state (`ESTABLISHED`, `CLOSING`), arbiter. Tier-3 pair: P-70 § 3.6 (vsock `CLOSING` refused) |
| `vs(s).err` — the vsock half's `sk_err` (while a watch is live it is also the sweep's first step taken; T-4, T-9) | S: `SimFlowForwarder`'s per-half `sk_err`, arbiter (row `vs(s)` of the `fwd_pair` map). Tier-3 pair: P-69 (the sweep's `sk_err`; 640 sweep-path observations) |
| `vs(s).sshut` — this side's own `sk_shutdown & SEND_SHUTDOWN` on the vsock half (T-8) | S: `SimFlowForwarder`'s per-half own-shutdown flag, arbiter. Tier-3 pair: P-71 `h_lateshut`. (this row is the classification of `sshut`) |
| `vs(s).misc` — a transition classified otherwise than with the socket's true send state (T-8) | model-only: ghost of `ClassFixedAtTransition`'s T-8 clause; discharged by P-71 `h_lateshut` |
| `attRes(s)` — the attach / watch result the owner received, `none`, `ok` or `halfEnded` (T-3, T-4) | O through the owner's cumulative counters, which stay readable after the flow has left the owner's table (D-5): the driver builds a fresh owner per run and `fwd_pair` carries one flow per side, so `halfEnded` ⇔ `forwarder_attach_ended` = 1 (host `flow_observation()`, guest `guest_observation()`); `ok` ⇔ `forwarder_attached` = 1; `none` ⇔ both 0. Cross-checked while the flow is held: `ok` ⇔ its phase is `Paired { pair, .. }` (QPROJ-3, QPROJ-5) |
| `attEnded(s)` — the owner's count of `halfEnded` refusals (T-4) | O: `forwarder_attach_ended` (above) |
| `strmAbort` — the dial's stream ended by the host owner (T-5) | O: the dial's entry is absent from `flow_observation().cids[cid].dials` while the driver still holds the stream (it has not performed `HolderDrop`). By the entry's lifetime rule (§ *Owner and provisioner*, "A dial's entry in `dials`", D-3) only the owner's abort removes the entry of a held `Paired` stream; reading the watch's end record leaves it with `guest_end: Some(_)`, so a guest end and an owner abort are told apart. Cross-checked by C, the stream's next call returning `Err(ConnectionAborted)`. After a host owner death (`CtxRelease(h)` with a live pair, the `fwd_pair` map) the owner is gone and `strmAbort` is not projected; the stream's result (`hres`, C) still is |
| `hres` — the outcome the `GuestStream` reported: `none`, `HalfClose`, `GuestAbort` or `OwnerAbort` (T-5, T-9) | C: what the driver, playing the holder, receives from the production `GuestStream` — `read` returning `Ok(0)` / `Err(ConnectionReset)` / `Err(ConnectionAborted)`, and `end()` — cross-checked against O `dials[h]` `Paired { guest_end, .. }` while the dial is held |
| `guestAbortSent` — `Abort { flow }` written for an aborted stream and not yet taken (T-5) | model-only in `fwd_pair` (the message's delivery is `owner_flows`' `toGuestAbort`, which the `owner_flows` driver consumes from the seam); the guest pair's resulting end is projected as for any guest pair (`pr(g)`) |
| `gh.hobs` — the holder's own end observation on `V_h`, `none`, `eof` or `err` (T-5, T-9) | model-only for the projection: it is the driver's own input — the action `HolderEnd` is the driver's `read` on `V_h` through the Sim vsock socket, which scripts the end fact (`Eof`, or `Err` with `ENOTCONN` / `ECONNRESET`); comparing it with the model would compare the driver with itself. What the stream reports for it is `hres` (above) |
| `gh.woken` — a holder woken by a watch's end (T-9) | model-only: ghost of `WatchRecordBeforeWake`; discharged by P-69 (record present at the holder's observation in 6,640 of 6,640) and hazard 4 / hazard 8, kept in the module's suite |
| `gh.vhTouched` — an owner abort of a watch changed `V_h` (T-5) | model-only: ghost of `WatchAbortLeavesHolderSocket`; the projected fact is `vs(h)` and the queues `dir(gh).q1` / `dir(hg).q1` of the Sim vsock socket (S, arbiter; Tier-3 pair: the module suite's case "`ABORT` of a watch sends nothing on the vsock and changes no socket state", P-70 § 3.8 for the spike's behaviour) |
| `gh.dropped` — the holder dropped its `GuestStream` (T-6) | model-only: the driver's own call (`HolderDrop` drops the stream); its effect is projected as `live(h)` below and the guest pair's end (`pr(g)`) |
| `live(t, h)` in mode watch — derived: the watch is live (T-6) | not projected as such; its input `pr(h).ph` is, and it is cross-checked against O `FlowForwarder::inventory().live_watches` of the host context through `SimFlowForwarder` (QPROJ-7, row "node flow places") |
| `headPartial(t, d)` over `dir(d).q1` in mode dgram — derived: the frame at the head of the vsock half's queue is incomplete (T-7) | not projected as such; its input, the Sim vsock queue `dir(d).q1`, is S (arbiter). Tier-3 pair: P-72 § 8 (the truncated-frame control) |

`forwarder_attach_ended` and `forwarder_attached` are the owner observation
surface these variables read (on both owners; § *Owner and
provisioner*, § *Guest adaptation contract*). Their contract: cumulative,
never decremented, across every context the owner held; `forwarder_attach_ended`
is raised in the same dispatch that ends the flow after a `HalfEnded`
refusal, `forwarder_attached` in the dispatch whose `attach` or `watch`
returned `Ok`; a call refused for any other reason raises neither; a
repeated call with no intervening owner step returns an equal value.

##### QPROJ-6 — Runtime supervisor recovery observation (`overdrive-control-plane`)

```rust
// overdrive_control_plane — public, read-only, compiled in production; on the
// runtime shared-network supervisor's handle (RUN-295-B) the composition
// retains (the handle type is crate-private, so the method is reached inside
// overdrive-control-plane; no exported API is added)
impl SharedNetworkSupervisorHandle {
    pub fn recovery_observation(&self) -> BTreeMap<SharedGuestNetworkComponent, RecoveryEpisode>;
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RecoveryEpisode {
    pub phase: RecoveryPhase,
    /// Failed attempts of this recovery: a failed repair, or a failed
    /// post-repair audit (D-295-R13, UP-7). Equals the `attempts` the EXEC
    /// gate's `recovery_progress()` reports for the same component.
    pub failed_attempts: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RecoveryPhase {
    /// Quiesced under the recovery's `QuiescenceHold`; repair not yet clean.
    Held,
    /// The repair returned `Ok`; the post-repair audit is pending.
    Repaired,
}
```

No recovery drops its hold (D-UP-3, approved 2026-10-14; § *Owner and
provisioner*): an episode is `Held` or `Repaired` until it ends by
`restore` (absent) or by the fail-stop of `serve`. A hold dropped by an
Overdrive defect is not an episode; it is counted by the owner's
`leaked_quiescence_holds`.

Contract of `recovery_observation`:

- **Preconditions:** none. Infallible; callable at any time on a spawned
  supervisor.
- **Postconditions:** an owned copy of the supervisor's per-component
  episodes, taken under the same gate lock that linearizes
  `recovery_progress()`; no lock is held on return; nothing is quiesced,
  repaired, audited or restored by the call.
- **Consistency point:** between two supervisor steps (one quiesce, one
  repair, one audit, one restore, one `complete_attempt`, one fail-stop).
- **Edge cases:** a component with no recovery in progress is absent; the map
  is empty while the gate is Open, BootClosed or FailStop.
- **Observable invariants:** the key set equals the set of components
  `recovery_progress()` reports (the EXEC gate contract); at a consistency
  point of both the supervisor and the owner, the number of episodes plus
  the owner's `flow_observation().leaked_quiescence_holds` equals its
  `quiescence_holds` (QHOLD `CountCoversRecoveries`, D-UP-3); a recovery's
  `failed_attempts` equals the
  `attempts` of its `recovery_progress()` entry; a repeated call with no
  intervening supervisor step returns an equal value.

The supervisor keeps each recovery's episode in the state this accessor
reads, beside the EXEC gate's per-recovery snapshots (the runtime
shared-network supervisor, RUN-295-B).

##### QPROJ-7 — Sim arbiters and their Tier-3 pairing

A sim arbiter is a projection source only for a driven-port fact the owner
under test does not hold (the kernel's, the VMM's, or a far end's). Each read
below is paired with the real-adapter evidence that reports the same fact;
DISTILL names the Tier-3 scenario that re-proves it on the production path.

| Arbiter (crate, visibility) | Read accessor | Fact it reports | Real-adapter evidence (Tier-3 pair) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SimVmm` (`overdrive-sim`, `pub`, existing) | `is_live(&self, pid: u32) -> bool` | the VMM process is alive | V-30 Q2c / Q2d |
| `SimVmm` (`overdrive-sim`, `pub`, **new**) | `vsock_device_holders(&self) -> BTreeMap<GuestCid, u32>` | the CIDs whose `/dev/vhost-vsock` instance a live VMM process holds, with that process's pid; a VMM is the only holder of its device (CID-NOCLAIM); the entry is gone at the VMM's exit, a guest reset included (RESET-EXIT) | the Tier-3 V-30 evidence Q2a / Q2c / Q2d (`spike/findings-v30-guest-reset.md`: device released, host flows reset with `ECONNRESET` at VMM exit, CID free at once); the open serve-restart reclamation item V-RECLAIM (an orphan of the previous process holds its CID until boot reclamation kills it) |
| `SimMtlsIntercept` (`overdrive-sim`, `pub`, existing) | `shared_table_state(&self) -> SimSharedTable` with `pub enum SimSharedTable { Absent, Complete }` | the shared table is absent, or present with every constant rule — the only two states a single nft transaction leaves (boot step 8); a scripted failed write leaves the state as it was | R5-30 (the ADR-0184 boot-table-write scenario): `nft list table` read-back of the production table (no table ↔ `Absent`; every constant rule present ↔ `Complete`), and the refused boot after a failed write; read-back R5-43, R5-48 |
| Owner seam sim `SimGuestFlowIo` — sockets (source-local, `overdrive-control-plane`) | `socket_observation(&self) -> SimOwnerSocketObservation` (below) | per fact: accept queues with buffered first records; connections the owner closed that it no longer reports; accepted connections whose peer VM is gone (K-A2′); each outer far end's first terminal event | `queued`, `peer_gone`: V-22 (P-37: queued records after VMM death and CID reuse; established connections fail at their next I/O) and R5-41 (the P-37 shape through `serve`); `closed_by_owner`: R5-16 and R5-41 (stale and unattributed connections closed by the production owner); `far_end`: V-31 item 2c (P-52: every far end reset on owner death) and R5-10 (Tier-3 through `serve` + `deploy`, each far end's first terminal event). Peer connects in flight, dial V_h closes and the session's end are owner facts, projected from QPROJ-3 (below), not from this arbiter |
| `SimFlowForwarder` (`overdrive-sim`, `pub`; the core `FlowForwarder` port, EVMOD-PORT) | `pair_state(id)`, `inventory()`, the end records `take_end()` returns (the port's own methods, QPROJ-8); the device's context table `SimForwarderDevice::contexts() -> Vec<SimContextState>` in open order, released contexts included, each row `SimContextState { open: bool, live_pairs: u32, live_watches: u32, queued_ends: Vec<ForwardId> }` — `queued_ends` the ids whose end record the context holds and nobody has taken, in queue order; a released context's row keeps the queue it held at its release (the kernel frees it unread; the row is the fact that it was produced, D-4); per-half facts on the half's shared `SimSocket` (`received_shutdown`, `sent_shutdown`, `sk_err`, `recorded_class`, `vsock_state`, `own_send_shut`), readable after the owner closed the half and then reporting its facts at the close | the forwarder's kernel facts: per-direction ends and target shutdowns, the class each vsock transition was given, the queued end records, live pairs and watches, a released context | V-EV-END (classification between two forwarders), V-EV-CTL (context release, one record per id), V-EV-PAIR (attach-time state), V-EV-DGRAM (datagram mode), and the module's Tier-3 suite through `KernelFlowForwarder` |
| `SimFlowForwarder` — node flow places (D-UP-17, approved 2026-10-14) | `inventory()` → `ForwarderInventory { live_pairs, live_watches, queued_ends, .. }` | node flow-place occupancy: the pairs and watches held by every flow on the node — guest-opened flows, datagram associations and dials of both purposes; the node-cap scenario's oracle is the public refusal (`GuestDialError::Capacity`, `FlowRefusal::Capacity`), not this read | R5-57 (the forwarder inventory through the production owner on the real `KernelFlowForwarder`, Tier-3) |
| `SimBeaconIo` (`overdrive-sim`, `pub`; the core `BeaconIo` port, DG-4) | `beacon_socket_observation(&self) -> SimBeaconSocketObservation { queued: BTreeMap<BeaconConnKey, Option<LaunchToken>>, closed_by_driver: BTreeSet<BeaconConnKey> }` (`pub`) | beacon accept queue with buffered READY (K-A2′); connections the driver closed | V-22 (P-37, beacon part) |
| Guest-owner seam sim `SimGuestOwnerIo` (source-local, `overdrive-init`) | `guest_socket_observation(&self) -> SimGuestSocketObservation` (below); the guest's forwarder facts through its `SimFlowForwarder` (row above) | V_g in the guest accept queue and torn down there (K-A4); readiness events not yet dispatched; datagrams queued in each slot socket, tagged by origin; queued `sock_release` reports; each guest far end's first terminal event | V-24 (P-38, K-A4); R5-14 (release reports); V-EV-DGRAM (the slot socket's queue and its discard); `far_end`: V-31 item 2c (P-52) and R5-10. The guest's session state is an owner fact, projected from QPROJ-5 `session` |

```rust
// source-local sim read surfaces (#[cfg(test)]); field names and meanings
// are the contract, the seams' other methods are the crafter's / DISTILL's
pub(crate) struct SimOwnerSocketObservation {
    pub(crate) queued: BTreeMap<GuestConnKey, Option<LaunchToken>>,   // None: nothing buffered
    pub(crate) closed_by_owner: BTreeSet<GuestConnKey>,               // closed; no longer in flow_observation()
    pub(crate) peer_gone: BTreeSet<GuestConnKey>,                     // accepted; peer VM dead, not yet observed
    pub(crate) far_end: BTreeMap<FlowId, FarEndEvent>,                // first terminal event: Eof | Reset
}
// The forwarder's facts are `SimFlowForwarder`'s (QPROJ-8).
impl SimGuestFlowIo {
    /// The shared `SimSocket` of `flow`'s host vsock half, keyed from the
    /// step the seam first carries the flow id on it (a guest-opened V_h:
    /// its request's read; a dial's V_h: its TcpAccept request's write),
    /// kept after the owner closed it,
    /// until the seam is dropped. `None` for a flow id the seam never saw
    /// (D-5; the `fwd_pair` row `vs(s)`).
    pub(crate) fn vsock_half(&self, flow: FlowId) -> Option<SimSocket>;
}
pub(crate) struct SimGuestSocketObservation {
    pub(crate) queued_inbound: BTreeSet<FlowId>,                      // V_g in the guest accept queue
    pub(crate) reset_in_queue: BTreeSet<FlowId>,                      // V_g torn down there (K-A4)
    pub(crate) readiness: BTreeSet<SocketAddrV4>,                     // undispatched readiness events, by slot
    pub(crate) parked: BTreeMap<SocketAddrV4, BTreeSet<(SocketCookie, SocketAddrV4)>>, // datagrams queued in each slot socket, by origin
    pub(crate) release_reports: BTreeSet<SocketCookie>,
    pub(crate) far_end: BTreeMap<FlowId, FarEndEvent>,
}
```

The sims enforce the real adapters' preconditions and model the facts in
the table and nothing else; a sim arbiter's fact with no real-adapter pairing
is not a projection source. The shared table is written and replaced only in
single nft transactions (boot step 8, ADR-0184), so the arbiter reports only
the states one transaction leaves, `Absent` and `Complete`; a partial table is
not a production state and no sim, projection or scenario models one
(U-QP-1).

**Where each sim lives, by the crate-graph rule of QPROJ-1** (every sim any
in-crate driver names, checked against it):

| Sim | Defined in | Trait / types it names | Unifies with the owner under test because |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SimVmm` | `overdrive-sim` | `overdrive_core::traits::vmm::Vmm`, `VmConfig`, `ConfinementControl` | core only; used by the pool, host-owner-lifecycle and worker drivers |
| `SimClock`, `SimEntropy`, `SimCgroupFs`, `SimCgroupAccounting` | `overdrive-sim` | core ports (`Clock`, `Entropy`, `CgroupFs`, `CgroupAccounting`) | core only; used by the `overdrive-control-plane` and `overdrive-worker` drivers (the worker driver builds `VmDriver` over them); `overdrive-init` uses `SimGuestClock` (DG-5) |
| `SimMtlsIntercept` | `overdrive-sim` | `overdrive_worker::mtls_intercept_port::MtlsIntercept` and `overdrive_worker::mtls_intercept` types | used only by the `overdrive-control-plane` `quiescence` driver, where `overdrive-worker` is a normal dependency of both the owner crate and `overdrive-sim`, so Cargo links one copy and the trait unifies. Not used by the `overdrive-worker` drivers |
| Owner seam sim `SimGuestFlowIo` — sockets (DG-3) | `overdrive-control-plane`, `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "integration-tests"))]`, crate-private, beside the seam (in-crate tests, conformance drivers and the composed rig only; NO-OVERRIDE-SEAMS) | `GuestFlowIo`, `GuestConnKey`, `FlowId`, `LaunchToken` | names the owner crate's own types, so it lives in the owner crate (a copy in `overdrive-sim` would name a second copy of the owner crate) |
| `SimFlowForwarder` (EVMOD-PORT) | `overdrive-sim`, `pub` | `overdrive_core::guest_transport::forwarder::{FlowForwarder, ForwardId, ForwardEnd, PairState, ForwarderInventory}` | core trait and core types only (rule 1); used by the host and guest owner drivers |
| `SimBeaconIo` (DG-4) | `overdrive-sim`, `pub` | `overdrive_core::vm::beacon::{BeaconIo, BeaconSocket, BeaconConnKey}` | core trait and core types only (rule 1); used by the `overdrive-worker` in-crate driver, out-of-crate `VmDriver` tests and `run_server` boots whose `NodeAdapters.vm` carries `SimVmm` (NO-OVERRIDE-SEAMS) |
| Guest-owner seam sim `SimGuestOwnerIo` with `SimGuestClock` (DG-5) | `overdrive-init`, `#[cfg(test)]`, beside the seam | `GuestOwnerIo`, `GuestClock`, `SocketCookie` | names the binary's own types; the binary has no library target |

`SimMtlsInterceptLifecycle` and `overdrive-sim`'s adapters that name
`overdrive-control-plane` types (guest network, guest DNS, view store,
journal) are not named by any driver in this section. A driver that needs
the lifecycle port uses a test double defined in `overdrive-control-plane`
beside the port.

##### Per-module projection and action map

Columns: *Var* = model variable; *Source* = O (owner accessor, QPROJ-2 to
QPROJ-6), S (sim arbiter, QPROJ-7), C (caller observation), or a
classification. Every action handler in a driver's `switch!` calls the
production call or releases the seam effect named here; an action not listed
is a hazard-only action and is not mapped (the driver fails on it).

**`cid_lease`** (driver in `overdrive-control-plane`; instance
`lease_conf_ok`, five offsets = the five usable offsets of the /29 test
pool, `lease_conf_325`, the same with the #325 window enabled, for one
run pending #325 (item 9), and `lease_conf_three`, `lease_ok`'s three
offsets with `conf_step` recorded, for the one pool-exhaustion run (D-18).
`lease_live` stays a model-checking instance with three abstract
offsets and is not a conformance target, D-UP-20)

**Projecting `lease_conf_three` onto the five-offset pool.** No
pool prefix yields exactly three usable offsets: a pool's usable offsets
are its prefix's addresses less the network, gateway and broadcast
addresses, `2^k − 3` (1 for a /30, 5 for a /29). The driver therefore keeps
the /29 test pool and pins this relabelling and exclusion rule, used only
on `lease_conf_three`:

- **Background leases.** Before the trace's first step the driver submits
  two Service workloads outside the model's workload set and runs ticks
  until production has placed them on offsets 0 and 1 (next-fit from a fresh
  pool; the driver checks the two leases' offsets and fails otherwise). At
  every compared step it checks that both background leases are still
  Admitted on offsets 0 and 1, and fails the step otherwise. The named run
  `PoolExhaustedRestartCleansThePredecessorThenPlaces` has no `Crash`,
  `Restart`, `Stop` or `Redeploy`, so nothing in it releases them; a run
  that does is not replayed on this main.
- **Relabelling.** Model offset `m` ∈ {0, 1, 2} is production offset
  `m + 2`. `lease` and `dev` are projected over production offsets 2..=4
  only, relabelled; offsets 0 and 1 are excluded, not compared.
  `al(a).off` and `al(a).pred` are the relabelled offsets; the model's
  workloads map to the two model workloads the driver submitted (the
  background workloads are never projected).
- **Cursor.** `cursor` is the model offset of the first usable production
  offset at or after `next_fit` (QPROJ-2) that is not a background offset:
  a production cursor at 0 or 1, or past 4 (wrapping to 0), projects to
  model 0, because next-fit from it skips the two always-held background
  offsets and reaches offset 2 first — the same choice the model's cursor
  0 makes.
- **CEIL.** `lease_conf_three` keeps `lease_ok`'s `CEIL` = 2 while
  production's `RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING` is 5. The run's trace keeps every
  workload's `att` below 2 (its last step places workload 2 with
  `att` = 1), and `restart_decision(att, ..) = att < CEIL` agrees for
  `att` ∈ {0, 1} under both values, so every compared `retry` / `ex` is
  the same. A randomized trace could reach `att` = 2 and diverge, so the
  driver runs no `#[quint_run]` on this main; its `#[quint_run]` stays on
  `lease_conf_ok`.

| Var | Source |
|---|---|
| `lease` | O QPROJ-2 `lease_observation().leases`: offset(`cid`) ↦ allocation, every lease; a free offset ↦ 0 |
| `cursor` | O QPROJ-2 `next_fit`, as the model offset of the first usable offset at or after it |
| `al(a).st` | The **placement lease** of `a` is the lease (QPROJ-2) of the allocation the workload's latest `Assign` step leased (C: the one lease that step added; none after a `Restart` until the next `Assign`); every other lease of an allocation of `a`'s workload is the **predecessor lease** (`pred`, below). `picked`: hazard-only (`assignSplit`, never reached by the design). With a placement lease: `leased` ⇔ Admitted ∧ S `vsock_device_holders()` maps the lease's CID to no VMM ∧ O the lease's allocation has no row in `hydrate_actual`'s `allocations` (the owner-read form: the substituted provisioner that holds the dispatch at `provision` is the step's pacing device only and is never read for a projected variable; at a step boundary an Admitted placement lease with no device holder and no row is exactly the dispatch held before `VmDriver::start`, because `Launch` creates the VMM and writes the `Running` row in one step and a crash-class end leaves a `Failed` / `Terminated` row); `running` ⇔ Admitted ∧ S `vsock_device_holders()` maps the lease's CID to the VMM the dispatch's `start` created; `ended` ⇔ Admitted ∧ no VMM holds its CID's device ∧ the lease allocation's row (`hydrate_actual`'s `allocations`) is `Failed` / `Terminated` (a crash-class end; no dispatch has run for it yet); `retiring` ⇔ Retiring. Without a placement lease, the placement owner's decision, O QPROJ-2W of `a`'s workload target, with `run` = `hydrate_desired`'s `job.is_some() ∧ ¬desired_to_stop`, `cur` = `current_alloc` over `hydrate_actual`'s `allocations` and `dec` = `restart_status_for_alloc(target, Service, run, cur, generation).1`: `done` ⇔ `desired_to_stop`; `failed` ⇔ `run` ∧ `cur` exists ∧ `cur.terminal` = `Some(BackoffExhausted { .. })` ∧ ¬`dec` (the budget-exhausted terminal `FinalizeFailed` wrote, `workload_lifecycle.rs:1172-1178`, with no pending generation that places it again); `ended` ⇔ `run` ∧ `cur` is `Failed` / `Terminated` with `cur.terminal` = `None` ∧ ¬`dec` (a budget-exhausted failure whose `FinalizeFailed` has not committed its terminal, e.g. after a `serve` crash); `wait` ⇔ `run` ∧ neither `failed` nor `ended` |
| `al(a).off` | O QPROJ-2 the placement lease's `cid` − `GUEST_CID_BASE`; −1 without one |
| `al(a).pred`, `al(a).pst` | O QPROJ-2: the predecessor lease's offset (−1 and `none` without one) and its state: `held` ⇔ Admitted (the predecessor's VMM has exited; the restart dispatch has not cleaned it), `retiring` ⇔ Retiring (the restart dispatch's predecessor cleanup is held at the provisioner's `teardown`). The model holds at most one predecessor lease per workload |
| `al(a).retry` | for a crash's `ended`, and for `Finalize`'s and a stop's `retiring`: O QPROJ-2W `restart_status_for_alloc(target, Service, run, row, generation).1`, where `row` is `hydrate_actual`'s row of the placement lease's allocation, or `cur` without a placement lease (a crash's row is terminal when its step returns: the exit observer wrote it; a stop's gives `run` false) and `run` and `generation` are `hydrate_desired`'s. For a launch clash's `retiring`: model-only — the successor has no row while its `teardown` is held (`cleanup_restart_successor` runs before the successor's `Failed` row write, `action_shim/mod.rs:2873-2886`, row at `:2960-2985`); the clash is hazard-only and unmapped, and the driver fails on it. `false` otherwise |
| `al(a).ex` | in the same states as `retry`: O QPROJ-2W `run` ∧ ¬`restart_status_for_alloc(target, Service, run, row, generation).1`, the same call (a crash-class failure the reconciler finalizes, clause 5 of `restart_after_failure` with `restart_decision` false); model-only for a launch clash's `retiring`; `false` otherwise |
| `att(a)` | O QPROJ-2W `attempt_index_for_alloc(target, x) − 1`, where `x` is the placement lease's allocation while one exists, else `current_alloc` over `hydrate_actual`'s `allocations`; 0 when there is neither (`WorkloadLifecycleView::restart_counts[x]`, persisted, so it survives a `serve` crash; an issued successor with no row is read through its lease). The predecessor lease never feeds `att` |
| `al(a).chg` | model-only: the next placement charges one (the predecessor is a crash-class row). Not projected; its effect is projected through `att` after the next `Assign` |
| `bootLeft` | stimulus |
| `dev` | S `vsock_device_holders()` with O QPROJ-2: offset ↦ 0 if unheld; the lease's allocation if held by the VMM of that lease's launch; −2 if held by a VMM process the current pool leases nothing for (an orphan of the previous `serve` process) |
| `up` | stimulus, not projected (`testing.md` checklist item 5): set and cleared by the driver's own `Restart` and `Crash` calls, so comparing it would compare the driver with itself. Its effects are projected at every step: `lease`, `cursor`, `al` and `att` from the composition while one exists; while none exists (from a `Crash` to the next boot's first step), `lease` and `cursor` are **not compared** — no pool exists to read (NO-SURVIVE), and a driver-chosen literal would be bookkeeping (`testing.md` checklist item 5); the model's own `Crash` empties them, so the next boot's first projected step compares them against the new pool — and `al` / `att` are read from the durable stores that survive the crash (the node's `LocalIntentStore`, `SimObservationStore` and view store), through the same `hydrate_desired` / `hydrate_actual` / `restart_status_for_alloc` / `attempt_index_for_alloc` reads the next boot makes, over a `HydrationContext` the driver builds on those stores (S-4); `dev` is compared across a crash |
| `reclaimed` | stimulus, not projected (same reason): set by the driver's own `Reclaim` call, which fails the step unless `vm_reclamation_boot::converge` returns `Ok`. Its effect is projected through `dev` (no orphan `−2` remains) and, for `Assign`'s guard (`AssignAfterReclaim`), through `lease` and `dev` together (no lease of a CID an orphan holds). For `Finalize` and `Redeploy` it is a fidelity guard on which no Safety property depends |
| `g` | ghost (including `g.lastEnd`, below) |

| Action | Production call or fault |
|---|---|
| `Assign(a)` | from `wait`, or from `ended` with `retry` (its lease becomes the predecessor lease, `pst = held`), with a free offset and no dispatch of `a`'s workload held at a predecessor `teardown`: one QPROJ-2W convergence tick for `a`'s workload target (the `SimClock` advanced past the reconciler's backoff for a workload placed again after a failure): `WorkloadLifecycle` emits `StartAllocation` (no current row, or a fresh lineage) or `RestartAllocation` (a successor of the current row) and the action shim's dispatch takes the lease with `pool.assign` (§ *Owner and provisioner*); the dispatch is held at the substituted provisioner's `provision`, so the step ends with the new lease Admitted and `start` not yet called. A `RestartAllocation` provisions the successor **before** it touches the predecessor (`action_shim/mod.rs:2707-2716`, `provision_and_inject_netns` → `pool.assign` at `:1471`), so a predecessor lease stays Admitted (`pst = held`) through this step. The attachment cap (`MAX_GUEST_NETWORK_ATTACHMENTS` = 16 384) is never reached by the five-offset pool, so the reconciler's at-cap reclaim of a due predecessor (`workload_lifecycle.rs:399-478`, `:1198-1203`) is not modelled |
| `AssignRefused(a)` | from `ended` with `retry` and **no** free offset: the same tick's `RestartAllocation`; `pool.assign` returns `PoolExhausted`, an admission refusal (`action_shim/mod.rs:540-548`), so the dispatch places nothing and runs the predecessor cleanup at once (`finish_restart`, `:2719-2731`): the lease is retired (`pst = retiring`) and the dispatch is held at its `teardown`; the workload is `wait`, its count unchanged (the current row is still the predecessor's). Unreachable on `lease_conf_ok` (two workloads hold at most four of the five offsets); reached on the three-offset instances, and replayed by the driver on the recording main `lease_conf_three` (D-18) |
| `Launch(a)` | from `leased`: the held `provision` returns; the same dispatch continues to `VmDriver::start` (`SimVmm::create`: the VMM opens its CID's device) and writes the new allocation's `Running` row. For a `RestartAllocation` with a predecessor lease (`pst = held`) the dispatch then runs the predecessor cleanup (`finish_restart` → `cleanup_restart_predecessor`, `:1760-1789`, `:1808`): it retires the predecessor lease (`pst = retiring`) and is held at that lease's `teardown`. A held device (hazard-only: `NoLaunchClash` is never violated by the design) makes the VMM exit before READY, `start` fails and `cleanup_restart_successor` (`:1734-1754`, `:2878-2892`) retires the new lease and is held at its `teardown` (`retiring`; the successor's `Failed` row is written only after that teardown, so `retry` / `ex` are model-only there); the predecessor cleanup follows at that `Release`. The driver fails on the clash branch |
| `Stop(a)` | from `running` or from `ended` with its placement lease, with no dispatch of `a`'s workload held at a predecessor `teardown`: `handlers::stop_workload` for `a`'s workload (the stop sentinel), then one convergence tick. From `running`: the reconciler emits the stop and the dispatch retires the lease, runs `VmDriver::stop` (the `SimVmm` process exits) and is held at the provisioner's `teardown`. From `ended`: the Stop branch emits nothing for a non-`Running` row; under a stop intent `pending_restart_owner` is `None` (`workload_lifecycle.rs:405-407`), so the reclaim pass emits `ReclaimAllocationNetwork` for the ended allocation (`:446-478`, `:481-510`) and its dispatch (`reclaim_guest_network`, `action_shim/mod.rs:1609-1652`) retires the lease and is held at the provisioner's `teardown` |
| `VmmCrash(a)` | from `running`: the `SimVmm` process exits (its device is released); the production exit observer writes the terminal row. **No convergence tick runs in this step**: the placement lease stays Admitted (`ended`) — no dispatch retires a crashed allocation's lease below the ceiling; `retry` / `ex` are the reconciler's decision on that row. The tick that follows is the workload's next `Assign`, `AssignRefused`, `Finalize` or `Stop` step |
| `GuestReset(a)` | `SimVmm` guest reset: the sim ends the VMM process (RESET-EXIT, ADR-0182); then as `VmmCrash(a)` |
| `Finalize(a)` | from `ended` with `ex`, after boot reclamation of the current composition (`reclaimed`: `run_server` runs `vm_reclamation_boot::converge`, `lib.rs:4024`, before it spawns the convergence loop, `:4281`, so no tick runs before it; the driver never steps `Finalize` before `converge` returned), with no dispatch of `a`'s workload held at a predecessor `teardown`: one convergence tick; the reconciler's ceiling check precedes its backoff check and emits `FinalizeFailed` (`workload_lifecycle.rs:1116-1179`). With a placement lease the dispatch retires it and is held at its `teardown` (`retiring` with `ex`); the terminal `BackoffExhausted` is written only after the teardown and release (`action_shim/mod.rs:2146-2176`). Without one (after a `serve` crash) the dispatch writes the terminal at once: `failed` |
| `Release(a)` | the held `teardown` returns and the dispatch runs `pool.release` (`action_shim/mod.rs:1596-1600`: release only after teardown, which runs only after the VMM exited; `ReleaseWhileTheVmmRunsIsRefused` checks the action is not enabled earlier). A held `teardown` of the placement lease (`retiring`) is released first: the workload becomes `wait` (a clash with `retry`), `failed` (`ex`) or `done` (a stop); if a predecessor lease is still `held` (the clash path) the dispatch then retires it and is held at its `teardown` (`pst = retiring`). Otherwise a predecessor `teardown` (`pst = retiring`) is released: `pred = −1`, `pst = none`, `st` unchanged. When the model's result is `done` (a stopped workload), the step then runs one convergence tick for that workload, which must take no lease |
| `Redeploy(a)` | after boot reclamation of the current composition (`reclaimed`: the handler is reachable only through the API listener, which `run_server` binds at `lib.rs:4437`, after `vm_reclamation_boot::converge` at `:4024`; the driver never steps `Redeploy` before `converge` returned): `handlers::restart_workload` for `a`'s workload; the generation is incremented and the stop sentinel deleted in one `IntentStore::txn` (`handlers.rs:976-983`). The step runs no tick; the next `Assign(a)` is the tick that places it, a `RestartAllocation` of the current row under the generation exemption, the successor keeping the count (`workload_lifecycle.rs:1214-1221`). Per pre-state (the model enables `Redeploy` only in these two): from `done` (a stopped workload; the sentinel exists) the handler's outcome is `RestartOutcome::Resumed` and the current row is the operator stop, a restart candidate under the pending generation (`:1090-1092`); from `failed` (a budget-exhausted Service; no sentinel) the outcome is `RestartOutcome::Restarted` (`handlers.rs:963-967`) and the current row is the `BackoffExhausted` one, whose next crash-class failure exhausts the budget at once (its count is already at the ceiling). The driver checks the outcome against the pre-state |
| `Crash` | drop the composition (pool, owner, VM driver, `ReconcilerRuntime` and its views, every held dispatch); every running `SimVmm` process survives as an orphan holding its device, and the `LocalIntentStore` survives (the node's persistent intent). Every lease is lost, predecessor leases included (`pred = −1`, `pst = none`). An `ended` workload with `retry` waits (`chg` true); an `ended` one with `ex`, and a `retiring` one with `ex` (its `FinalizeFailed` held before the terminal write), stay `ended` with no lease — the reconciler of the new process emits `FinalizeFailed` again |
| `Restart` | a new composition over the same `SimVmm` and the same `LocalIntentStore`, with `WorkloadLifecycle` registered again; boot reclamation not yet run |
| `Reclaim` | one `vm_reclamation_boot::converge` call: it kills every orphan and returns (D-UP-19: no per-orphan order is modelled, and no invariant depends on the `AllocationId` order `converge` kills in; the hazard flag `reclaimNeverCompletes` keeps `reclaimed` false after the kills; hazard-only, never reached by the design). The step then runs one convergence tick for every workload whose projection is `done`, each of which must take no lease (`StoppedWorkloadNotPlaced` checked against the reconciler across a `serve` crash) |
| `OrphanExit(o)` | the orphan `SimVmm` process exits by itself (an orphan killed before a crash interrupted `converge` is an `OrphanExit`) |
| `AssignPick(a)`, `AssignTake(a)` | hazard-only (`assignSplit`: the offset chosen and taken in two steps); not mapped |

Initial state (every allocation `wait`): before the first step the driver
calls `handlers::submit_workload` for each model workload (a VM **Service**
with the `/29` pool's transport), with no stop sentinel. A Service, not a
Job: `WorkloadLifecycle` finalizes a Job's first natural exit, a crash
included, and never places it again (`workload_lifecycle.rs:1035-1057`), so
only a Service has the crash-then-place-again behaviour the model's
`VmmCrash`, `GuestReset` and `Launch` clash steps assume. **T-5 ruling (architect,
2026-10-18):** the
production owner of placement is `WorkloadLifecycle`, so the composition
runs it. Every lease the driver observes is taken and returned by the action
shim dispatching that reconciler's actions; the driver never calls
`pool.assign`, `pool.retire` or `pool.release` itself, and never writes the
`IntentStore`. The step boundaries the model has inside one dispatch (a
lease taken before launch; a lease retired before its release; for a
restart, the successor's launch before the predecessor's retirement) are the
substituted `GuestNetworkProvisioner`'s `provision` and `teardown`, held by
the driver and returned at `Launch` and `Release` — the accepted driven port
of that tick, so the dispatch's own order is what is compared. `wait` /
`done` and `retry` come from the reconciler (QPROJ-2W), not from the store
directly, and the "stopped workload is never placed again" rule is checked
where the model claims no placement: the ticks the `Release` of a stopped
workload and `Reclaim` run must take no lease. If the production reconciler
does not decompose a step this way (for example, a crash's dispatch both
releases and places in one tick), the step's comparison fails; that is a
finding against the model's granularity and returns to DESIGN, not a driver
fix. The model's rules for this:

1. `Crash` maps an allocation that was stopped
   and not yet released (`retiring` with `retry` false) to `done`, not
   `wait`: the stop sentinel survives a `serve` crash.
2. (RESTART-SSOT, GH #324.) **Budget exhaustion is in the model:**
   `cid_lease` models the restart budget to and past its end,
   because the CID lease's behaviour differs there — an exhausted workload
   holds no lease and is never placed again until a `Redeploy` — and the
   boundary between the fifth and sixth failure is exactly where #324 was
   wrong. The model's restart state and its rules, each the reconciler's:
   - **`att(a)`** is `WorkloadLifecycleView::restart_counts` of `a`'s
     current allocation (the lease's allocation while a lease exists, else
     the `current_alloc` row's), 0 before the first placement. **It changes
     only at placement**, as `restart_counts` does (`:1214-1221`, `:1339`):
     `Assign` sets the new allocation's count to `att + 1` when the
     predecessor is a crash-class row (`chg`), and to `att` under the
     platform-reclaim or the generation exemption; a first placement gets 0.
     A failure does not change it (a count raised at the failure would be no
     production allocation's count while the lease is Retiring, so it would
     have no owner accessor).
   - **The decision at a failure.** A crash-class failure (`VmmCrash`,
     `GuestReset`, a `Launch` clash; neither exemption) sets
     `retry = restart_decision(att, false, false)` = `att < CEIL` and
     `ex = ¬retry`. After a `VmmCrash` / `GuestReset` the workload is
     `ended` with its lease still Admitted; `retry` leads to `Assign` (the
     successor, with the old lease as the predecessor lease, item 7) and
     `ex` to `Finalize` then `Release` (`failed`). A clash's `Release` gives
     `wait` with `chg` (retry) or `ended` with no lease (ex; the next
     `Finalize` writes the terminal: `failed`); a stop's gives `done`.
   - **The exemptions.** A `serve` crash with a running VMM: boot
     reclamation ends the allocation `StoppedBy::PlatformReclaimed`
     (`vm_reclamation_boot.rs:347`), so the workload waits whatever its
     count (`restart_decision(att, true, _)`), with `chg` false. `Redeploy`
     (from `done` or `failed`) is a generation replacement: the workload
     waits whatever its count, with `chg` false.
   - **CEIL** = `RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING` = 5
     (`overdrive-reconcilers/src/workload_lifecycle.rs:34`) on `lease_conf_ok`
     and `lease_five`, scaled to 2 on `lease_ok`, `lease_live` and the hazard
     model-checking instances (the predicate's shape is the same). With 5,
     the fifth crash-class failure (`att = 4`) is placed again and the sixth
     (`att = 5`) exhausts the budget.
   - **State `failed`** (budget exhausted, `FinalizeFailed` /
     `BackoffExhausted`) holds no lease and persists across a `serve` crash
     (the row and the count are persisted); only `Redeploy` leaves it.
   - **Invariants.** `ExhaustsOnlyAtCeiling` (an exhausted workload has
     `att ≥ CEIL`) and `ExhaustsOnlyOnACrashClassFailure` (an exhausted
     workload's last ending, ghost `g.lastEnd(a)`, is a crash-class
     failure — never a reclamation and never a `Redeploy`), both in
     `Safety`.
   A bound of `RESTART_BACKOFF_CEILING − 1` = 4 with `retry` always true
   would stop one failure short of the boundary and hide #324; exhaustion is
   inside the CID-lease protocol.
3. **A leased but not yet launched workload at a `serve` crash.** The lease's allocation has no row (the
   dispatch is held at `provision`; no dispatch writes a `Pending` row), so
   after the crash the workload's current allocation is its predecessor
   (or none). The model: the workload goes to `wait` with `att` = the
   predecessor's count (`att − 1` when its placement charged, `att`
   otherwise; 0 for a first placement) and the same `chg`, so the next
   `Assign` gives the new allocation the same count the lost one had
   (production mints a new id past every issued one, `:1377-1387`, and
   inserts the same count). For a crash-class or reclaimed predecessor this
   is production today. For a **generation replacement** (a `Redeploy`'s
   placement leased at the crash) the model places it again — the behaviour
   GH #325 is to deliver; production today loses that restart (§ *Restart
   decision*, "Defect RESTART-GEN-CRASH"; not fixed in #295). Run `RedeployLeasedAtServeCrashIsPlacedAgain` and hazard
   `crashLosesPlacedGeneration` encode it, both **pending #325** (item 9).
   A predecessor lease of a leased successor is lost with the pool
   (`pred = −1`).
4. **`Redeploy` from `failed`** is a generation replacement that keeps its
   count: the next `Assign` places a successor with `att` unchanged
   (`= CEIL` or more), and that successor's next crash-class failure
   exhausts the budget at once (`ex`, `att ≥ CEIL`). `Redeploy` is enabled
   only from `done` and `failed`, and only once `reclaimed` (DR6-CLOSE: the
   handler is unreachable before the listener bind that follows boot
   reclamation); the action map above pins both.
5. **The RESTART-SSOT runs, on `lease_conf_ok`** (each `.expect` names the
   projected `st`, `att`, `pst` and, at a failure, `retry` / `ex`; the
   sequences are those of item 7's granularity; CEIL = 5):
   - `FifthCrashAtCeilingBoundaryIsPlacedAgain` — `Assign`, `Launch`
     (`running`, `att = 0`), then four cycles of `VmmCrash`, `Assign`
     (`att` + 1, `pst = held`), `Launch` (`pst = retiring`), `Release`
     (`pst = none`): `running` with `att = 4`; then `VmmCrash` (the fifth
     failure, at `att = 4`) gives `ended` with `retry`, `¬ex`, its lease
     still Admitted; `Assign` leases the successor with `att = 5`,
     `pst = held`.
   - `FailureAtCeilingExhaustsTheBudget` — continues: `Launch`, `Release`,
     `VmmCrash` at `att = 5` gives `ended` with `ex`; `Finalize` gives
     `retiring` with `ex`; `Release` gives `failed` with no lease; no
     `Assign` is enabled.
   - `RedeployPlacesAnExhaustedWorkloadAgainWithItsCount` — from
     `FifthCrashAtCeilingBoundaryIsPlacedAgain`, through `failed` as above;
     `Redeploy` gives `wait` with `att = 5`, `chg` false; `Assign` leases with
     `att = 5` and no predecessor lease (the exhausted row holds none);
     `Launch`, `VmmCrash` gives `ended` with `ex` at once; `Finalize`,
     `Release` give `failed`.
   - `ServeCrashPlacesAWorkloadAtTheCeilingAgain` — from
     `FifthCrashAtCeilingBoundaryIsPlacedAgain`: `Launch` (`running`,
     `att = 5`, `pst = retiring`), `Crash` gives `wait` with `att = 5`,
     `chg` false, no lease; `Restart`, `Reclaim`, `Assign` leases with
     `att = 5`.
   - `ReclaimedWorkloadPastTheCeilingIsPlacedAgain` — continues: `Launch`,
     a second `Crash` / `Restart` / `Reclaim`, `Assign` leases with
     `att = 5` (repeated reclamations never charge); `Launch`, `VmmCrash`
     gives `ended` with `ex`.
   - `ServeCrashBeforeLaunchPlacesTheSuccessorAgainWithItsCount` —
     `Assign`, `Launch`, `VmmCrash` (`ended`, `retry`, `att = 0`), `Assign`
     leases the successor with `att = 1`, `pst = held`; `Crash` gives `wait`
     with `att = 0`, `chg` true and no lease (the predecessor lease is lost
     with the pool); `Restart`, `Assign` leases with `att = 1`.
   - `ServeCrashDuringFinalizeFinalizesAfterRestart` — from
     `FifthCrashAtCeilingBoundaryIsPlacedAgain`: `Launch`, `Release`,
     `VmmCrash` (`ended`, `ex`), `Finalize` (`retiring`, `ex`); `Crash`
     gives `ended` with `ex` and no lease (the terminal was not written);
     `Restart`, `Finalize` gives `failed`.
   - `StopOfAnEndedWorkloadReclaimsItsLease` — `Assign`, `Launch`,
     `VmmCrash` (`ended`, lease Admitted); `Stop` gives `retiring` with
     `¬retry`, `¬ex`; `Release` gives `done` with no lease.
   - `RedeployLeasedAtServeCrashIsPlacedAgain` — `Assign`, `Launch`,
     `Stop`, `Release` (`done`), `Redeploy`, `Assign` (`leased`); `Crash`
     gives `wait`, not `done`; `Restart`, `Assign` leases. **Pending #325**:
     checked on `lease_conf_325`, not `lease_conf_ok` (item 9).
   - `PoolExhaustedRestartCleansThePredecessorThenPlaces` (on `lease_ok`
     and on the three-offset recording main `lease_conf_three`, D-18, which
     the driver replays; unreachable on `lease_conf_ok`) — `Assign(1)`, `Launch(1)`, `Assign(2)`,
     `Launch(2)`, `VmmCrash(1)`, `Assign(1)` (the successor takes the last
     free offset; `pst(1) = held`), `VmmCrash(2)`: no free offset;
     `AssignRefused(2)` gives `wait` with `pst(2) = retiring`, `att(2) = 0`;
     `Release(2)` frees it; `Assign(2)` leases with `att(2) = 1`.
6. **Hazards and what each recorded check refutes** (each an `OFF` flag with
   a `lease_bug<Flag>` instance and, where a run is refuted, a
   `lease_conf_bug<Flag>` instance). Only checks in `checks.toml` are
   claimed:
   - `retryOffByOne` — an off-by-one decision:
     exhaust iff `att + 1 ≥ CEIL`, with **no exemptions** (the reclaim and
     generation exemptions both dropped). Refutes `ExhaustsOnlyAtCeiling`
     (`cid-lease-hazard-retry-off-by-one`).
   - `reclaimNotExempt` — only the platform-reclaim exemption removed
     (`att ≥ CEIL` exhausts after a reclamation). Refutes
     `ExhaustsOnlyOnACrashClassFailure` (`cid-lease-hazard-reclaim-not-exempt`).
   - `crashLosesPlacedGeneration` — production's behaviour today (GH
     #325): a generation replacement leased at a `serve` crash returns to
     `done` / `failed`. Refutes the run
     `RedeployLeasedAtServeCrashIsPlacedAgain`
     (`cid-lease-hazard-crash-loses-placed-generation-run`, instance
     `lease_conf_bugCrashLosesPlacedGeneration`, which must enable the #325
     window: `CFG = "conf_325"`, item 9). Pending #325.
   - `crashForgetsStop` — a `serve` crash forgets the stop intent. Refutes
     `StoppedWorkloadNotPlaced` (`cid-lease-hazard-crash-forgets-stop`).
   - `releaseBeforeVmm` — refutes `LeaseOutlivesVmm`
     (`cid-lease-hazard-release-before-vmm-outlives`). `assignBeforeReclaim`
     — refutes `NoLaunchClash` (`cid-lease-hazard-assign-before-reclaim`).
     `resetReboots` — refutes `GuestResetEndsVmm`
     (`cid-lease-hazard-reset-reboots`). `assignSplit` — refutes
     `CidUnique` (`cid-lease-hazard-assign-split`).
     `reclaimNeverCompletes` — refutes `EventuallyPlaced`
     (`cid-lease-hazard-reclaim-never-completes`).
   - **Hazards of item 7's rules.** The two invariants item 7's rules need
     are in `Safety`: `FailedHoldsNoLease` (a `failed` workload holds no
     lease: no offset maps to it) and `NoUntrackedLease` (every leased
     offset is its holder's placement lease `off` or predecessor lease
     `pred`; a lease no workload tracks is a leaked CID). Rule 7.1 (a VMM
     exit touches no lease), rule 7.2 (the successor is leased before the
     predecessor is retired) and rule 7.3 (the predecessor is cleaned only
     after the successor launches) are production's dispatch structure, not
     CID-safety rules: `Safety` holds without them, and the conformance run
     `VmmCrashFreesItsCidAndPlacementRetries` is their discriminator, so
     they carry no hazard check.
     - `refusalKeepsPredecessor` — rule 7.4 (a pool refusal cleans the
       predecessor at once): `AssignRefused` leaves `pst = held`, the
       cleanup deferred to the next `Launch`. Refutes the run
       `PoolExhaustedRestartCleansThePredecessorThenPlaces`
       (`cid-lease-hazard-refusal-keeps-predecessor-run`, instance
       `lease_bugRefusalKeepsPredecessor`, `CFG = "ok"`: the run is a
       `lease_ok` run). `Safety` holds: the refusal is reachable only on the
       three-offset instances, and a deferred cleanup delays the
       predecessor's release without leaking it.
     - `terminalBeforeRelease` — rule 7.5 (`FinalizeFailed` retires and
       releases before it writes the terminal): `Finalize` with a lease
       writes `failed` at once, the lease released by a later `Release`.
       Refutes `FailedHoldsNoLease`
       (`cid-lease-hazard-terminal-before-release`).
     - `tickDuringPredecessorTeardown` — the step boundary of rule 7.3 (no
       tick of a workload runs while its dispatch is held at a predecessor
       `teardown`; the dispatch runs inside its tick): the `predRetiring`
       guard dropped from `Assign`, `Stop` and `Finalize`. `Assign` from
       `ended` then overwrites a retiring predecessor lease. Refutes
       `NoUntrackedLease`
       (`cid-lease-hazard-tick-during-predecessor-teardown`).
     - The boot-reclamation guard of `Finalize` (item 7) is not a new rule:
       it is the existing NO-SURVIVE rule "no tick before reclamation",
       whose hazard `assignBeforeReclaim` removes it for `Assign`.
       `assignBeforeReclaim` does not bypass `Finalize`'s guard.
7. **Crash-class restart granularity (DR5-CLOSE).** Production's steps and dispatch boundaries
   for a crash-class failure of a Service below the ceiling, verified in
   `workload_lifecycle.rs` and `action_shim/mod.rs`:
   1. The VMM exits; the exit observer writes the terminal row. No dispatch
      touches the lease: only the action shim retires or releases a lease,
      and below the attachment cap the reclaim pass skips the current row
      while its restart is pending (`pending_restart_owner`,
      `workload_lifecycle.rs:399-442`, consulted at `:461-471`). The lease
      stays Admitted with no VMM.
   2. A tick past the backoff deadline emits `RestartAllocation` for the
      current row (`:1093-1238`; at the crash tick itself when the failed
      allocation has no `last_failure_seen_at`, `:1191-1197`). Its dispatch
      provisions the successor first (`action_shim/mod.rs:2707-2716` →
      `pool.assign`, `:1471`): two leases of the workload are held at once.
   3. The same dispatch starts the successor and writes its row, then runs
      `finish_restart` → `cleanup_restart_predecessor` (`:1760-1789`,
      called at `:1808`): it retires the predecessor's lease, stops its
      drivers, and tears down then releases it (`teardown_guest_network`,
      `:1591-1607`).
   4. A pool refusal at step 2 (`PoolExhausted`, `:540-548`) skips the
      successor and runs the predecessor cleanup (`:2719-2731`). A successor
      start failure retires and tears down the successor's lease first
      (`cleanup_restart_successor`, `:1734-1754`, `:2878-2892`), then the
      predecessor's.
   5. At the ceiling, the next tick emits `FinalizeFailed` before any
      backoff check (`workload_lifecycle.rs:1116-1179`); its dispatch
      retires the lease, tears it down and releases it, and only then writes
      the terminal (`action_shim/mod.rs:2146-2176`).
   **The model** (`cid_lease.qnt`):
   - `type A` gains `pred: int` (−1 none) and `pst: str`
     (`none` | `held` | `retiring`); `st` gains `ended` (the placement
     allocation ended crash-class; its lease, if any, still Admitted; no
     dispatch has run for it). `lease(o) = a` for both `off(a)` and
     `pred(a)`.
   - `vmmExit(a)` (used by `VmmCrash` and `GuestReset`) frees the device
     and sets `st = ended` with `retry = restartDecision(a, false, false)`,
     `ex = ¬retry`, `chg = retry`; the lease is unchanged. It does not go
     to `retiring`.
   - `Assign(a)` is enabled from `wait`, or from `ended` with `retry` and
     `off ≥ 0`, with `pst ≠ retiring`, a free offset and the existing
     guards. From `ended` it sets `pred = off`, `pst = held` and leases the
     new offset (`att' = placedAtt(a)`; `chg` keeps its meaning). From
     `ended` with `retry` and `off = −1` it is not enabled: `Crash` maps
     that state to `wait`.
   - New `AssignRefused(a)`: `up`, `reclaimed`, `st = ended`, `retry`,
     `off ≥ 0`, `pst = none`, `freeOffs = Set()`: `pred = off`,
     `pst = retiring`, `st = wait`, `off = −1`, `chg` true, `att`
     unchanged; ConfStep variant `AssignRefused({ a })`.
   - `Launch(a)` from `leased`: device free → `running` and, if
     `pst = held`, `pst = retiring`; device held (clash) → the successor
     `retiring` with the failure decision, `pst` unchanged (still `held`).
   - New `Finalize(a)`: `up`, `st = ended`, `ex`, `pst ≠ retiring`: with
     `off ≥ 0`, `st = retiring` (`ex` kept); with `off = −1`,
     `st = failed`. ConfStep variant `Finalize({ a })`.
   - `Stop(a)` is enabled from `running` or from `ended` with `off ≥ 0`,
     with `pst ≠ retiring`; both give `retiring` with `retry`, `ex`, `chg`
     false (the device release applies only from `running`).
   - `Release(a)`: if `st = retiring` (and the existing VMM guard), release
     `off` as today, except that an `ex` result is `ended` with `off = −1`
     when the retiring lease came from a clash (no terminal yet) and
     `failed` when it came from `Finalize`; then, if `pst = held`, set
     `pst = retiring`. Else if `pst = retiring`: `lease(pred) = 0`,
     `pred = −1`, `pst = none`, `st` unchanged. (A model-only field or the
     ghost may record whether a retiring lease came from `Finalize`; it is
     not projected — the projection reads `ex` and the row.)
   - `Crash`: `pred = −1`, `pst = none` for every workload; `ended` with
     `retry` → `wait` (`chg` true, `att` unchanged); `ended` with `ex`, and
     `retiring` with `ex`, → `ended` with `off = −1` (`ex` kept); the other
     mappings unchanged (a `leased` successor: `crashAtt`, `chg` kept).
   - `exhausted(a)` adds `st = ended ∧ ex`; `CidUnique` covers every held
     offset (`off` and `pred`, within and across workloads); `step` adds
     `Finalize(a)` and `AssignRefused(a)`; `EventuallyPlaced` treats
     `ended ∧ retry` like `wait` and adds `weakFair(Release(a))` (a held
     predecessor teardown completes).
   - The runs `VmmCrashFreesItsCidAndPlacementRetries` and
     `GuestResetEndsTheVmmAndPlacementRetries` are: `Assign`, `Launch`,
     `VmmCrash` / `GuestReset` → `ended` with `retry`, `dev(0) = 0`,
     `lease(0) = 1` (and `¬g.rebooted`); `Assign` → `leased` at offset 1,
     `pred = 0`, `pst = held`, `att = 1`; `Launch` → `running`,
     `dev(1) = 1`, `pst = retiring`, `lease(0) = 1`; `Release` →
     `pst = none`, `lease(0) = 0`. The item 5 runs take the sequences
     written there; each run is an evaluator check (`ci` per the
     60-second rule).
   - `retryOffByOne` disables the generation exemption of `Redeploy` along
     with the plain decision.
   **Guards, invariants and flags** (`cid_lease.qnt`,
   `hazard/cid_lease_hazards.qnt`, `checks.toml`, README):
   - `Finalize(a)` gains the guard `reclaimed` (strict: `assignBeforeReclaim`
     does not bypass it). `Redeploy(a)` gains the guard `reclaimed` too (the
     handler is reachable only after the listener bind that follows
     `converge`). Both guards keep conformance traces in production's boot
     order and carry no `Safety` property.
   - New invariants, both in `Safety`:
     `FailedHoldsNoLease = ALLOCS.forall(a => st(a) == "failed" implies
     OFFS.forall(o => lease.get(o) != a))` and
     `NoUntrackedLease = OFFS.forall(o => lease.get(o) != 0 implies { val b
     = lease.get(o); (hasOff(b) and al.get(b).off == o) or (hasPred(b) and
     al.get(b).pred == o) })`.
   - Three `OFF` flags, each with its `BUG_*` val and a hazard check:
     - `refusalKeepsPredecessor`: `AssignRefused` sets `pst = "held"`
       instead of `"retiring"`.
     - `terminalBeforeRelease`: `Finalize` with `off ≥ 0` sets
       `st = "failed"` (`off` kept, `retry`, `ex`, `chg` false, `g.fin`
       unchanged); `Release` gains the hazard-only branch
       `BUG_TERMINAL_BEFORE_RELEASE and st = failed and off ≥ 0`, which
       sets `lease(off) = 0`, `off = −1`.
     - `tickDuringPredecessorTeardown`: the `not(predRetiring(a))` guard is
       dropped from `Assign`, `Stop` and `Finalize`.
   - Instances (`hazard/cid_lease_hazards.qnt`):
     `lease_bugRefusalKeepsPredecessor` (`CFG = "ok"`, `REC = false`),
     `lease_bugTerminalBeforeRelease` and
     `lease_bugTickDuringPredecessorTeardown`. The `lease_bug*` instances
     use `CFG = "ok"`, all with `REC = false` (the `conf_ok` guard of item 9
     applies only with `REC`).
   - Checks (TLC exhaustive or evaluator runs, `ci` per the 60-second
     rule): `cid-lease-hazard-refusal-keeps-predecessor-run` (violation),
     `cid-lease-hazard-terminal-before-release` (`FailedHoldsNoLease`,
     violation), `cid-lease-hazard-tick-during-predecessor-teardown`
     (`NoUntrackedLease`, violation), and the four item-9 checks. A hazard
     is one check per decision, not one per clause or form. If a check
     that the delta expects to hold is violated, the counterexample is a
     finding for the architect, not an `expect` change.
