9. **The #325 window is excluded from the conformance main (pending #325).**
   Production loses a `Redeploy`'s placement leased at a `serve` crash
   (GH #325); the model places it again. So that no randomized
   `#[quint_run]` trace on `lease_conf_ok` replays a state production
   handles differently, `Crash` is not enabled on the recording conformance
   main while some workload is `leased` with `g.pendingGen ≠ ""`: in the
   spec, `CONF` becomes `CFG.in(Set("conf_ok", "conf_325"))` and `Crash`
   gains the guard `not(CFG == "conf_ok" and REC) or ALLOCS.forall(a =>
   not(al.get(a).st == "leased" and g.pendingGen.get(a) != ""))`. The new
   main `lease_conf_325` (`CFG = "conf_325"`, `REC = true`) keeps the window
   and carries the run `RedeployLeasedAtServeCrashIsPlacedAgain`
   (the check
   `cid-lease-run-conf-325-redeploy-leased-at-serve-crash-is-placed-again`;
   its DISTILL `#[quint_test]` is `#[ignore = "pending #325"]`), and
   `lease_conf_bugCrashLosesPlacedGeneration` uses `CFG = "conf_325"` so its
   run fails for the hazard's reason, not for the guard. `lease_five`
   (`REC = false`) and the model-checking instances keep the window. When
   #325 lands, its change deletes the guard and `lease_conf_325` and
   activates the test.
   **The guard's own check (DR6-CLOSE).** The run
   `CrashIsNotEnabledInThe325Window` — `Assign(1)`, `Launch(1)`, `Stop(1)`,
   `Release(1)` (`done`), `Redeploy(1)`, `Assign(1)` (`leased`,
   `g.pendingGen(1) ≠ ""`; the last `.expect` before `Crash` also asserts
   `up`, `bootLeft ≠ 0` and `inGenWindow(1)`, every other precondition of
   `Crash`), then `Crash` `.fail()` — is checked twice:
   `cid-lease-run-conf-ok-crash-is-not-enabled-in-the-325-window` on
   `lease_conf_ok`, expect `holds` (the guard refuses `Crash` there), and
   `cid-lease-run-conf-325-crash-is-not-enabled-in-the-325-window` on
   `lease_conf_325`, expect `violation` (`Crash` is enabled in the window
   without the guard, so the run's `.fail()` fails). The pair shows the
   guard, not some other condition, is what refuses `Crash`. Its positive
   twin `CrashIsEnabledInThe325WindowWithoutTheGuard` takes the same prefix,
   then `Crash` with `.expect(Safety and not(up) and st(1) == "wait")`:
   `cid-lease-run-conf-325-crash-is-enabled-in-the-325-window-without-the-guard`
   on `lease_conf_325`, expect `holds`, and
   `cid-lease-run-conf-ok-crash-is-enabled-in-the-325-window-without-the-guard`
   on `lease_conf_ok`, expect `violation`. All four are evaluator checks,
   with their expected outcomes in `evidence/summary.json`. When
   #325 lands, all four are deleted with the guard.

**`owner_flows` `flows_conf`, host side** (`overdrive-control-plane`; the
model-checking instances `flows_ok`, `flows_one` and `flows_sess` share this
map and are not replayed)

| Var | Source |
|---|---|
| `alloc` | O QPROJ-3 `cids[cid].phase`; absent there → O QPROJ-2 (`Retiring` while the pool lease is Retiring, else `Absent`) |
| `gen` | O QPROJ-2 / QPROJ-3 `launch`, relabelled |
| `quiesced` | O QPROJ-3 `admission` |
| `claim` | O QPROJ-3 `cids[cid].session` |
| `sess(c).st` | `pending` ⇔ S `queued`; `reading` ⇔ O `cids[cid].unread`; `live` ⇔ O `cids[cid].session = c` ∧ ¬S `peer_gone`; `dead` ⇔ O `session = c` ∧ S `peer_gone`; `closed` ⇔ S `closed_by_owner`; `none`: stimulus |
| `flows(f).st`, `.req`, `.inFlight` | `queued` ⇔ S `queued`; `accepted` ⇔ O `cids[cid].guest_flows[key]` = `Registered` (`Nothing` → `req` 0, `Partial` → 1); `read`, `connecting`, `paired` ⇔ O `Attributed`, `Connecting`, `Paired` (`req` 2); `closed` ⇔ S `closed_by_owner`; `inFlight` ⇔ O `Connecting` for a flow the owner holds; for a closed flow `inFlight` is model-only (a connect completion in flight that the seam delivers and the owner must discard: the step fails if production sends `Paired`) |
| `hf(h).st` | `req` ⇔ O `cids[cid].dials[h]` = `AwaitingReply`; `paired` ⇔ `Paired { .. }`; `closed` ⇔ `dials[h]` absent after it was present; `none`: never issued |
| `hf(h).gen` | O `cids[cid].launch` of the CID holding `dials[h]`, relabelled |
| `dl.res(h)` | C: the dialer's `GuestStreamDial::dial` call for slot `h` — `pending` while its future has not returned; then `Ok` / `Refused` / `TimedOut` / `PairingDeadline` / `NotServing` / `Quiesced` / `NoSession` / `Unreachable` as it returned; `Cancelled` ↔ the driver dropped the future (`DialCancel`), which returns no result. An in-flight dial the owner ends returns the admission result of the cause: `Quiesced` (first quiescence hold), `NotServing` (teardown), `NoSession` (observed session loss); a VMM exit with the dial in flight returns `Unreachable` (`ECONNRESET`). With the VM gone a new dial returns `Unreachable` while the session's loss is unobserved and `NoSession` once it is observed (§ *Driving port — guest stream dial*) |
| `act` | C: the result of the `owner.activate(&plan)` call made in that step — `Activated`, `ControlSessionPending`, `QuiescenceLatched`, or `LeaseRetiring` for `Err(PostconditionMismatch { operation: ForwardingActivate, .. })`; `none` in every other step |
| `vmGen`, `vmUp`, `sess(c).gen`, `flows(f).gen` | stimulus |
| `gf`, `gSess`, `toHostPaired`, `toHostRefused`, `toGuestAbort`, `toHostAbort`, `dl.tout` | model-only (guest state and messages in flight; the driver plays their delivery from the trace) |
| `badPaired`, `badAct`, `crossMsg`, `heldByOther`, `resurrected`, `abortDiscarded`, `phantom`, `dl.earlyDl`, `dl.lateReply` | ghost |
| `drvLive`, `bclaim`, `bcn`, `readyCross`, `bHeldByOther` | constant in this instance |
| `conf_step` | model-only, write-only step record, read through `Config::nondet = &["flows_conf::owner_flows::conf_step"]` (D-UP-1); never projected |

| Action | Production call or fault |
|---|---|
| `Provision` | the pool's `assign`, then `owner.provision(&plan)` |
| `VmStart` / `VmStop` | seam: the guest of that launch comes up / dies (K-A2′: accepted connections fail at their next I/O, queued ones keep their buffered record); at `VmStop` the seam resets the V_h of every in-flight dial of that launch (the device-release orphan sweep, `ECONNRESET`), so each such dial returns `Unreachable` |
| `Activate`, `Teardown`, `Release` | `owner.activate(&plan)` → `Activated`; `owner.teardown(&plan)` → `Ok` (an in-flight dial returns `NotServing`); `pool.release(&a)` |
| `ActivatePending`, `ActivateQuiesced`, `ActivateRetiring` | the refused activations: `owner.activate(&plan)` with no live control session → `ControlSessionPending`; while quiesced → `QuiescenceLatched`; for a Retiring CID → `Err(PostconditionMismatch { operation: ForwardingActivate, .. })`; each changes no owner state |
| `Quiesce` / `Restore` | `owner.quiesce()` → a `QuiescenceHold` the driver keeps / `owner.restore(hold)` |
| `GuestOpenSession(c)`, `GuestOpenFlow(f)` | seam: queue a 1243 / 1240 connection from the CID with its `ControlOpen` / request (token of `vmGen`) buffered |
| `WorkloadOpenSession(c)` | seam: queue a second 1243 connection from the CID with a `ControlOpen` of the live token buffered — the racing first connect of L-3 (R5-18), opened by a guest workload, not the guest owner (D-UP-8, approved 2026-10-14) |
| `HostAcceptSession(c)`, `HostAcceptFlow(f)` | seam releases the accept to the owner |
| `HostReadOpen(c)`, `HostReadReqN(f, n)` (`HostReadReq`) | seam releases the buffered record (for a request, in the trace's 1 or 2 pieces) |
| `HostClaimSession(c)` | hazard-only (`sessionSplitClaim`) |
| `HostSessionLoss(c)`, `HostDeadSessionLoss(c)` | seam: the session's peer ends; the owner processes it (a trace shows `HostDeadSessionLoss` from `dead` with the same mapping) |
| `HostStartConnect(f)` | seam releases the owner's connect effect |
| `HostConnectDone(f)`, `HostConnectDiscard(f)` | seam completes the peer connect (for a live / an aborted flow); for a live flow the owner attaches the pair on `SimFlowForwarder` and writes `Paired` in that dispatch (EVMOD-PAIR) |
| `HostFlowEndsMsg(f, msg)` (`HostFlowEnds`) | seam: a scripted refusal, connect failure or peer error, or `SimClock` past `FLOW_REQUEST_DEADLINE` (no message for an unattributed flow) |
| `HostCheckFlow`, `HostRegisterFlow` | hazard-only (`admitSplit`) |
| `DialOpen(h)` | `GuestStreamDial::dial(target, DialPurpose::Relay)` with `target` = the lease's guest address and a declared port; the seam holds the owner's V_h connect and request write and the driver releases them |
| `DialNotServing(h, declared)`, `DialQuiesced(h)`, `DialNoSession(h)`, `DialUnreachable(h)` | `GuestStreamDial::dial(target, DialPurpose::Relay)` with an address that is not an Active lease or an undeclared port / while quiesced / while no session is live as the owner observes it (including a gone VM whose session loss was observed) / with the VM gone while the owner has not yet observed the session's loss (the seam fails the vsock connect with `ENODEV`); each returns its typed error immediately |
| `GuestAcceptV(h)`, `GuestPairOrRefuseOk(h, ok)` (`GuestPairOrRefuse`), `GuestConnectTimesOut(h)`, `GuestRecvAbort(h)`, `GuestSeesHostClose(h)`, `GuestAcceptedError(h)`, `GuestSessionLossObserved(c)`, `GuestQueueReset(h)` | stimulus (the guest side) |
| `HostRecvPaired(h)`, `HostRecvRefused(h)`, `HostRecvTimedOut(h)`, `HostRecvAbort(h)` | seam releases the guest's `Paired` / `Refused { errno }` / `TimedOut { errno }` / `Abort` on the session to the owner |
| `HostAbortAccept(h)` | seam: an error on V_h (a failed vsock write or read) |
| `HostDialDeadline(h)` | `SimClock` past the slot's `GUEST_DIAL_PAIRING_DEADLINE` |
| `DialCancel(h)` | the driver drops the pending `GuestStreamDial::dial` future of slot `h`; the owner ends the dial as at the pairing deadline (§ *Driving port — guest stream dial*, Cancellation); the future returns no result |
| `GuestNeverReplies(h)` | seam: the guest's handling of V_g on a running VM stalls and writes no `Paired`, `Refused` or `TimedOut` (the scripted guest never answers), so only `HostDialDeadline(h)` can end the dial. A stimulus, not an owner call: a guest that never answers is the guest's behaviour, which `SimGuestOwnerIo` scripts; the host owner under test has no state that produces it |

**`owner_flows` `flows_conf`, guest side** (`overdrive-init`):
`gf(h).st` ← `acc` ⇔ O QPROJ-5 `accepted[h] = Accepted`, `attached` ⇔
`Paired { .. }`, `closed` / `tomb` ⇔ `accepted[h]` absent after it was
present (`tomb` is the model's record of a flow closed after its session
was lost, model-internal), `reset` ⇔ S
`reset_in_queue`, `none` ⇔ never held and not queued, `silent` → stimulus
(`GuestNeverReplies`: the guest holds V_g and never answers — the guest's behaviour, scripted by `SimGuestOwnerIo`, not a state the owner under test produces); `gf(h).c` → stimulus
(the session connection, relabelled by the bijection); `gf(h).gen` → ghost
(one guest owner holds one launch). `toHostPaired`, `toHostRefused`,
`toHostAbort`, `toGuestAbort`, `dl` → model-only (the replies the guest
writes are consumed from the seam by the driver as the trace's next host
step; a reply the guest did not write fails that step). `gSess` (the
connection the guest owner holds as its session, 0 = none; D-UP-8, approved
2026-10-14) ← O QPROJ-5 `session`: `session ⇔ gSess ≠ 0`, compared once the
seam has delivered every released session event; while the VM is down the
guest owner does not exist and the driver projects `session = false` (it
constructs a fresh owner at `VmStart`). The host's `sess` table is not a
source for it. Every other host variable → stimulus.
`WorkloadOpenSession(c)` → stimulus (a guest workload's connection, not a
guest-owner call; `gSess` is unchanged). Actions: `GuestOpenSession(c)` →
`dispatch_next` with no session — the first dispatch, or the
`CONTROL_RECONNECT_BACKOFF` deadline on `SimGuestClock` after an observed
loss — issues `start_connect_host(Control)`; the seam completes it and the
owner writes its `ControlOpen` (token of `vmGen`) with `write_host`. An owner
that issues that connect while a flow of the lost session is still open, or
while it holds a session it has not observed lost (D-UP-8), fails the step,
so DG-5-F's reconnect rule is checked against `overdrive-init`. `GuestOpenFlow(f)` → the seam injects `OutboundCaptured`
for an application `connect()` (its intake child accepted, nothing
attached); the owner's dispatches issue `start_connect_host(FlowStream)` and
`write_request` (token of `vmGen`), and `awaiting_paired[f]` appears in
QPROJ-5.
`DialOpen(h)` → seam queues V_g with its `TcpAccept`
request (peer = gateway:0, the live token); `GuestAcceptV(h)` → seam releases
the accept and the request; `GuestPairOrRefuseOk(h, ok)` → seam completes the
application connect (scripted accepted / refused); `GuestConnectTimesOut(h)`
→ `SimGuestClock` advanced to that flow's `GUEST_INBOUND_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`
deadline (the owner aborts C and writes `TimedOut`); `GuestRecvAbort(h)` →
seam releases the host's `Abort`; `GuestSeesHostClose(h)` /
`GuestQueueReset(h)` → seam delivers the host's close of V_h (K-A4) after /
before the guest's accept — after it, a `Hangup { ReadHangup }` on the
accepted, unattached V_g while `accepted[h]` is `Accepted` (DG-5-E), or the
pair's end record once `Paired`; `GuestAcceptedError(h)` → seam delivers
`Hangup { Error }` on the accepted V_g (DG-5-E); `GuestSessionLossObserved(c)`
→ seam ends the session; the owner aborts every flow of it in that one
dispatch (DG-5-F); host actions → stimulus. Every guest timer action →
`SimGuestClock` advanced to exactly that timer's production deadline
(DG-5-A), then dispatch until quiescent (DG-5-Q).

**`owner_flows` `flows_beacon_conf`** (`overdrive-worker`; `Config::nondet =
&["flows_beacon_conf::owner_flows::conf_step"]`; the model-checking instance
`flows_beacon` shares the map): `drvLive` ← O QPROJ-4
`live`; `bclaim` ← O `claims`; `bcn(b).st` ← `pending` ⇔ S `queued`,
`reading` ⇔ O `unread`, `live` ⇔ O `claims`, `closed` ⇔ S
`closed_by_driver`; `vmGen`, `vmUp`, `alloc`, `gen`, `bcn(b).gen` →
stimulus; `readyCross`, `bHeldByOther` → ghost; every flow, session and dial
variable → constant in this instance. The instance enables only the actions
with a VM-driver driving port or stimulus (D-UP-20): `Provision` (a new
launch token), `VmStart`, `VmStop`, `DriverStop` and the beacon actions.
Actions: `VmStart` → `VmDriver::start` of a spec whose transport carries the
launch's token (`SimVmm::create` `Ok`); `VmStop` → `SimVmm` process exit
(K-A2′ on the beacon seam), which the driver observes and handles in the
per-CID step that ends the launch's liveness and releases its beacon claim
(D-UP-9, approved 2026-10-14: the CID leaves `live` and `claims` there, not
at `driver.stop`); `DriverStop` → `VmDriver::stop` (the hazard flag
`driverStopKeepsClaim` leaves the beacon claim held; hazard-only);
`GuestOpenBeacon(b)` → seam queues a 1234 connection with READY (token of
`vmGen`) buffered; `HostAcceptBeacon(b)` / `HostReadReady(b)` → seam
releases the accept / READY; `Provision` → stimulus (a new assignment,
`GuestTransportAssignment::new` with `LaunchToken::generate(&SimEntropy)`);
activation, teardown, release, quiescence and every owner session, flow
and dial action → never enabled in this instance.

**`fwd_pair`** (conformance main `pair_conf`; per side `s` under test: `h`
in `overdrive-control-plane`, `g` in `overdrive-init`). The driving ports
are the owner's dispatch (the host owner's event step; the guest's
`dispatch_next`) and the `FlowForwarder` calls it makes; the forwarder's
runs and callbacks, the far ends and the side not under test are the Sim
adapters' scripted facts (`SimFlowForwarder`, Sim sockets), named arbiters
paired with V-EV-END, V-EV-CTL, V-EV-PAIR and the module's Tier-3 suite.

| Var (at side `s`) | Source |
|---|---|
| `ctx(s)` | O `open` while the owner holds a context; `released` after the owner's context was released (`CtxRelease`, the owner's death included) — S `SimFlowForwarder` context state, arbiter. `gone` is **stimulus-only, not projected**: the model writes it only in `VmmExit`, for side `g`, in the same step that sets the stimulus `vmUp` false (`fwd_pair.qnt:1084-1091`), and nothing sets `vmUp` true again after `Init` (`:516`) or reopens side `g` (`Reopen` requires `s == "h"`, `:667`), so in every reachable state `ctx(g) = gone ⇔ ¬vmUp`; this is a checked invariant of the spec, `CtxGoneIffVmDown` (`ctx.get("g") == "gone" iff not(vmUp)`, in `Safety` and `DgramSafety`; no witness check stands for it on the stream main because the named run `VmmExitAbortsHostHalf` reaches the state, and the datagram witness `fwd-pair-dgram-witness-vmm-exit` on `pair_dgram` is kept), rather than an argued one. **What the init driver compares after `VmmExit`.** The same model step also writes `pr(g).ph = gone` (unless the flow had already `ended` or been `refused`) and `ep(g) = gone` (`:1088-1089`). After `VmmExit` no guest kernel or guest owner exists to observe, so the init driver gates on the `VmmExit` stimulus it applied itself: from that step on it compares none of `ctx(g)`, the `pr(g)` fields, or the guest-side socket view (`vs(g)` and the guest-held halves' facts in `dir(d)`). Stimulus is driven and never projected (`vmUp` is listed as stimulus below), so the driver's own record that it applied `VmmExit` is the stimulus, not a projection from its bookkeeping (`testing.md` checklist item 5). Host-side variables (`ctx(h)`, `pr(h)`, `vs(h)`, which `VmmExit` sets `err`, and the host halves) are compared at every step as before. Before `VmmExit`, `ctx(g)` is `open` from O and `released` from the arbiter; `gone` is never projected from a driver flag (the driver keeps no `gone` flag). Side `h` never reaches `gone` |
| `pr(s)` `.ph`, `.out`, `.cause`, `.errno` | O the flow's phase (QPROJ-3 `guest_flows[key]` / `dials[id]` / `datagrams[id]`; QPROJ-5 `flows[id]` / `accepted[id]` / `slots`), and the end record the owner consumed, read through the owner's `last_consumed_end` (host `flow_observation()`, guest `guest_observation()`; D-11): when its `id` is the flow's pair or watch id, `out` / `cause` / `errno` are its `outcome`, its `SocketError` errno included (QPROJ-8). The driver never compares a record it took from `SimGuestFlowIo` / `SimGuestOwnerIo` itself |
| `pr(s)` `.rec`, `.nrec`, `.closed`, `.byRel` | `rec = read` ⇔ O the owner consumed the record: `last_consumed_end.id` is the flow's pair or watch id (the flow has left its table, `held_flows` dropped); `rec = queued` ⇔ S the flow's record is in the end queue of the context that attached it — the row of `SimForwarderDevice::contexts()` at the flow's `cgen` (row index `cgen − 1`; the host device has one owner per run), keyed by the flow's `ForwardId` in `SimContextState::queued_ends`, released contexts included, so a record left unread in a replaced context is compared (D-4); `rec = none` otherwise. `nrec` = 1 if the owner consumed the flow's record, plus the number of its records in that row's `queued_ends`. `closed` ⇔ O the flow left the owner's table and the S vsock half (`vsock_half`, row `vs(s)`) is closed. `byRel` ⇔ the flow left the owner's table and no record was produced for it — the owner consumed none and the row at its `cgen` holds none, or it was never attached (its context's release with the pair live, a close of a flow it never attached, or a `HalfEnded` refusal); a flow the `Forwarder` recovery dropped after an owner abort had queued its record is not `byRel` (its record is `queued` in the replaced context) — S arbiter for the record's absence |
| `pr(s).cgen`, `gen(s)`, `oldCtx(s)` | QPROJ-8, "Context-generation variables" |
| `dir(d)` `.srcEnd`, `.srcShut`, `.dstEnd`, `.dstShut` | O `FlowForwarder::pair_state(pair)` of the side holding the half: `source_end`, `target_shut` (QPROJ-8) |
| `dir(d)` `.q0`, `.q1`, `.q2`, `.got`, `.eof`, `.rst`, `.shutRd`, `.wr`, `.wfin` | S the Sim sockets' queues and the far readers' and writers' facts, arbiters |
| `vs(s)` `.ps`, `.sent`, `.err`, `.cls`, `.st`, `.sshut` | S the per-half facts of side `s`'s vsock half, arbiter, read on the half's shared `SimSocket` (D-5): `.ps` `received_shutdown()`, `.sent` `sent_shutdown()`, `.err` `sk_err()`, `.cls` `recorded_class()`, `.st` `vsock_state()`, `.sshut` `own_send_shut()`. Host side: the half is `SimGuestFlowIo::vsock_half(flow)` (QPROJ-7), which keeps returning it after the owner closed it; guest side: the handle `SimGuestOwnerIo` issued for the flow's `V_g`, kept the same way. After the owner's close the accessors report the half's facts at its close |
| `tcpErr(s)`, `attRes(s)`, `attEnded(s)`, `strmAbort`, `hres`, `guestAbortSent` | QPROJ-8, "Ended-half, watch and stream variables" |
| `ctl(d)`, `terr(s)`, `ep(s)`, `dg(d)`, `vmUp`, `mode` | S scripted facts / stimulus |
| `loss`, `lost`, `tcls`, `ucls`, `vs(s)` `.att`, `.clsAt`, `.ncls`, `.snap`, `.misc`, `gh` (every field except `gh.unclassified`, which is O `inventory().unclassified_eof`), `conf_step` | model-only (QPROJ-8) |

| Action | Production call or fault |
|---|---|
| `InitWith(m)` | the driver builds the owner over `SimFlowForwarder` for one flow of mode `m` (stream: a TcpConnect; watch: a dial; dgram: a datagram association) |
| `Attach(s)` | side `s`'s owner dispatch that attaches the pair (host before `Paired`; guest TcpConnect on `Paired`; guest TcpAccept and datagram as pinned in "Sides and pairs") or installs the dial's watch |
| `Abort(s)` | side `s`'s owner aborts the id (teardown, quiescence, session loss): `FlowForwarder::abort` |
| `CtxRelease(s)` | side not under test: the Sim context's release (`SimFlowForwarder::release`, scripted). Side under test `h`, one mapping chosen by the state, never by what follows: with no host pair or watch live, the `Forwarder` recovery's context close — the driver damages `Forwarder` with a scripted context `Io` failure, the supervisor's repair runs `abort_all` (a no-op, nothing is live) and `close_forwarder`, and its `open_forwarder` is held by the seam until `Reopen(h)`; with a pair or watch live, the host owner's death — the driver drops the host owner with its context, after which the host owner's O facts are not projected (no owner exists; production's successor is a new `serve` process whose boot reclamation ends the VM, NO-SURVIVE) and only S and C facts are. Side under test `g`: the driver drops the guest owner with its context (the guest owner is PID 1; its death ends the VM, RESET-EXIT) (D-3 to D-5) |
| `TakeEnd(s)` | the owner's dispatch on its context's readiness: `take_end` and the flow's release; on the host this one dispatch also closes the flow's descriptors (the host's `OwnerClose`, below) |
| `OwnerClose(s)` | guest: the owner closes the flow's descriptors after the record (datagram: the slot-queue discard), a dispatch of its own. Host: not a separate owner step — the host owner closes in the dispatch that reads the record, so the model takes `OwnerClose(h)` together with `TakeEnd(h)` as one step (rule 1 of the host-side projection pins below) |
| `Hop0(d)`, `Hop1(d)`, `HopEnd0(d)`, `HopEnd1(d)`, `VCtl(d)`, `FwdErr(s)` | `SimFlowForwarder` runs and callbacks (scripted) |
| `Write`, `Fin`, `Read`, `ReadEof`, `ShutRd`, `VmmExit`, `TrailingRst`, `SendDg`, `DRead`, `UdpBlock`, `UdpUnblock`, `UdpErr` | Sim socket and far-end faults (scripted); `VmmExit` is `SimVmm` exit, which sets the host half's `sk_err` and state — the first of the orphan sweep's two steps; its `sk_error_report` is the separate `FwdErr(h)` (T-9); `ReadEof` on the dialer is the stream's resolved result |
| `TcpRst(s, after_fin)` (T-1) | Sim: the far TCP peer resets after or before its FIN; `SimFlowForwarder` runs the half's `sk_error_report` in the same step. `after_fin` equals the far writer's FIN in the state; a trace names it explicitly |
| `Attach(s)` with an ended half (T-4) | the same owner dispatch as `Attach(s)`; `SimFlowForwarder::attach` / `watch` returns `HalfEnded { side, errno }` from the half's scripted state, and the owner ends the flow in that dispatch |
| `Abort(h)` on a watch (T-5) | the host owner's stream abort (quiescence's first hold, teardown, session loss): `FlowForwarder::abort(watch)` and the owner's `Abort { flow }` write, in one owner step; the pending stream call the driver holds returns |
| `GuestAbort(g)` (T-5) | the guest owner's `dispatch_next` of `Abort { flow }`: `FlowForwarder::abort(pair)` |
| `HolderDrop(h)` (T-6) | the driver drops its `GuestStream` |
| `HolderEnd(h)` (T-5, T-9) | the driver's own `read` on its `GuestStream`'s `V_h` in the Sim vsock socket, which scripts the end fact (`Eof`, or `Err`); not a driving port of the owner |
| `Reopen(s)` | the host owner's `Forwarder` recovery: `abort_all` (`Abort` in the model), the drop of the old `KernelFlowForwarder` (`CtxRelease`), `KernelFlowForwarder::open()` and `probe()` (`Reopen`) |
| `CloseUnattached(g)` | the guest owner's close of a flow it has not attached (`dispatch_next`) |
| `DgHalfClose(d)` (T-7) | a scripted vsock fact of the Sim adapter: a datagram-mode `0x2` from the peer, which no owner path produces (U-EV-5, U-EV-9) |
| `DropRecord(s)`, `AttachRead(s)` / `AttachHook(s)`, `UnclassifiedEof(s)`, `WatchRecord(h)`, `SendShutLate(s)` | hazard-only (`UnclassifiedEof` is otherwise the `unclassified_eof` counter of `inventory()`) |

**Host-side projection pins (D-3 to D-5).** The host
driver's per-step comparison covers `strmAbort` (the dial-entry lifetime
rule), `pr(h).rec` / `.nrec` across a replaced context (the device's
context table with its end queues), `attRes(h)` after the flow has left the
owner's table (`forwarder_attached` / `forwarder_attach_ended`), and
`vs(h)` in full (`vsock_half`). Two rules of `fwd_pair.qnt` follow from the
production steps:

1. **Host close with the record.** On side `h` outside watch mode (in watch
   mode the holder owns `V_h` and `OwnerClose` is not enabled), `TakeEnd(h)` also performs
   `OwnerClose(h)`'s effect (`closed`, the vsock close's `{S, R}`, the TCP
   half's linger clearing) in the same step, and `OwnerClose(h)` is not
   enabled on its own: the host owner reads the record and closes in one
   dispatch, so no production state lies between them. The guest's
   `OwnerClose(g)` stays a separate action.
2. **A host owner death is final in the trace.** `Reopen(h)` is enabled
   only after a `CtxRelease(h)` that found no host pair or watch live (the
   recovery's close). A `CtxRelease(h)` with one live is the host owner's
   death: production has no in-process successor, so no `Reopen(h)` and no
   host owner action follows it. The driver drives it as the seam's
   process exit plus dropping the runtime the owner's tasks run on (S-3).
   That death is more graceful than a SIGKILL: dropping the runtime runs
   the owner tasks' destructors, which a real death never runs. The cell
   proves the modelled protocol only; that nothing the owner holds needs a
   destructor to be released at a real death is the Tier-3 `serve`-death
   cell's (every far end reset after `kill_for_test`) and V-EV-CTL's (the
   kernel's context release), not this driver's.

**`flow_quota`** (`overdrive-control-plane`; conformance main `quota_conf`,
the configuration of `quota_ok`: three allocations with quota 1 over a
node of two flow places)

| Var | Source |
|---|---|
| `slot(s).own` | O `cids[cid].held_flows` for every allocation's CID, and the place ↔ flow bijection (a flow holds a node flow place from admission to the owner's read of its end record) with O `cids[cid].alloc` of the CID holding the flow; a place with no held flow ↦ 0 |
| `slot(s).st` | `active` ⇔ the flow is held and `pair_state` shows no direction ended; `half` ⇔ one direction has `source_end = Some(Clean)` and `target_shut`, the other open; `ended` ⇔ the pair's end record is queued and not yet read (S `SimFlowForwarder` `queued_ends`, arbiter); `free` ⇔ no flow (QPROJ-3, QPROJ-8) |
| `slot(s).fwd` | S the pair is live in `SimFlowForwarder` (attached, no end record queued), arbiter — model-only for the `clash` ghost |
| `endq` — the places whose end records are queued and not yet read, in queue order (D-12) | S `SimFlowForwarder` `queued_ends` of the context row the owner holds, in queue order, each record's `ForwardId` relabelled to its place through the place ↔ flow bijection — the same arbiter `slot(s).st = ended` reads, so the two cannot disagree. Tier-3 pair: `take_end` returns the oldest queued record (the `FlowForwarder` contract); the module suite (EVMOD-REC, DELIVER step 4) carries the cell `take_end_returns_records_in_end_order`: pair A is ended and its record observed queued (the context's readiness and `OVD_FWD_INVENTORY.queued_ends` = 1) before pair B is ended, so the queue order is fixed by an explicit sequence, not by EVMOD-WQ's per-CPU completion; then two `take_end` calls return A's record, then B's, compared in order. The existing `end_record_abi.rs:69-108` sorts the ids before comparing and does not discharge this. `ReadEnd` takes the head of `endq` |
| `g` | ghost |

| Action | Production call or fault |
|---|---|
| `Admit(a)` | seam: the guest of `a` opens a TcpConnect flow; the seam releases accept, request, connect; the owner attaches the pair and sends `Paired` |
| `Refuse(a)` | the same, refused at admission with the typed capacity outcome (§ *Typed error taxonomy*): the flow is closed, `held_flows` of `a`'s CID unchanged |
| `HalfClose(s)` | Sim: the far end of the place's flow sends FIN; the forwarder carries it after the last accepted byte |
| `Complete(s)` | Sim: the other direction ends cleanly; the pair completes and queues its record |
| `Abort(s)` | Sim: the far end resets, or the owner aborts the id |
| `ReadEnd(s)` | the owner's dispatch reads the pair's end record and releases the place (EVMOD-AB) |

**`udp_slots`, guest side** (`overdrive-init`; instance `slots_conf`):
`slots(s).owned`, `.sock`, `.dest`, `.fid`, `.attached` ← O QPROJ-5 `slots`
(`owner`, `association`, `attached.is_some()`; slot `s` ↔ the slot socket's
address);
`slots(s).parked` ← S the slot socket's receive queue (Sim socket, arbiter);
`ready` ← S `readiness`;
`releasePending` ← S `release_reports`; `toHostAbort`, `toHostEnd`,
`toGuestPaired`, `toGuestRefused`, `toGuestAbort` → model-only; `sockAlive`,
`host` → stimulus; `nextFid`, `guestEnded`, `slots(s).holders`, `endedNoNew`
→ ghost / model-internal (their effect is compared through `fid` and the
action's enabledness); `misdelivered`, `lateIgnored`, `staleReassoc` → ghost; `picks`, `residue` → hazard-only. Actions:
`AppClaim`, `AppSendOnSlot` → seam: the application sends to `(k, d)`;
`GuestReady(s, cur)` → seam releases that readiness event; `GuestRecvPaired`,
`GuestRecvEnd` → seam releases the host's message; `GuestPairingTimeout(s)` →
`SimGuestClock` past `FLOW_PAIRING_DEADLINE` for the slot's association;
`SockClose(k)` / `SockCloseReportLost(k)` → seam: the socket is released with
/ without a report; `GuestReleaseSock(k)` → seam releases the report;
`GuestAuditIdle(idle)` (`GuestAudit`) → `SimGuestClock` to the next audit tick
(DG-5-A; it also performs the idle release of every slot idle for
`GUEST_DATAGRAM_SLOT_IDLE`. In the model the idle release applies only to a
routed (`Paired`) slot, with no condition on other slots: a slot awaiting
`Paired` reaches its 5 s pairing deadline long before its 120 s idle,
D-UP-20); `AppPick`, `AppTake`, `Refill(s)` → hazard-only;
host actions → stimulus. `MAXFID` is a model-checking bound with no
production counterpart (DG-5-B): it only disables minting, and the `conf`
instance sizes it so no trace within the driver's step bound reaches it.

**`udp_slots`, host side** (`overdrive-control-plane`): `host(i).st` ←
`req` / `paired` ⇔ O QPROJ-3 `cids[cid].datagrams[i].phase` (`AwaitingPaired` / `Paired`), `closed` ⇔ S `closed_by_owner`
for its legs; `toGuestPaired`, `toGuestRefused`, `toGuestAbort` →
model-only; every guest variable, `host(i).sock`, `.dest`, `.slot` →
stimulus. Actions: `GuestReady` that starts association `i` → seam queues
its one 1240 stream (kind 2) with its request; `HostPair(i)` → seam completes the
host UDP connect; `HostRefuse(i)` → the destination's policy class (scripted
route class at the seam for a `HostInternal` refusal); `HostAbortAssoc(i)` →
seam: error on H (`DestinationUnreachable`); `HostRecvEnd(i)` → seam releases
the guest's `Abort` or the association's end record; guest actions → stimulus.
Empty-datagram order is checked by `fwd_pair`'s datagram instance.

**`quiescence`** (`overdrive-control-plane`; conformance main
`quiesce_conf`: `quiesce_ok`'s crash and `quiesce_live`'s unbounded repair
failures; components `C1`, `C2` ↦ two
runtime components of `SharedGuestNetworkComponent`, e.g. the flow
listeners and the control listener)

| Var | Source |
|---|---|
| `cnt` | O `flow_observation().quiescence_holds` |
| `latch` | O `flow_observation().admission` |
| `rec(c)` | O QPROJ-6: `Held` → `held`, `Repaired` → `repaired`, absent → `idle` (no dropped phase, D-UP-3) |
| `leaked` | O `flow_observation().leaked_quiescence_holds` (the owner's ledger's `leaked()`, D-UP-3 / D-UP-4) |
| `foreign` | C: the driver's own `restore` call of `ForeignRestore` returned `Err(QuiescenceRestoreError::ForeignHold)`; false again once the composition is dropped (D-UP-4, PD-1) |
| `att(c)` | O QPROJ-6 `failed_attempts` |
| `table` | S `shared_table_state()` (`Complete` ⇔ true) |
| `up`, `stop` | C: `up` ⇔ the composition is running; `stop` = `crash` after the driver dropped it, `failstop` after it received the supervisor's `ServeShutdownRequest::SharedGuestNetwork`, `refused` after the composed rig's boot (`boot_server`) returned the typed boot refusal of ADR-0184 |
| `flowsOpen` | O `flow_observation()`: the number of flows the owner holds — the sum over `cids` of the entries in `guest_flows`, `dials` and `datagrams` (0 or 1 in the instance). `OpenFlow` is the stimulus that opens one; the abort at the first hold is the owner's effect this projection compares |
| `dmg`, `repLeft` | stimulus (the driver's damage, the repair-failure budget) |
| `g` | ghost |

`CountCoversRecoveries` reads: the count equals the holds of the recoveries
plus the leaked holds (D-UP-3).

| Action | Production call or fault |
|---|---|
| `Damage(c)` | seam: component `c`'s task exits |
| `OpenFlow` | seam: a guest-opened flow is admitted and paired |
| `Crash` | drop the composition |
| `RestartWith(writeOk)` (`Restart`) | recompose through the in-crate composed rig: phase 1 over the rig's `SimGuestFlowIo`, then `boot_server` with `GuestNetworkSource::Composed { io, dial }` over that seam and the rig's `BootAdapters` (its intercept the `SimMtlsIntercept` the action maps), which is the same `boot_server` `run_server` calls; boot step 8's table transaction on that intercept scripted to succeed or fail; a failure makes `boot_server` return the typed refusal `ControlPlaneError::MtlsBoot(MtlsBootError::SharedOwner { .. })` with `health.startup.refused`, reason `mtls.shared_owner` (ADR-0184), and the driver tries again. Not `run_server`: it takes only `GuestFlowAdapter::host()`, so through it `Damage(c)` and `RepFail(c)` could not be scripted at the seam |
| `RecQuiesce(c)` | `SimClock` to the supervisor's audit tick (it calls `quiesce()` for `c`'s recovery) |
| `RecRepair(c)` / `RepFail(c)` | the repair (`converge_shared` for `c`) returns `Ok` / a scripted `Err` |
| `RecRedo(c)` | damage re-applied before the post-repair audit |
| `RecRestore(c)` | the clean audit, then `restore(hold)` |
| `LeakHold` | the driver calls the composed owner's `quiesce()` and drops the returned hold (D-UP-3, approved 2026-10-14). Component-free: it stands for an Overdrive defect that drops a hold (§ *Owner and provisioner*, "Leaked hold → fail-stop"), not for a recovery; no recovery path drops one, so `rec(c)` is unaffected |
| `ForeignRestore` | the driver builds a second `QuiescenceLedger::new()` (public, PD-2), issues a hold from it and calls the composed owner's `restore(hold)`; the owner's `quiescence_holds`, `admission` and `leaked_quiescence_holds` are compared unchanged (D-UP-4, PD-1). Component-free: in production only a composition defect produces it |
| `FailStop(c)` | `SimClock` past the recovery's bound, or to the audit tick after a leaked hold; the driver receives `ServeShutdownRequest::SharedGuestNetwork` (the model's `MAXATT` abstracts the time bound of ADR-0124). After `ForeignRestore`, the supervisor's fail-stop with cause `ForeignQuiescenceHold` is not driven: the foreign `restore` is the driver's call, not the supervisor's, and no production path presents a foreign hold to the supervisor. That fail-stop is checked by `quiescence-foreign-hold-ends-in-fail-stop` and by the supervisor's unit test of the `ForeignHold` → `ForeignQuiescenceHold` mapping, with no seam (FHOLD-CHECK, user ruling 2026-10-15). The driver therefore does not pin `ForeignHoldRestoreChangesNothingThenFailStops` with `#[quint_test]`, as it does not pin `DroppedHoldKeepsForwardingQuiescedThenFailStops` (UI-V-QHOLD-DROP); the `ForeignRestore` step itself, with its owner-unchanged comparison, is driven. How randomized traces treat the supervisor's step after a `ForeignRestore` is DISTILL's, within `.claude/rules/testing.md` § "Quint conformance" (no empty handler) |
| `RecRepairNoHold(c)` | hazard-only |

##### Named runs pinned by each driver

Each driver pins with `#[quint_test(main = <its conformance main>,
max_samples = 1)]` every named run of its module's critical scenarios, and
runs `#[quint_run]` randomized traces on the same conformance main with the
seed printed on failure (D-UP-1; QPROJ-1). Every run below is checked in
`checks.toml` on that main (`backend = "evaluator"`, `expect = "holds"`) and
holds in `evidence/summary.json`.

The `SessionBecomesLive` liveness property is model-checked on `flows_sess`
(sessions only), a non-recording main that no driver replays; the session
behaviour it constrains is replayed through `flows_conf`'s session runs and
randomized traces. The instance steps by `sessStep` (`owner_flows.qnt`, the
session, session-loss and quiescence actions of `coreStep`, selected by
`CFG == "sess"`): before 2026-10-14 it stepped by `coreStep`, whose flow
and dial-slot picks range over empty sets on this instance, so the check
held vacuously on 34 states; with `sessStep` it explores 2,470 states. Its
hazard is the environment variant
`owner-flows-sess-env-guest-misses-session-loss` (assumption K-A5 dropped),
which violates it (§ *Formal protocol model*).

#### [REF] DISTILL interface contracts (DG-1 to DG-16)

**Status: approved under user delegation 2026-10-09** (DG-2-R2, DG-4-CTOR,
DG-5-A, DG-5-E, DG-5-F, DG-5-Q and DG-CONST approved by the user
2026-10-10); the items follow the contracts of INB-1, R2-END, R2-DRAIN,
CID-NOCLAIM, RESET-EXIT, UDP-EMPTY, QHOLD and NO-SURVIVE, approved by the
user 2026-10-11. Each item below is an interface contract; what it does not
name (private helpers, module-private types, the sims' stepping and
scripting methods) stays the crafter's or DISTILL's.

##### DG-1 — No binary identification of the VMM (user mandate)

Overdrive runs only with the vendored Cloud Hypervisor fork
(`vendors/cloud-hypervisor`, branch `overdrive/vhost-kernel-vsock`, ADR-0161).
No probe stage, provisioning check or typed error identifies which Cloud
Hypervisor build is installed: `VmmProbeError` gains no variant, `Vmm::probe`
keeps today's stages, provisioning keeps today's `--landlock` check, and
`infra/metal/native-preflight.sh` adds nothing. The provisioning checksum
(ADR-0161 decision 3) is the identity check. `/dev/vhost-vsock` is opened by
the VMM itself, under the fork's Landlock rule for the device
(CID-NOCLAIM, ADR-0146); no Overdrive process opens it and no startup probe
checks it. A launch whose device cannot be opened fails before READY through
the existing typed VMM-exit start failure. UI-HOST-2 has no subject.

##### DG-2 — Single-cut migration of the replaced signatures (UI-C1; DG-2-R2, approved by the user 2026-10-10)

The pinned signatures replace live ones with no deprecation shim, alias,
feature flag or parallel old path (single-cut greenfield). **Every row is
scaffolded in DISTILL, in place** — no test, body or conformance driver
waits for a later authoring time:

- **The pinned signature replaces the live one** in the DISTILL increment.
  No old and new API exist side by side, and no shim forwards one to the
  other.
- **Every production caller is adapted to the pinned shape** in the same
  increment. Where a caller can supply the new arguments and keep today's
  behaviour, it does. Only genuinely new behaviour gets a RED-scaffold body
  (`panic!("Not yet implemented -- RED scaffold")`, marked
  `// SCAFFOLD: true`), never a method, type, variant or parameter the
  contract does not name.
- **Every body and driver over the replaced surface is authored now**,
  compiled, and marked `#[ignore = "pending DELIVER <step>"]` where its
  owner is a RED scaffold, the step being the one in the last column. None
  is committed uncompiled (no unregistered file, no always-false `cfg`).
- **Existing tests turned red by a scaffold body are expected RED.** Each is
  listed in `distill/red-classification.md` with the DELIVER step that turns
  it green; none is weakened or rewritten to stay green.
- **Tests that defend only deleted surface are deleted with it**, in the
  same increment: rows 5 and 17, and the TAP allocation and scratch seams of
  row 9 (deletion discipline).

The last column names the DELIVER step that replaces the scaffold bodies
with the implementation and activates the bodies over them. A crafter does
not edit those bodies; a body that does not compile against the pinned
contract goes back to DISTILL. Step numbers are those of § *Roadmap
impact*; **the attachment-cut step** is defined below the table. Line
numbers are those of the live source before the DISTILL increment.
